Every change made to the site in this pass, page by page. Nothing is committed; use `git diff` to see exact markup, or `git checkout -- <file>` to undo a page.

## Site-wide changes

- Removed the yellow "official ruling" highlight: the `<span class="ruling">` wrappers on 11 items, the `.ruling` rule in `style.css`, and the footer line explaining the highlight. Those 11 items were then sourced or removed like any other note (see their pages below).
- Added the official Fantasy Flight documents (Codex volumes, Prophecy of Kings Rulebook, Learn to Play, Thunder's Edge Rulebook) and two ruling collections (Compiled Designer Rulings 2018–2019; unofficial Rules-as-Written & Community Consensus Rulings) as sources: removed notes they support were restored, and existing items they also state got their numbers added.
- Footer (`suffix.php`) now lists the numbered sources with links.
- Every kept item ends with a superscript naming its source number(s).
- Added the RulesPal TI4 FAQ (community consensus and designer rulings, linked to dated BoardGameGeek posts) as a source. Its unconfirmed "best reading" entries were not used. Removed notes it supports were restored, existing items it states got its number, and rulings missing from the site were added.
- Removed notes that the site already states elsewhere (other wording or another page) are listed separately under "Removed notes that the site already covers elsewhere", with a pointer to the covering item.
- Notes that were removed and later restored are listed only under "Removed notes restored".
- Owner decision: all strategy cards use the Thunder's Edge versions. The Warfare and Construction rules sections were rewritten to the revised cards (card text as transcribed on the Twilight Imperium Wiki, confirmed by RulesPal and the Thunder's Edge Rulebook), and notes that only applied to the original cards were removed (Arborec, Ul, Keleres, Mahact). Conflicts below about the old Warfare/Construction cards are resolved by this.
- Owner decision: notes that were removed only because no source could be found were restored with an asterisk (*) instead of a number. The footer explains the asterisk on a separate line. Notes contradicted by a source, navigation pointers, and notes that only applied to the original Warfare/Construction cards stay removed.
- Named components (cards, technologies, abilities, units, leaders, planets) now link to the Twilight Imperium Wiki (https://twilight-imperium.fandom.com/wiki): to the component's own page or section where one exists, otherwise to the section of the faction/card page that lists it plus a text fragment (#Section:~:text=Name) that scrolls to and highlights the name in supporting browsers. 2,170 links, including the component headings on faction and component pages; within a component's own section only the heading links to it. Names the wiki spells slightly differently are still linked; eight real misspellings on the site were corrected to the wiki name (Technological Singularity, Cosmic Phenomenae, 4X41C "Helios", Lyra Keen, Fires of the Gashlai, Trillossa Aun Mirik, Rowl Sarrig, Light/Wave Deflector). Components the wiki does not list are in WIKI_GAPS.md.
- Short faction names in page text (e.g. "the Creuss player", "the Ul player") link to the faction's page on the Twilight Imperium Wiki (394 links); a faction's own page does not link its own name. Bold cross-references in Rules Reference sections (e.g. the Movement step) link to the matching rule page.
- Owner decision: Component Limitations 23.4 now reads "except for fighters and infantry" (LRR v2.0 says "ground forces").

## Conflicts between sources (decide these; nothing was changed)

1. **Space stations and voting.** The Designer Q&A says players may vote with space stations; the Thunder's Edge Rulebook (p.10) says space stations "do not count as planets for the purpose voting, objectives, or controlling a home system". The site follows the Designer Q&A on [R_space_stations.php](R_space_stations.php) and [R_agenda_phase.php](R_agenda_phase.php).
2. **Gravity rift bonus.** The Thunder's Edge Rulebook (p.16): a gravity rift "can only contribute its movement bonus to ships that pass through it once per ship. This is a change from previous rulings." The site still says the same rift can affect a ship multiple times: the LRR item and a note on [R_gravity_rift.php](R_gravity_rift.php), and the Dimensional Tear note on [F_vuilraith.php](F_vuilraith.php).
3. **Quantum Dissemination Ω.** The Codex III card says "resolve invasions on those planets"; the FAQ note on [F_yin.php](F_yin.php) says only ground combats are resolved, not full invasion steps. The FAQ note was kept.
4. **Vuil'raith ingress placement.** The Designer Q&A says Al'raith Ix Ianovar places ingress tokens by the Cabal breakthrough's synergy; the Thunder's Edge Rulebook (p.9) uses the synergy method only when The Fracture enters via a breakthrough roll, and the four-planet method for "another ability". See [F_vuilraith.php](F_vuilraith.php).
5. **Mecatol Rex as a legendary planet.** The Thunder's Edge setup uses a Mecatol Rex tile with a legendary planet icon. The removed note "Mecatol Rex is not a legendary planet" stays removed.
6. **X-89 and Planetary Shield.** LRR 65.1 says Planetary Shield does not stop X-89 Bacterial Weapon (original card). Codex I's X-89 Ω only triggers after BOMBARDMENT is used, so the shield does block it. The restored note on [R_planetary_shield.php](R_planetary_shield.php) follows the Codex version; the LRR item is unchanged.
7. **Infantry/fighter tokens destroyed vs removed.** LRR 36.3a and 46.3a say "destroyed"; the FAQ notes say "removed". Both are kept and cited (owner's decision).
8. **Out-of-date LRR items after Thunder's Edge.** [R_anomalies.php](R_anomalies.php) says there are four types of anomaly (Thunder's Edge adds the entropic scar). [R_warfare.php](R_warfare.php) and the Construction card describe the original strategy cards, which Thunder's Edge replaces (new card text is not in any source).
9. **Acquiescence Ω (Winnu).** The Thunder's Edge reprint drops "or place" from the Codex I text ("You do not have to spend or place a command token"). The related note stays removed; the page does not mention the text change.
10. **Learn to Play vs LRR wording.** Learn to Play says excess units after combat are "destroyed" (LRR: "removed"), limits scoring to one public and one secret objective per "step of the action phase" (LRR 61.7 differs), and prints the original Diplomacy and Unstable Planet text. Learn to Play was not cited on those items.

11. **Gravity rift bonus (update).** The community consensus document agrees with the Thunder's Edge Rulebook: the +1 applies once per ship per tactical action. The site's LRR-cited items still say each pass gives +1 (see item 2).
12. **Space stations and voting (update).** The community consensus document agrees with the Designer Q&A (players may vote with space stations); only the Thunder's Edge Rulebook disagrees (see item 1).
13. **Argent Zeal and Executive Order.** The community consensus document says the Argent player does not vote first during *Executive Order* (but still casts additional votes). The Argent note says they "always vote first" ([F_argent.php](F_argent.php)); it may need an exception.
14. **Coexistence details.** The community consensus document says a player may remove coexisting infantry on a planet they control to pay a hazardous exploration cost; the Designer Q&A note says a player cannot spend another player's coexisting units. It also describes Establish Control timing and bombardment against coexisting players differently from the Thunder's Edge notes on [R_coexistence.php](R_coexistence.php). The site follows the Designer Q&A and the Thunder's Edge Rulebook.
15. **Lucky Shot / "no offensive cards on yourself"** ([R_action_cards.php](R_action_cards.php)). The community consensus document is cited on this note, but it also says a player may target themselves with *Crisis*. If *Crisis* counts as offensive, remove that citation.
16. **Old designer rulings rejected as superseded** (not used): Mentak cannot Pillage Creuss through Quantum Entanglement (LRR FAQ says it can); Nekro copied war suns/space docks are "destroyed" (LRR 90.19–90.20: returned to reinforcements); *Minister of Industry* replacing a space dock (overturned in the FAQ); *Classified Document Leaks* with *Repeal Law* (LRR FAQ differs); gravity rift rolls after all movement (LRR 41: immediately before exiting); retreating ground forces picked up during Announce Retreats (Codex I differs).

## Weakest calls in the Codex/rulebook pass

- **Ω secret objectives** ([C_objectives.php](C_objectives.php)): four notes restored on the strength of a Codex III designer note that these cards "should now synergize with various action cards and abilities", not card text.
- **Circlet of the Void** ([C_relics.php](C_relics.php)) and **X-89 with Harrow** ([F_lizix.php](F_lizix.php)): restored notes that apply card text with one step of reasoning.
- **"On the edge of the board"**: Prophecy of Kings citations were added to LRR 39.2a and 100.1c, but the rulebook's statement is limited to "the purpose of scoring objectives".

## Weakest calls in the designer-rulings / community-consensus pass

- **Pillage, one use per trade good when gained one at a time** ([F_mentak.php](F_mentak.php)): restored from a general 2018 designer statement.
- **Adapt New Strategies with Valefar Assimilator** ([F_nekro.php](F_nekro.php), [C_objectives.php](C_objectives.php)): a 2017 designer statement of intent, while the card says Valefar Assimilator technologies "do not count".
- **Minister of Peace and Coup D'etat "end of turn" abilities** ([C_agendas.php](C_agendas.php), [C_action_cards.php](C_action_cards.php)): the community consensus support is the premise of a different question.
- **Notes that rest only on the community consensus document** carry only its number; readers can tell them apart from officially sourced notes.

## Page details

### C_action_cards.php

**Notes kept**

- [Bribery] Bribery may be played after the speaker has abstained, or would vote if they are unable to. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (FAQ appendix p.42-43, Bribery): "Yes, even if the speaker cannot vote, or chooses not to vote,"
- [Bribery] A player must have cast votes for an outcome to play Bribery, and the additional votes must be cast for the same outcome. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (Errata p.40, Bribery): "For each trade good spent, cast 1 additional vote for the outcome on which you voted."
- [Confounding Legal Text] Confounding Legal Text is played before revealing the hidden agenda for the Covert Legislation agenda, and before the Drive the Debate objective may be scored. <sup>4</sup>
  - Edited from: Confounding Legal Text is played before Deadly Plot is played, before revealing the hidden agenda for the Covert Legislation agenda, and before the Drive the Debate objective may be scored.
  - Source 4 (Agendas, Covert Legislation / Legal Text): "The “Legal Text” action cards and Deadly Plot must be played before the agenda that was voted on is revealed."
  - Source 4 (Objectives, when are secrets scored): "“Legal Text” ACs would be played before Drive the Debate can be scored."
- [Confusing Legal Text] Confusing Legal Text is played before revealing the hidden agenda for the Covert Legislation agenda, and before the Drive the Debate objective may be scored. <sup>4</sup>
  - Edited from: Confusing Legal Text is played before Deadly Plot is played, before revealing the hidden agenda for the Covert Legislation agenda, and before the Drive the Debate objective may be scored.
  - Source 4 (Agendas, Covert Legislation / Legal Text): "The “Legal Text” action cards and Deadly Plot must be played before the agenda that was voted on is revealed."
  - Source 4 (Objectives, when are secrets scored): "“Legal Text” ACs would be played before Drive the Debate can be scored."
- [Courageous to the End] Effects that cancel hits, such as Sustain Damage, cannot be used to prevent ships from being destroyed. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (FAQ appendix p.42, Action Cards): "No, “Courageous to the End” does not produce hits."
- [Deadly Plot] Any prediction made for a rider or similar ability is incorrect, and will not resolve. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Agendas, Deadly Plot and predictions): "“Resolved with no effect” is not an outcome that could have been predicted, so no prediction abilities can trigger."
- [Deadly Plot] A player cannot make the prediction that Deadly Plot will be played when they predict the outcome of an agenda. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Agendas, Deadly Plot and predictions): "“Resolved with no effect” is not an outcome that could have been predicted, so no prediction abilities can trigger."
- [Deadly Plot] Deadly Plot is played before revealing the hidden agenda for the Covert Legislation agenda. <sup>4</sup>
  - Edited from: Deadly Plot is played before revealing the hidden agenda for the Covert Legislation agenda, and before the Drive the Debate objective may be scored.
  - Source 4 (Agendas, Covert Legislation / Legal Text): "The “Legal Text” action cards and Deadly Plot must be played before the agenda that was voted on is revealed."
- [Decoy Operation] If a mech is damaged when it is removed, it will remain damaged when it is placed. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (General, removed and placed damaged unit): "If it is being removed and placed via an ability such as Transit Diodes it stays in the same state."
- [Direct Hit] If multiple ships use their Sustain Damage ability, a Direct Hit may be played for each. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (FAQ appendix p.42, Action Cards): "Yes. Because the two “Direct Hit” cards are targeting different targets, this is allowed."
- [Direct Hit] A Direct Hit may be used whenever hits produced by a player’s units or abilities are cancelled by a ship using its Sustain Damage ability. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (Errata p.40, Direct Hit): "After another player’s ship uses ‘Sustain Damage’ to cancel a hit produced by your units or abilities: Destroy that ship."
  - Source 1 (FAQ appendix p.42, Action Cards): "“Direct Hit” can be used to follow up hits that are assigned by “Ambush,” “Dimensional Splicer,” “Devotion,” and other similar abilities."
- [Distinguished Councilor] A player must have cast votes for an outcome to play Distinguished Councilor. <sup>1</sup>
  - Edited from: A player must have cast votes for an outcome to play Distinguished Councilor, and the additional votes must be cast for the same outcome.
  - Source 1 (FAQ appendix p.42, Action Cards): "The “Distinguished Councilor” action card can only be played after you vote during the “V ote” step of resolving an agenda."
- [Distinguished Councilor] A player may only play Distinguished Councilor after their normal vote, not after they cast additional votes at another point. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (FAQ appendix p.42, Action Cards): "The “Distinguished Councilor” action card can only be played after you vote during the “V ote” step of resolving an agenda."
- [Divert Funding] A player must still meet the prerequisites for the technology they research. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Technology, prerequisites via action card): "If an ability instructs you to “research” a technology, you require the prerequisites on that technology to do so."
- [Experimental Battlestation] The selected space dock will use the Space Cannon ability during the Space Cannon Offense step of the current tactical action. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (FAQ appendix p.43): "“Experimental Battlestation” operates in the same timing window as “Space Cannon Offense,” can only target the active player’s ships, and can only be resolved if ships actually move into the active system."
- [Experimental Battlestation] Hits may only be assigned to the active player’s ships. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (FAQ appendix p.43): "“Experimental Battlestation” operates in the same timing window as “Space Cannon Offense,” can only target the active player’s ships, and can only be resolved if ships actually move into the active system."
- [Experimental Battlestation] Experimental Battlestation cannot be played if no ships are moved into the active system, even if the active player already has ships in that system. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (FAQ appendix p.43): "“Experimental Battlestation” operates in the same timing window as “Space Cannon Offense,” can only target the active player’s ships, and can only be resolved if ships actually move into the active system."
- [Focused Research] A player must still meet the prerequisites for the technology they research. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Technology, prerequisites via action card): "If an ability instructs you to “research” a technology, you require the prerequisites on that technology to do so."
- [Ghost Ship] If a player wishes to place a destroyer, but there are none left in their reinforcements, they may remove a destroyer from any system that does not contain one of their command tokens and place that instead. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (23.4a): "When a player would place a unit, if there are none of that type left in their reinforcements, that player can remove a unit from any system that does not contain one of their command tokens and place that unit in their reinforcements."
- [Construction Rider] If a player wishes to place a space dock, but there are none left in their reinforcements, they may remove a space dock from any system that does not contain one of their command tokens and place that instead. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (23.4a): "When a player would place a unit, if there are none of that type left in their reinforcements, that player can remove a unit from any system that does not contain one of their command tokens and place that unit in their reinforcements."
- [Ghost Squad] The Ul player cannot use Ghost Squad to move a Hel–Titan. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Titans of Ul, Hel-Titan and Ghost Squad): "No, structures cannot move."
- [Harness Energy] If a player has their maximum number of commodities, they may still play Harness Energy. If they do, they will still trigger any “when [this] player replenishes commodities” effects, most notably the Trade Agreement promissory note. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (FAQ appendix p.41, General): "Even if that player gains zero commodities when their commodities are refreshed, their “Trade Agreement” may still be played against them."
- [Impersonation] A player with three secret objectives may draw a fourth, and then shuffle one of their unscored secret objectives into the secret objective deck. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (61.21a): "If a player draws a secret objective and has more than three, that player must choose one of their unscored secret objectives and return it to the deck."
- [Impersonation] If a player has scored three secret objectives, they may use Impersonation to draw a secret objective, then immediately shuffle it into the secret objective deck. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Objectives, Impersonation): "Yes, you could draw an additional secret but would then need to return it and shuffle the secret objective deck"
- [Infiltrate] If a player wishes to place a structure, but there are none of that type left in their reinforcements, they may remove a structure of that type from any system that does not contain one of their command tokens and place that instead. That player may make the choice for each structure. <sup>1,4</sup>
  - Source 1 (23.4a): "When a player would place a unit, if there are none of that type left in their reinforcements, that player can remove a unit from any system that does not contain one of their command tokens and place that unit in their reinforcements."
  - Source 4 (General, keyword replace): "Any instance of “replace” can be considered to say “remove and place” if no units are left in reinforcements, and would be covered by Component Limitations in the LRR."
- [Infiltrate] The Ul player will place each of their Hel Titan PDS undamaged. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (General, removed and placed damaged unit): "If it is produced, placed, or replaced which would require a remove and place it is no longer damaged."
- [Intercept] Intercept cannot be played to prevent Skilled Retreat. <sup>1</sup>
  - Edited from: Intercept cannot be played to prevent Skilled Retreat or the Naalu player’s Foresight faction ability.
  - Source 1 (FAQ appendix p.42, Action Cards): "No, “Skilled Retreat” is not a retreat and cannot be canceled in this way."
- [Lucky Shot] A player cannot use Lucky Shot against their own units. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (FAQ appendix p.42, Action Cards): "“Lucky Shot” and other similar effects can only be used against other player’s units and planets."
- [Morale Boost] Morale Boost has no effect on anti–fighter barrage rolls. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (10.1c): "Game effects that reroll, modify, or otherwise affect combat rolls do not affect anti-fighter barrage rolls."
- [Plagiarize] A player does not need to meet the prerequisites of the technology they gain from Plagiarize. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Technology, prerequisites via action card): "If you are instructed to “gain” or “replace” a technology, you do not require prerequisites."
- [Refit Troops] If a player has no mechs left in their reinforcements, they may remove a mech from any system that does not contain one of their command tokens and place that instead. The mech will be placed undamaged. <sup>1,4</sup>
  - Source 1 (23.4a): "When a player would place a unit, if there are none of that type left in their reinforcements, that player can remove a unit from any system that does not contain one of their command tokens and place that unit in their reinforcements."
  - Source 4 (General, keyword replace): "Yes Refit Troops could be played with no mechs in reinforcements."
  - Source 4 (General, removed and placed damaged unit): "If it is produced, placed, or replaced which would require a remove and place it is no longer damaged."
- [Reflective Shielding] If Reflective Shielding is played after a ship uses its Sustain Damage ability during an Assign Hits step, then the hits produced by Reflective Shielding are added to any other hits produced in the immediately proceeding Roll Dice step. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (General, reflective shielding): "The hits are immediately assigned if not during the normal assign hits step. If during the normal assign hits step, they are added to the pool of hits already generated."
- [Reflective Shielding] If Reflective Shielding is played after a ship uses its Sustain Damage ability at any other time during combat, the hits are assigned immediately. <sup>4</sup>
  - Edited from: If Reflective Shielding is played after a ship uses its Sustain Damage ability at any other time during combat (for example, when the Creuss player uses their Dimensional Splicer faction technology ability), the hits are assigned immediately.
  - Source 4 (General, reflective shielding): "The hits are immediately assigned if not during the normal assign hits step. If during the normal assign hits step, they are added to the pool of hits already generated."
- [Reveal Prototype] A player must still meet the prerequisites for the technology they research. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Technology, prerequisites via action card): "If an ability instructs you to “research” a technology, you require the prerequisites on that technology to do so."
- [Reverse Engineer] It is public knowlege which action cards a player takes using Reverse Engineer. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Exploration, The Codex): "the discard is public knowledge, so anything removed from the discard is also public knowledge."
- [Rout] A player cannot announce a retreat if there is not at least one eligible system to retreat to. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (78.4c): "A player cannot announce a retreat if there is not at least one eligible system to retreat to."
- [Sabotage] A player playing an action card announces the following before Sabotage may be played: <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (FAQ appendix p.42, Action Cards): "The “Sabotage” action can be played after card targets (such as units, planets, systems, cards, outcomes, or players) have been decided on, but must be played before any effects have been resolved, votes have been cast, or any dice have been rolled."
- [Sabotage] Any targeted planets, system, units, players, cards, outcomes, and/or other such objects. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (FAQ appendix p.42, Action Cards): "The “Sabotage” action can be played after card targets (such as units, planets, systems, cards, outcomes, or players) have been decided on, but must be played before any effects have been resolved, votes have been cast, or any dice have been rolled."
- [Sabotage] Any dice are rolled and any cards are drawn only after all other players has declined to play Sabotage. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (FAQ appendix p.42, Action Cards): "The “Sabotage” action can be played after card targets (such as units, planets, systems, cards, outcomes, or players) have been decided on, but must be played before any effects have been resolved, votes have been cast, or any dice have been rolled."
- [Shields Holding] Shields Holding may be used to cancel hits produced by any ability during space combat. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (FAQ appendix p.42, Action Cards): "Yes. “Shields Holding” may be used to cancel hits that are produced by these abilities."
- [Skilled Retreat] Using Skilled Retreat is not a retreat. As such, it cannot be cancelled with the Intercept action card. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (FAQ appendix p.42, Action Cards): "No, “Skilled Retreat” is not a retreat and cannot be canceled in this way."
- [Skilled Retreat] Ground forces may be transported. <sup>1</sup>
  - Edited from: Fighters are moved without being transported. Ground forces may be transported.
  - Source 1 (FAQ appendix p.41, General): "Any effect that moves a ship allows that ship to transport units in its system, if it has available capacity."
- [Skilled Retreat] If a player has no command tokens in their reinforcements, they must take one from any pool of their command sheet and place that instead. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (20.3b): "If a game effect would place a player’s command token from their reinforcements and none are available, that player must take a token from a pool on their command"
- [Technology Rider] A player must still meet the prerequisites for the technology they research. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Technology, prerequisites via action card): "If an ability instructs you to “research” a technology, you require the prerequisites on that technology to do so."
- [Technology Rider] A player may exhaust a planet with a technology specialty to ignore a prerequisite on a technology as normal. <sup>1</sup>
  - Edited from: A player may exhaust a planet with a technology specialty to ignore a prerequisite on a technology as normal. This planet will ready at the end of the agenda phase.
  - Source 1 (64.4): "Some planets have a technology specialty, which allows those planets to be exhausted to satisfy a prerequisite when researching technology."
- [Unstable Planet] A player may select a planet with fewer than three infantry on it (including zero). <sup>1</sup>
  - Edited from: A player may select an exhausted planet, and they may select a planet with fewer than three infantry on it (including zero).
  - Source 1 (Errata p.40, Unstable Planet): "Choose 1 hazardous planet. Exhaust that planet and destroy up to 3 infantry on it."
- [Upgrade] The cruiser must be in the system when it is activated for Upgrade to be played. Upgrade cannot be played if the cruiser is moved into the active system later in the turn. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (FAQ appendix p.43): "Yes. The cruiser must already be in the activated system."
- [Upgrade] A player must have at least one cruiser in the active system to play and resolve Upgrade. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (FAQ appendix p.43): "Yes. The cruiser must already be in the activated system."
- [Upgrade] If a player wishes to place a dreadnought, but there are none left in their reinforcements, they may remove a dreadnought from any system that does not contain one of their command tokens and place that instead. This dreadnought will be placed undamaged. <sup>1,4</sup>

  - Source 4 (General, removed and placed damaged unit): "If it is produced, placed, or replaced which would require a remove and place it is no longer damaged."
- [Veto] If Veto is used after any Political Secret promissory notes have been played, those will have no effect on the replacement agenda. <sup>1</sup>
  - Edited from: If Veto is used after any Political Secret promissory notes have been played, those are immediately returned and will have no effect on the replacement agenda.
  - Source 1 (FAQ appendix p.42, Action Cards): "Yes. It is a new agenda and thus the effect of the player’s “Political Secret” is ended."
- [War Effort] If a player wishes to place a cruiser, but there are none left in their reinforcements, they may remove a cruiser from any system that does not contain one of their command tokens and place that instead. This cruiser will be placed undamaged. <sup>1,4</sup>
  - Source 1 (23.4a): "When a player would place a unit, if there are none of that type left in their reinforcements, that player can remove a unit from any system that does not contain one of their command tokens and place that unit in their reinforcements."
  - Source 4 (General, removed and placed damaged unit): "If it is produced, placed, or replaced which would require a remove and place it is no longer damaged."
- [Warfare Rider] If a player wishes to place a dreadnought, but there are none in their reinforcements, they may remove a dreadnought from any system that does not contain one of their command tokens and place that instead. This dreadnought will be placed undamaged. <sup>1,4</sup>
  - Source 1 (23.4a): "When a player would place a unit, if there are none of that type left in their reinforcements, that player can remove a unit from any system that does not contain one of their command tokens and place that unit in their reinforcements."
  - Source 4 (General, removed and placed damaged unit): "If it is produced, placed, or replaced which would require a remove and place it is no longer damaged."

  - Edited from: After playing a Construction Rider, a player may use additional abilities, including playing other rider cards.

**Removed notes restored**

- [Fighter Conscription] Only one fighter will be placed in a system containing both a space dock and a ship with capacity. <sup>10</sup>
  - Source 10 (ti_codex_1_cards_crop_marks.txt p1 Fighter Conscription card): "Place 1 fighter from your reinforcements in each system that contains 1 or more of your space docks or units that have capacity"
- [Ghost Squad] Ghost Squad is played after the active player has assigned which planet each of their ground forces are being committed to. <sup>10</sup>
  - Trimmed from: Ghost Squad is played after the active player has assigned which planet each of their ground forces are being committed to. They cannot modify this after Ghost Squad has been played.
  - Source 10 (ti_codex_1_cards_crop_marks.txt p3 Ghost Squad card): "After a player commits units to land on a planet you control"
- [Ghost Squad] A player may move zero ground forces with Ghost Squad. <sup>10</sup>
  - Source 10 (ti_codex_1_cards_crop_marks.txt p3 Ghost Squad card): "Move any number of ground forces from any planet you control in the active system"
- [Hack Election] The speaker will still vote last. <sup>10</sup>
  - Source 10 (ti_codex_1_cards_crop_marks.txt p3 Hack Election card): "voting begins with the player to the right of the speaker and continues counterclockwise"
- [Impersonation] A player cannot play Impersonation if they have less than three influence available. <sup>10</sup>
  - Source 10 (ti_codex_1_cards_crop_marks.txt p3 Impersonation card): "ACTION: Spend 3 influence to draw 1 secret objective."
- [Plagiarize] A player cannot play Plagiarize if they have less than five influence available. <sup>10</sup>
  - Source 10 (ti_codex_1_cards_crop_marks.txt p1 Plagiarize card): "ACTION: Spend 5 influence and choose a non-faction technology owned by 1 of your neighbors; gain that technology."
- [Solar Flare] The active player may still use the Space Cannon ability of their units. <sup>10</sup>
  - Source 10 (ti_codex_1_cards_crop_marks.txt p3 Solar Flare card): "After you activate a system: During this movement, other players cannot use SPACE CANNON against your ships."
- [War Machine] War Machine may only be used by effects that cause a unit to use its Production ability. It cannot be used for other effects that produce units. <sup>10</sup>
  - Source 10 (ti_codex_1_cards_crop_marks.txt p3 War Machine card): "When 1 or more of your units use PRODUCTION: Apply +4 to the total PRODUCTION value of your units and reduce the combined cost of the produced units by 1."
- [Ancient Burial Sites] A player with zero cultural planets may be chosen. <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (x3n d0g, 1/25/2019): "Can I play Ancient Burial Sites on someone who has no cultural planets?"
  - Source 5 (x3n d0g, 1/25/2019): "I would say that both are legal plays"
- [Coup D’etat] The active player may still use any “at the end of your turn” abilities. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (Legendary Planets: Jupiter Brain): "if an effect ends a player's turn, they may still use "at the end of your turn" abilities"
  - Source 6 (Legendary Planets: Jupiter Brain): "A: Yes."
- [Direct Hit] When Direct Hit is used outside of combat, if used on a ship with capacity, then fighters and/or ground forces must immediately be removed from the space area to meet the capacity limit. <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (Milty, 08/02/2018): "Player B fires PDS and produces two hits. Before assigning hits, Player A sustains damage to cancel one hit, and Player B plays a Direct Hit."
  - Source 5 (Milty, 08/02/2018): "You can’t claim “Turn Their Fleets to Dust” in this manner. During a combat, the fighters would persist until the end of combat, but in this case they are immediately destroyed."
- [Direct Hit] For example, say a player has a dreadnought, a destroyer and a fighter in a system ... The fighter in that system is immediately removed. The player must then assign the other produced hit to their destroyer. <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (Milty, 08/02/2018): "A) Immediately destroy the fighter, since there's no capacity?"
  - Source 5 (Milty, 08/02/2018): "You can’t claim “Turn Their Fleets to Dust” in this manner. During a combat, the fighters would persist until the end of combat, but in this case they are immediately destroyed."
- [Economic Initiative] A player with zero cultural planets may play Economic Initiative. <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (x3n d0g, 1/25/2019): "1) Can I play Economic Initiative when I have no cultural planets?"
  - Source 5 (x3n d0g, 1/25/2019): "I would say that both are legal plays"
- [Experimental Battlestation] If ships are moved into the active system, ships that were already in that system may be assigned any hits produced. <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (CreussEmissary (Dane), Nov 14, 2018): "it is only triggered by the move step of the tactical action and is only fireable at the active player and at his ships in the active system"
- [Experimental Battlestation] Experimental Battlestation cannot be played if ships are moved outside of the Move Ships step, such as during a retreat, or while resolving the Mahact player’s Benediction hero ability. <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (CreussEmissary (Dane), Nov 14, 2018): "it is only triggered by the move step of the tactical action and is only fireable at the active player and at his ships in the active system"
  - Source 5 (CreussEmissary (Dane), Nov 14, 2018): "I think I’ll have to walk my most recent ruling back"
- [Focused Research] Other players must decide whether to play Sabotage, or otherwise cancel the action card, before the player playing Focused Research announces which technology they are researching. <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (sigmazero13, Jan 23, 2019): "You would not have to decide which technology you are researching when “Focused Research” is played before the sabotage window."
- [Lost Star Chart] If the Enforced Travel Ban law is in play, Lost Star Chart will allow a player to move through wormholes during this action. <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (sigmazero13, Feb 19, 2018): "Lost Star Charts during Enforced Travel Ban would more or less nullify Enforced Travel Ban"
- [Lost Star Chart] A player may move from a system containing an alpha wormhole to a system containing an alpha wormhole, and similarly for beta wormholes. <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (sigmazero13, Feb 19, 2018): "All are connected to all—alpha to alpha, alpha to beta, beta to beta."
- [Lucky Shot] Effects that cancel hits, such as Sustain Damage, cannot be used to prevent ships from being destroyed. <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (@cornb93, 02/23/2018): "sustain damage cannot be used against abilities that ‘destroy’."
- [Mercenary Contract] If the planet card is returned to the planet card deck, then when a player later gains control of that planet, they will explore it. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (Action Cards: Mercenary Contract): "Yes, the planet card will be retrieved from the planet card deck and it will trigger both exploration and relic depending on its traits."
- [Mercenary Contract] The planet will not be explored if it does not have a trait. If the planet is in The Fracture, however, the gaining player will draw a relic. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (Action Cards: Mercenary Contract): "does it get re-explored (or does it re-relic for The Fracture planets)"
  - Source 6 (Action Cards: Mercenary Contract): "Yes, the planet card will be retrieved from the planet card deck and it will trigger both exploration and relic depending on its traits."
- [Puppets On A String] It is not considered the turn of the player who played Puppets On A String for game effects. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (Action Cards: Puppets on a String): "A: No, it is not your turn."
  - Source 6 (Action Cards: Puppets on a String): "it is not Yssaril’s turn, they are performing an action outside of their turn."
- [Puppets On A String] They cannot use any “at the start/end of your turn” abilities. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (Action Cards: Puppets on a String): "Can you perform transactions or "Start/end of your turn" abilities?"
  - Source 6 (Action Cards: Puppets on a String): "A: No, it is not your turn."
- [Puppets On A String] If the Yssaril player plays Puppets On A String, and owns their Transparasteel Plating faction technology, passed players may still play action cards during the action. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (Action Cards: Puppets on a String): "If Yssaril plays this, and has Transparasteel Plating, can other players play action cards?"
  - Source 6 (Action Cards: Puppets on a String): "A: Yes, it is not Yssaril’s turn"
- [Puppets On A String] The active player cannot use the Fleet Logistics technology to perform an additional action. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (Action Cards: Puppets on a String): "Fleet Logistics = no, it is not a turn, only an action."
- [Puppets On A String] The active player may use the Master Plan action card to perform an additional action. <sup>6</sup>
  - Trimmed from: The active player may use the Master Plan action card or the Minister of War agenda to perform an additional action.
  - Source 6 (Action Cards: Puppets on a String): "Master Plan = yes"
- [Puppets On A String] If the active player performs a component action, they may then use the ability of Suffi An, the Keleres commander, to perform additional actions. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (Action Cards: Puppets on a String): "you can use Keleres commander if the action you perform is itself a component action"
- [Repeal Law] There must be at least one law in play for a player to play and resolve Repeal Law. <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (x3n d0g, 1/25/2019): "'No, you can't just play an action card that has no legal target in order to skip a turn' (think Repeal Law when there are no laws in play)"
- [Rescue] If the chosen ship is in a gravity rift, it must roll for removal. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (Action Cards: Rescue): "Rescue: If the ship is in a gravity rift, does it roll for it?"
  - Source 6 (Action Cards: Rescue): "A: Yes."
- [Sabotage] If a player has a second copy of an action card, they may play it if the first was cancelled by Sabotage. <sup>1,5</sup>
  - Source 5 (sigmazero13, Jan 11, 2018): "Because the card was cancelled, yes, you can play another copy of the same action card."
  - Source 1 (2.6b): "Canceled cards are not treated as being played."
- [Shields Holding] A player cannot play a second Shields Holding to cancel a second pair of hits produced by the same dice roll or other source. <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (mjdomask, Dec 20, 2017): "Only one instance of Shields Holding may be played to cancel hits from an incoming group of hits."
- [Veto] Each agenda is considered separate for the purpose of limiting each pair of players to one transaction per agenda. <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (sigmazero13, Jun 19, 2018): "I would also say that they could perform new transactions"
  - Source 5 (sigmazero13, Jun 19, 2018): "If players (for some reason) made transactions prior to the Quash, does the new agenda "reset" this?"
- [Assassinate Representative] The chosen player may still play rider cards or use other abilities. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (assassinate-representative-riders (Community consensus)): "Yes — it only stops that player voting; unlike Political Secret, it doesn't block action cards."
- [Bribery] If the Argent player is speaker, only they can play Bribery, and must do so immediately after they cast votes. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (bribery-rules (Community consensus)): "Only a player who actually voted."
  - Source 2 (bribery-rules (Community consensus)): "If an Argent speaker votes first with Zeal, Bribery comes right after that vote."
- [Confounding Legal Text] Any predictions made on the outcome of the agenda resolve based on the newly elected player. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (legal-text-cards-and-riders (Community consensus)): "riders and agenda-phase secrets like Drive the Debate use the final elected player"
- [Confusing Legal Text] Any predictions made on the outcome of the agenda resolve based on the newly elected player. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (legal-text-cards-and-riders (Community consensus)): "riders and agenda-phase secrets like Drive the Debate use the final elected player"
- [Construction Rider] The effect of a successful Construction Rider will be resolved after the effect of the agenda. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (agenda-before-riders-resolution (Community consensus)): "The agenda's outcome resolves first, then the riders that predicted it."
- [Diplomacy Rider] The effect of a successful Diplomacy Rider will be resolved after the effect of the agenda. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (agenda-before-riders-resolution (Community consensus)): "The agenda's outcome resolves first, then the riders that predicted it."
- [Imperial Rider] The effect of a successful Imperial Rider will be resolved after the effect of the agenda. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (agenda-before-riders-resolution (Community consensus)): "The agenda's outcome resolves first, then the riders that predicted it."
- [Leadership Rider] The effect of a successful Leadership Rider will be resolved after the effect of the agenda. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (agenda-before-riders-resolution (Community consensus)): "The agenda's outcome resolves first, then the riders that predicted it."
- [Politics Rider] The effect of a successful Politics Rider will be resolved after the effect of the agenda. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (agenda-before-riders-resolution (Community consensus)): "The agenda's outcome resolves first, then the riders that predicted it."
- [Technology Rider] The effect of a successful Technology Rider will be resolved after the effect of the agenda. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (agenda-before-riders-resolution (Community consensus)): "The agenda's outcome resolves first, then the riders that predicted it."
- [Trade Rider] The effect of a successful Trade Rider will be resolved after the effect of the agenda. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (agenda-before-riders-resolution (Community consensus)): "The agenda's outcome resolves first, then the riders that predicted it."
- [Warfare Rider] The effect of a successful Warfare Rider will be resolved after the effect of the agenda. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (agenda-before-riders-resolution (Community consensus)): "The agenda's outcome resolves first, then the riders that predicted it."
- [Construction Rider] If a player successfully resolves a Construction Rider while they own the Minister of Industry law, they use the Production ability of their units in the system where they place their space dock. They may exhaust planets for resources, but those planets cannot be used to cast votes for the remainder of the agenda phase. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (minister-of-industry-trigger (Community consensus)): "a dock placed by a Construction Rider in the agenda phase does, payable only with planets you haven't exhausted"
  - Source 2 (exhausting-planets-in-agenda-phase (Community consensus)): "but those planets then can't vote"
- [Courageous to the End] Any combat roll modifiers will not apply to the dice roll for Courageous to the End. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (what-is-a-combat-roll (Community consensus)): "Sardakk's Courageous to the End are ability rolls, so Morale Boost, Sardakk's +1, Jol-Nar's Fragile and effects that reroll combat rolls don't touch them"
- [Diplomatic Pressure] The target player chooses which promissory note they give. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (target-chooses-promissory-note (Community consensus)): "The target does; the other player can't look at or name a specific note."
- [Diplomatic Pressure] A player cannot play a second Diplomatic Pressure targeting the same player during the same agenda. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (same-name-action-cards-one-window (Community consensus)): "you cannot play more than one action card with the same name in a single timing window to affect the same units or effect"
- [Diplomatic Pressure] A player may play a second Diplomatic Pressure targeting a different player during the same agenda. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (same-name-action-cards-one-window (Community consensus)): "you cannot play more than one action card with the same name in a single timing window to affect the same units or effect"
  - Source 2 (same-name-action-cards-one-window (Community consensus)): "Direct Hit can be played more than once because each copy targets a different ship."
- [Diplomatic Pressure] A player may play a second Diplomatic Pressure targeting the same player during a later agenda. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (same-name-action-cards-one-window (Community consensus)): "you cannot play more than one action card with the same name in a single timing window to affect the same units or effect"
- [Direct Hit] When a player uses the Sustain Damage ability of one of their ships, they do not have to decide if another of their ships in the same combat will use its Sustain Damage ability until after their opponent has used or declined to use a Direct Hit. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (multiple-direct-hits-and-shields-holding (Community consensus)): "Sustain Damage is used unit by unit, so you can wait to see a Direct Hit before sustaining with more"
- [Direct Hit] A mech cannot be destroyed by Direct Hit. <sup>2</sup>
  - Trimmed from: A mech cannot be destroyed by Direct Hit, unless a game effect causes the mech to be considered a ship.
  - Source 2 (direct-hit-vs-mechs (Community consensus)): "No — Direct Hit targets ships, and mechs are ground forces"
- [Disable] Disable has no effect on the Magen Defense Grid Ω technology. <sup>2</sup>
  - Trimmed from: Disable has no effect on the Magen Defense Grid Ω or Magen Defense Grid ΩΩ technologies.
  - Source 2 (magen-defense-grid-disabled-pds (Community consensus)): "Yes — Disable only strips the PDS's Planetary Shield and Space Cannon; it is still a structure, so Magen Defense Grid still produces its hit."
- [Disable] Disable does not affect the Space Cannon Offense step, and is not played until the start of the Invasion step. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (ceasefire-and-disable-vs-space-cannon (Community consensus)): "Disable is played at invasion and only shuts off PDS on the planets being invaded; Space Cannon Offense has already been fired by then."
- [Experimental Battlestation] If all moving ships are lost to a gravity rift, and none arrive in the active system, Experimental Battlestation cannot be played. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (experimental-battlestation-trigger (Designer ruling)): "not when nothing moves in"
- [Flank Speed] A second Flank Speed cannot be played to give +2 to the move value of each ship. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (movement-bonuses-stack (Community consensus)): "Two Flank Speeds can't be played together, though."
- [Flank Speed] Cancelling Flank Speed will not cancel the system activation. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (sabotaged-action-card-turn-not-used (Community consensus)): "if Flank Speed or Upgrade is Sabotaged after you activated a system, the system stays activated and you carry on without the bonus"
- [Lost Star Chart] If the active system contains a beta wormhole, a player that has a unit with the Deep Space Cannon ability in an alpha wormhole may produce hits against ships in the active system during the Space Cannon Offense step of the tactical action, and vice versa. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (lost-star-chart (Community consensus)): "every alpha and beta wormhole system is adjacent to every other, for everyone, including other players' Space Cannon"
- [Maneuvering Jets] Maneuvering Jets may cancel hits produced during either the Space Cannon Offense or the Space Cannon Defense step. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (maneuvering-jets-ground-forces (Community consensus)): "it cancels Space Cannon hits on your ground forces as well as your ships"
- [Maneuvering Jets] A player cannot play a second Maneuvering Jets to cancel a second hit produced by the same Space Cannon roll. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (same-name-action-cards-one-window (Community consensus)): "you cannot play more than one action card with the same name in a single timing window to affect the same units or effect"
- [Maneuvering Jets] During the Space Cannon Offense step, each player makes their Space Cannon roll independent of each other player, in clockwise order. As such, a player may use one Maneuvering Jets after each other player makes a space cannon roll. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (space-cannon-one-player-at-a-time (Community consensus)): "Each player's roll, hit assignment, Sustain Damage and responses like Direct Hit finish before the next fires"
- [Master Plan] If a player’s turn is ended by a game effect, they cannot use Master Plan to perform an additional action. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (xxcha-nullification-field-timing (Community consensus)): "Once the turn ends, nothing more happens in it: no further after-activation abilities, no transactions and no extra action from Master Plan."
- [Morale Boost] A second Morale Boost cannot be played during a combat round to give +2 to the combat rolls of a player’s units. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (same-name-action-cards-one-window (Community consensus)): "you cannot play more than one action card with the same name in a single timing window to affect the same units or effect"
- [Nav Suite] Wormholes are not anomalies. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (which-systems-are-anomalies (Community consensus)): "Empty systems and wormhole systems are not anomalies unless bordered."
- [Nav Suite] A player may move ships into a supernova. After moving into, those ships may remain there and move out during a later action without harm. <sup>2</sup>
  - Trimmed from: A player may move ships through or into a supernova. After moving into, those ships may remain there and move out during a later action without harm.
  - Source 2 (supernova-planets-and-activation (Community consensus)): "entering with Nav Suite all work, and ships can always move out"
  - Source 2 (anomalies-restrict-moving-in-only (Community consensus)): "Ships already there stay and may leave normally"
- [Parley] The returned ground forces cannot be committed to another planet during the same tactical action. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (parley-timing (Community consensus)): "to try again you need the system free of your command token"
- [Plagiarize] The active player must announce which technology they are gaining before other players decide whether to play a Sabotage, or otherwise cancel the action card. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (sabotage-timing (Community consensus)): "After the player announces the card's choices"
- [Plague] A planet with zero infantry on it may be targeted by Plague. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (action-card-with-zero-effect (Community consensus)): "Players relaying an official reply confirmed Plague for zero."
- [Public Disgrace] If the originally chosen strategy card has trade goods on it, those will not be taken if Public Disgrace is played. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (public-disgrace-trade-goods (Community consensus)): "Trade goods are collected once the choice sticks, so they stay on the returned card for the next chooser."
- [Public Disgrace] Public Disgrace may only be played during the regular choosing of a strategy card during the strategy phase. It cannot be played when other effects cause a player to take a strategy card, such as the Imperial Arbiter agenda. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (public-disgrace-vs-swaps (Community consensus)): "Public Disgrace triggers when a player chooses a strategy card, and those swaps at the end of the strategy phase aren't choices."
- [Reactor Meltdown] A player cannot destroy their own space dock with Reactor Meltdown. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (destroy-effects-on-own-units (Community consensus)): "abilities that destroy units can only be used against other players' units and planets"
- [Reverse Engineer] Reverse Engineer may be played if the action card is discarded after being played or cancelled, if it is discarded due to hand size limits, or if it is discarded for another game effect. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (reverse-engineer-just-played-card (Community consensus)): "It takes a component action card another player discards for any reason, so one they just played or one cancelled by Sabotage"
- [Rout] A player cannot announce a retreat from the space combat initiated by the Mahact player’s Benediction hero ability. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (mahact-hero-benediction (Community consensus)): "Neither side may retreat or use abilities that move ships, Skilled Retreat included."
- [Sabotage] If an action card is cancelled by Sabotage, no costs are paid. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (sabotage-timing (Community consensus)): "but before anything changes the game state, such as rolling dice or spending trade goods"
- [Sabotage] If an action card instructs a player to research a technology, that player need not announce what technology they are researching until all other players has declined to play Sabotage. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (sabotage-timing (Community consensus)): "Focused Research is the exception: its technology is chosen during resolution, after the Sabotage window."
- [Sabotage] If the action card that was cancelled by Sabotage was to be used to perform a component action, the active player must perform a different action, or pass. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (sabotaged-action-card-turn-not-used (Community consensus)): "a cancelled card counts as not played, so you still take an action (or pass, if allowed)"
- [Sabotage] If the component action was to be the second action the active player was to perform on their turn, through an effect such as the Fleet Logistics technology, the active player may end their turn without performing a second action and without passing. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (sabotaged-action-card-turn-not-used (Community consensus)): "If it was the optional extra action from Fleet Logistics, you can just end your turn."
- [Shields Holding] Shields Holding cannot be used to cancel hits produced by Space Cannon abilities. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (shields-holding-which-hits (Community consensus)): "Not Space Cannon Offense or Defense, which happen outside space combat, and not 'destroy' effects such as Courageous to the End."
- [Shields Holding] Shields Holding cannot be used to prevent an effect that directly destroys a unit. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (shields-holding-which-hits (Community consensus)): "Not Space Cannon Offense or Defense, which happen outside space combat, and not 'destroy' effects such as Courageous to the End."
- [Shields Holding] Shields Holding cannot be used during ground combat. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (shields-holding-which-hits (Community consensus)): "Hits during space combat, including Anti-Fighter Barrage in the first round"
- [Shields Holding] Shields Holding may be used to cancel hits produced by an anti–fighter barrage roll. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (shields-holding-which-hits (Community consensus)): "Hits during space combat, including Anti-Fighter Barrage in the first round"
- [Skilled Retreat] A player may use Skilled Retreat to move into a system that does not contain their ships, as long as it does not contain another player’s ships. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (skilled-retreat-rules (Community consensus)): "It can go to any adjacent system without other players' ships"
- [Skilled Retreat] After moving, capacity and fleet pool limits apply in the destination system. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (skilled-retreat-rules (Community consensus)): "Capacity and fleet limits apply again at the destination"
- [Skilled Retreat] If the destination system already contains a player’s command token, no command token is placed. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (skilled-retreat-own-command-token (Community consensus)): "you just don't place a second one"
- [Tactical Bombardment] A player must have at least one unit with the Bombardment ability to play and resolve Tactical Bombardment. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (tactical-bombardment-no-enemy-planets (Community consensus)): "it only requires that you have a unit with Bombardment in that system"
- [Tactical Bombardment] A player may select a system that contains zero readied planets controlled by other players. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (tactical-bombardment-no-enemy-planets (Community consensus)): "it only requires that you have a unit with Bombardment in that system"
- [Uprising] Uprising cannot be played if all planets owned by each other player is exhausted. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (component-action-must-fully-resolve (Community consensus)): "use Uprising on an exhausted planet"
- [Uprising] Uprising cannot target an exhausted planet. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (component-action-must-fully-resolve (Community consensus)): "use Uprising on an exhausted planet"
- [Veto] Veto, the Xxcha Quash faction ability, the Xxcha Political Favor promissory note, and the Political Secret promissory note are all played in the same timing window, before the rider timing window. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (when-effects-before-after-effects (Community consensus)): "'when' effects (Quash, Veto, Political Favor, Political Secret) resolve first, then 'after' effects (Riders"
- [Waylay] A ship with the Sustain Damage ability may cancel a hit produced by an anti–fighter barrage roll if Waylay causes that ship to be eligible to be hit. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (raid-formation-and-waylay (Community consensus)): "With Waylay, those hits still hit ships and the opponent assigns them normally, using Sustain Damage on undamaged ships if they like."

**Notes added** (rulings that were not on the site before)

- [Bribery] The text of Bribery is changed to: “After the speaker votes on an agenda: Spend any number of trade goods. For each trade good spent, cast 1 additional vote for the outcome on which you voted.” <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (Errata: Bribery): "cast 1 additional vote for the outcome on which you voted"
- [Unstable Planet] The text of Unstable Planet is changed to: “Action: Choose 1 hazardous planet. Exhaust that planet and destroy up to 3 infantry on it.” <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (Errata: Unstable Planet): "Action: Choose 1 hazardous planet. Exhaust that planet and destroy up to 3 infantry on it."
- [Veto] The text of Veto is changed to: “When an agenda is revealed: Discard that agenda and reveal 1 agenda from the top of the deck. Players vote on this agenda instead.” <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (Errata: Veto): "Discard that agenda and reveal 1 agenda from the top of the deck. Players vote on this agenda instead."
- [Shields Holding] During a space combat, each player may play a Shields Holding during the same timing window, as each card cancels a different set of hits. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (FAQ Action Cards): "it is legal to play both cards."
- [Extreme Duress] If Coup D’etat cancels the strategic action the affected player performs, that player has not yet performed their next action. Extreme Duress remains in play until that player’s next turn, when they must still resolve a strategic action or suffer its effect. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (Action Cards): "Extreme Duress will remain in play until that player’s next turn, where they must still resolve a Strategic Action or suffer the consequences."
- [Mercenary Contract] If the planet card is returned to the planet card deck, all cards attached to that planet are purged. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (Action Cards): "The attachments are purged (according to Dane)."
- [Crisis] A player may target themselves with Crisis. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (Action Cards): "Yes, you are a valid target for Crisis."
- [Exchange Program] The agreement between the players includes the planets on which the infantry will be placed. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (Action Cards): "The agreement includes the planets where infantry will be placed."
- [Lie In Wait] If players make a deal for one of them to play an action card, Lie In Wait resolves after that action card is played and resolved. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (Action Cards): "Lie in Wait would resolve after that action card is played and resolved."
- [Puppets On A String] The player who played Puppets On A String cannot resolve transactions during that action, as it is not their turn. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (Action Cards): "No, it is not your turn."
- [Puppets On A String] Abilities that end a player’s turn, such as Minister of Peace, do not prevent the action from being performed, and cannot fully resolve, as there is no turn to end. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (Action Cards): "Those abilities do not prevent the action being taken, and cannot fully resolve as there is no turn to end."
- [Public Disgrace] The player who must choose a different strategy card does not gain any trade goods that are on the strategy card they originally chose. Trade goods on a strategy card are gained by the player who ends up with that strategy card. <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (Fazuul 10/17/2018): "Public Disgrace is intended to replace that effect and force them to choose a different card instead. The trade good should go to the person who actually ends up with the card."
  - Source 5 (Milty 10/30/2018): "The reason you don’t for Public Disgrace ... is that it is a replacement effect that uses the word “instead.”"
- [Skilled Retreat] A player may move their ships to a system that already contains one of their command tokens. <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (JamesG, Jan 19, 2018): "For both Skilled Retreat and Foresight, can the player move to a system that already contains one of their command tokens"
  - Source 5 (JamesG, Jan 19, 2018): "Dane's Answer: That is correct."
- [Skilled Retreat] All of the player’s ships in the active system are moved, including fighters, even if there is not enough capacity to transport them. <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (sigmazero13, Jul 18, 2018): "Would this include fighters (even if there's not enough transport to move them)? As written, I'd say yes.
- [Unstable Planet] A player may choose an exhausted hazardous planet. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (unstable-planet-up-to-three (Community consensus)): "It can also target an exhausted hazardous planet, since its effects are joined by 'and'."
- [Emergency Repairs] Emergency Repairs cannot prevent a ship from being destroyed by the Direct Hit action card, as Emergency Repairs is played at the end of the combat round. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (emergency-repairs-vs-direct-hit (Community consensus)): "Direct Hit is played as Sustain Damage is used, while hits are being assigned; Emergency Repairs comes at the end of the round, too late."
- [Scramble Frequency] Scramble Frequency rerolls all of the dice rolled for that ability, including dice rolled against different planets. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (scramble-frequency-all-dice (Community consensus)): "all of that ability's dice are rolled together, so the card rerolls all of them"
- [Signal Jamming] The command token is placed from a single chosen player’s reinforcements. Signal Jamming cannot be played choosing a player who has no command tokens in their reinforcements. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (signal-jamming-one-player (Community consensus)): "it names a single other player, whose reinforcements supply the one token you place"
- [Coup D’etat] Coup D’etat cannot be played when a player resolves the primary ability of a strategy card through a component action, such as with the Winnu player’s hero, Mathis Mathinus, as that is not a strategic action. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (coup-detat-vs-component-primaries (Community consensus)): "those are component actions that resolve a primary, not strategic actions"
- [Insider Information] If the Covert Legislation agenda is revealed, it resolves before Insider Information; the player looks at the agenda after the one drawn by the speaker. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (insider-information-covert-legislation (Community consensus)): "Covert Legislation is a 'when' effect that takes the next agenda first, so Insider Information, an 'after' effect, sees the card after that"
- [Rescue] The chosen ship cannot be moved out of a system that contains the player’s command token. It may transport fighters and ground forces. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (rescue-action-card (Community consensus)): "not from a system with your command token"
- [Brilliance] The chosen player gains their own faction’s breakthrough. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (te-small-clarifications (Community consensus)): "Brilliance's chosen player gains their own breakthrough"
