- [Ancient Burial Sites] Ancient Burial Sites is played before the first agenda is revealed. <sup>*</sup>
- [Archaeological Expedition] A player must control at least one planet with a trait to play and resolve Archaeological Expedition. <sup>*</sup>
- [Bribery] A player may spend zero trade goods when they play Bribery. <sup>*</sup>
- [Bribery] The speaker may play Distinguished Councilor after another player plays Bribery. <sup>*</sup>
- [Bribery] Bribery is played before any effects that change the outcome of an agenda. <sup>*</sup>
- [Brilliance] A player may choose themself as the player who gains their breakthrough. <sup>*</sup>
- [Bunker] The modifier will apply to bombardment rolls for each planet in the active system. <sup>*</sup>
- [Confounding Legal Text] Confounding Legal Text is played after any effects that allow a player to cast additional votes. <sup>*</sup>
- [Confounding Legal Text] Confounding Legal Text may be played after Confusing Legal Text is played. <sup>*</sup>
- [Confusing Legal Text] Confusing Legal Text is played after any effects that allow a player to cast additional votes. <sup>*</sup>
- [Confusing Legal Text] Confusing Legal Text may be played after Confounding Legal Text is played. <sup>*</sup>
- [Construction Rider] The Saar player may play a Construction Rider, and may place a space dock in a system containing a planet they control if successful. <sup>*</sup>
- [Crisis] Crisis will skip the turn of the next unpassed player. <sup>*</sup>
- [Deadly Plot] Deadly Plot is played after any effects that allow a player to cast additional votes, and after any effects that change the outcome of an agenda. <sup>*</sup>
- [Deadly Plot] If a player predicts multiple outcomes, they may play Deadly Plot regardless of which outcome would be resolved. <sup>*</sup>
- [Deadly Plot] If the Xxcha player uses their commander, Elder Qanoj, to vote for one outcome, when they have predicted another, they may play Deadly Plot regardless of which outcome would be resolved. <sup>*</sup>
- [Diplomacy Rider] The Mecatol Rex system may be chosen. <sup>*</sup>
- [Diplomatic Pressure] Giving a promissory note because of Diplomatic Pressure is not resolving a transaction. <sup>*</sup>
- [Disable] If the Ul player is targeted, their Hel–Titans will still participate in the ground combat during the current invasion. <sup>*</sup>
- [Distinguished Councilor] The speaker may play Distinguished Councilor after another player plays Bribery. <sup>*</sup>
- [Distinguished Councilor] Distinguished Councilor is played before any effects that change the outcome of an agenda. <sup>*</sup>
- [Divert Funding] The returned technology does not count towards meeting the prerequisites. <sup>*</sup>
- [Divert Funding] The researched technology may be a unit upgrade technology, and it may be a faction technology. <sup>*</sup>
- [Divert Funding] The researched technology cannot be the returned technology. <sup>*</sup>
- [Divert Funding] If a player later gains the technology they returned, they gain it readied. <sup>*</sup>
- [Divert Funding] If the player returns the Antimass Deflectors technology, their units may remain in and move out of any asteroid fields they are currently in, but cannot move additional units into or through. <sup>*</sup>
- [Emergency Repairs] A player may play Emergency Repairs at the start of the first round of combat to repair ships damaged in a previous combat, or during the Space Cannon Offense step of the current action. <sup>*</sup>
- [Exchange Program] The player who played Exchange Program does not have to agree to place the infantry. <sup>*</sup>
- [Experimental Battlestation] If a ship is moved out of the active system and then back in, Experimental Battlestation may be played. <sup>*</sup>
- [Extreme Duress] If that player has the ability to perform multiple actions in a turn, their first action must be a strategic action to avoid the penalty. <sup>*</sup>
- [Extreme Duress] If a player has multiple strategy cards, at least one of them needs to be readied to target them with Extreme Duress <sup>*</sup>
- [Extreme Duress] If they have multiple readied, they may perform a strategic action with any to avoid the penalty. <sup>*</sup>
- [Fire Team] Any modifiers on the original combat roll will apply to the reroll. <sup>*</sup>
- [Focused Research] A player cannot play Focused Research if they have less than four trade goods. <sup>*</sup>
- [Frontline Deployment] All three infantry must be placed on a single planet. <sup>*</sup>
- [Ghost Ship] A player may place the destroyer in the Creuss gate (tile 17), the wormhole nexus, or any system with a printed wormhole or wormhole token. <sup>*</sup>
- [Ghost Ship] The destroyer cannot be placed in the home system of an eliminated player. <sup>*</sup>
- [Ghost Squad] Ghost Squad may be played whenever ground forces are committed, such as from the Yin player’s Quantum Dissemination Ω hero ability. <sup>*</sup>
- [Ghost Squad] Ghost Squad cannot be played in response to abilities that place ground forces on a planet without committing them, such as the Colonial Redistribution agenda. <sup>*</sup>
- [Hack Election] The Argent player will still vote before all other players. <sup>*</sup>
- [Hack Election Ω] The speaker votes before the player that played Hack Election Ω. <sup>*</sup>
- [Hack Election Ω] Players will play Bribery after the speaker votes. The player that played Hack Election Ω cannot play Bribery. <sup>*</sup>
- [Hack Election Ω] If the Argent player plays Hack Election Ω, they will vote last. <sup>*</sup>
- [In The Silence Of Space] Only the ships in the chosen system may move through systems that contain other players’ ships. Ships in other systems may still move to the active system if they are able to do so without moving through systems that contain other players’ ships. <sup>*</sup>
- [Infiltrate] If the L1Z1X player plays Infiltrate before they resolve their Assimilate ability, or vice versa, they will replace zero PDS and space docks with zero PDS and space docks when they resolve the latter ability. <sup>*</sup>
- [Intercept] During the next round of combat, the targeted player may declare another retreat. <sup>*</sup>
- [Maneuvering Jets] Maneuvering Jets cannot be used to cancel hits during combat. <sup>*</sup>
- [Maneuvering Jets] During the Space Cannon Defense step, the units on each planet make their Space Cannon roll independent of the units on each other planet. The active player chooses the order. As such, a player may use one Maneuvering Jets for each planet they are committing ground forces to. <sup>*</sup>
- [Manipulate Investments] If a player still has a strategy card because of Political Stability, trade goods may be placed on that strategy card. However, those trade goods will remain on that strategy card until it is chosen from the common area. <sup>*</sup>
- [Manipulate Investments] If a player takes the strategy card with trade goods on it from the player who played Political Stability, using the ability of the Imperial Arbiter law or similar, they will not gain the trade goods, which will remain on the strategy card. <sup>*</sup>
- [Master Plan] Effects that trigger at the start or end of a player’s turn will not trigger between each of those player’s actions. <sup>*</sup>
- [Master Plan] A player cannot use Master Plan to pass on the same turn they performed an action. <sup>*</sup>
- [Master Plan] If a player’s second action would be to use a component action to play an action card, and that card is cancelled, they are not required to perform an alternate second action on that turn. <sup>*</sup>
- [Mercenary Contract] When a planet card is returned to the planet card deck, the player that previously controlled it will no longer do so. They remove their control token from the planet. <sup>*</sup>
- [Mercenary Contract] If the Mecatol Rex planet card is returned to the planet card deck, the custodians token is not replaced. A player will be able to later commit ground forces without paying influence, and without gaining a victory point. <sup>*</sup>
- [Mercenary Contract] If a legendary planet card is returned to the planet card deck, the player that controlled it also loses the associated legendary planet ability card. <sup>*</sup>
- [Mining Initiative] Mining Initiative does not exhaust the chosen planet. <sup>*</sup>
- [Morale Boost] The +1 will apply to any rerolls during the combat round. <sup>*</sup>
- [Nav Suite] An anomaly will retain its regular effect if a player retreats. <sup>*</sup>
- [Nav Suite] A player may move ships through or into an asteroid field without the Antimass Deflectors technology. After moving into, those ships may remain there and move out during a later action without harm. <sup>*</sup>
- [Nav Suite] A player may move ships through or out of a gravity rift without rolling for removal. Those ships will not get +1 to their move value. <sup>*</sup>
- [Nav Suite] A player may move ships through a nebula. Ships moving out of a nebula retain their normal move value. <sup>*</sup>
- [Nav Suite] Other players cannot ignore the effect of anomalies during this tactical action. <sup>*</sup>
- [Nav Suite] The Naalu player will still be affected by anomalies if they use their Foresight faction ability. <sup>*</sup>
- [Parley] If a player commits ground forces to multiple planets, Parley will affect ground forces on only one planet. <sup>*</sup>
- [Plagiarize] If a player’s neighbor owns a faction–specific unit upgrade, it cannot be chosen in order to gain the generic version of that unit upgrade by using Plagiarize. <sup>*</sup>
- [Political Stability] During the upcoming agenda phase, all abilities stay resolved in speaker order, not initiative order. <sup>*</sup>
- [Political Stability] The strategy cards are readied when Political Stability is played. <sup>*</sup>
- [Political Stability] The “Return Strategy Cards” step is the last step of the status phase. All other steps must be completed by all players before Political Stability may be played. This includes scoring and revealing objectives, drawing action cards (and discarding down to hand limit, if necessary), and gaining and redistributing command tokens. <sup>*</sup>
- [Political Stability] If a player draws Political Stability during the status phase, they may play it during the same phase. <sup>*</sup>
- [Puppets On A String] The player who played Puppets On A String is considered the active player during their action. <sup>*</sup>
- [Puppets On A String] The active player may use any “before/after you perform an action” abilities. <sup>*</sup>
- [Puppets On A String] The active player is still considered passed during their action. They do not pass at the end of the action. <sup>*</sup>
- [Puppets On A String] The active player cannot score the Prove Endurance secret objective at the end of their action. <sup>*</sup>
- [Reactor Meltdown] If a player owns a space dock in another player’s home system, that space dock cannot be targeted by Reactor Meltdown. <sup>*</sup>
- [Reactor Meltdown] A space dock in an eliminated player’s home system cannot be targeted. <sup>*</sup>
- [Reflective Shielding] A unit that used its Sustain Damage ability to cancel some of those other hits, and been repaired, cannot use its Sustain Damage ability again to cancel the hits produced by Reflective Shielding. <sup>*</sup>
- [Reparations] Reparations may be played by a player with no exhausted planets, or when they lose control of a planet to a player with no readied planets. <sup>*</sup>
- [Reparations] Reparations cannot be played by a player with no exhausted planets when they lose control of a planet to a player with no readied planets. <sup>*</sup>
- [Reveal Prototype] A player cannot play Reveal Prototype if they have less than four resources available. <sup>*</sup>
- [Reveal Prototype] A player cannot play Reveal Prototype if they already own the unit upgrade technology for each unit they have in the combat. <sup>*</sup>
- [Rise of a Messiah] A player that controls zero planets may play Rise of a Messiah. <sup>*</sup>
- [Sabotage] The value of any variable cost to be paid. <sup>*</sup>
- [Sabotage] If an action card is played that will have an effect later, such as a rider, that card may only be cancelled by Sabotage when it is originally played. <sup>*</sup>
- [Sanction] After playing a Sanction, a player may use additional abilities, including playing rider cards. <sup>*</sup>
- [Signal Jamming] The Mecatol Rex system may be chosen. <sup>*</sup>
- [Signal Jamming] A command token cannot be placed in an eliminated player’s home system. <sup>*</sup>
- [Solar Flare] During the Space Cannon Defense step of an invasion during the same tactical action, other players may use the Space Cannon ability of their units. <sup>*</sup>
- [Spy] If the targeted player has Reverse Engineer in their hand, they must first give a random action card to the player who played Spy. Only if the card they gave was not Reverse Engineer may then then play it to take Spy into their hand from the discard pile. <sup>*</sup>
- [Strategize] The active player must still spend a command token to perform the secondary ability, other than for Leadership. <sup>*</sup>
- [Veto] A second Veto may be used on the replacement agenda. <sup>*</sup>

- [Publicize Weapon Schematics] If the Muaat does not own their Prototype War Sun II faction unit upgrade technology, they do not own a war sun technology. <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (BGG, sigmazero13, Jan 11 2018): "Do pre-printed units count as "technologies"? Specifically, does Prototype War Sun I count as a technology?"
  - Source 5 (BGG, sigmazero13, Jan 11 2018): "They do not. Preprinted units do not count as technologies."
- [Publicize Weapon Schematics] If the “Against” outcome of Publicize Weapon Schematics is resolved, the Muaat player will not discard their action cards if they do not own their Prototype War Sun II faction unit upgrade technology. <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (BGG, sigmazero13, Jan 11 2018): "It does not count against the "Against" effects of Publicize Weapons Schematics"
  - Source 5 (BGG, sigmazero13, Jan 11 2018): "They do not. Preprinted units do not count as technologies."
- [Wormhole Reconstruction] The “Against” effect of Wormhole Reconstruction will cause each player to place command tokens in each system that contains an alpha, beta or delta wormhole and one or more of that player’s ships. <sup>5</sup>
  - Trimmed from: The “Against” effect of Wormhole Reconstruction will cause each player to place command tokens in each system that contains an alpha, beta, delta or gamma wormhole and one or more of that player’s ships.
  - Source 5 (FFG Boards, Sevdome, December 15, 2017): "The Creuss home and gate systems are eligible to be affected by Wormhole Reconstruction, but keep in mind that a player only places a command token into the system if his own ships are in it."
- [Wormhole Research] A player with ships in a delta wormhole may research a technology from the “For” effect. Those ships will not be destroyed. <sup>5</sup>
  - Trimmed from: A player with ships in a delta or gamma wormhole may research a technology from the “For” effect. Those ships will not be destroyed.
  - Source 5 (FFG Boards, Sevdome, December 15, 2017): "The Creuss will gain the benefit of having ships in a system that contains a wormhole, but only the ships in systems with alpha and beta wormholes (not D) will be destroyed"
- [Anti–Intellectual Revolution] The Nekro player is never affected by the Anti–Intellectual Revolution law. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (anti-intellectual-revolution (Community consensus)): "The Nekro are unaffected, since Propagation gains tokens instead of researching."
- [Anti–Intellectual Revolution] A player with no non–fighter ships on the game board may still research technology when Anti–Intellectual Revolution is a law in play. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (anti-intellectual-revolution (Community consensus)): "a player with no such ships can still research"
- [Committee Formation] Committee Formation is resolved after any riders have been played, if the owner so chooses. Riders will resolve if the predicted outcome matches the player elected by the effect of Committee Formation. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (committee-formation-timing (Community consensus)): "Just before voting, after the 'when' and 'after' windows, so riders are already down."
- [Committee Formation] The owner of Committee Formation may play riders before they resolve Committee Formation. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (committee-formation-timing (Community consensus)): "playing a rider and then electing that player works"
- [Compensated Disarmament] All trade goods are gained together. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (swords-to-plowshares-one-infantry (Community consensus)): "All the trade goods from Swords to Plowshares or Compensated Disarmament arrive in a single step"
- [Enforced Travel Ban] The effect of the Enforced Travel Ban law does not affect the Creuss player. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (enforced-travel-ban (Community consensus)): "The Creuss ignore it, since no game effect can prevent Quantum Entanglement."
- [Enforced Travel Ban] When the Enforced Travel Ban law is in play, units cannot move through wormholes, even by effects that move ships outside of the Movement step of a tactical action, such as while retreating. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (retreat-destinations (Per the rulebook — Space Combat)): "Under Enforced Travel Ban, alpha and beta wormholes give no adjacency for a retreat."
  - Source 2 (enforced-travel-ban (Community consensus)): "alpha and beta wormholes have no effect on movement"
- [Enforced Travel Ban] Players may still be neighbors via systems that are adjacent via wormholes. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (enforced-travel-ban (Community consensus)): "the systems stay adjacent for everything else"
- [Enforced Travel Ban] The “Against” effect of Enforced Travel Ban will affect PDS in or adjacent to systems containing an alpha, beta, delta or gamma wormhole. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (enforced-travel-ban (Community consensus)): "Against: every PDS in or next to a system with any wormhole, gamma and delta included, is destroyed."
- [Fleet Regulations] The effect of the Fleet Regulations law does not prevent the Letnev player from using their Armada faction ability. They may have up to six non–fighter ships in a system if they have four command tokens in their fleet pool. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (fleet-regulations-excess (Community consensus)): "Abilities that raise fleet limits, like Letnev's, still add on top."
- [Ixthian Artifact] A player with three or fewer units in a system adjacent to the Mecatol Rex system destroys all of their units in that system. <sup>2</sup>
  - Trimmed from: A player with three or fewer units in a system adjacent to the Mecatol Rex system destroys all of their units in that system. Otherwise, a player chooses which three units are destroyed.
  - Source 2 (ixthian-artifact-adjacency (Community consensus)): "3 units of each player in every adjacent system (all of them if a player has fewer)"
- [Judicial Abolishment] If Judicial Abolishment is revealed when only one law is in play, players may only vote for that law or abstain. If no votes are cast, the speaker must decide for that law to be elected. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (judicial-abolishment-one-law (Community consensus)): "that law is the only eligible outcome. Abstaining isn't an outcome, and if nobody votes the speaker must break the 0-0 tie by choosing it."
- [Minister of Peace] Once a player resolves the ability of Minister of Peace, the active player cannot use any “after you activate a system” abilities. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (minister-of-peace-timing (Community consensus)): "Once it ends the active player's turn, no other abilities in that window can be resolved"
- [Minister of Peace] Other players, including the Minister of Peace player, cannot use any “after another player activates a system that…” abilities. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (minister-of-peace-timing (Community consensus)): "no other abilities in that window can be resolved"
- [Minister of Peace] The player that owns Minister of Peace does not have to have any of their units in the active system to resolve Minister of Peace, so long as any non–active player owns at least one unit in the active system. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (minister-cards-details (Community consensus)): "Minister of Peace's owner needn't have units in the activated system."
- [Miscount Disclosed] If Representative Government is elected by Miscount Disclosed, each player will cast only one vote during the revote. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (miscount-disclosed-law-stays-in-effect (Community consensus)): "so Representative Government, for example, still limits everyone to 1 vote"
- [Miscount Disclosed] Once the law is elected, any riders on Miscount Disclosed will resolve. Following that, the elected law is then treated as being revealed. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (miscount-disclosed-procedure (Community consensus)): "First vote on Miscount Disclosed, with riders predicting only which law is chosen. Then vote on that law as if it had just been revealed"
- [Miscount Disclosed] After the elected law is treated as revealed, riders may be played to predict the outcome of the elected law. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (miscount-disclosed-procedure (Community consensus)): "so Veto, Quash and a fresh round of riders can be played on it"
- [Political Censure] When a player is elected for Political Censure, they may play the Confusing Legal Text action card before it resolves. <sup>2</sup>
  - Trimmed from: When a player is elected for Political Censure, they may play the Confusing Legal Text or Deadly Plot action cards before it resolves.
  - Source 2 (legal-text-cards-and-riders (Community consensus)): "only the player originally elected can play them. They act before the outcome resolves"
- [Prophecy of Ixth] Other effects that produce units without a unit using its Production ability will not cause Prophecy of Ixth to be discarded. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (sling-relay-and-prophecy-of-ixth (Community consensus)): "it only applies when you use a unit's Production ability"

**Notes added** (rulings that were not on the site before)

- [Classified Document Leaks] If Classified Document Leaks is discarded, the elected secret objective does not count toward the secret objective total of the player who originally owned it. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (FAQ Action Cards): "it does not count toward the secret objective total of the player who originally owned it."
- [Minister of War] Performing any action is the trigger for the remainder of the ability of Minister of War. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (FAQ Action Cards): "Performing any action is the trigger for the remainder of the “Minister of War” agenda card’s ability."
- [Classified Document Leaks] If the Firmament player has their control token on the elected secret objective, they do not gain a victory point, and they cannot score it again. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (Firmament\Obsidian): "They do not gain a VP and they are unable to score it again."
- [Compensated Disarmament] If the elected planet contains coexisting units, the player that controls the planet gains all of the trade goods, including those for destroyed coexisting units. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (Coexistence): "The planet controller gains all trade goods."
- [Miscount Disclosed] If Holy Planet of Ixth, Shard of the Throne or The Crown of Emphidia is elected by Miscount Disclosed, the newly elected owner gains a victory point, even if they were also the previous owner. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (law-victory-points-kept-when-discarded (Community consensus)): "a newly elected owner gains one, and the same player re-elected scores again."
- [The Crown of Emphidia] The owner of The Crown of Emphidia only loses it if they lose control of a planet in their own home system, not a planet they control in another player’s home system. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (crown-of-emphidia-home-system-only (Community consensus)): "No — only planets in your own home system count for it."
- [Miscount Disclosed] Planets are not readied between the vote on Miscount Disclosed and the vote on the elected law. The vote on the elected law does not replace the second agenda of the agenda phase, so three agendas may be voted on during that agenda phase. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (miscount-disclosed-procedure (Community consensus)): "Planets are not readied in between, and the revote doesn't replace the phase's second agenda, so a phase can have three votes."
- [Arms Reduction] The “For” outcome of Arms Reduction only affects dreadnoughts and cruisers. Afterward, if a player’s fighters or ground forces in a space area exceed their capacity, the excess units are removed; they are not destroyed. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (arms-reduction-scope (Community consensus)): "No — For only cuts dreadnoughts beyond 2 and cruisers beyond 4."
- [Fleet Regulations] When Fleet Regulations becomes a law, any command tokens in excess of four in a player’s fleet pool are returned to their reinforcements; they cannot be moved to other pools. Any ships in excess of the new fleet pool limit are removed immediately. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (fleet-regulations-excess (Community consensus)): "Excess fleet tokens return to reinforcements; you can't move them to other pools."
- [Public Execution] The Yssaril player’s Crafty faction ability does not prevent them from discarding their action cards if they are elected by Public Execution, as the discard is not caused by the hand limit. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (public-execution-effects (Community consensus)): "The discard comes from being elected, not from the hand limit, so Yssaril must discard too."
- [Committee Formation] The Nekro player may own and resolve Committee Formation, even though they cannot vote. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (committee-formation-timing (Community consensus)): "The Nekro can hold and use it despite not voting, and Political Secret doesn't stop it."
- [Minister of Industry] Moving the Saar player’s Floating Factory into a system is not placing a space dock, and does not trigger Minister of Industry. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (minister-of-industry-trigger (Community consensus)): "A Saar Floating Factory moving into a system doesn't trigger it"
- [Swords to Plowshares] If a planet contains only one infantry, that infantry is destroyed and its owner gains one trade good. All trade goods from Swords to Plowshares are gained together, so the Mentak player may use their Pillage faction ability on each affected neighbor only once. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (swords-to-plowshares-one-infantry (Community consensus)): "Half of one rounded up is one, so the lone infantry is destroyed and you gain 1 trade good."
- [The Crown of Thalnos] Only combat rolls may be rerolled with The Crown of Thalnos; anti–fighter barrage and bombardment rolls, including those from the L1Z1X player’s Harrow faction ability, cannot. A player may reroll dice for units that would otherwise be destroyed, as hits are not assigned until after rolling; each unit whose rerolled die does not produce a hit is destroyed, even if its other dice produced hits. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (crown-of-thalnos-rerolls (Community consensus)): "Only combat rolls, not Anti-Fighter Barrage, Bombardment (L1Z1X Harrow included) or Sardakk's Courageous to the End."
- [Demilitarized Zone] If the planet elected by Demilitarized Zone is given to another player by the Colonial Redistribution agenda, no units are placed on it. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (cultural-planet-agendas (Community consensus)): "A Demilitarized Zone planet given away by Colonial Redistribution gets no units, since none can be placed there."
- [Minister of Commerce] The owner of Minister of Commerce gains trade goods from Minister of Commerce when they replenish commodities, even if they already have their maximum number of commodities. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (minister-cards-details (Community consensus)): "Minister of Commerce still pays 1 trade good per neighbor when your commodities were already full, since you still replenished."
- [Minister of War] Resolving Minister of War is not an action. As such, a player with the Fleet Logistics technology may perform three actions in one turn. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (minister-cards-details (Community consensus)): "Minister of War isn't an action itself, so with Fleet Logistics you can take three actions in a turn."
- [Shard of the Throne] Shard of the Throne does not change hands if a combat ends in a draw, or if no combat occurs, such as when ground forces land on a planet without opposing ground forces or the Bombardment ability destroys the last defending ground forces. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (shard-of-the-throne-draw (Community consensus)): "No — if neither player has ground forces left, nobody won the combat, so the Shard stays put."
- [Research Team: Biotic] The elected planet does not gain a technology specialty, and does not count as a planet with a technology specialty for objectives. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (research-team-agendas (Community consensus)): "They don't give the planet a technology specialty, so they don't count for objectives about specialty planets."
- [Research Team: Cybernetic] The elected planet does not gain a technology specialty, and does not count as a planet with a technology specialty for objectives. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (research-team-agendas (Community consensus)): "They don't give the planet a technology specialty, so they don't count for objectives about specialty planets."
- [Research Team: Propulsion] The elected planet does not gain a technology specialty, and does not count as a planet with a technology specialty for objectives. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (research-team-agendas (Community consensus)): "They don't give the planet a technology specialty, so they don't count for objectives about specialty planets."
- [Research Team: Warfare] The elected planet does not gain a technology specialty, and does not count as a planet with a technology specialty for objectives. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (research-team-agendas (Community consensus)): "They don't give the planet a technology specialty, so they don't count for objectives about specialty planets."
- [Publicize Weapon Schematics] If the Nekro player has copied a faction–specific war sun unit upgrade technology with Valefar Assimilator, they own a war sun technology for the purposes of Publicize Weapon Schematics. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (nekro-valefar-what-can-be-copied (Community consensus)): "Copying a faction war sun technology does make the Nekro subject to Publicize Weapon Schematics."
- [Checks and Balances] Players choose strategy cards in the normal order, but each player gives the card they choose to another player who does not yet have their full number of strategy cards. A player keeps the card they chose only if no other player can receive it. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (checks-and-balances-selection (Community consensus)): "on your pick you give the card you choose to a player who doesn't yet have their full number of cards"
- [Political Censure] If Political Censure is elected by Miscount Disclosed, the previous owner loses one victory point when they lose the card, and the newly elected player gains one victory point. If the same player is elected again, they lose and then regain the victory point. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (political-censure-revote (Community consensus)): "the previous owner loses 1 and the new owner gains 1; the same player re-elected loses and regains it"
- [Armed Forces Standardization] If the elected player is the Mahact player, they choose which command tokens to remove from their fleet pool. Any other players’ command tokens removed are returned to those players’ reinforcements. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (armed-forces-standardization-mahact (Community consensus)): "Mahact chooses which tokens to remove, and other players' tokens removed go back to their owners' reinforcements"
- [Political Censure] Political Censure only prevents the elected player from playing action cards; it does not affect strategy cards. The elected player cannot discard Political Censure themselves. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (political-censure-rules (Community consensus)): "Only playing action cards; strategy cards are unaffected. The elected player can't discard it themselves"
- [Checks and Balances] If the “For” outcome is resolved, a player who has been given a strategy card still chooses a strategy card on their turn and gives it to an eligible player. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (checks-and-balances-given-card (Community consensus)): "they still pick and pass one to an eligible player"
- [Galactic Crisis Pact] If Leadership is elected, players may still spend influence to gain additional command tokens when resolving its secondary ability. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (galactic-crisis-pact-leadership (Community consensus)): "spending influence for tokens still applies"
- [Articles of War] Mechs lose all of their printed abilities other than Sustain Damage, including Bombardment, Space Cannon and Production. Their cost and combat values are unchanged, including any additional dice they roll, such as for the Naaz–Rokha player’s mechs. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (articles-of-war-mechs (Community consensus)): "Their cost and combat stats stay, so they still fight, and a mech that rolls 2 dice still does"
  - Source 2 (articles-of-war-naaz-rokha-dice (Community consensus)): "extra dice are part of the combat value, not a printed ability"
- [Checks and Balances] If the “Against” outcome is resolved, it applies to every player, regardless of how they voted; each player readies only three of their exhausted planets, and any planets that were not exhausted remain readied. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (checks-and-balances-against (Community consensus)): "It replaces the readying at the end of the agenda phase for everyone, however they voted"

**Restored without a source** (marked * on the site)

- [Anti–Intellectual Revolution] The Nekro player’s Valefar Assimilator technologies count for the “Against” effect, whether their tokens are on another player’s faction technology or not. <sup>*</sup>
- [Anti–Intellectual Revolution] A player may only exhaust planets they control for the “Against” effect of Anti–Intellectual Revolution. <sup>*</sup>
- [Archived Secret] If a player draws the Drive the Debate secret objective while resolving Archived Secret, they cannot score it immediately. <sup>*</sup>
- [Checks and Balances] The Public Disgrace action card may be played after a player has chosen a strategy card and announced which player will be receiving it. The player must choose a different strategy card, and then choose the same or a different player to receive it. <sup>*</sup>
- [Classified Document Leaks] If Classified Document Leaks is revealed when only one secret objective is in play, players may only vote for that secret objective or abstain. If no votes are cast, the speaker must decide for that secret objective to be elected. <sup>*</sup>
- [Classified Document Leaks] Players may still play riders if only one secret objective has been scored. <sup>*</sup>
- [Classified Document Leaks] If there are no other secret objectives eligable to be elected by the Miscount Disclosed revote, Classified Document Leaks will be discarded, and another agenda will be revealed and voted on. <sup>*</sup>
- [Colonial Redistribution] If the player that originally controlled the elected planet has the fewest victory points, they may choose themselves to place an infantry on that planet. <sup>*</sup>
- [Committee Formation] The Confusing Legal Text and Confounding Legal Text action cards may be played after Committee Formation has been discarded to change who the elected player is, which will negate the effects of Committee Formation. <sup>*</sup>
- [Committee Formation] The Deadly Plot action card may be played after Committee Formation has been discarded to discard the agenda without resolving it, but only if that player predicted a different outcome from some other game effect. <sup>*</sup>
- [Compensated Disarmament] Each destroyed infantry will provide one trade good and each destroyed mech will provide one trade good. <sup>*</sup>
- [Compensated Disarmament] A planet with zero units on it is eligible to be elected. <sup>*</sup>
- [Compensated Disarmament] Structures are unaffected by Compensated Disarmament. <sup>*</sup>
- [Compensated Disarmament] The Titans of Ul’s Hel–Titans are also ground forces and are thus affected by Compensated Disarmament. <sup>*</sup>
- [Core Mining] A planet with zero infantry on it may be elected. <sup>*</sup>
- [Covert Legislation] Any effects that take place when or after an agenda is revealed instead take place when or after the speaker has drawn and announced the possible outcomes for the hidden agenda. <sup>*</sup>
- [Covert Legislation] If an effect, such as the Veto action card, would discard Covert Legislation, both it and the hidden agenda are discarded. <sup>*</sup>
- [The Crown of Emphidia] If the player that gains The Crown of Emphidia controls no planets in their home system, they cannot lose it. <sup>*</sup>
- [Economic Equality] If the “For” outcome of Economic Equality is resolved, the Mentak player may resolve their Pillage faction ability against each of their neighbors. <sup>*</sup>
- [Executive Sanctions] The effect of the Executive Sanctions law does not affect the Yssaril player. <sup>*</sup>
- [Galactic Crisis Pact] The secondary ability is resolved immediately, during the agenda phase. <sup>*</sup>
- [Galactic Crisis Pact] Players must pay the influence or resource costs to resolve the abilities of the Leadership, Warfare or Technology strategy cards if they are elected. Any planets used to pay these costs will ready at the end of the agenda phase. <sup>*</sup>
- [Galactic Crisis Pact] If the Technology strategy card is elected, a player may exhaust a planet with a technology specialty to ignore a prerequisite on a technology as normal. This planet will ready at the end of the agenda phase. <sup>*</sup>
- [Galactic Crisis Pact] A player may exhaust the AI Development Algorithm technology to ignore a prerequisite on a unit upgrade technology as normal. AI Development Algorithm will not ready at the end of the agenda phase. <sup>*</sup>
- [Galactic Crisis Pact] If a player has a strategy card in their play area due to the effect of the Political Stability action card, that strategy card is eligible to be elected. <sup>*</sup>
- [Homeland Defense Act] If the  Homeland Defense Act law is discarded, players might have to remove PDS so that they have no more than two on each planet. <sup>*</sup>
- [Imperial Arbiter] In a three– or four–player game, the owner of Imperial Arbiter chooses which strategy cards are swapped. <sup>*</sup>
- [Ixthian Artifact] A player may use the first technology they research to meet the prerequisites of the second technology they research. <sup>*</sup>
- [Ixthian Artifact] A player may exhaust the AI Development Algorithm technology to ignore a prerequisite on a unit upgrade technology as normal. AI Development Algorithm will not ready at the end of the agenda phase. <sup>*</sup>
- [Ixthian Artifact] To cast votes against or to play a rider on Ixthian Artifact is to commit heresy. <sup>*</sup>
- [Judicial Abolishment] Players may still play riders if only one law is in play. <sup>*</sup>
- [Minister of Commerce] Minister of Commerce triggers when its owner has their commodities replenished by any game effect. <sup>*</sup>
- [Minister of Commerce] Gaining a fixed number of commodities does not trigger Minister of Commerce, even if doing so would result in its owner having commodities equal to their commodity value. <sup>*</sup>
- [Minister of Commerce] All trade goods are gained together. <sup>*</sup>
- [Minister of Exploration] If the owner of Minister of Exploration gains control of multiple planets during one invasion, the trade goods are gained one at a time. <sup>*</sup>
- [Minister of Industry] All units in that system may use their Production ability, not just the placed space dock. <sup>*</sup>
- [Minister of Industry] An ability that puts a space dock on the game board by “replacing”, rather than “placing”, such as the Infiltrate action card, will trigger Minister of Industry. <sup>*</sup>
- [Minister of Policy] The owner of Minister of Policy will draw action cards during the Draw Action Cards step of the status phase, and again at the end of the status phase. <sup>*</sup>
- [Minister of War] Effects that trigger at the start or end of a player’s turn will not trigger between each of those player’s action. <sup>*</sup>
- [Miscount Disclosed] If Miscount Disclosed is revealed when only one law is in play, players may only vote for that law or abstain. If no votes are cast, the speaker must decide for that law to be elected. <sup>*</sup>
- [Miscount Disclosed] Players may still play riders if only one law is in play. <sup>*</sup>
- [Miscount Disclosed] If Committee Formation is elected by Miscount Disclosed, the owner may use its ability. The elected player will receive Committee Formation from the discard pile. <sup>*</sup>
- [Miscount Disclosed] If Political Censure is elected by Miscount Disclosed, the current owner cannot play action cards, including Confounding Legal Text, if another player is elected. If another player is elected, that player may play the Confusing Legal Text action card. <sup>*</sup>
- [Miscount Disclosed] If Classified Document Leaks is elected by Miscount Disclosed, and there are no other secret objectives eligable to be elected by the Miscount Disclosed revote, Classified Document Leaks will be discarded and replaced. <sup>*</sup>
- [Miscount Disclosed] After all players have voted for Miscount Disclosed, the Deadly Plot action card may be played. If so, the elected law is not voted on and remains in play. <sup>*</sup>
- [Miscount Disclosed] After all players have voted for the elected law, the Deadly Plot action card may be played. If so, the elected law is discarded. <sup>*</sup>
- [Mutiny] If the “For” outcome of Mutiny is resolved, players gain victory points in speaker order. <sup>*</sup>
- [Nexus Sovereignty] The effect of the Nexus Sovereignty law does not affect the Creuss player. <sup>*</sup>
- [Nexus Sovereignty] When the Nexus Sovereignty law is in play, units cannot move through the alpha and beta wormholes in the wormhole nexus, even by effects that move ships outside of the movement step of a tactical action, such as while retreating. <sup>*</sup>
- [Nexus Sovereignty] When the Nexus Sovereignty law is in play, hits may still be produced against ships in the active system by units with the Deep Space Cannon ability in systems that are adjacent via a wormhole during the Space Cannon Offense step of a tactical action. <sup>*</sup>
- [Nexus Sovereignty] Players may still be neighbors via systems that are adjacent via wormholes. <sup>*</sup>
- [Publicize Weapon Schematics] If the Publicize Weapon Schematics law is in play, and a player is the first to gain the war sun unit upgrade technology, from then on, prerequisites for the war sun unit upgrade technology will be ignored. <sup>*</sup>
- [Publicize Weapon Schematics] If the Publicize Weapon Schematics law is in play, the Muaat player will not cause prerequisites for the War Sun unit upgrade technology to be ignored if they do not own their Prototype War Sun II faction unit upgrade technology. <sup>*</sup>
- [Publicize Weapon Schematics] The Muaat player’s Prototype War Sun will lose its Sustain Damage ability, regardless of if the Muaat player owns their Prototype War Sun II faction unit upgrade technology. <sup>*</sup>
- [Rearmament Agreement] A player that controls no planets in their home system will not place a mech if the “For” outcome of Rearmament Agreement is resolved. <sup>*</sup>
- [Rearmament Agreement] A player that has no mechs on the game board is unaffected by the “Against” effect of Rearmament Agreement. <sup>*</sup>
- [Research Grant Reallocation] A player may gain any technology, regardless of the number of command tokens in their fleet pool. <sup>*</sup>
- [Research Grant Reallocation] If a player must remove more command tokens than they have in their fleet pool, they remove all their command tokens from their fleet pool instead. <sup>*</sup>
- [Research Grant Reallocation] The number and colors of technologies a player owns will have no effect on the number of command tokens they remove. <sup>*</sup>
- [Research Grant Reallocation] A player cannot exhaust a planet with a technology specialty to reduce the number of command tokens they remove. <sup>*</sup>
- [Search Warrant] If the elected player has three secret objective cards, and they would draw another, the drawn secret objective card is revealed before that player chooses which card to discard. This applies both when the elected player initially draws the secret objective cards from the effect of Search Warrant when they are elected, and if they later draw secret objective cards from another effect. <sup>*</sup>
- [Search Warrant] If a player draws the Drive the Debate secret objective while resolving Search Warrant, they cannot score it immediately. <sup>*</sup>
- [Seed of an Empire] If multiple players have the most or fewest victory points, they gain victory points in speaker order. <sup>*</sup>
- [Swords to Plowshares] Mechs are ignored by the “For” effect of Swords to Plowshares. <sup>*</sup>
- [Wormhole Reconstruction] While Wormhole Reconstruction is in play, Enforced Travel Ban will have no effect. <sup>*</sup>
- [Wormhole Research] If a system contains both a delta and gamma wormhole and an alpha or beta wormhole, such as the active wormhole nexus, then ships in that system will be destroyed. <sup>*</sup>
- [Wormhole Research] A player may exhaust the AI Development Algorithm technology to ignore a prerequisite on a unit upgrade technology as normal. AI Development Algorithm will not ready at the end of the agenda phase. <sup>*</sup>
- [Wormhole Research] Ground forces in the space area of a system containing an alpha or beta wormhole will be removed due to lack of capacity after the ships in that system are destroyed; those ground forces will not trigger any “destroyed” effects. Fighters will be destroyed, and will trigger any “destroyed” effects. <sup>*</sup>
- [Wormhole Research] If Anti–Intellectual Revolution is in play as a law, players who research a technology will destroy a ship due to Anti–Intellectual Revolution before they destroy ships in systems containing alpha or beta wormholes. As such, they may choose a ship in a system containing an alpha or beta wormhole to destroy for Anti–Intellectual Revolution <sup>*</sup>
- [Wormhole Research] If the Vuil’raith player has their flagship, The Terror Between, in a system containing an alpha or beta wormhole, and they choose to destroy it for Anti–Intellectual Revolution, then they will not capture the other ships in that system that are destroyed by Wormhole Research. <sup>*</sup>
- [Wormhole Research] If the Vuil’raith player has their flagship, The Terror Between, in a system containing an alpha or beta wormhole, and they choose to destroy another ship with capacity, they must resolve capacity before Wormhole Research destroys any ships. Any fighters they remove due to capacity will not be captured when ships are destroyed for Wormhole Research. <sup>*</sup>
- [Wormhole Research] The Saar player’s Floating Factories will not be destroyed by Wormhole Research. <sup>*</sup>

**Removed notes that the site already covers elsewhere**

### C_events.php

**Notes kept**

- [Monuments to the Ages] If multiple players would gain their final victory point simultaneously, the player with the lowest initiative wins. <sup>1,4</sup>
  - Edited from: If multiple players would gain their final victory simultaneously, the player with the lowest initiative wins.
  - Source 1 (98.7): "If multiple players would simultaneously gain their 10th victory point, the player who is earliest in initiative order among those players is the winner"
  - Source 4 (Xxcha Kingdom, simultaneous win): "Initiative order determines the winner. Initiative order is always the lowest initiative player onwards, regardless of who the active player is."

**Removed notes restored**

- [Age of Exploration] New tiles cannot be placed adjacent to the Creuss or Rebellion home systems, the wormhole nexus, or systems that comprise The Fracture. <sup>7</sup>
  - Source 7 (te_rulebook_web.txt p16 Clarifications, Age of Exploration (Galactic Event)): "New tiles cannot be placed off of the Ghosts of Creuss home system, the Crimson Rebellion home system, the Wormhole Nexus, or any Fracture tiles."
- [Minor Factions] During setup, if a player places a minor faction system with two planets, that player chooses which planet gets two neutral infantry and which planet gets one. <sup>11</sup>
  - Source 11 (ti_codex_4_rules.txt p15 Minor Factions event): "Then, that player places 3 neutral infantry on that system’s planets, split as evenly as possible."
- [Minor Factions] During setup, if a player is dealt the Creuss reference card, they place the Creuss Gate (tile 17) in the equidistant, and place the Creuss home system (tile 51) in the common play area. <sup>7</sup>
  - Source 7 (te_rulebook_web.txt p16 Clarifications, Minor Factions (Galactic Event)): "When the Ghosts of Creuss or Crimson Rebellion faction is chosen as a minor faction, the Creuss Gate or the Sorrow, respectively, is placed in a minor faction spot, while the home system is placed near the game board."
- [Minor Factions] During setup, if a player is dealt the Rebellion reference card, they place the Sorrow (tile 94) in the equidistant, and place the Rebellion home system (tile 118) in the common play area. <sup>7</sup>
  - Source 7 (te_rulebook_web.txt p16 Clarifications, Minor Factions (Galactic Event)): "When the Ghosts of Creuss or Crimson Rebellion faction is chosen as a minor faction, the Creuss Gate or the Sorrow, respectively, is placed in a minor faction spot, while the home system is placed near the game board."
- [Minor Factions] During setup, if a player is dealt the Keleres reference card, then they select a home system at random from amongst the Argent, Mentak and Xxcha. <sup>7</sup>
  - Trimmed from: During setup, if a player is dealt the Keleres reference card, then they select a home system at random from amongst the Argent, Mentak and Xxcha, excluding any that have already been placed.
  - Source 7 (te_rulebook_web.txt p14 "Subjugation" map (Minor Factions)): "If Keleres is a minor faction, choose one of its three possible home systems at random."
- [Minor Factions] Commander abilities of minor factions do not need to be unlocked; they are available as soon as a player takes the corresponding alliance card. <sup>7</sup>
  - Source 7 (te_rulebook_web.txt p12 Alliance Reference Cards): "When gained for any reason other than a reference to an “Alliance” promissory note, the gaining player places the card in their play area. They can use its ability."
  - Source 7 (te_rulebook_web.txt p12 Alliance Reference Cards): "These cards are also used in the Alliance game variant, in some Galactic Events"
- [Minor Factions] A player only loses a minor faction’s alliance card if a single other player controls each planet in that minor faction’s system. <sup>11</sup>
  - Source 11 (ti_codex_4_rules.txt p15 Minor Factions event): "When a player controls each planet in a minor faction system, they take that faction’s alliance card from the deck or from the player that owned it previously."
- [Minor Factions] A player will retain a minor faction’s alliance card even if they control no planets in that minor faction’s system, should two or more other players each control planets in that system. <sup>11</sup>
  - Source 11 (ti_codex_4_rules.txt p15 Minor Factions event): "When a player controls each planet in a minor faction system, they take that faction’s alliance card from the deck or from the player that owned it previously."
- [Minor Factions] The planets in a minor faction’s system are not home planets, nor is the system a home system. <sup>11</sup>
  - Source 11 (ti_codex_4_rules.txt p15 Minor Factions event): "These systems are minor faction systems and do not count as home systems."
- [Minor Factions] All neutral infantry have a combat value of 8. <sup>11</sup>
  - Trimmed from: All neutral infantry have a combat value of 8, and otherwise have no special abilities, regardless of which minor faction they belong to.
  - Source 11 (ti_codex_4_rules.txt p15 Galactic Events): "Use proxy components or figures for neutral infantry; they have a combat value of 8."
- [Wild, Wild Galaxy] A player with no planets remaining in their home system is not prevented from scoring public objectives. <sup>7</sup>
  - Source 7 (te_rulebook_web.txt p16 Clarifications, Wild, Wild Galaxy (Galactic Event)): "if there are no planets in a player’s home system, they still control every planet in their home system and can score public objectives."
- [Wild, Wild Galaxy] If the Muaat player’s Nova Seed hero ability replaces a player’s home system with a supernova, then that supernova becomes that player’s home system. <sup>7</sup>
  - Source 7 (te_rulebook_web.txt p16 Clarifications, Wild, Wild Galaxy (Galactic Event)): "If a player’s home system is replaced by a supernova, it is still that player’s home system."

**Notes added** (rulings that were not on the site before)

- [Total War] Units that are captured without being destroyed, such as by the Vuil’raith player’s hero, do not add commodities. If another player gains control of the home system planet holding the commodities, they also take those commodities. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (total-war-variant (Community consensus)): "Units captured without being destroyed, as by the Vuil'raith hero, add nothing."
- [Mercenaries for Hire] Players cannot look through the mercenaries deck. Only the faceup top card is known. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (mercenaries-deck-hidden (Community consensus)): "only the face-up top card is known"
- [Total War] Neutral units have no cost; destroying them does not count toward Total War. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (neutral-units (Community consensus)): "They have no cost, so destroying them adds nothing for Total War"

**Restored without a source** (marked * on the site)

- [Age of Commerce] Players must still be neighbors on the game board for the purpose of resolving game effects that depend on players being neighbors. <sup>*</sup>
- [Age of Commerce] For example, the Mentak player must still be neighbors with another player on the game board to resolve their Pillage faction ability against that player. <sup>*</sup>
- [Age of Commerce] The Hacan player’s Guild Ships faction ability and Trade Convoys promissory note provide no benefit while playing with the Age of Commerce event. However, Trade Convoys may still be played as a component action. <sup>*</sup>
- [Age of Commerce] If the Empyrean player receives commodities from a player with their Dark Pact promissory note in their play area equal to that player’s printed commodity value, then both players will gain one trade good. This need not be all of the giving player’s current commodities. <sup>*</sup>
- [Age of Commerce] If the giving player owns the Dynamis Core relic, they must give two commodities above their faction’s printed commodity value to trigger the effect of Dark Pact. <sup>*</sup>
- [Age of Commerce] When a player’s Trade Agreement promissory note is played, they give only the number of commodities that they just gained due to replenishing commodities. <sup>*</sup>
- [Age of Commerce] A player may share any number of technologies in a single transaction. <sup>*</sup>
- [Age of Exploration] If there are no more blue–backed or red–backed tiles available, a player does not place any tile if they roll the corresponding dice result. <sup>*</sup>
- [Age of Fighters] The Vuil’raith player still captures ships that they destroy via their various abilities. These ships are purged when they would be returned to their original owner. <sup>*</sup>
- [Cosmic Phenomanae] Only ships moving out of gravity rifts may apply the +2 to their move value; ships moving through cannot. <sup>*</sup>
- [Cosmic Phenomanae] For ships moving out of a gravity rift, the active player chooses for each one whether it applies +1 or +2 to its move value, and then rolls for removing with the corresponding threshold. <sup>*</sup>
- [Cosmic Phenomanae] Ships that move out of a gravity rift outside of the movement step of a tactical action, such as through retreating from a space combat, must still roll for removal. Their owner may choose which threshold to use. <sup>*</sup>
- [Dangerous Wilds] The player may research the technology before or after they explore the planet. <sup>*</sup>
- [Minor Factions] Should another player have the reference card for that faction, then they take that home system, and the player with the Keleres reference card places a different home system at random. <sup>*</sup>
- [Minor Factions] The pool of player factions and minor factions cannot contain all four of the Argent, Keleres, Mentak and Xxcha. <sup>*</sup>
- [Minor Factions] When a player controls each planet in this system, they take the Keleres alliance card, granting them the ability of Suffi An, the Keleres commander. They are not granted the ability of the Argent, Mentak or Xxcha commanders. <sup>*</sup>
- [Minor Factions] If Mahact exists as a minor faction, the player that controls Ixth gains access to the ability of Il Na Viroset, the Mahact commander. <sup>*</sup>
- [Minor Factions] When a player gains control of a minor faction planet, if it is not controlled by another player, they explore it. They choose which planet trait they explore it as. <sup>*</sup>
- [Minor Factions] The minor faction systems cannot be used to score objectives such as Conquer the Weak or Darken the Skies, but may be used to score objectives such as Expand Borders. <sup>*</sup>
- [Minor Factions] The minor faction systems may be targeted by action cards such as Reactor Meltdown, Signal Jamming or Uprising. <sup>*</sup>
- [Minor Factions] The minor faction systems may be elected for agendas such as Colonial Redistribution. They will be unaffected by agendas such as New Constitution or Shared Research. <sup>*</sup>
- [Minor Factions] The minor faction systems may be targeted with the Stellar Converter relic or with the Muaat player’s Nova Seed hero ability. These will not cause a player to lose an alliance card. <sup>*</sup>
- [Minor Factions] Planets with neutral infantry cannot be targeted with action cards such as Plague or Uprising. <sup>*</sup>
- [Minor Factions] Planets with neutral infantry cannot be elected by “elect planet” agendas, and are unaffected by agendas such as Swords to Plowshares. <sup>*</sup>
- [Minor Factions] Planets with neutral infantry cannot be used to score objectives such as Make an Example of their World or Stake Your Claim. <sup>*</sup>
- [Stellar Atomics] Players may still resolve non–action card abilities during the action phase. <sup>*</sup>
- [Stellar Atomics] If the Xxcha player has Elder Qanoj, their commander, unlocked, they will be able to vote after removing their control token from Stellar Atomics. <sup>*</sup>
- [Total War] Commodities on planets are not treated as commodities for any game effect, other than those that appear on the Total War event card. <sup>*</sup>
- [Total War] The Mentak player cannot use their Pillage faction ability to target the commodities on planets. <sup>*</sup>
- [Total War] The Salvage action card cannot be used to target the commodities on planets. <sup>*</sup>
- [Total War] If a player gains control of a planet in another player’s home system, without controlling at least one planet in their own home system, then any commodities on the planet they gained control of remain on that planet. <sup>*</sup>
- [Total War] The commodities on the planet in the other player’s home system cannot be discarded to gain a victory point. <sup>*</sup>
- [Total War] If that player still controls that planet in another player’s home system when they regain control of a planet in their own home system, they then move the commodities from the planet in the other player’s home system to the planet in their own home system. <sup>*</sup>

**Notes kept**

- [Ion Storm] All ship movement is simultaneous. If the Ion Storm token system is the active system, and the token is currently on the alpha side, a player cannot move a ship from a system with an alpha wormhole, flip the token, then move a ship from a system with the beta wormhole (then flip the token again). _(no source)_
  - Covered by [R_movement.php](R_movement.php) [Tactical Action Movement / Notes]: Ships arrive in the active system simultaneously; all movement is simultaneous.
- [Ion Storm] As a system is never adjacent to itself, a ship cannot move out through one wormhole and in through the other while remaining in the system. The ship must pass through another system with a wormhole to use both wormholes. _(no source)_

- [Maxis Central Control — Faunus] If the gained planet was not controlled by another player, it is explored. <sup>2</sup>

- [Dok ’N Pic’s Salvage Yard — Garbozia] Cards on Dok ’N Pic’s Salvage Yard do not count towards a player’s action card hand limit. <sup>*</sup>
- [Dok ’N Pic’s Salvage Yard — Garbozia] The player with The Codex cannot take cards that are on Dok ’N Pic’s Salvage Yard. <sup>*</sup>

- [The Galactic Council — Mecatol Rex] The Galactic Council cannot be exhausted by a player that has no unscored secret objective cards in their hand. <sup>*</sup>
- [The Galactic Council — Mecatol Rex] When using The Galactic Council, the active player first discards a secret objective, shuffling it into the secret objective deck. Then, they draw a secret objective. This may result in them drawing the secret objective they discarded. <sup>*</sup>

- [Prove Endurance] Prove Endurance is scored when the player passes during the action phase. <sup>6</sup>
  - Trimmed from: Prove Endurance is scored when the player passes during the action phase. They may then score another secret objective in the status phase immediately following.
  - Source 6 (Ral Nel Consortium, Director Nel (Hero)): "No, the active player can score Prove Endurance when they pass."
- [Become a Martyr] The attacker will have the opportunity to score a secret objective before the defender has the opportunity to score Become a Martyr. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (two-players-score-in-same-combat (Community consensus)): "Whichever condition is met first."
  - Source 2 (two-players-score-in-same-combat (Community consensus)): "If both trigger at the same moment, the active player goes first."
- [Control the Borderlands] When using the five– and seven–player hyperlane setups, the system tile in the center of the ring of hyperlanes is not on the edge of the game board. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (edge-of-board-with-hyperlanes (Community consensus)): "tiles beside hyperlanes, and a system enclosed by them, aren't edge systems"
- [Populate the Outer Rim] When using the five– and seven–player hyperlane setups, the system tile in the center of the ring of hyperlanes is not on the edge of the game board. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (edge-of-board-with-hyperlanes (Community consensus)): "tiles beside hyperlanes, and a system enclosed by them, aren't edge systems"
- [Destroy Their Greatest Ship] Destroy their Greatest Ship is scored as soon as the war sun or flagship is destroyed; it does not require waiting until the end of the combat. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (two-players-score-in-same-combat (Community consensus)): "Destroying a flagship or war sun happens during a combat round, before the combat ends and has a winner."
- [Destroy Their Greatest Ship] A player does not have to win a combat to score Destroy their Greatest Ship. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (two-players-score-in-same-combat (Community consensus)): "Destroying a flagship or war sun happens during a combat round, before the combat ends and has a winner."
- [Expand Borders] The planets cannot be in any player’s home system. <sup>2</sup>
  - Trimmed from: The planets cannot be in any player’s home system, including those of eliminated players.
  - Source 2 (non-home-planets-objectives (Community consensus)): "'non-home' excludes every home system, including other players' that you control"
- [Subdue the Galaxy] The planets cannot be in any player’s home system. <sup>2</sup>
  - Trimmed from: The planets cannot be in any player’s home system, including those of eliminated players.
  - Source 2 (non-home-planets-objectives (Community consensus)): "'non-home' excludes every home system, including other players' that you control"
- [Foster Cohesion] The Hacan player’s Guild Ships faction ability does not make a player neighbors with all other players. <sup>2</sup>
  - Trimmed from: The Hacan player’s Guild Ships faction ability and Trade Convoys promissory note does not make a player neighbors with all other players.
  - Source 2 (who-are-neighbors (Per the rulebook — The Economy: Resources, Trade Goods, and Commodities)): "The Hacan can transact with non-neighbors, and anyone can with them, but that doesn't make them neighbors for Pillage."
- [Foster Cohesion] If a player has units or controls a planet in a system containing an alpha wormhole, and the Creuss player has units or controls a planet in a system containing a beta wormhole, or vice versa, those two players are neighbors. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (creuss-quantum-entanglement-neighbors (Community consensus)): "Quantum Entanglement makes alpha and beta wormholes adjacent for Creuss, and adjacency created that way also makes them neighbors"
- [Push Boundaries] If a player has units or controls a planet in a system containing an alpha wormhole, and the Creuss player has units or controls a planet in a system containing a beta wormhole, or vice versa, those two players are neighbors. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (creuss-quantum-entanglement-neighbors (Community consensus)): "Quantum Entanglement makes alpha and beta wormholes adjacent for Creuss, and adjacency created that way also makes them neighbors"
- [Intimidate Council] Any ships in the Mecatol Rex system are irrelevant. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (adjacent-objectives-not-in-system (Community consensus)): "Intimidate Council needs ships in two different systems next to Mecatol Rex"
- [Learn the Secrets of the Cosmos] Having ships in an anomaly is irrelevant, unless that system is also adjacent to another anomaly. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (adjacent-objectives-not-in-system (Community consensus)): "ships inside an anomaly don't count as adjacent to it"
- [Make an Example of Their World] Scoring Make an Example of Their World will not prevent that player from scoring a secret objective in any ground combats during this tactical action. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (action-phase-secret-objectives (Per the rulebook — Objectives and Victory Points)): "You may score several in a turn but only one per combat or step"
- [Make an Example of Their World] The L1Z1X player may score Make an Example of Their World by using their Harrow faction ability. <sup>2</sup>
  - Trimmed from: The L1Z1X player may score Make an Example of Their World by using their Harrow faction ability. If they do they cannot score another objective during that ground combat.
  - Source 2 (objective-specific-clarifications (Community consensus)): "destroying the last ground forces with L1Z1X's Harrow counts for Make an Example, since Harrow is Bombardment"
- [Make an Example of Their World Ω] Scoring Make an Example of Their World Ω will not prevent that player from scoring a secret objective in any ground combats during this tactical action. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (action-phase-secret-objectives (Per the rulebook — Objectives and Victory Points)): "You may score several in a turn but only one per combat or step"
- [Spark a Rebellion] A player that currently outright has the most victory points cannot score Spark a Rebellion. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (beat-player-with-most-points (Community consensus)): "If you lead alone, nobody else qualifies."
- [Spark a Rebellion] If multiple players are tied for the most victory points, Spark a Rebellion may be scored by winning a combat against any of them. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (beat-player-with-most-points (Community consensus)): "when players are tied for most points, each of them counts as having the most"
- [Spark a Rebellion] Spark a Rebellion may be scored by winning a combat against a player with zero victory points if all players have zero victory points. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (beat-player-with-most-points (Community consensus)): "when players are tied for most points, each of them counts as having the most"
- [Threaten Enemies] Any ships in another players home system are irrelevant. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (adjacent-objectives-not-in-system (Community consensus)): "a system isn't adjacent to itself"
- [Turn Their Fleets to Dust] Scoring Turn Their Fleets to Dust will not prevent that player from scoring a secret objective in the Space Combat step during this tactical action. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (action-phase-secret-objectives (Per the rulebook — Objectives and Victory Points)): "You may score several in a turn but only one per combat or step"
- [Turn Their Fleets to Dust Ω] Scoring Turn Their Fleets to Dust Ω will not prevent that player from scoring a secret objective in the Space Combat step during this tactical action. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (action-phase-secret-objectives (Per the rulebook — Objectives and Victory Points)): "You may score several in a turn but only one per combat or step"

**Notes added** (rulings that were not on the site before)

- [Become a Martyr] A player who loses their home system due to The Silver Flame relic may score Become a Martyr. <sup>9</sup>
  - Source 9 (General / Silver Flame): "You can lose your home system from the relic to satisfy BAM."
- [Stake Your Claim] A player coexisting on a planet may score Stake Your Claim using that planet, even if it is the only planet in its system, as the planet is also controlled by another player. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (Coexistence): "Yes, you control a planet in a system that contains a planet controlled by another player if you are in coexistence."
- [Spark a Rebellion] A player who wins a combat against the owner of the Shard of the Throne law, who has the most victory points, may both score Spark a Rebellion and gain Shard of the Throne. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (spark-a-rebellion-and-shard (Community consensus)): "Yes, both."
- [Become the Gatekeeper] The Creuss player’s Quantum Entanglement faction ability only makes alpha and beta wormhole systems adjacent; a player still needs ships in both a system containing an alpha wormhole and a system containing a beta wormhole. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (objective-specific-clarifications (Community consensus)): "Become the Gatekeeper needs ships in both an alpha and a beta system, as Creuss's Quantum Entanglement only makes them adjacent"
