**Restored without a source** (marked * on the site)

- [Achieve Supremacy] The flagship or war sun may be in the home system of an eliminated player. <sup>*</sup>
- [Become a Legend] A ship, ground force, or structure will all qualify for Become a Legend. <sup>*</sup>
- [Become a Legend] If one player has a ground force or structure on a planet in a qualifying system, and another player has a ship in the same system, both players may count the system towards the requirements of Become a Legend. <sup>*</sup>
- [Become a Legend] A player may have ships in the system containing a legendary planet or Mecatol Rex without controlling the planet for that system to count towards the requirements of Become a Legend. <sup>*</sup>
- [Become a Legend] If Mirage is placed in an anomaly, or the Nano–Forge relic is attached to a planet in an anomaly, that system will only count as one system towards the requirements of Become a Legend. <sup>*</sup>
- [Become a Legend] If a Vuil’raith player’s Dimensional Tear is in a system containing another anomaly, a legendary planet, or Mecatol Rex, that system will only count as one system towards the requirements of Become a Legend. <sup>*</sup>
- [Become a Martyr] The lost planet may be in any player’s home system. It does not have to be a planet in the home system of the player scoring Become a Martyr. <sup>*</sup>
- [Become a Martyr] The lost planet may be in the home system of an eliminated player. <sup>*</sup>
- [Become the Gatekeeper] A player with a ship in the wormhole nexus, or in any other system with both an alpha and beta wormhole, qualifies for Become the Gatekeeper. <sup>*</sup>
- [Become the Gatekeeper] Any ground forces or structures are irrelevant. <sup>*</sup>
- [Betray a Friend] The defender cannot score Betray a Friend. <sup>*</sup>
- [Conquer the Weak] The planet may be in the home system of an eliminated player. <sup>*</sup>
- [Control the Borderlands] A ship, ground force, or structure will all qualify for Control the Borderlands. <sup>*</sup>
- [Control the Borderlands] If one player has a ground force or structure on a planet in a qualifying system, and another player has a ship in the same system, both players may count the system towards the requirements of Control the Borderlands. <sup>*</sup>
- [Control the Borderlands] The units may be in another player’s home system. <sup>*</sup>
- [Control the Borderlands] The Creuss Gate is not a home system. <sup>*</sup>
- [Control the Borderlands] When using the seven– and eight–player alternate setups, only the system tiles designated as “Ring 3”, and home systems are on the edge of the game board, along with the Creuss home system and the wormhole nexus. <sup>*</sup>
- [Control the Region] Any ground forces or structures are irrelevant. <sup>*</sup>
- [Darken the Skies] Darken the Skies may be scored by winning a combat in an eliminated player’s home system. <sup>*</sup>
- [Defy Space and Time] A ship, ground force, or structure will all qualify for Defy Space and Time. <sup>*</sup>
- [Defy Space and Time] If one player has a ground force or structure on Mallice, and another player has a ship in the wormhole nexus, both players may score Defy Space and Time, if it is elected by the Classified Document Leaks agenda. <sup>*</sup>
- [Demonstrate Your Power] A player need not win the combat to score Demonstrate Your Power; they are able to score it if their opponent plays the Skilled Retreat action card. <sup>*</sup>
- [Demonstrate Your Power] A player involved in a combat due to the Mahact player’s Benediction hero ability may score Demonstrate Your Power after that combat. <sup>*</sup>
- [Demonstrate Your Power] Units that are temporarily ships for the duration of a space combat, such as those made so by the Nekro player’s flagship, The Alastor, or the Naaz–Rokha player’s Z–Grav Eidolon mechs, may count towards scoring Demonstrate Your Power. <sup>*</sup>
- [Demonstrate Your Power] The Mentak player may use the Sleeper Cell ability of their hero, during the last round of combat to place ships before scoring Demonstrate Your Power. However, fleet pool limits are also checked before scoring. <sup>*</sup>
- [Demonstrate Your Power] The Mentak player cannot use the ability of their Salvage Operations technology until after the window in which to score Demonstrate Your Power. <sup>*</sup>
- [Destroy Heretical Works] A player will not gain a relic when scoring Destroy Heretical Works. <sup>*</sup>
- [Destroy Heretical Works] The relic fragments may be the same or different types. <sup>*</sup>
- [Destroy Their Greatest Ship] If a player destroys their own flagship or war sun during combat, such as via the effect of The Crown of Thalnos relic, their opponent cannot score Destroy their Greatest Ship. <sup>*</sup>
- [Dictate Policy] Dictate Policy is scored after the third law resolves. As such, the Deadly Plot action card will prevent any player from scoring Dictate Policy. <sup>*</sup>
- [Dictate Policy] Dictate Policy is scored before any rider action cards are resolved. <sup>*</sup>
- [Dictate Policy] If there are three laws in play at the start of the agenda phase, a player may score Dictate Policy immediately. <sup>*</sup>
- [Dictate Policy] If the Political Data Nexus Xxcha hero ability puts a third law in play during the action phase, Dictate Policy cannot be scored until the agenda phase. <sup>*</sup>
- [Discover Lost Outposts] The number of attachments a planet has is irrelevant, if it has at least one. <sup>*</sup>
- [Drive the Debate] Any “For”/“Against” agenda cannot count for Drive the Debate, even if the outcome affects only a single player. <sup>*</sup>
- [Drive the Debate] Scoring Drive the Debate immediately before the Colonial Redistribution agenda is resolved may change which player(s) can be chosen to place the infantry on the elected planet. <sup>*</sup>
- [Drive the Debate] If a player draws Drive the Debate while resolving the Archived Secret or Search Warrant agendas, they cannot score it immediately. <sup>*</sup>
- [Establish Hegemony] With the right attachments, the requirements of Establish Hegemony may be met with a single planet. <sup>*</sup>
- [Fight with Precision] A player does not have to win a combat to score Fight with Precision. <sup>*</sup>
- [Fight with Precision Ω] A player does not have to win a combat to score Fight with Precision. <sup>*</sup>
- [Fight with Precision Ω] For example, say a player plays the Courageous to the End action card when one of their fighters are destroyed during the Anti–Fighter Barrage step. If the dice roll causes their opponent to destroy their ships, and they choose their last fighter, that would allow the player to score Fight with Precision Ω. <sup>*</sup>
- [Form Galactic Brain Trust] The number of technology specialties a planet has is irrelevant, if it has at least one. <sup>*</sup>
- [Found Research Outposts] The number of technology specialties a planet has is irrelevant, if it has at least one. <sup>*</sup>
- [Galvanize the People] Any effect that triggers when a command token is spent will be triggered six times. For example, if the Muaat player has unlocked their commander, Magmus, they will gain six trade goods, one at a time, when scoring Galvanize the People. <sup>*</sup>
- [Hoard Raw Materials] With the right attachments, the requirements of Hoard Raw Materials may be met with a single planet. <sup>*</sup>
- [Improve Infrastructure] The number of structures on the planet is irrelevant, if there is at least one. <sup>*</sup>
- [Improve Infrastructure] The structures may be on planets in another player’s home system. <sup>*</sup>
- [Improve Infrastructure] The Saar player’s Floating Factories cannot be used to score Improve Infrastructure. <sup>*</sup>
- [Intimidate Council] Any ground forces or structures are irrelevant. <sup>*</sup>
- [Lead From the Front] Any effect that triggers when a command token is spent will be triggered three times. For example, if the Muaat player has unlocked their commander, Magmus, they will gain three trade goods, one at a time when scoring Lead From the Front. <sup>*</sup>
- [Learn the Secrets of the Cosmos] The three systems may be mutually adjacent to one system, or separate systems. <sup>*</sup>
- [Learn the Secrets of the Cosmos] Any ground forces or structures are irrelevant. <sup>*</sup>
- [Make an Example of Their World] If a player’s last ground force on a planet is destroyed, but an ability allows that player to then place ground forces onto that planet, Make an Example of Their World may still be scored. <sup>*</sup>
- [Make an Example of Their World Ω] If a player’s last ground force on a planet is destroyed, but an ability allows that player to then place ground forces onto that planet, Make an Example of Their World Ω may still be scored. <sup>*</sup>
- [Make History] A ship, ground force, or structure will all qualify for Make History. <sup>*</sup>
- [Make History] If one player has a ground force or structure on a planet in a qualifying system, and another player has a ship in the same system, both players may count the system towards the requirements of Make History. <sup>*</sup>
- [Make History] A player may have ships in the system containing a legendary planet or Mecatol Rex without controlling the planet for that system to count towards the requirements of Make History. <sup>*</sup>
- [Make History] If Mirage is placed in an anomaly, or the Nano–Forge relic is attached to a planet in an anomaly, that system will only count as one system towards the requirements of Make History. <sup>*</sup>
- [Make History] If a Vuil’raith player’s Dimensional Tear is in a system containing another anomaly, a legendary planet, or Mecatol Rex, that system will only count as one system towards the requirements of Make History. <sup>*</sup>
- [Occupy the Fringe] The Saar player’s Floating Factories are never on a planet. <sup>*</sup>
- [Populate the Outer Rim] A ship, ground force, or structure will all qualify for Populate the Outer Rim. <sup>*</sup>
- [Populate the Outer Rim] If one player has a ground force or structure on a planet in a qualifying system, and another player has a ship in the same system, both players may count the system towards the requirements of Populate the Outer Rim. <sup>*</sup>
- [Populate the Outer Rim] The units may be in another player’s home system. <sup>*</sup>
- [Populate the Outer Rim] The Creuss Gate is not a home system. <sup>*</sup>
- [Populate the Outer Rim] When using the seven– and eight–player alternate setups, only the system tiles designated as “Ring 3” and home systems are on the edge of the game board, along with the Creuss home system and the wormhole nexus. <sup>*</sup>
- [Protect the Border] The number of structures on the planet is irrelevant, if there is at least one. <sup>*</sup>
- [Protect the Border] The structures may be on planets in another player’s home system. <sup>*</sup>
- [Protect the Border] The Saar player’s Floating Factories cannot be used to score Protect the Border. <sup>*</sup>
- [Reclaim Ancient Monuments] The number of attachments a planet has is irrelevant, if it has at least one. <sup>*</sup>
- [Rule Distant Lands] The planets may meet the criteria by being adjacent to an eliminated player’s home system. <sup>*</sup>
- [Threaten Enemies] The ships may be adjacent to the home system of an eliminated player. <sup>*</sup>
- [Threaten Enemies] Any ground forces or structures are irrelevant. <sup>*</sup>
- [Turn Their Fleets to Dust Ω] If a player still has fighters in a system after assigning all hits produced during the Space Cannon Offense step, Turn Their Fleets to Dust Ω may be scored. <sup>*</sup>
- [Turn Their Fleets to Dust Ω] If a system contains only fighters, then Turn Their Fleets to Dust Ω cannot be scored by destroying them. <sup>*</sup>
- [Turn Their Fleets to Dust Ω] For example, say the Yin player has their flagship, the Van Hauge, destroyed during the Space Cannon Offense step. They may score Turn Their Fleets to Dust Ω if the effect of their flagship destroys all non–fighter ships owned by another player in the active system. <sup>*</sup>

### C_promissory_notes.php

**Notes kept**

- [Political Secret] A player may still use abilities from their faction technology after their Political Secret has been played. <sup>1</sup>
  - Edited from: A player may still use abilities from their faction technology, leaders, or mechs after their Political Secret has been played.
  - Source 1 (FAQ appendix: Political Secret and faction technology): "A: No. The “Political Secret” promissory note does not prevent a"
- [Political Secret] If an agenda is discarded, the effect of each Political Secret that has been played ends. The affected players may vote on the next agenda as normal. <sup>1</sup>
  - Edited from: If an agenda is discarded, each Political Secret that has been played is returned. The affected players may vote on the next agenda as normal.
  - Source 1 (FAQ appendix: Political Secret and discarded agenda): "A: Yes. It is a new agenda and thus the effect of the player’s"
- [Political Secret] The effect of Political Secret does not stop a player from using their passive faction ability, only the abilities that player may choose to use. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (FAQ appendix: Political Secret and passive abilities): "A: No. The “Political Secret” promissory note only prevents the use"
- [Trade Agreement] If a player has their maximum number of commodities, and is instructed to replenish their commodities, they will take no commodities. However, that player’s Trade Agreement may be played. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (FAQ appendix: Trade Agreement at maximum commodities): "A: Yes. Even if that player gains zero commodities when their"

**Removed notes restored**

- [Support For The Throne] A Support For The Throne must be played by the receiving player as soon as it is received. It cannot be kept secret. <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p.21 Support for the Throne card): "you must place it faceup in your play area and gain 1 victory point."
- [Support For The Throne] Support For The Throne is returned when the system is activated, even if the active player will perform no hostile acts towards the other player this turn. <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p.21 Support for the Throne card): "If you activate a system that contains 1 or more of the blue player’s units, or if the blue player is eliminated, lose 1 victory point and return this card to the blue player."
- [Trade Agreement] Trade Agreement cannot be played when a player gains commodities, only when they replenish commodities. <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p.4 Trade Agreement card): "When the blue player replenishes commodities: The blue player gives you all of his commodities."
- [Ceasefire] The active player may still use the Space Cannon ability of any units during the Space Cannon Offense step of the tactical action. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (ceasefire-and-disable-vs-space-cannon (Community consensus)): "Ceasefire only stops ships moving in, so Space Cannon, Bombardment, invasion and production all still happen."
- [Ceasefire] Ceasefire does not prevent a player from producing units in the active system. <sup>2</sup>
  - Trimmed from: Ceasefire does not prevent a player from producing or placing units in the active system.
  - Source 2 (ceasefire-and-disable-vs-space-cannon (Community consensus)): "Space Cannon, Bombardment, invasion and production all still happen"
- [Support For The Throne] If the active player receives a Support For The Throne, they cannot then attempt to trade it with another player. It must be played immediately. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (trading-received-promissory-notes (Community consensus)): "Notes face up in your play area, like Support for the Throne, can't be traded or handed back voluntarily."
  - Source 2 (promissory-notes-optional-to-play (Community consensus)): "promissory notes are never mandatory unless the note says to play it immediately or place it face up"
- [Support For The Throne] If an effect other than activating a system during a tactical action places a command counter in a system with the other player’s units (for example, the primary ability of the Diplomacy strategy card), this will not cause Support For The Throne to be returned. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (support-for-the-throne-return (Community consensus)): "Putting a command token in a system by other means is not activating it."
  - Source 2 (what-counts-as-activating (Community consensus)): "Tokens placed by Diplomacy or a retreat and cards aimed at a system don't activate it, so they don't trigger Space Cannon Offense, Support for the Throne returns"
- [Support For The Throne] Activating a system containing only a player’s structures will still cause their Support For The Throne to be returned. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (support-for-the-throne-return (Community consensus)): "Units include their ships, ground forces, space docks and PDS"
- [Support For The Throne] If two players trade their Support For The Throne to one another simultaneously, the active player will be the first to gain a victory point. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (support-for-the-throne-swap-win (Community consensus)): "The swapped notes resolve one after the other in normal timing order, so the player who gains the point first wins"
  - Source 2 (order-of-simultaneous-abilities (Community consensus)): "In the action phase, the active player goes first"
- [Support For The Throne] During the agenda phase, the first player in speaker order will be the first to gain a victory point. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (support-for-the-throne-swap-win (Community consensus)): "The swapped notes resolve one after the other in normal timing order"
  - Source 2 (order-of-simultaneous-abilities (Community consensus)): "In the strategy and agenda phases, go in order starting with the speaker instead."

**Notes added** (rulings that were not on the site before)

- [Support For The Throne] A player may give their Support for the Throne to another player even if doing so gives that player the victory point they need to win the game. The player who gave it may activate systems containing the holder’s units without penalty. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (support-for-the-throne-trading (Community consensus)): "Yes to both."
- [Support For The Throne] Activating a system that contains only another player’s control tokens does not cause their Support For The Throne to be returned, as control tokens are not units. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (support-for-the-throne-return (Community consensus)): "but not control tokens, so activating a system where they only have control tokens is fine"

**Citations added to existing items**

- [Political Secret] If an agenda is discarded, the effect of each Political Secret that has been played ends. The affected players may vote on the next agenda as normal. now also cites <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (BGG, sigmazero13, Jun 6, 2018): "If you "Quash" an agenda, the "quashed" agenda is "resolved", correct? [...] Dane: Yup yup. If that specific agenda didn't get resolved then I guess by what Political Secret said, that player would never get to vote ever again!"
- [Political Secret] The effect of Political Secret does not stop a player from using their passive faction ability, only the abilities that player may choose to use. now also cites <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (BGG, kaiteinomen, Mar 2, 2018): "Any faction ability that requires the player to make any kind of active decision cannot be used. [...] Letnev's ability is active at all times whether the Letnev player decides to make use of it or not, so it is not affected."
- [Political Secret] The effect of Political Secret does not stop a player from using their passive faction ability, only the abilities that player may choose to use. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (political-secret-what-it-blocks (Community consensus)): "Mandatory and passive abilities still apply"
- [Support For The Throne] A Support For The Throne must be played by the receiving player as soon as it is received. It cannot be kept secret. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (promissory-notes-optional-to-play (Community consensus)): "promissory notes are never mandatory unless the note says to play it immediately or place it face up"
- [Support For The Throne] Support For The Throne is returned when the system is activated, even if the active player will perform no hostile acts towards the other player this turn. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (support-for-the-throne-return (Community consensus)): "As soon as you activate a system containing any of that player's units, whether or not you move in or attack."

**Restored without a source** (marked * on the site)

- [Ceasefire] If a player has units in the active system from before the tactical action in which their Ceasefire is played, those units will remain in the active system. <sup>*</sup>
- [Ceasefire] If the active player already has units with capacity in the active system, they may transport ground forces on planets in that system into the space area of that system. Those units may then be committed to invade a planet during this tactical action. <sup>*</sup>
- [Ceasefire] If a system containing only a player’s ground forces or structures is activated, that player may still play the active player’s Ceasefire. <sup>*</sup>
- [Political Secret] If a player has had their Political Secret played, other players may still use that player’s other promissory notes. <sup>*</sup>
- [Trade Agreement] A player does not have to be neighbors with the player that plays their Trade Agreement to give them their commodities. <sup>*</sup>

### C_relics.php

**Notes kept**

- [The Codex] The action card discard is shuffled to form a new action card deck as soon as the action card deck has zero cards in it. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (23.5): "23.5 CARDS: When a deck is depleted, players shuffle the deck’s"
- [The Codex] It is public knowledge which action cards a player takes using The Codex. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Exploration: The Codex): "A: Yes, the discard is public knowledge, so anything removed from the discard is also public knowledge."
- [The Crown of Thalnos] A player may only reroll combat rolls with The Crown of Thalnos. They cannot reroll anti–fighter barrage rolls and similar. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Exploration: Crown of Thalnos): "No to Infantry 2, no to Courageous to the End, no to Anti-Fighter Barrage. The intent is ONLY combat rolls."
- [Dynamis Core] If a player uses the purge ability of Dynamis Core, they will need to return commodities if they now exceed their original commodity value. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Exploration: Dynamis Core): "A: Yes, you discard down."
- [Heart of Ixth] The “0” side of the d10 represents a result of 10. <sup>1</sup>
  - Edited from: The “0” side of the d10 represents a result of 10. Heart of Ixth may be used to turn this result into a 9, or vice versa.
  - Source 1 (FAQ appendix, General: dice): "A: Yes, the “0” face is a “10” result."
- [Neuraloop] If a player uses Neuraloop to purge the Dynamis Core, and they have more commodities than their faction’s printed commodity value, they return any extras to the supply. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Exploration: Dynamis Core): "A: Yes, you discard down."
- [Neuraloop] A player can score a maximum of one objective of any type during or after each combat. A player cannot score the secret objective revealed by Neuraloop and one of their own secret objectives from the same combat. <sup>1</sup>

**Restored without a source** (marked * on the site)

- [Book of Latvinia] If the Nekro player draws the Book of Latvinia, they will gain six command tokens and zero technologies, even if they own all technologies without prerequisites. <sup>*</sup>
- [The Crown of Thalnos] For each unit that rolls multiple combat dice, the player with The Crown of Thalnos should roll those unit’s dice separately from any other combat dice. <sup>*</sup>
- [The Crown of Thalnos] A reroll caused by any other effect will not cause a unit to be destroyed. <sup>*</sup>
- [The Crown of Thalnos] Units destroyed by The Crown of Thalnos are destroyed at the end of the Roll Dice step, before the Assign Hits step. <sup>*</sup>
- [The Crown of Thalnos] A unit with the Sustain Damage ability cannot use it to avoid being destroyed when it fails to produce a hit with the reroll from The Crown of Thalnos. <sup>*</sup>
- [Lightrail Ordnance] The space docks may use the Space Cannon ability during both the Space Cannon Offense and Space Cannon Defense steps. <sup>*</sup>
- [Maw of Worlds] The player does not have to meet the prerequisites of the technologies they acquire using Maw of Worlds. <sup>*</sup>
- [Metali Void Shielding] The affected ship may be destroyed by the Direct Hit action card after it uses the Sustain Damage ability. <sup>*</sup>
- [Metali Void Shielding] A player may play the Reflective Shielding action card after it uses the Sustain Damage ability via Metali Void Shielding. <sup>*</sup>
- [Metali Void Shielding] If a player owns Metali Void Shielding, and their opponent plays the Waylay action card, they may use Metali Void Shielding for both the Anti–Fighter Barrage and combat rolls in that round of space combat. <sup>*</sup>
- [Metali Void Shielding] Metali Void Shielding has no effect when the Argent player resolves their Raid Formation faction ability. <sup>*</sup>
- [Neuraloop] A player may use Neuraloop to purge Nano–Forge, even if it is attached to a planet, if they control that planet. That planet loses the increase to its resources and influence values, and is no longer legendary. <sup>*</sup>
- [Neuraloop] If a player uses Neuraloop to purge another relic that has a purge ability, that purge ability is not resolved. <sup>*</sup>
- [Neuraloop] If a player uses Neuraloop to purge the Circlet of the Void, that player’s units may remain in and move out of any supernovae and/or asteroid fields they are currently in, but cannot move additional units into or through, unless they have another ability that would allow them to do so, such as the Antimass Deflectors technology. <sup>*</sup>
- [Neuraloop] If a player uses Neuraloop to purge The Obsidian, that player must discard one unscored secret objective if they have a total of four scored or unscored secret objectives. There is no effect if they have four scored secret objectives. <sup>*</sup>
- [Neuraloop] If a player uses Neuraloop to purge the Shard of the Throne, that player loses a victory point. <sup>*</sup>
- [Neuraloop] If a player uses Neuraloop to purge another relic, then that player may use Neuraloop again to replace the new objective with yet another objective. <sup>*</sup>
- [Neuraloop] If a player uses Neuraloop to reveal a secret objective as a public objective, that objective does not count towards the limit of three scored or unscored secret objectives for any player that scores it. <sup>*</sup>
- [Neuraloop] The discarded objective is shuffled into its respective deck after the replacement objective is revealed. <sup>*</sup>
- [Neuraloop] This happens before the player with Neuraloop chooses if they wish to purge another relic to replace the new objective. As such, it is possible for the player to reveal the original objective after purging two or more relics. <sup>*</sup>
- [The Prophet’s Tears] A player cannot use the ability of The Prophet’s Tears when they directly gain a technology. <sup>*</sup>
- [Scepter of Emelpar] If a player has no command tokens in their reinforcements, they must use a command token from their command sheet instead when they use the ability of the Scepter of Emelpar. <sup>*</sup>
- [Scepter of Emelpar] The Scepter of Emelpar may be used whenever a command token would be spent from a player’s strategy pool. This includes when spending to perform the secondary ability of a strategy card, for faction abilities, and when scoring objectives. <sup>*</sup>
- [Scepter of Emelpar] If the Muaat player uses the ability of the Scepter of Emelpar, they will not gain a trade good from the ability of their commander, Magmus. <sup>*</sup>
- [Shard of the Throne] When the player that owns the Shard of the Throne loses control of a legendary planet or a planet in their home system, they immediately give it to the player who gained control of that planet. No abilities may be resolved before this. <sup>*</sup>
- [Shard of the Throne] If the player that gains Shard of the Throne controls no legendary planets or planets in their home system, they cannot lose it. <sup>*</sup>
- [Stellar Converter] A player cannot target a planet they control with Stellar Converter. <sup>*</sup>
- [The Triad] The Triad may be readied by effects that ready planets, such as the Diplomacy strategy card. <sup>*</sup>
- [The Triad] The Triad is not considered a planet for other game effects. <sup>*</sup>
- [The Triad] Units cannot be placed on The Triad. <sup>*</sup>
- [The Triad] The Triad cannot be elected by an “elect planet” agenda, nor can it be exhausted by agenda effects such as the “For” effect of the New Constitution agenda. <sup>*</sup>
- [The Triad] The Triad does not have a planet trait; it cannot be explored. <sup>*</sup>

- [X–89 Bacterial Weapon ΩΩ] Effects that cancel hits will only cancel hits based on the doubled number of hits. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (Last Bastion: Proxima Targeting VI / X-89): "X89 turns all hits into 2 before abilities and effects like Titan’s agent or Proxima."
- [Assault Cannon] If a player loses ships before they can resolve the Assault Cannon ability, they will be unable to resolve it if they no longer have three or more non–fighter ships. <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (livestrongbelwas, reddit, Feb 08, 2018): "The second player doesn’t get to use his Assault Cannons"
- [Assault Cannon] This will most commonly happen when both players in a combat have Assault Cannon, and the defender has exactly three non–fighter ships. <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (livestrongbelwas, reddit, Feb 08, 2018): "Two players have Assault Cannon Tech. Player 1 is the active player. He attacks player 2. Both players have exactly 3 destroyers."
  - Source 5 (livestrongbelwas, reddit, Feb 08, 2018): "The second player doesn’t get to use his Assault Cannons"
- [Assault Cannon] Effects that cancel hits, such as Sustain Damage, cannot be used to prevent ships from being destroyed. <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (garfielder, Sep 19, 2017): "sustain damage cannot be used against abilities that ‘destroy’."
- [Integrated Economy] A player may produce ships with Integrated Economy, unless another player has ships in the space area of that planet’s system. <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (eumaies, Feb 21, 2018): "Dane: That is correct. You can build ships normally, but if enemy ships are present, you cannot."
- [Antimass Deflectors] The −1 applies to space cannon rolls during both the Space Cannon Offense and Space Cannon Defense steps. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (antimass-deflectors (Community consensus)): "other players' Space Cannon rolls get -1 against all your units, ground forces in Space Cannon Defense included"
- [Fleet Logistics] A player may use the ability of Fleet Logistics the same turn they gain it. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (new-tech-usable-immediately (Community consensus)): "Research Fleet Logistics with the Technology primary on your turn, and once that strategic action, secondaries included, is done you may take a second action that turn"
- [Fleet Logistics] If a player’s turn is ended by a game effect, they cannot use Fleet Logistics to perform an additional action. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (xxcha-nullification-field-timing (Community consensus)): "Once the turn ends, nothing more happens in it"
- [Fleet Logistics] If a player’s second action would be to use a component action to play an action card, and that card is cancelled, they are not required to perform an alternate second action on that turn. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (sabotaged-action-card-turn-not-used (Community consensus)): "If it was the optional extra action from Fleet Logistics, you can just end your turn."
  - Source 2 (fleet-logistics (Community consensus)): "the second action is optional"
- [X–89 Bacterial Weapon ΩΩ] A war sun must target the same planet with all three of its bombardment dice. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (bombardment-assignment (Community consensus)): "a unit bombards a single planet with all its dice"
- [X–89 Bacterial Weapon ΩΩ] If a unit may roll additional bombardment dice, such as by the Plasma Scoring technology, that additional dice must target the same planet. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (bombardment-assignment (Community consensus)): "a unit bombards a single planet with all its dice"
- [X–89 Bacterial Weapon ΩΩ] A player may roll for bombardment against a planet that contains no ground forces. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (bombardment-assignment (Community consensus)): "You may pick any planet in the system, since bombardment comes before ground forces are committed."
- [AI Development Algorithm] When a player exhausts AI Development Algorithm to ignore a prerequisite of a unit upgrade technology that they are researching, they may still use AI Development Algorithm itself for meeting a warfare technology (red) prerequisite on that unit upgrade technology in the same manner as any other technology. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (prerequisites-and-exhausted-tech (Community consensus)): "you can exhaust AI Development Algorithm and still count it"
- [AI Development Algorithm] For example, AI Development Algorithm alone may be used to research the Destroyer II unit upgrade. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (prerequisites-and-exhausted-tech (Community consensus)): "you can exhaust AI Development Algorithm and still count it"
- [Self–Assembly Routines] A mech cannot be placed in a space area with Self–Assembly Routines, and so cannot be placed in a system that does not contain a planet. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (self-assembly-routines-supernova (Community consensus)): "No — there is no planet in a supernova to place it on."
- [Duranium Armor] A player uses Duranium Armor only once during each round of combat, at the end of the Assign Hits substep. Hits assigned outside of this substep will not allow Duranium Armor to repair an additional unit. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (duranium-armor-rules (Community consensus)): "Once per combat round, after hits are assigned"
- [Duranium Armor] Duranium Armor is used even if a player’s opponent produced no hits during a round of combat. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (duranium-armor-rules (Community consensus)): "even if you had no hits to assign"
- [Duranium Armor] If a player starts a combat with a damaged unit, they use Duranium Armor in the first round of combat. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (duranium-armor-rules (Community consensus)): "it repairs one of your damaged units in that combat that did not use Sustain Damage that round"
- [Duranium Armor] A player may use Duranium Armor to repair a unit damaged by Space Cannon or Bombardment hits that occurred immediately before the combat. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (duranium-armor-rules (Community consensus)): "A unit damaged by Space Cannon before combat can be repaired at the end of round one."
- [Assault Cannon] A player with Assault Cannon must mandatorily resolve its ability if they meet the requirement. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (assault-cannon-order-and-targets (Community consensus)): "Assault Cannon is mandatory when it applies"
- [Scanlink Drone Network] The units must be on the planet before the Movement step of the tactical action. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (scanlink-needs-unit-on-planet (Community consensus)): "explore one planet there that already contains any of your units"
  - Source 2 (scanlink-needs-unit-on-planet (Community consensus)): "It won't explore planets your ships merely fly past."
- [Integrated Economy] There is no limit on the number of units produced, so long as the combined cost does not exceed the planet’s resource value. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (integrated-economy (Community consensus)): "Any units, ships or ground forces, up to the new planet's resource value in cost, paid normally"

**Notes added** (rulings that were not on the site before)

- [Hyper Metabolism] The text of Hyper Metabolism is changed to: “During the status phase, gain 3 command tokens instead of 2.” <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (Errata: Hyper Metabolism): "During the status phase, gain 3 command tokens instead of 2."
- [Plasma Scoring] If a player makes separate Bombardment rolls against multiple coexisting players on the same planet, Plasma Scoring adds one additional dice to only one of those rolls. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (Coexistence): "Plasma Scoring is applied to one unit during the bombard step.  Plasma will not trigger multiple times."
- [X–89 Bacterial Weapon ΩΩ] A player who bombards another player’s coexisting units on a planet they control must still exhaust that planet. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (Coexistence): "Do you exhaust your own planets when you bombard the coexisting units with x89?"
- [Gravity Drive] The +1 from Gravity Drive may be combined with the +1 from the Flank Speed action card, applying +2 to the move value of that ship. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (movement-bonuses-stack (Community consensus)): "Gravity Drive gives +1 to one ship and Flank Speed +1 to all your ships, so that ship can get +2"
- [Light/Wave Deflector] A ship that uses Light/Wave Deflector to move through a system containing another player’s ships may pick up and transport units from that system. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (lightwave-deflector-pickup (Community consensus)): "moving through such a system is allowed, and ships can pick up units in any system they pass through"
- [Magen Defense Grid Ω] The hit is produced at the start of ground combat, before any dice are rolled. A ground force destroyed by this hit does not roll. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (magen-defense-grid-disabled-pds (Community consensus)): "That hit lands at the start of ground combat, before dice are rolled, so the destroyed unit never rolls."
- [Graviton Laser System] Graviton Laser System has no effect during the Space Cannon Defense step, as hits can only be assigned to ground forces. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (graviton-laser-system-space-cannon-defense (Community consensus)): "the only targets during Space Cannon Defense are the invading ground forces"
- [Graviton Laser System] Hits produced while Graviton Laser System is in effect may still be cancelled by the Sustain Damage ability. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (graviton-laser-system-hits (Community consensus)): "They are still ordinary hits, so Sustain Damage can cancel them before assignment."
- [Fleet Logistics] If a player’s first action is a strategic action, the other players resolve the secondary ability of that strategy card before the player performs their second action. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (fleet-logistics (Community consensus)): "If the first is Warfare, other players resolve its secondary before your second action."
- [Plasma Scoring] A space dock using the Space Cannon ability due to the Experimental Battlestation action card rolls an additional die from Plasma Scoring. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (plasma-scoring-optional (Community consensus)): "including a space dock firing through Experimental Battlestation, which then rolls 4 dice"
- [Light/Wave Deflector] Light/Wave Deflector does not allow a player to produce ships in a system that contains another player’s ships. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (light-wave-deflector-limits (Community consensus)): "It doesn't let you produce ships in a blockaded system."
- [X–89 Bacterial Weapon Ω] X–89 Bacterial Weapon Ω cannot be used unless the player’s Bombardment destroys at least one infantry; if all hits are assigned to mechs, it has no effect. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (x-89-omega-rules (Community consensus)): "It needs your Bombardment to destroy at least one infantry"
- [Integrated Economy] No unit is using its Production ability. The Sarween Tools technology and similar effects will not apply. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (integrated-economy (Community consensus)): "It isn't a Production ability, so Sarween Tools and the original Yin Spinner don't apply."
- [Graviton Laser System] Graviton Laser System applies to every die rolled for the Space Cannon roll, including dice rolled by units using another unit’s Space Cannon, such as the Ral Nel player’s Linkships. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (graviton-laser-all-dice (Community consensus)): "it applies to the whole Space Cannon roll, borrowed dice included"

- [Assault Cannon] If a player loses ships before they can resolve the Assault Cannon ability, they will be unable to resolve it if they no longer have three or more non–fighter ships. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (assault-cannon-order-and-targets (Community consensus)): "each trigger re-checked when its turn comes"

  - Source 2 (assault-cannon-order-and-targets (Community consensus)): "the attacker's Assault Cannon can push the defender below 3 non-fighter ships and deny the defender's own Assault Cannon"
- [Assault Cannon] Effects that cancel hits, such as Sustain Damage, cannot be used to prevent ships from being destroyed. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (sustain-damage-vs-destroy-effects (Community consensus)): "Sustain Damage only cancels hits, and these effects destroy units without producing hits"

**Restored without a source** (marked * on the site)

- [Dark Energy Tap] The Saar player cannot explore a frontier token with a Floating Factory. However, if they produce a ship during the Production step, they will be able to use that ship to explore the token. <sup>*</sup>
- [Fleet Logistics] Effects that trigger at the start or end of a player’s turn will not trigger between each of those player’s actions. <sup>*</sup>
- [Fleet Logistics] A player cannot use Fleet Logistics to pass on the same turn they performed an action. <sup>*</sup>
- [X–89 Bacterial Weapon Ω] X–89 Bacterial Weapon Ω may be used against each planet in a system, if the conditions are met. <sup>*</sup>
- [X–89 Bacterial Weapon Ω] X–89 Bacterial Weapon Ω will trigger only after all bombardment hits have been assigned. <sup>*</sup>
- [X–89 Bacterial Weapon Ω] The L1Z1X may use X–89 Bacterial Weapon Ω after they use their Harrow faction ability. <sup>*</sup>
- [X–89 Bacterial Weapon ΩΩ] Ground forces that are participating in space combat as though they were ships do not double the hits they produce. <sup>*</sup>
- [X–89 Bacterial Weapon ΩΩ] Ships that are participating in ground combat as though they were ground forces double the hits they produce. <sup>*</sup>
- [Magen Defense Grid Ω] The chosen ground force may cancel the hit by using its Sustain Damage ability, if present. A different ground force with the Sustain Damage ability cannot do so. <sup>*</sup>
- [Magen Defense Grid Ω] If the last of a player’s ground forces in a ground combat are destroyed by the effect of Magen Defense Grid Ω, that player loses the combat immediately. They will be unable to use any “start of combat” abilities. <sup>*</sup>
- [Magen Defense Grid ΩΩ] The chosen ground force may cancel the hit by using its Sustain Damage ability, if present. A different ground force with the Sustain Damage ability cannot do so. <sup>*</sup>
- [Magen Defense Grid ΩΩ] If the last of a player’s ground forces in a ground combat are destroyed by the effect of Magen Defense Grid ΩΩ, that player loses the combat immediately. They will be unable to use any “start of combat” abilities. <sup>*</sup>
- [Magen Defense Grid ΩΩ] If the Saar player owns Magen Defense Grid ΩΩ, and a system containing a Floating Factory is activated, then the infantry will be placed in the space area. <sup>*</sup>
- [Assault Cannon] Examples of other abilities that may remove units at the start of a space combat include the Creuss player’s Dimensional Splicer faction technology ability, the Mentak player’s Ambush faction ability, the Yin player’s Impulse Core faction technology ability, as well as abilities such as the Courageous to the End action card or the Reflective Shielding action card that may trigger off of any of the previous abilities. <sup>*</sup>
- [Assault Cannon] A player may use an ability to add ships at the start of combat. If this brings the number of non–fighter ships to three or more, the player may then use the ability of Assault Cannon. <sup>*</sup>
- [Assault Cannon] Each other player may use one ability after that player has gained ships, and before that player has the opportunity to use the Assault Cannon ability. This may prevent that player from using the ability, as above. <sup>*</sup>
- [Assault Cannon] Examples of abilities that may add units at the start of space combat include a combination of the Mentak player’s Sleeper Cell hero ability and their Ambush faction ability, the ability of the Nekro player’s flagship, The Alastor, and the Naaz–Rokha player’ Eidolon mech ability. <sup>*</sup>
- [Transit Diodes] When resolving the ability of Transit Diodes, that player may remove ground forces from a system containing their command token. <sup>*</sup>
- [Transit Diodes] The ground forces may be removed from on a planet or from in a space area. <sup>*</sup>
- [Transit Diodes] The ground forces may be removed from different systems. <sup>*</sup>
- [Transit Diodes] The ground forces may be placed on different planets. <sup>*</sup>

### C_units.php

**Notes kept**

- [War Sun] A player without the war sun unit upgrade technology cannot produce a war sun. <sup>1</sup>
  - Edited from: A player without the war sun unit upgrade technology cannot produce, place or have a war sun on the board for any reason.
  - Source 1 (FAQ appendix p.44, Mentak): "Without war sun technology, they cannot produce a war sun, even using “Salvage Operations.”"
- [Fighter] Fighters and ground forces do not count towards capacity during combat. When combat ends however, units will need to be removed to meet capacity requirements. <sup>1</sup>
  - Edited from: Fighters and ground forces do not count towards capacity during combat. As such, any number of Fighter II may be in a system during combat, regardless of capacity and fleet pool. This will usually only be caused by effects that place units in a system during combat. When combat ends however, units will need to be removed to meet capacity and fleet pool requirements.
  - Source 1 (16.3c): "A player’s fighters and ground forces do not count against capacity during combat. At the end of combat, any excess units are removed and returned to that player’s reinforcements."
- [Fighter] A ship cannot move through a system that contains fighters that are controlled by another player during the Movement step of a tactical action. <sup>1</sup>
  - Edited from: A ship cannot move through a system that contains Fighter II that are controlled by another player during the Movement step of a tactical action.
  - Source 1 (FAQ appendix p.40, General): "Yes, fighters can block ship movement"
- [Infantry] If a player controls no planets in their home system, at the start of their turn, any Infantry II that have been placed on that player’s Infantry II unit upgrade technology card are returned to that player’s reinforcements. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (FAQ appendix p.41, General): "When those infantry would be placed on a home planet, they are returned to that player’s reinforcements instead."

**Removed notes restored**

- [Fighter] Ships may be moved into or produced in a system even if doing so would exceed the fleet pool limit. However, some of those ships must immediately be removed to satisfy the limit. <sup>5</sup>
  - Trimmed from: Ships may be moved into, produced in or placed in a system even if doing so would exceed the fleet pool limit. However, some of those ships must immediately be removed to satisfy the limit. If some of those ships are fighters II, they may instead count towards that player’s capacity in that system. If capacity is exceeded, fighters or ground forces must be removed to meet the limit.
  - Source 5 (garfielder, Sep 28, 2017): "it is a legal move as long as you respect fleet supply once you’ve moved. For #2, you could build 3 dreadnoughts and destroy the destroyer that was there initially."
- [War Sun] If a war sun’s ability results in no units on a planet having the Planetary Shield ability, then the ability of the Magen Defense Grid technology cannot be used during ground combat on that planet. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (magen-defense-grid-versions-war-sun (Community consensus)): "Only the original version, which needs a unit with Planetary Shield: a war sun makes other players' units lose Planetary Shield."
- [War Sun] A war sun has no effect on the Magen Defense Grid Ω technology. <sup>2</sup>
  - Trimmed from: A war sun has no effect on the Magen Defense Grid Ω or Magen Defense Grid ΩΩ technologies.
  - Source 2 (magen-defense-grid-versions-war-sun (Community consensus)): "The Codex Omega version only needs a structure and isn't affected by war suns."

**Notes added** (rulings that were not on the site before)

- [Space Dock] A space dock does not have a capacity value. It allows up to three fighters in its system to not count against capacity, but it cannot hold ground forces in the space area. If a player has two space docks in a system, up to six fighters in that system do not count against capacity. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (space-dock-fighter-allowance (Community consensus)): "a normal space dock lets up to 3 fighters in its system ignore capacity"
- [Space Dock] A space dock’s Production value is not affected by whether its planet is exhausted. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (space-dock-production-value (Community consensus)): "The planet being exhausted doesn't matter."
- [Flagship] If a player’s flagship is destroyed, it is returned to their reinforcements and may be produced again. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (rebuilding-flagship (Community consensus)): "it goes back to reinforcements and can be produced again"
- [Fighter] Fighter II units are still fighters for all other game effects. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (advanced-fighters-still-fighters (Community consensus)): "they remain fighters for every other effect"

### F_arborec.php

**Notes kept**

- [Letani Warrior (Unit)] When multiple units use their Production ability, the Production value is pooled. As such, if the Arborec player has two Letani Warrior I in a system, they may produce two infantry for one resource, rather than two. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (FAQ appendix, The Arborec; 68.1a): "Production value is totaled when the “Production” ability of units in a system is used."
- [Duha Menaimon (Flagship)] The produced units must be paid for. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (FAQ appendix, Production): "a unit that is produced must always be paid for."
- [Duha Menaimon (Flagship)] The Duha Menaimon does not have Production. As such, the Sarween Tools technology and similar such effects do not apply to the Duha Menaimon. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (FAQ appendix, Production): "“Sarween Tools” is only used with the “Production” ability."
- [Duha Menaimon (Flagship)] The Duha Menaimon must be in the system when it is activated for its effect to trigger. It will not trigger if it is moved into the active system later in the turn. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (FAQ appendix, The Arborec): "The “Duha Menaimon” can only be used to produce units when it is in a system at the moment it is activated."
- [Letani Ospha (Agent)] If the player wishes to place a ship, but there are none of that type left in their reinforcements, they may remove a ship of that type from any system that does not contain one of their command tokens and place that instead. This ship will be placed undamaged. <sup>1,4</sup>
  - Source 1 (23.4a): "When a player would place a unit, if there are none of that type left in their reinforcements, that player can remove a unit from any system that does not contain one of their command tokens and place that unit in their reinforcements."
  - Source 4 (General, damaged unit removed and placed): "If it is produced, placed, or replaced which would require a remove and place it is no longer damaged."
- [Dirzuga Rophal (Commander)] The produced unit must be paid for. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (FAQ appendix, Production): "a unit that is produced must always be paid for."
- [Dirzuga Rophal (Commander)] A ship may be produced only if no other player currently has ships in that system. <sup>1</sup>

This unit will be placed undamaged. <sup>1,4</sup>
  - Source 1 (67.5a): "If a player cannot produce a unit because it is not in their reinforcements, that player can remove a unit from any system that does not contain one of their command tokens and place that unit in their reinforcements."
  - Source 4 (General, damaged unit removed and placed): "If it is produced, placed, or replaced which would require a remove and place it is no longer damaged."

  - Source 1 (67.6): "A player cannot produce ships in a system that contains other players’ ships."
- [Letani Miasmiala — Ultrasonic Emitter (Hero)] No unit is using its Production ability. The Sarween Tools technology and similar effects will not apply. <sup>1</sup>

### F_argent.php

**Notes kept**

- [Raid Formation] The Anti–Fighter Barrage ability can still be used even if no fighters are present in the system. <sup>1</sup>
  - Edited from: The Anti–Fighter Barrage step happens during each space combat, even if no fighters are present in the system.
  - Source 1 (10.1d): "This ability can still be used if no fighters are present"
- [Raid Formation] Raid Formation occurs when hits are produced, not after hits are assigned. As such, cancelling any hits will not prevent an opponent’s ships from becoming damaged. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Argent Flight, Raid Formation timing): "Raid formation is applied after rolling, before cancelling or assigning hits."
- [Raid Formation] The chosen ship becomes damaged, it does not use its Sustain Damage ability. As such, effects that trigger when a ship uses its Sustain Damage ability, such as the Direct Hit action card, cannot be played. <sup>4</sup>
  - Edited from: The chosen ship becomes damaged, it does not use its Sustain Damage ability. As such, effects that trigger when a ship uses its Sustain Damage ability, such as the Direct Hit or Reflective Shielding action cards, cannot be played.
  - Source 4 (Argent Flight, Raid Formation and Direct Hit): "Raid Formation does not cause the ship to use its Sustain Damage ability, it only causes it to become damaged, so there is no window for Direct Hit to be used."
- [Strike Wing Alpha (Unit)] When a Strike Wing Alpha II rolls a 9 or 10 for their anti–fighter barrage ability, infantry are destroyed before any hits are cancelled. <sup>4</sup>
  - Edited from: When a Strike Wing Alpha II rolls a 9 or 10 for their anti–fighter barrage ability, infantry are destroyed at the end of the Roll Dice step. This occurs before any ship may use its Sustain Damage ability at the start of the Assign Hits step.
  - Source 4 (Argent Flight, Strike Wing Alpha II): "the infantry would be destroyed BEFORE any cancellation of hits."
- [Strike Wing Alpha (Unit)] Effects that cancel hits, such as the Shields Holding action card, cannot prevent the infantry from being destroyed. If an effect rerolls any anti–fighter barrage dice, the new result will determine how many infantry are destroyed. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Argent Flight, Strike Wing Alpha II): "The rolls from Strike Wing Alpha II can be subject to rerolls before the ability is applied, but the infantry would be destroyed BEFORE any cancellation of hits."
- [Trrakan Aun Zulok (Commander)] “Combat” is a unit attribute, not a unit ability. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (18): "Combat is an attribute of some units"
- [Mirik Aun Sissiri — Helix Protocol (Hero)] Ships may transport units out of systems that contain one of the Argent player’s command tokens. <sup>4</sup>
  - Edited from: Ships may transport units only if their origin system does not contain one of the Argent player’s command tokens.
  - Source 4 (General, Transport and Movement Abilities (Argent Hero)): "During Movement abilities, you can transport units out of systems that contain your tokens."

**Removed notes restored**

- [Zeal] The Argent player always votes first, even if they are the speaker. <sup>14</sup>
  - Source 14 (ti_codex_2_cards.txt p.7): "You always have to vote first, but you get extra votes"
- [Zeal] Other players vote in their regular order after the Argent player votes; clockwise starting with the player to the left of the speaker (skipping over the Argent player as necessary). <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (argent-zeal-voting-order (Community consensus)): "Argent votes first, even as speaker, then voting resumes as normal from the speaker's left."
- [Raid Formation] If the Letnev player owns their Non–Euclidean Shielding faction technology, this will not reduce the number of ships that the Argent player chooses. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (argent-raid-formation-no-fighters (Community consensus)): "It produces no hits and those ships don't use Sustain Damage, so it can't destroy anything and Direct Hit or Non-Euclidean Shielding don't come into it."
- [Raid Formation] If the Argent player plays the Waylay action card, hits in excess of their opponent’s fighters will first cause chosen ships to become damaged, then those same hits must still be assigned. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (raid-formation-and-waylay (Community consensus)): "Raid Formation works off the barrage roll without using up the hits. With Waylay, those hits still hit ships and the opponent assigns them normally"
