- [Aerie Sentinel (Mech)] An Aerie Sentinel cannot be transported by a ship without a capacity value. _(no source)_
  - Covered by [R_capacity.php](R_capacity.php) [Rules Reference]: A unit’s capacity value indicates the maximum combined number of fighters and ground forces that it can transport.

**Notes removed**

- [Mirik Aun Sissiri — Helix Protocol (Hero)] Ships cannot move into a nebula or supernova, even if it contains one of the Argent player’s command tokens. _(contradicted by FAQ Anomalies (a nebula no longer requires being the active system to move into it))_

### F_bastion.php

**Removed notes restored**

- [Dame Briar (Agent)] Any type of unit in the same system may be galvanized; it need not match the type of the destroyed unit. <sup>7</sup>
  - Source 7 (te_rulebook_web.txt p.4 (Dame Briar card, Bastion Valiant)): "You may exhaust this card to galvanize another of that player’s units in the destroyed unit’s system."
- [Liberate] If the Bastion player gains control of an uncontrolled planet, they may choose if they resolve Liberate before or after they explore that planet. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (doc5.txt, Last Bastion): "Bastion must choose which order to resolve Liberate and Exploration per planet, then resolve those abilities in full before the other."
- [Lura Keen — Entity 4X41A “Apollo” (Hero)] Effects that cancel hits, such as Sustain Damage, cannot be used to prevent units from being destroyed. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (sustain-damage-vs-destroy-effects (Community consensus)): "Sustain Damage only cancels hits, and these effects destroy units without producing hits."
- [Lura Keen — Entity 4X41A “Apollo” (Hero)] During the Space Cannon Offense step of a tactical action, players resolve the Space Cannon ability of their eligible units starting with the active player, and going around the table in a clockwise order. Each player will make their space cannon roll and have the hits assigned, likely destroying some units, before the next player begins their own space cannon roll. Should the Bastion player have one of their units destroyed by another player’s space cannon roll, and choose to use the ability of Entity 4X41A “Apollo”, then in doing so they destroy a unit with the Space Cannon ability, that unit will not perform a space cannon roll if the player that owns that unit has not yet made their space cannon roll. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (space-cannon-one-player-at-a-time (Community consensus)): "Each player's roll, hit assignment, Sustain Damage and responses like Direct Hit finish before the next fires, so a unit destroyed earlier, such as an Xxcha flagship, never gets to shoot."

**Notes added** (rulings that were not on the site before)

- [Galvanize] Galvanize tokens are placed from the Bastion player’s reinforcements. If there are none in their reinforcements, a galvanize token cannot be moved from elsewhere on the board. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (Last Bastion / Galvanize): "No, Galvanise tokens are placed from reinforcements.  Unlike Sleepers there is no move or place option."
- [Galvanize] The additional die rolled by a galvanized unit is mandatory. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (Last Bastion / Galvanize): "Galvanize: Is the extra dice mandatory?"
- [Proxima Targeting VI (Technology)] The X–89 Bacterial Weapon technology doubles hits before abilities that cancel hits, such as Proxima Targeting VI, are resolved. The planet is still exhausted if the Bastion player controls it. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (Last Bastion / Proxima Targeting VI): "X89 turns all hits into 2 before abilities and effects like Titan’s agent or Proxima. You will exhaust the planet."
- [Proxima Targeting VI (Technology)] Abilities that affect bombardment rolls, such as the Plasma Scoring technology, the Argent player’s commander, Trrakan Aun Zulok, or the Jol–Nar player’s commander, Ta Zern, may be applied to the Bombardment roll from Proxima Targeting VI. <sup>6,9</sup>
  - Source 6 (Last Bastion / Proxima Targeting VI): "Proxima Targeting VI (Technology): Can the Bastion player apply abilities such as Plasma Scoring/Argent commander or Jol-Nar commander to the BOMBARDMENT roll?"
  - Source 9 (Unit Abilities imply Units?): "Yes I'd say let them combo and be shut down."
- [Galvanize] Abilities referring to the Bastion player’s galvanized units being “present” count only galvanized units that are participating in the combat. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (Last Bastion): "Present == participating"
- [4X31C “Helios” (Unit)] The planet’s resource value is increased by two with Helios II, not three; the bonuses of Helios I and Helios II do not stack. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (last-bastion-components (Community consensus)): "Helios II replaces Helios I, so +2, not +3"

**Citations added to existing items**

- [Galvanize] Galvanize tokens are placed from the Bastion player’s reinforcements. If there are none in their reinforcements, a galvanize token cannot be moved from elsewhere on the board. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (last-bastion-components (Community consensus)): "Galvanize tokens are limited; with all 7 in use the effect fails until one is freed."

**Restored without a source** (marked * on the site)

- [Liberate] If they explore first, and the number of infantry or the resource value of the planet changes while resolving the exploration, then the new values will be used when resolving Liberate. <sup>*</sup>
- [Liberate] The number of mechs is irrelevant for determining which effect to resolve. <sup>*</sup>
- [Proxima Targeting VI (Technology)] When the Bastion player makes the Bombardment roll against their own units, they will be able to cancel a hit for each of their present galvanized units. <sup>*</sup>
- [Proxima Targeting VI (Technology)] Other players with galvanised units cannot cancel the Bombardment hits produced by Proxima Targeting VI. <sup>*</sup>
- [4X31C “Helios” (Unit)] The Production value of the 4X31C “Helios” will be calculated from the modified resource value of the planet, after the increase from the 4X31C “Helios” present. <sup>*</sup>
- [The Egeiro (Flagship)] If the Bastion player controls multiple planets in a system, The Egeiro will apply +1 to its combat rolls just once. <sup>*</sup>
- [The Egeiro (Flagship)] If the Bastion player controls a planet in a system, and other players control other planets in that system, The Egeiro will still apply +1 to its combat rolls from that system. <sup>*</sup>
- [Nip and Tuck (Commander)] The Bastion player’s action cards may still be cancelled by other game effects. <sup>*</sup>
- [Nip and Tuck (Commander)] If the Nekro player already has a Valefar Assimilator token on one of the Bastion player’s components, it will remain there when Nip and Tuck are unlocked. <sup>*</sup>
- [Lura Keen — Entity 4X41A “Apollo” (Hero)] Any combat roll modifiers will not apply to the dice roll for Entity 4X41A “Apollo”. <sup>*</sup>
- [Lura Keen — Entity 4X41A “Apollo” (Hero)] Units can only be destroyed by the dice specifically allocated to it. <sup>*</sup>
- [Lura Keen — Entity 4X41A “Apollo” (Hero)] All units belonging to other players in the system may be destroyed, including structures. <sup>*</sup>
- [Lura Keen — Entity 4X41A “Apollo” (Hero)] If Entity 4X41A “Apollo” is resolved during combat, units that belong to another player other than the Bastion player’s opponent could be destroyed. <sup>*</sup>
- [Lura Keen — Entity 4X41A “Apollo” (Hero)] If Entity 4X41A “Apollo” is resolved during a space combat, ground forces on planets or being transported in that system could be destroyed. <sup>*</sup>
- [Lura Keen — Entity 4X41A “Apollo” (Hero)] If Entity 4X41A “Apollo” is resolved during a ground combat, ground forces on other planets or units in the space area of that system could be destroyed. <sup>*</sup>
- [Lura Keen — Entity 4X41A “Apollo” (Hero)] During combat, both players assign hits simultaneously. If the Bastion player wishes to use Entity 4X41A “Apollo” after destroying one of their units by assigning a hit to it, their opponent would first finish assigning the hits produced by the Bastion player. Only then could the Bastion player resolve Entity 4X41A “Apollo”, rolling for just their opponent’s units that were not destroyed by the assigned hits. <sup>*</sup>
- [Lura Keen — Entity 4X41A “Apollo” (Hero)] Before assigning hits, players may cancel the produced hits by using the Sustain Damage ability of their units in the combat, one at a time, starting with the active player (intermixed with any other abilities either player wishes to resolve during the same window). Should any of the Bastion player’s units be destroyed by a Direct Hit action card, then they can immediately trigger Entity 4X41A “Apollo”. They will roll dice for all of their opponent’s remaining units in the system, which may include some units that their opponent would have otherwise gone on to cancel a hit with by using its Sustain Damage ability. Once Entity 4X41A “Apollo” has finished resolving, both players must assign any remaining hits; they may cancel some number of these by using the Sustain Damage ability of any surviving units in the combat. <sup>*</sup>

**Removed notes that the site already covers elsewhere**

- [Dame Briar (Agent)] A structure may be galvanized this way. _(no source)_
  - Covered by [F_bastion.php](F_bastion.php) [Dame Briar (Agent)]: Any type of unit in the same system may be galvanized; it need not match the type of the destroyed unit.

### F_creuss.php

**Notes kept**

- [Quantum Entanglement] If the Creuss player has units or controls planets in a system with an alpha wormhole, and another player has units or controls planets in a system with a beta wormhole, or vice versa, then the Creuss player and that player are neighbors. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (FAQ (Mentak Coalition), p.44): "because the ‘neighbor’ status is active as a result of the ability"
- [Quantum Entanglement] The Mentak player may use their Pillage ability against the Creuss player in this manner. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (FAQ (Mentak Coalition), p.44): "Yes, even in the case of “Quantum Entanglement” only being active from the Creuss’ point of view"
- [Quantum Entanglement] If Mecatol Rex contains an alpha wormhole, then the “For” effect of the Ixthian Artifact agenda will not affect the Creuss player’s units in a system with a beta wormhole (and no alpha wormhole), and vice versa. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (FAQ (Agendas), p.42): "No. Only the Creuss treats those systems as adjacent."
- [Creuss Gate] A frontier token is placed in the Creuss Gate system during setup. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (38.1d): "A frontier token is placed in the Creuss gate system."
- [Creuss IFF (Promissory Note)] A player may receive the Creuss IFF in a transaction during their turn. If received at the start of that player’s turn, that player may play it immediately. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (FAQ (General), p.41): "Yes. For example, a promissory note with “At the start of your turn:” timing may be immediately played if the transaction occurred within the “start of turn” timing window."
- [Creuss IFF (Promissory Note)] Any deal between the Creuss player and another player regarding where the wormhole tokens will be placed, if made before the Creuss IFF is exchanged, is non–binding. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (28.4): "If the terms of a deal cannot be resolved immediately, it is a non-binding deal."
- [Creuss IFF (Promissory Note)] The Creuss IFF may be played even if the Creuss player has not researched Wormhole Generator. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (FAQ (Ghosts of Creuss), p.44): "Yes, the promissory note does not require that the “Wormhole Generator” technology is researched."
- [Dimensional Splicer (Technology)] The Shields Holding action card may be used to cancel the hit. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (FAQ (Action Cards), p.42): "“Shields Holding” may be used to cancel hits that are produced by these abilities."
- [Dimensional Splicer (Technology)] If the chosen ship cancels the hit by using its Sustain Damage ability, the Direct Hit action card may be used. <sup>1</sup>
  - Edited from: If the chosen ship does so, the Direct Hit and/or Reflective Shielding action cards may be used.
  - Source 1 (FAQ (Action Cards), p.42): "“Direct Hit” can be used to follow up hits that are assigned by “Ambush,” “Dimensional Splicer,” “Devotion,” and other similar abilities."
- [Hil Colish (Flagship)] If another player uses the Light/Wave Deflector technology to move through a system that contains the Creuss player’s ships, that player may move through the delta wormhole in the Hil Colish’s system. <sup>1</sup>
  - Edited from: If an effect allows another player to move through a system that contains the Creuss player’s ships (such as the Light/Wave Deflector technology), that player may move through the delta wormhole in the Hil Colish’s system.
  - Source 1 (FAQ (Ghosts of Creuss), p.44): "“Light/Wave Deflector” allows a player other than the Ghosts of Creuss to move their fleet through the “Hil Colish’s” system into the Creuss home system or the Creuss Gate system."
- [Sai Seravus (Commander)] The fighters are placed one at a time, until either one has been placed for each ship with capacity that moved through a wormhole, or the capacity of the system is reached. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Ghosts of Creuss, Sai Seravus): "fighters are placed in the active system one at a time, up to the number of ships with capacity that moved through wormholes, or the capacity limit in the system is reached, whichever happens first."
- [Riftwalker Meian — Singularity Reactor (Hero)] Any tokens on either system are moved with their system. <sup>4</sup>
  - Edited from: Any units and tokens on either system are moved with their system.
  - Source 4 (Ghosts of Creuss, Singularity Reactor): "All tokens stay with their original tile"

**Removed notes restored**

- [Creuss Gate] The Creuss home system (in standard game board setups) is on the edge of the board. <sup>8</sup>
  - Trimmed from: Both the Creuss Gate and the Creuss home system (in standard game board setups) are on the edge of the board.
  - Source 8 (ti10_rulebook_web-good.txt, Clarifications: Objectives): "The wormhole nexus and the Ghosts of Creuss’ home system are on the edge of the game board for the purpose of scoring objectives."
- [Emissary Taivra (Agent)] A delta wormhole in the system (such as from the Hil Colish) does not prevent this ability from being usable. <sup>8</sup>
  - Source 8 (ti10_rulebook_web-good.txt p.8, Emissary Taivra card): "After any player activates a system that contains a non-delta wormhole: You may exhaust this card"
- [Emissary Taivra (Agent)] If this ability is used, the active system will be adjacent to systems with delta wormholes. <sup>8</sup>
  - Source 8 (ti10_rulebook_web-good.txt p.8, Emissary Taivra card): "that system is adjacent to all other systems that contain wormholes during this tactical action."
- [Emissary Taivra (Agent)] The system must have a non–delta wormhole in it at the moment of activation. <sup>8</sup>
  - Trimmed from: The system must have a non–delta wormhole in it at the moment of activation. If a wormhole is placed in a system with no other wormholes using the ability of an Icarus Drive, then Emissary Taivra cannot be used during the same activation.
  - Source 8 (ti10_rulebook_web-good.txt p.8, Emissary Taivra card): "After any player activates a system that contains a non-delta wormhole"
- [Riftwalker Meian — Singularity Reactor (Hero)] Systems that comprise The Fracture and the Rebellion player’s home system cannot be swapped with other system tiles. <sup>7</sup>
  - Source 7 (te_rulebook_web.txt p.16, Riftwalker Meian (Creuss Hero)): "This hero cannot swap the Ahk Creuxx system or the systems that make up The Fracture."
  - Source 7 (te_rulebook_web.txt, Crimson Rebellion faction reference): "HOME SYSTEM Ahk Creuxx: 16 THE CRIMSON REBELLION"
- [Creuss IFF (Promissory Note)] The Creuss IFF cannot be played twice in one timing window. <sup>5</sup>
  - Trimmed from: If the active player received the Creuss IFF on a previous turn, they may play it and immediately perform a transaction with the Creuss player to regain it. However, the Creuss IFF cannot be played twice in one timing window. The active player cannot play the Creuss IFF again until their next turn.
  - Source 5 (doc4.txt, Clipper, Jun 6, 2018): "that PN cannot be traded and resolved multiple times during the same window"
- [Dimensional Splicer (Technology)] Any wormhole may trigger Dimensional Splicer, including the one produced by the ability of the Hil Colish. <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (doc4.txt, Vinci, 12/11/2018): "Creuss can use dimensional splicer regardless of the answer to this question because their flagship was in the system."
- [Wormhole Generator (Technology)] This ability is mandatory for the Creuss player in every status phase after it has been researched. <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (doc4.txt, kaiteinomen, Mar 29, 2018 (Dane answer dated 17/09/28)): "The effect is mandatory, once researched"
- [Wormhole Generator (Technology)] The Creuss player may move a wormhole token from the system it is in into the same system. <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (doc4.txt, kaiteinomen, Mar 29, 2018 (Dane answer dated 17/09/28)): "there is nothing stopping the Creuss from “moving” the token into the system that it is already in."
- [Particle Synthesis (Breakthrough)] Each wormhole in the system provides the Production value and discount, even those of the same type. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (doc5.txt, Ghosts of Creuss): "Yes, each wormhole, even wormholes of the same type, provide additional benefits"
- [Quantum Entanglement] The effect of the Enforced Travel Ban law does not affect the Creuss player. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (enforced-travel-ban (Community consensus)): "The Creuss ignore it, since no game effect can prevent Quantum Entanglement."
  - Source 2 (creuss-quantum-entanglement-scope (Community consensus)): "no game effect, Enforced Travel Ban included, can stop that. Other players can't fire Space Cannon or move through that connection."
- [Quantum Entanglement] Other players cannot use Quantum Entanglement to produce hits from a unit with the Deep Space Cannon ability against the Creuss player’s units. <sup>2</sup>
  - Trimmed from: The Creuss player’s Quantum Entanglement ability applies to their units with the Deep Space Cannon ability. Other players cannot use Quantum Entanglement to produce hits from a unit with the Deep Space Cannon ability against the Creuss player’s units.
  - Source 2 (creuss-quantum-entanglement-scope (Community consensus)): "no game effect, Enforced Travel Ban included, can stop that. Other players can't fire Space Cannon or move through that connection."
- [Dimensional Splicer (Technology)] The Creuss player chooses which ship the hit is assigned to. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (dimensional-splicer-flagship-wormhole (Community consensus)): "the Creuss player then picks which enemy ship takes the hit"
  - Source 2 (assigned-ability-hits-and-sustain (Community consensus)): "The Creuss or Yin player chooses which of your ships takes the hit"
- [Dimensional Splicer (Technology)] The chosen ship may cancel the hit by using its Sustain Damage ability, if present. A different ship with the Sustain Damage ability cannot do so. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (assigned-ability-hits-and-sustain (Community consensus)): "Only that ship can use its own Sustain Damage to cancel it; you can't move the hit elsewhere."
- [Hil Colish (Flagship)] If the Hil Colish moves first, then the Creuss player uses the new position of the Hil Colish when determining if the active system may be reached by their other ships. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (creuss-flagship-movement (Community consensus)): "If it moves into the active system first, that system becomes adjacent to other delta wormholes such as the Creuss home system, so your other ships can come in through it"
- [Hil Colish (Flagship)] If the Hil Colish moves last, then it may move itself into (or through, if its move value is increased) the Creuss Gate or Creuss home system. Before it does so, the Creuss player’s other ships may move through the wormhole created by the Hil Colish. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (creuss-flagship-movement (Community consensus)): "or it can move after them. It can also use its own wormhole, for example to go home."
- [Hil Colish (Flagship)] The delta wormhole moves with the Hil Colish. <sup>2</sup>
  - Trimmed from: The delta wormhole moves with the Hil Colish; it cannot move back to its origin system using its own delta wormhole.
  - Source 2 (creuss-wormhole-token-limit (Community consensus)): "The flagship's delta wormhole needs no token; it travels with the ship."
- [Emissary Taivra (Agent)] The Creuss player may use this ability to access the inactive wormhole nexus without a gamma wormhole. Moving ships into the wormhole nexus this way will cause it to flip. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (reaching-wormhole-nexus (Community consensus)): "You can activate the inactive Nexus, and the Creuss agent, used after activation and before movement, makes it adjacent to a delta wormhole system, so ships can move in that turn. Once a unit enters or someone gains Mallice, the Nexus flips."
- [Emissary Taivra (Agent)] If a ship moves from the system containing the Ion Storm, it will not flip, unless the active player may move ships through the Ion Storm wormhole and chooses to do so. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (ion-storm-flipping (Community consensus)): "With several wormhole routes, the moving player chooses which, if any, they use, which decides whether the Ion Storm flips"
- [Icarus Drive (Mech)] The Icarus Drive does not have to be in the activated system. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (creuss-mech-this-system (Community consensus)): "The system the mech was in, not necessarily the one another player activated"
- [Icarus Drive (Mech)] The wormhole token is placed in the system the Icarus Drive was in. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (creuss-gamma-wormhole-placement (Community consensus)): "the Creuss mech, which reacts to any system activation by putting a token in the mech's own system"

  - Source 2 (dimensional-splicer-flagship-wormhole (Community consensus)): "which can set up Direct Hit."
  - Source 2 (direct-hit-and-shields-holding-vs-ability-hits (Designer ruling)): "Direct Hit was errata'd to cover hits produced by your units or abilities"
- [Wormhole Generator (Technology)] This ability is mandatory for the Creuss player in every status phase after it has been researched. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (creuss-wormhole-generator (Community consensus)): "A player relays a developer email saying it is mandatory each status phase, since it lacks 'may'."
- [Wormhole Generator (Technology)] Creuss wormhole tokens may be placed in The Fracture, including with the Creuss IFF promissory note. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (fracture-no-frontier-tokens (Community consensus)): "Wormholes can be placed there, since nothing forbids it."
- [Hil Colish (Flagship)] If another player uses the Light/Wave Deflector technology to move through a system that contains the Creuss player’s ships, that player may move through the delta wormhole in the Hil Colish’s system. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (creuss-wormholes-usable-by-all (Community consensus)): "enemies need a way to move through it (such as Light/Wave Deflector) or must stop and fight there."
- [Hil Colish (Flagship)] If the Hil Colish is returned to the reinforcements by a gravity rift, its delta wormhole ceases to exist; other ships cannot use it to reach the active system. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (creuss-flagship-movement (Community consensus)): "If it moves first through a gravity rift and is destroyed, the wormhole is gone before the others move."

**Restored without a source** (marked * on the site)

- [Slipstream] Slipstream does not apply to the Creuss Gate or to the Hil Colish, or to gamma wormholes. <sup>*</sup>
- [Creuss IFF (Promissory Note)] The Creuss IFF cannot place wormhole tokens in the home system of an eliminated player. <sup>*</sup>
- [Dimensional Splicer (Technology)] One hit will be produced even if the system contains multiple wormholes. <sup>*</sup>
- [Wormhole Generator (Technology)] Wormhole Generator cannot place wormhole tokens in the home system of an eliminated player. <sup>*</sup>
- [Wormhole Generator Ω (Technology)] Wormhole Generator cannot place wormhole tokens in the home system of an eliminated player. <sup>*</sup>
- [Hil Colish (Flagship)] If the Hil Colish is moved first, and is removed due to the effect of a gravity rift, other ships that were declared to move that can reach the destination system must do so, even if the path is through the gravity rift. Ships that cannot reach the active system do not move. <sup>*</sup>
- [Hil Colish (Flagship)] If the Hil Colish moves before or after other ships, it does not generate a second Space Cannon Offense step. <sup>*</sup>
- [Hil Colish (Flagship)] During space combat involving the Hil Colish, either player may retreat to another system containing a delta wormhole, if that system meets the other requirements for retreating. <sup>*</sup>
- [Hil Colish (Flagship)] If the Hil Colish is destroyed between the Announce Retreats step and the Retreat step, then the retreating player must retreat to a different eligible system. If no such system exists, then their retreat is cancelled. <sup>*</sup>
- [Hil Colish (Flagship)] When the Hil Colish retreats, it may retreat before or after the Creuss player’s other ships, but cannot retreat in such a way that would prevent the other ships from retreating to the same system. <sup>*</sup>

- [Sai Seravus (Commander)] The Creuss player cannot remove a ground force to create capacity for a fighter. <sup>*</sup>
- [Sai Seravus (Commander)] If the Creuss player has a space dock in the active system, they may consider some of the fighters they place as held by the space dock, in order to continue placing fighters. <sup>*</sup>
- [Sai Seravus (Commander)] This ability may be used whenever the Creuss player’s ships move, not just during the movement step of a tactical action. <sup>*</sup>
- [Sai Seravus (Commander)] If the Creuss player retreats from a combat, then they will have no capacity in the active system, and so cannot place any fighters there. <sup>*</sup>
- [Sai Seravus (Commander)] If the Mahact player uses their Benediction hero ability to move the Creuss player’s ships, then the Creuss player may use this ability. <sup>*</sup>
- [Particle Synthesis (Breakthrough)] If the Creuss player moves the Hil Colish into a system, the Creuss player may use the Production ability of the associated delta wormhole during the production step of the same tactical action. <sup>*</sup>

**Removed notes that the site already covers elsewhere**

- [Creuss IFF (Promissory Note)] The active player may perform a transaction with each other player at most once per turn. As such, the active player cannot receive the Creuss IFF more than once per turn. _(no source for the conclusion (multi-step deduction from LRR 94.1; parent removed and LRR 94.1 limits to neighbors, not 'each other player'))_
  - Covered by [R_transactions.php](R_transactions.php) [Rules Reference]: During the active player’s turn, they may resolve up to one transaction with each of their neighbors; multiple actions still allow only one transaction with each neighbor.
- [Hil Colish (Flagship)] The Creuss player must declare all ships that will moving before they move the Hil Colish or their other ships. They then declare the path that the first ship(s) to move will travel along, and move those ship(s). They then declare the path that the other ship(s) to move will travel along, and move those ships. Any ships that were declared to move must, if it is possible to do so. _(no source)_
  - Covered by [R_gravity_rift.php](R_gravity_rift.php) [Notes]: All ship movement must be declared before any of them roll for gravity rift removal.
- [Hil Colish (Flagship)] The Creuss player cannot wait to see the result of their other ships’ gravity rift rolls before deciding to move the Hil Colish; they must declare if the Hil Colish is moving at the same time they declare which other ships are moving. _(no source)_
  - Covered by [R_gravity_rift.php](R_gravity_rift.php) [Notes]: All ship movement must be declared before any of them roll for gravity rift removal. A player may not choose additional ships to move after seeing the result of this roll.
- [Hil Colish (Flagship)] A unit with the Deep Space Cannon ability may produce hits in systems adjacent to that unit via the delta wormhole in the Hil Colish’s system. Most commonly, this will allow the Creuss player to target units in the Hil Colish’s system from the space cannon rolls of units in their home system. _(no source)_
  - Covered by [R_wormholes.php](R_wormholes.php) [Rules Reference]: Systems that contain identical wormholes are adjacent.
- [Sai Seravus (Commander)] The Creuss cannot place additional fighters once they have fighters and infantry in the space area equal to their capacity in that system, even if they have unused fleet pool and the fighter II unit upgrade technology. _(no source)_
  - Covered by [F_creuss.php](F_creuss.php) [Sai Seravus (Commander)]: The fighters are placed one at a time, until either one has been placed for each ship ... or the capacity of the system is reached.
- [Sai Seravus (Commander)] A ship may move out of a system and back into the same system during tactical action movement, if its move value is high enough. If the Creuss player does this with a ship with capacity, and moves in this manner via a wormhole, they may place a fighter, if possible. _(no source)_
  - Covered by [R_movement.php](R_movement.php) [Rules Reference (Tactical Action Movement)]: The ship can move out of the active system and back into it if its move value is high enough.
- [Sai Seravus (Commander)] When the Creuss player moves a ship through a wormhole, ending in a system that contains an alpha or beta wormhole and unlocks Sai Seravus, they cannot apply its ability to that movement. _(no source)_
  - Covered by [R_leaders.php](R_leaders.php) [Notes]: A commander’s ability cannot be applied to the instance of the effect that unlocked it.
- [Sai Seravus (Commander)] If the Creuss player moves the Hil Colish separately from other ships during the same Move Ships step, Sai Seravus cannot unlock until all movement is completed. _(no source)_
  - Covered by [R_leaders.php](R_leaders.php) [Rules Reference (Commanders)]: A commander’s unlock conditions cannot be met while an ability or game effect is being resolved.

### F_deepwrought.php

**Removed notes restored**

- [Aello (Commander)] The Deepwrought player does not have the capability to prevent other players from using the ability of Aello. <sup>7</sup>
  - Source 7 (te_rulebook_web.txt p.16, Aello (Deepwrought Commander)): "The Deepwrought player cannot choose to disallow Aello from being used by other players."
- [Share Knowledge (Promissory Note)] If a player gains then loses the Antimass Deflectors technology, their units may remain in and move out of any asteroid fields they are currently in, but cannot move additional units into or through. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (anomalies-restrict-moving-in-only (Community consensus)): "anomaly rules restrict moving into or through them, not being in them or moving out. Ships already there stay and may leave normally"
- [Radical Advancement (Technology)] If the Deepwrought player replaces the Antimass Deflectors technology, their units may remain in and move out of any asteroid fields they are currently in, but cannot move additional units into or through. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (anomalies-restrict-moving-in-only (Community consensus)): "anomaly rules restrict moving into or through them, not being in them or moving out. Ships already there stay and may leave normally"
- [Aello (Commander)] If a player has the Deepwrought player’s Alliance promissory note, then other players may use the ability of either or both (or neither): <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (deepwrought-commander-alliance-stack (Community consensus)): "Yes — each is a separate optional trigger, and the Deepwrought and their ally can't refuse."
- [Aello (Commander)] Another player may use the ability from both for a two resource discount, triggering the commodity ability for both the Deepwrought player and the player with their Alliance promissory note. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (deepwrought-commander-alliance-stack (Community consensus)): "Yes — each is a separate optional trigger, and the Deepwrought and their ally can't refuse."
- [Aello (Commander)] Another player may use the ability from only the Deepwrought player for a one resource discount, triggering the commodity ability for just the Deepwrought player. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (deepwrought-commander-alliance-stack (Community consensus)): "Yes — each is a separate optional trigger, and the Deepwrought and their ally can't refuse."
- [Aello (Commander)] Another player may use the ability from only the player with the Alliance promissory note for a one resource discount, triggering the commodity ability for just the player with the Alliance promissory note. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (deepwrought-commander-alliance-stack (Community consensus)): "Yes — each is a separate optional trigger, and the Deepwrought and their ally can't refuse."
- [Aello (Commander)] Another player may use the ability from neither player, and receive no discount; the commodity ability will trigger for neither the Deepwrought player nor the player with their Alliance promissory note. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (deepwrought-commander-alliance-stack (Community consensus)): "Yes — each is a separate optional trigger, and the Deepwrought and their ally can't refuse."

**Notes added** (rulings that were not on the site before)

- [Research Team] Research Team may be used both when the Deepwrought player commits ground forces to a planet another player controls and when another player commits ground forces to a planet the Deepwrought player controls. If the Deepwrought player uses Research Team when another player commits ground forces to a planet they control, the invading player cannot engage in ground combat with the Deepwrought player on that planet during the same activation in which the Deepwrought player enters coexistence. <sup>9</sup>
  - Source 9 (Coexist / Deepwrought Scholorate’s Research Team Offensive Use): "Deepwrought may use their Research Teams ability whether they are committing ground forces on a planet another player controls or if another player is committing ground forces on a planet they control."
- [Doctor Carrina (Agent)] Doctor Carrina may be used even if no prerequisite is skipped, but the coexisting infantry is not placed. This includes when the player chooses not to ignore any prerequisites, or researches a technology with no prerequisites. The player may ignore prerequisites they already fulfill on a technology that has at least one prerequisite. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (Deepwrought Scholarate / Doctor Carrina): "The agent may be used, but the coexisting infantry is not placed if a prerequisite was not skipped"
- [Oceanbound] Ocean cards are spent as though they were planet cards. However, oceans are not planets, and do not count as planets for the purpose of scoring objectives, such as Push Boundaries. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (Deepwrought Scholarate): "Oceans do not count as planets for scoring. They may be spent as planet cards."
  - Source 9 (Voting with Space Stations): "Yeah you can vote with them."
- [Oceanbound] If all of the Deepwrought player’s ocean cards are already in play, they cannot resolve Oceanbound to ready one of their oceans. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (Deepwrought Scholarate / Oceanbound): "Oceanbound (Ability): If the Deepwrought player has all their oceans out, can they still resolve Oceanbound if they start another coexistence, so as to ready one of their oceans?"
- [Oceanbound] Attachments such as the Nano–Forge relic and the Ul player’s Terraform promissory note cannot be attached to an ocean card. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (Deepwrought Scholarate): "Can Nano-Forge and/or Terraform be attached to an Ocean Card?"
- [D.W.S. Luminous (Flagship)] The D.W.S. Luminous gains +1 for each system it moves through that contains the Deepwrought player’s units, regardless of any other units present. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (Deepwrought Scholarate / D.W.S. Luminous): "It gains +1 for each system if it moves through that contains your units, regardless of any other units present."
- [D.W.S. Luminous (Flagship)] The Argent player’s Aerie Hololattice technology prevents the D.W.S. Luminous from moving through systems containing the Argent player’s structures. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (Deepwrought Scholarate / D.W.S. Luminous): "Aerie Hololattice stops it moving through."
- [Doctor Carrina (Agent)] The Deepwrought player cannot use Doctor Carrina to start coexisting with the Nekro player, as the Nekro player cannot skip a prerequisite. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (Deepwrought Scholarate / Doctor Carrina): "No, there is no way for Nekro to fulfill the “they do skip a prerequisite” requirement of the agent."
- [Research Team] If the Deepwrought player uses Research Team when another player commits ground forces to a planet the Deepwrought player controls, the ground combat is skipped and the invading player gains control of the planet during the Establish Control step. If another player was already coexisting on that planet, the invading player may instead choose to end that player’s coexistence, resolving a ground combat against them; the winner gains control during the Establish Control step. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (Coexistence): "When DWS uses research teams to coexist, this occurs during the commit ground forces step, so when you get to the ground combat step you skip it, moving straight to the Establish Control step, where you gain control."

**Citations added to existing items**

- [Aello (Commander)] The Deepwrought player does not have the capability to prevent other players from using the ability of Aello. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (deepwrought-commander-alliance-stack (Community consensus)): "Yes — each is a separate optional trigger, and the Deepwrought and their ally can't refuse."

The Deepwrought player, the player with their Alliance promissory note, and the Mahact player may choose up to two of the other players with the ability, triggering their commodity ability, and resulting in a corresponding discount of up to two resources. ### F_empyrean.php

**Notes kept**

- [Dark Pact (Promissory Note)] A player cannot have more commodities than their commodity value. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (21.2): "The commodity value on a player’s faction sheet indicates the maximum number of commodities that player can have."
- [Dark Pact (Promissory Note)] The trade goods gained from Dark Pact are gained simultaneously with the commodities transacted between the two players. <sup>4</sup>
  - Edited from: The trade goods gained from Dark Pact are gained simultaneously with the commodities transacted between the two players. As a pair of players is limited to one transaction per turn (which must involve the active player) or per agenda, the two players cannot then perform a transaction for these trade goods on the same turn.
  - Source 4 (Empyrean, Dark Pact): "It is a single gain of commodities and 1 TG simultaneously."
- [Dark Pact (Promissory Note)] As the trade goods from Dark Pact are gained simultaneously with any commodities and/or trade goods transacted, the Mentak player may only use their Pillage ability on each player once per Dark Pact transaction. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Empyrean, Dark Pact (For the purposes of Pillage)): "It is a single gain of commodities and 1 TG simultaneously."
- [Dynamo (Flagship)] A unit may only use its Sustain Damage ability once in each timing window, even if it is repaired. <sup>4</sup>
  - Edited from: A unit may only use its Sustain Damage ability once in each Assign Hits step, even if it is repaired.
  - Source 4 (Empyrean, Dynamo): "the same unit could not use its Sustain Damage ability multiple times during the same timing window."
- [Dynamo (Flagship)] Influence must be spent separately for each use of this ability. As such, any excess influence used to repair a ship is wasted, and cannot be used to repair a different ship. <sup>4</sup>
  - Edited from: Each unit using its Sustain Damage ability creates a separate timing window. As such, any excess influence used to repair a ship is wasted, and cannot be used to repair a different ship.
  - Source 4 (Empyrean, Dynamo): "The Dynamo’s ability can be used multiple times in the same combat round by spending 2 influence, individually, each time."
- [Acamar (Agent)] A system that contains a planet destroyed by the Stellar Converter relic, and no other planets, is considered to contain no planets. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Objectives, destroyed planet token): "if it is covering the only planet in a system, that system contains no planets."
- [Conservator Procyon — Multiverse Shift (Hero)] A system that contains a planet destroyed by the Stellar Converter relic, and no other planets, is considered to contain no planets. <sup>4</sup>
  - Edited from: A system that contains a planet destroyed by the Stellar Converter relic, and no other planets, is considered to contain no planets. Multiverse Shift will place a frontier token in such a system.
  - Source 4 (Objectives, destroyed planet token): "if it is covering the only planet in a system, that system contains no planets."

**Removed notes restored**

- [Xuange (Commander)] While the agenda phase allows a player to resolve transactions with all other players, it does not make that player neighbors with all other players. <sup>5</sup>
  - Trimmed from: While the agenda phase and the Hacan player’s Trade Convoys promissory note allow a player to resolve transactions with all other players, they do not make that player neighbors with all other players.
  - Source 5 (doc4.txt CreussEmissary/x3n d0g, Jan 17, 2019 (Dane)): "Simply being in the agenda phase does not confer neighbor status to all players."
- [Conservator Procyon — Multiverse Shift (Hero)] If The Fracture is in play when the Empyrean player resolves Multiverse Shift, frontier tokens will be placed in the systems in The Fracture that do not contain a planet. <sup>6</sup>
  - Trimmed from: If The Fracture is in play when the Empyrean player resolves Multiverse Shift, frontier tokens will be placed in the systems in The Fracture that do not contain a planet, and then the Empyrean player will explore those tokens if they have ships present.
  - Source 6 (doc5.txt The Fracture): "The Empyrean Hero will place frontier tokens into the empty systems of the Fracture if it is in play."
- [Void Tether (Breakthrough)] Other players treat the systems that share the border with the Void Tether token as not being adjacent for all game effects. The Empyrean player continues to treat them as adjacent. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (doc5.txt Empyrean): "RAW the systems are not adjacent via any means because of the breakthrough ability."
  - Source 6 (doc5.txt Empyrean): "Does Void Tether block Benediction, Crimson Destroyer placing Breaches? A: Yes, they are not adjacent unless Empyrean allows it."
  - Source 6 (doc5.txt Empyrean): "Empyrean cannot block themselves with void tether."

- [Blood Pact (Promissory Note)] Blood Pact is returned when the system is activated, even if the active player will perform no hostile acts towards the Empyrean player this turn. <sup>*</sup>
- [Blood Pact (Promissory Note)] Activating a system containing only the Empyrean player’s structures will still cause Blood Pact to be returned. <sup>*</sup>
- [Blood Pact (Promissory Note)] If an effect other than activating a system during a tactical action places a command counter in a system with the Empyrean player’s units (for example, the primary ability of the Diplomacy strategy card), this will not cause Blood Pact to be returned. <sup>*</sup>
- [Dark Pact (Promissory Note)] If the Empyrean player plays a player’s Trade Agreement promissory note, this will count for that player giving the Empyrean player all their commodities. <sup>*</sup>
- [Dark Pact (Promissory Note)] Dark Pact is returned when the system is activated, even if the active player will perform no hostile acts towards the Empyrean player this turn. <sup>*</sup>
- [Dark Pact (Promissory Note)] Activating a system containing only the Empyrean player’s structures will still cause Dark Pact to be returned. <sup>*</sup>
- [Dark Pact (Promissory Note)] If an effect other than activating a system during a tactical action places a command counter in a system with the Empyrean player’s units (for example, the primary ability of the Diplomacy strategy card), this will not cause Dark Pact to be returned. <sup>*</sup>
- [Aetherstream (Technology)] The Empyrean player does not decide to use this ability until after the other player has activated a system. Any deal made to use this ability before the system has been activated is non–binding. <sup>*</sup>
- [Voidwatch (Technology)] The active player chooses which promissory note they give the Empyrean player. <sup>*</sup>
- [Voidwatch (Technology)] Giving a promissory note because of Voidwatch is not resolving a transaction. <sup>*</sup>
- [Dynamo (Flagship)] A unit that becomes damaged without using its Sustain Damage ability will not trigger this effect. <sup>*</sup>
- [Dynamo (Flagship)] As an example, The Dark may be exhausted to repair only one ship, not two. <sup>*</sup>
- [Xuange (Commander)] Any movement of ships can trigger this ability, not just movement during the Move Ships step of a tactical action. <sup>*</sup>
- [Xuange (Commander)] If the Empyrean player becomes neighbors with all players when the final player moves ships into a system containing one of the Empyrean player’s command tokens, Xuange will unlock, but the Empyrean player will not be able to resolve its ability from that movement. <sup>*</sup>
- [Xuange (Commander)] If the Empyrean player moves a ship into a system containing one of the Saar player’s Floating Factories, and no other ships, that Floating Factory will by blockaded and destroyed before the Empyrean player can unlock Xuange. If the Empyrean and Saar players are not neighbors in any other way, then Xuange will not unlock. <sup>*</sup>
- [Watcher (Mech)] This effect may cancel a Sabotage action card. <sup>*</sup>
- [Watcher (Mech)] The Watcher must be adjacent to the other player’s units during the timing window when the action card is played in order to cancel it. <sup>*</sup>
- [Watcher (Mech)] In particular, if an action card is played “when/after you activate a system” or similar, then the Watcher must be adjacent before any ships move during that tactical action. <sup>*</sup>
- [Watcher (Mech)] If an action card is cancelled by a Watcher, no costs are paid. <sup>*</sup>
- [Watcher (Mech)] A player playing an action card announces the following before a Watcher may be triggered: <sup>*</sup>
- [Watcher (Mech)] Any targeted planets, system, units, players, cards, outcomes, and/or other such objects. <sup>*</sup>
- [Watcher (Mech)] The value of any variable cost to be paid. <sup>*</sup>
- [Watcher (Mech)] Any dice are rolled and any cards are drawn only after the Empyrean player has declined to remove a Watcher. <sup>*</sup>
- [Watcher (Mech)] If an action card instructs a player to research a technology, that player need not announce what technology they are researching until the Empyrean player has declined to remove a Watcher. <sup>*</sup>
- [Watcher (Mech)] If an action card is played that will have an effect later, such as a rider, that card may only be cancelled by a Watcher when it is originally played. <sup>*</sup>
- [Watcher (Mech)] If the component action was to be the second action the active player was to perform on their turn, through an effect such as the Fleet Logistics technology, the active player may end their turn without performing a second action and without passing. <sup>*</sup>

**Removed notes that the site already covers elsewhere**

  - Covered by [R_nebula.php](R_nebula.php) [Rules Reference]: If a space combat occurs in a nebula, the defender applies +1 to each combat roll of their ships during that combat.
- [Blood Pact (Promissory Note)] Blood Pact has no effect while it is in a player’s hand. _(no source)_
  - Covered by [R_promissory_notes.php](R_promissory_notes.php) [Rules Reference]: A player can resolve any of their promissory note cards by following the text on the card; an unrevealed promissory note is not subject to effects in its ability text ...
- [Dark Pact (Promissory Note)] Dark Pact has no effect while it is in a player’s hand. _(no source)_
  - Covered by [R_promissory_notes.php](R_promissory_notes.php) [Rules Reference]: An unrevealed promissory note is not subject to effects in its ability text ...

  - Covered by [R_adjacency.php](R_adjacency.php) [Rules Reference]: A system is not adjacent to itself.

### F_firmament.php

**Removed notes restored**

- [⚪ Puppets of the Blade] When the Firmament player flips their home system, the Obsidian player places any units that were on Cronos onto Cronos Hollow, and places any units on Tallin onto Tallin Hollow. Any units that were in the space area pre–flip are placed in the space area post–flip. <sup>7</sup>
  - Source 7 (p.16, Clarifications, Cronos and Tallin (Firmament Home System)): "When the Firmament’s home system is flipped, units on Cronos are placed on Cronos Hollow. Units on Tallin are placed on Tallin Hollow. Units in the space area remain in the space area."

**Notes added** (rulings that were not on the site before)

- [⚪ Black Ops (Promissory Note)] The Firmament player may choose not to place a plot. If they do not, the rest of Black Ops still resolves, including purging it. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (Firmament\Obsidian / Black Ops): "The Firmament player may choose not to play a plot. The rest of the note, including purging it, still resolves."
- [⚪ Myru Vos (Agent)] Space cannon cannot be used against any of the moving ships. However, only ships that are not transporting units may move through systems containing other players’ ships. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (Firmament\Obsidian): "No space cannon against any ships moving. Only ships not transporting may move through other player’s ships."
- [⚪ Plots Within Plots] The Enervate plot may be resolved whenever the puppeted player resolves the secondary ability of a strategy card in their play area, including via the Strategize action card. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (Firmament\Obsidian / Enervate): "The puppeted player must have the strategy card in their play area, if you then play Strategize or otherwise resolve the secondary you may resolve Enervate."
- [✖ The Reaping (Breakthrough)] The trade goods from The Reaping are gained as two separate gains. The Mentak player may use their Pillage faction ability for each. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (Firmament\Obsidian / The Reaping): "Two separate gains."
- [✖ Planesplitter (Technology)] Planesplitter resolves before the Coup D’etat action card can be played and resolved. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (Firmament\Obsidian): "Planesplitter would resolve before Coup D’etat is played and resolved."
- [⚪ Viper EX–23 (Mech)] The Firmament player may use this ability while they are the active player, to commit the mech and start coexisting. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (Firmament\Obsidian): "Can you use Firmament’s mech when you are the active player (to commit the Mech & start coexisting)?"
- [⚪ Captain Aroz (Commander)] The Firmament player may score the Stake Your Claim objective using Captain Aroz with ships in a single–planet system where the planet is controlled by another player. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (Firmament\Obsidian): "Can you score Stake Your Claim via commander with ships in a single planet system controlled by another player?"
- [⚪ Plots Within Plots] If a player is eliminated, their control tokens are removed from any plot cards. If a plot card then has no control tokens on it, the Firmament player draws it. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (Firmament\Obsidian / Plots Within Plots): "Remove that players token and draw it if it has no players’ tokens on it."
- [⚪ Puppets of the Blade] Purging the Firmament player’s home planet cards does not allow them to score the Become a Martyr objective. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (Firmament\Obsidian / Puppets of the Blade): "Puppets of the Blade (FirmamentAbility): When The Firmament player purges their home planet cards, do they qualify for BecomeA Martyr?"
- [✖ Malevolency (Promissory Note)] Malevolency remains in the receiving player’s hand, not their play area. However, it is mandatory during the status phase; this is an exception to all other promissory notes. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (Firmament\Obsidian / Malevolency): "It remains in a player’s hand but is mandatory during status, this is an explicit exception to all other promissory notes."
- [⚪ Captain Aroz (Commander)] If Captain Aroz causes the Firmament player to treat a planet as controlled by them, both the Firmament player and the planet’s actual controller are treated as controlling it for the purpose of scoring objectives. This also applies to Aroz Hollow. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (Firmament\Obsidian / Captain Aroz): "No, both are treated as controlling it for purposes of scoring objectives."
- [⚪ Plots Within Plots] If the only player token on a plot card belongs to an eliminated player, that plot card returns to the Firmament player’s hand. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (Elimination): "If there are no other player tokens on the Plot, it returns to hand."

- [⚪ Puppets of the Blade] The Obsidian player will always gain Sharsiss Hollow, regardless of whether or not they purged Sharsiss as the Firmament. <sup>*</sup>

### F_hacan.php

**Notes kept**

- [Guild Ships] Either player may initiate negotiations for a transaction. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (FAQ appendix, The Emirates of Hacan): "either player may suggest the opening of negotiations during either player’s turn."
- [Arbiters] If the Hacan player has more than seven action cards, they must immediately discard down to seven action cards. <sup>1</sup>
  - Edited from: If the Hacan player has more than seven action cards, they must immediately discard down to seven action cards. They cannot trade away the excess.
  - Source 1 (2.4): "If a player ever has more than seven action cards, that player must choose seven cards to keep and discard the rest."
- [Arbiters] If the Hacan player has their Political Secret played during an agenda, they may still trade action cards, as Arbiters is a passive ability. <sup>1,4</sup>
  - Source 1 (FAQ appendix, General (Political Secret)): "The “Political Secret” promissory note only prevents the use of faction abilities that a player must choose to use."
  - Source 4 (Emirates of Hacan, Political Secret): "Arbiters is a passive ability and the Emirates of Hacan can trade Action cards regardless of having their Political Secret played against them."
- [Carth of Golden Sands (Agent)] A player that has their maximum number of commodities may have their commodities replenished. If this happens, they will take no commodities. However, they will still trigger any “when [this] player replenishes commodities” effects, most notably the Trade Agreement promissory note. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (FAQ appendix, General (Trade Agreement)): "Even if that player gains zero commodities when their commodities are refreshed, their “Trade Agreement” may still be played against them."
- [Carth of Golden Sands (Agent)] The ability of Carth of Golden Sands cannot be resolved while another ability is resolving. For example, if the Hacan player is exploring an industrial planet and has revealed the card, they cannot use the ability of Carth of Golden Sands until after they resolve the card’s effect. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Nekro Virus, abilities used during the action phase (Hacan Agent)): "any ability that is used “during the action phase” cannot be resolved unless there are no other abilities currently being resolved."
  - Source 4 (Exploration, transaction in middle of exploration): "other abilities may not be used until after the effect is resolved."
- [Pride of Kenara (Mech)] The planet cannot be traded during combat. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Emirates of Hacan, mech): "A planet that has the Hacan Mech can’t be traded in combat."

**Removed notes restored**

- [Quantum Datahub Node (Technology)] If either strategy card had trade goods on it at the start of the strategy phase, those trade goods remain with the player that originally chose the strategy card. <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (doc4.txt Milty, 10/30/2018 (Dane)): "In both the situations you mentioned there (Quantum Datahub Node and Acquiescence) the player who picked the strategy card originally would get the trade goods."
- [Guild Ships] This ability does not make the Hacan player neighbors with all other players. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (who-are-neighbors (Per the rulebook — The Economy)): "The Hacan can transact with non-neighbors, and anyone can with them, but that doesn't make them neighbors for Pillage."
- [Guild Ships] The Hacan player is still limited to one transaction with every other player per turn. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (hacan-arbiters-trading (Community consensus)): "still within one transaction per player per turn."
- [Arbiters] Any number of action cards may be traded. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (hacan-arbiters-trading (Community consensus)): "Any number of action cards can go either way in a transaction the Hacan are part of"
- [Quantum Datahub Node (Technology)] In a three– or four–player game, the Hacan player chooses which strategy cards are swapped. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (quantum-datahub-node-swap (Community consensus)): "Hacan chooses both which of their cards to give and which face-up card to take."
- [Wrath of Kenara (Flagship)] This ability may be triggered only once for each die rolled. The Hacan player cannot spend two (or more) trade goods to apply +2 (or more) to a single die, but they may spend two (or more) trade goods to apply +1 to each of two (or more) dice. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (hacan-flagship-trade-goods (Community consensus)): "spend 1 trade good for +1 on any of your units' dice in its system, at most once per die."

**Notes added** (rulings that were not on the site before)

- [Auto–Factories (Breakthrough)] The new fleet pool token may be used to support the ships just produced. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (The Emirates of Hacan / Auto-Factories): "Auto-Factories (Breakthrough): Can the new fleet token be used to support the newly placed ship?"
- [Auto–Factories (Breakthrough)] The produced ships do not need to remain to gain the fleet pool token. For example, a Hacan player with no command tokens in their fleet pool may produce three ships, gain the command token, then remove two of those ships due to their fleet pool. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (The Emirates of Hacan / Auto-Factories): "No, with zero in fleet you can produce 3 ships, gain the fleet token, then remove 2 ships to fleet pool."
- [Pride of Kenara (Mech)] If the planet traded contains coexisting units, those units remain coexisting. Because the mech is moved after control of the planet is exchanged, the player gaining the planet may use their Integrated Economy technology before coexistence would end. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (Coexistence): "Coexisting units remain in a state of coexistence as ownership changes through Hacan mech or other game effects, unless they become the only units on the planet."

**Citations added to existing items**

- [Arbiters] If the Hacan player has more than seven action cards, they must immediately discard down to seven action cards.LRR now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (ti-k0289_learn_to_play_2020_web.txt p.17): "Each player can have a maximum of seven action cards in their hand. If a player exceeds this number, they must choose which seven cards they wish to keep and discard the rest."
- [Arbiters] If the Hacan player has their Political Secret played during an agenda, they may still trade action cards, as Arbiters is a passive ability. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (political-secret-what-it-blocks (Community consensus)): "Mandatory and passive abilities still apply, such as Saar's Scavenge, Nekro's Propagation or Hacan's Arbiters"
- [Quantum Datahub Node (Technology)] If either strategy card had trade goods on it at the start of the strategy phase, those trade goods remain with the player that originally chose the strategy card. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (quantum-datahub-node-swap (Community consensus)): "Only the cards move: trade goods were already collected when the cards were picked"

**Restored without a source** (marked * on the site)

- [Masters of Trade] If the Hacan player has the Muaat player’s Alliance promissory note, they will not gain a trade good from it when they use their Masters of Trade ability. <sup>*</sup>
- [Trade Convoys (Promissory Note)] Trade Convoys is returned when the system is activated, even if the active player will perform no hostile acts towards the Hacan player this turn. <sup>*</sup>
- [Trade Convoys (Promissory Note)] Activating a system containing only the Hacan player’s structures will still cause Trade Convoys to be returned. <sup>*</sup>
- [Trade Convoys (Promissory Note)] If an effect other than activating a system during a tactical action places a command counter in a system with the Hacan player’s units (for example, the primary ability of the Diplomacy strategy card), this will not cause Trade Convoys to be returned. <sup>*</sup>
- [Quantum Datahub Node (Technology)] The Hacan player must have three trade goods before they spend the command token; they cannot use the Muaat player’s Alliance promissory note to gain the third trade good. <sup>*</sup>
- [Gila the Silvertongue (Commander)] If the Hacan player abstains or otherwise casts zero votes, they cannot cast additional votes. <sup>*</sup>
- [Harrugh Gefhara — Galactic Securities Net (Hero)] Production limits still apply. <sup>*</sup>
- [Pride of Kenara (Mech)] Structures are also moved. <sup>*</sup>
- [Pride of Kenara (Mech)] If the Pride of Kenara is on a planet in a gravity rift, any units moved must roll for removal if the planet is transacted. <sup>*</sup>

**Removed notes that the site already covers elsewhere**

- [Arbiters] A player may receive action cards even if doing so would put them over the seven action card hand limit. They must immediately discard down to seven action cards in this case. _(no source)_
  - Covered by [R_action_cards.php](R_action_cards.php) [Rules Reference]: If a player ever has more than seven action cards, that player must choose seven cards to keep and discard the rest.

### F_jol_nar.php

**Notes kept**

- [Fragile] The Fragile ability does not affect anti–fighter barrage, bombardment or space cannon rolls. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (10.1c): "Game effects that reroll, modify, or otherwise affect combat rolls do not affect anti-fighter barrage rolls."
  - Source 1 (15.1c): "Game effects that reroll, modify, or otherwise affect combat rolls do not affect bombardment rolls."
  - Source 1 (77.3d): "Game effects that reroll, modify, or otherwise affect combat rolls do not affect space cannon rolls."
- [Research Agreement (Promissory Note)] If a player receives Research Agreement in a transaction immediately after the Jol–Nar player researched a technology, that player may play it immediately to gain that technology. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (FAQ (General), p.41): "Yes. For example, a promissory note with “At the start of your turn:” timing may be immediately played if the transaction occurred within the “start of turn” timing window."
- [Research Agreement (Promissory Note)] Any deal between the Jol–Nar player and another player regarding when Research Agreement will be played, if made before Research Agreement is exchanged, is non–binding. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (28.4): "If the terms of a deal cannot be resolved immediately, it is a non-binding deal."
- [Rin, The Master’s Legacy — Genetic Memory (Hero)] All replacements happen simultaneously. If this ability returns a specific technology, it cannot then be regained via this ability. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Universities of Jol-Nar, Rin): "Simultaneously, that is to say the Universities of Jol-Nar player cannot swap out a tech and re-take it during this component action."

**Removed notes restored**

- [Research Agreement (Promissory Note)] Research Agreement may be triggered when the Jol–Nar player researches a technology outside of the Technology strategy card. For example, it may be triggered by the Divert Funding action card, the Focused Research action card, the Reveal Prototype action card, the Technology Rider action card, the Ixthian Artifact agenda, the Wormhole Research agenda, or the Enigmatic Device exploration card. <sup>2</sup>
  - Trimmed from: Research Agreement may be triggered when the Jol–Nar player reseaches a technology outside of the Technology strategy card. For example, it may be triggered by the Divert Funding action card, the Focused Research action card, the Reveal Prototype action card, the Technology Rider action card, the Ixthian Artifact agenda, the Wormhole Research agenda, or the Enigmatic Device exploration card.
  - Source 2 (jol-nar-research-agreement (Community consensus)): "When Jol-Nar researches a non-faction technology, by any means, while you hold the note, both of you end up with it"
- [Research Agreement (Promissory Note)] Research Agreement cannot be triggered by a game effect that instructs the Jol–Nar player to directly gain a technology, without researching. For example, it cannot be triggered by the Fire of the Gashlai Muaat faction promissory note, the Plagiarize action card, the Research Grant Reallocation agenda, or the Maw of Worlds relic. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (jol-nar-research-agreement (Community consensus)): "It doesn't trigger when Jol-Nar merely gains a tech"
- [E–Res Siphons (Technology)] If an effect other than activating a system during a tactical action places a command counter in a system with the Jol–Nar player’s ships (for example, the primary ability of the Diplomacy strategy card), this will not cause E–Res Siphons ability to trigger. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (what-counts-as-activating (Community consensus)): "a system is activated only by placing a command token as the first step of a tactical action. Tokens placed by Diplomacy or a retreat and cards aimed at a system don't activate it"
- [Doctor Sucaban (Agent)] If the Jol–Nar player has the Infantry II unit upgrade, any of their infantry removed with Doctor Sucaban will not roll for resurrection. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (removed-not-destroyed-sucaban (Community consensus)): "No — removing isn't destroying."

**Notes added** (rulings that were not on the site before)

- [Rin, The Master’s Legacy — Genetic Memory (Hero)] If this ability is used to replace a faction technology which is currently being copied by the Nekro player’s Valefar Assimilator technology, the Valefar Assimilator token stays on that technology while it is in the technology deck, and Valefar Assimilator still has that technology’s text. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Factions/Universities of Jol-Nar): "The token stays on the tech in the tech-deck and Valefar Assimilator still has that technology’s text."
- [Specialized Compounds (Breakthrough)] Due to the synergy of Specialized Compounds, the Jol–Nar player may exhaust a planet with a yellow technology specialty to research a green technology, and vice versa. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (The Universities of Jol-Nar / Specialised Compounds): "Specialised Compounds (Breakthrough): Can Jol-Nar use the SYNERGY to exhaust a yellow skip planet to pay for researching a green technology, or vice versa?"
- [Specialized Compounds (Breakthrough)] The Psychoarchaeology technology cannot be used to avoid exhausting the planet with the technology specialty. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (The Universities of Jol-Nar / Specialised Compounds): "Can Jol-Nar use Psychoarchaeology to bypass exhausting the technology specialty when using Specialised Compounds?"
- [Brilliant] When using Brilliant, the Jol–Nar player spends only the command token from their strategy pool, not the four resources. They then resolve the primary ability of the Technology strategy card, and may research an additional technology by spending six resources. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (jol-nar-brilliant-cost (Community consensus)): "Only the strategy token for the Technology secondary — not the 4 resources — and then they resolve the primary, with the optional second tech for 6 resources."
- [Spatial Conduit Cylinder (Technology)] Spatial Conduit Cylinder is exhausted after the system is activated, before movement; the active system must already contain one of the Jol–Nar player’s units. The Jol–Nar player’s PDS II units in systems made adjacent by Spatial Conduit Cylinder may use their Space Cannon ability against the active system. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (jol-nar-spatial-conduit (Community consensus)): "It is exhausted right after activation, before movement, so the system must already contain your units."
- [Brilliant] When the Jol–Nar player uses Brilliant, they may research a second technology by spending six resources, without spending an additional command token. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (jol-nar-brilliant-second-tech (Community consensus)): "they pay one strategy token, then resolve the full primary"
- [J.N.S. Hylarim (Flagship)] Each result of 9 or 10 produces three hits in total: its normal hit and two additional hits. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (jol-nar-flagship-hits (Community consensus)): "Each die showing 9 or 10 produces its normal hit plus 2 more"

**Citations added to existing items**

- [Fragile] The Fragile ability does not affect anti–fighter barrage, bombardment or space cannon rolls. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (jol-nar-fragile-fighters (Community consensus)): "Fragile only affects combat rolls, not Space Cannon, Bombardment or Anti-Fighter Barrage."
  - Source 2 (what-is-a-combat-roll (Community consensus)): "Jol-Nar's Fragile and effects that reroll combat rolls don't touch them."

**Restored without a source** (marked * on the site)

- [Fragile] The effect of the Fragile ability is mandatory. <sup>*</sup>
- [Research Agreement (Promissory Note)] If the Jol–Nar player will research several technologies in a row, then after each, the player holding Research Agreement may play it. The Jol–Nar player does not decide the next technology they will research until after the player holding the Research Agreement plays it or declines to. <sup>*</sup>
- [Research Agreement (Promissory Note)] Once a player has used Research Agreement after the Jol–Nar player researches a technology, no other player may use Research Agreement for that same Jol–Nar research instance to gain the same technology. <sup>*</sup>
- [Research Agreement (Promissory Note)] If the active player received the Research Agreement on a previous turn, they may play it and immediately perform a transaction with the Jol–Nar player to regain it. They may then play it when the Jol–Nar player researches their next technology. <sup>*</sup>
- [Research Agreement (Promissory Note)] If a faction has a faction–specific unit upgrade as one of their faction technologies, they cannot gain that unit upgrade from Research Agreement when the Jol–Nar player researches the generic version of that unit upgrade. <sup>*</sup>
- [Research Agreement (Promissory Note)] Research Agreement cannot be triggered when the Jol–Nar player resolves Genetic Memory. <sup>*</sup>
- [E–Res Siphons (Technology)] E–Res Siphons ability is triggered when the system is activated, even if the active player will perform no hostile acts towards the Jol–Nar player this turn. <sup>*</sup>
- [Spatial Conduit Cylinder (Technology)] Other players may use the Deep Space Cannon ability of units in the same system as a Jol–Nar player’s unit to produce hits during the Space Cannon Offense step. <sup>*</sup>
- [Ta Zern /Agnlan Oln (Commander)] “Combat” is a unit attribute, not a unit ability; Ta Zern cannot reroll combat dice. <sup>*</sup>
- [Ta Zern /Agnlan Oln (Commander)] Ta Zern cannot be used to reroll dice for an Infantry II resurrection ability. <sup>*</sup>
- [Rin, The Master’s Legacy — Genetic Memory (Hero)] The Jol–Nar player does not have to meet the prerequisites of the technologies they acquire. <sup>*</sup>
- [Rin, The Master’s Legacy — Genetic Memory (Hero)] If the Jol–Nar player later gains a technology they returned, they gain it readied. <sup>*</sup>
- [Rin, The Master’s Legacy — Genetic Memory (Hero)] If the Jol–Nar player has the Nekro player’s Alliance promissory note in their play area, they will not draw any action cards from the ability of the Nekro Acidos commander when they resolve Genetic Memory. <sup>*</sup>

- [Specialized Compounds (Breakthrough)] The Jol–Nar player cannot use Specialized Compounds when researching a unit upgrade. <sup>*</sup>
- [Specialized Compounds (Breakthrough)] A technology with zero or completely ignored prerequisites must still match the color of the planet’s technology specialty to use Specialized Compounds. <sup>*</sup>
- [Specialized Compounds (Breakthrough)] The Jol–Nar player cannot use a technology specialty planet to both pay for the research with Specialized Compounds and to ignore a prerequisite of the researched technology simultaneously. <sup>*</sup>

- [Spatial Conduit Cylinder (Technology)] If its move value is high enough, a ship may still travel through other systems as it moves to the active system. This will allow a ship with capacity to transport units as normal from a system it did not start its movement in. _(no source)_
