### F_keleres.php

**Notes kept**

- [The Tribunii] The Keleres player chooses their starting technology after all other players have gained their starting technologies. <sup>4</sup>
  - Edited from: The Keleres player chooses their starting technology after all other players, including the Argent, Bastion, Deepwrought, Firmament, Ral Nel, Rebellion, and Winnu players, have gained their starting technologies.
  - Source 4 (Council Keleres, starting technology): "Keleres selects after all other players have selected their starting technology."
- [The Tribunii] If there is only one unique starting technology amongst those owned by other players, the Keleres player will start the game with only one technology. <sup>4</sup>
  - Edited from: If there are not two unique starting technologies amongst those owned by other players, the Keleres player will start the game with fewer technologies. This will most commonly happen in a three player game, where one of the other players is playing as N’orr or Winnu.
  - Source 4 (Council Keleres, starting technology): "Keleres only gets one starting technology if there is only one other starting technology among all other factions at the table."
- [Council Patronage] If the Keleres player already has their maximum number of commodities, they will still replenish their commodities during the strategy phase. This will not give them additional commodities, but will trigger any effects that happen when the Keleres player replenishes their commodities. <sup>1</sup>
  - Edited from: If the Keleres player already has two commodities, they will still replenish their commodities during the strategy phase. This will not give them additional commodities, but will trigger any effects that happen when the Keleres player replenishes their commodities.
  - Source 1 (FAQ appendix, General (Trade Agreement)): "Even if that player gains zero commodities when their commodities are refreshed, their “Trade Agreement” may still be played against them."
- [Law’s Order] The blanked laws come back into effect at the end of the turn. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Council Keleres, Law’s Order): "All agendas are treated as blank for all players for the duration of that Council Keleres player’s turn."
- [Law’s Order] If this ability is used, all laws are blanked. The Keleres player cannot choose for some laws to remain in effect. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Council Keleres, Law’s Order): "All agendas are treated as blank for all players for the duration of that Council Keleres player’s turn."
- [Law’s Order] The Keleres player and all of the other players treat all laws as blank for the turn. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Council Keleres, Law’s Order): "All agendas are treated as blank for all players for the duration of that Council Keleres player’s turn."
- [Agency Supply Network (Technology)] Any abilities that trigger “when/after a unit uses Production” will trigger an additional time, for example, the Sarween Tools technology. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Council Keleres, Agency Supply Network): "Yes, Sarween Tools would trigger with each instance of PRODUCTION (twice)."
- [Agency Supply Network (Technology)] The additional Production ability cannot belong to the same unit as the original Production ability. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Council Keleres, Agency Supply Network): "No, the second PRODUCTION instance must be different than one of the units that used the ability to trigger Agency Supply Network."
- [Agency Supply Network (Technology)] During a tactical action, the active player must use every Production ability of their units in the active system, or none of them. As such, the additional Production ability must belong to a unit in a different system. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Council Keleres, Agency Supply Network): "PRODUCTION is all or nothing during tactical actions, so you couldn’t choose to only use one ability in a system to then use another one in the same system."
- [Executive Order (Technology)] Riders may be played when resolving Executive Order. <sup>9</sup>
  - Edited from: When resolving Executive Order, players go through the normal when/after timing windows. Abilities that resolve when the agenda outcome is revealed and abilities that resolve after the agenda outcome is resolved both occur. Riders may be cast during this resolution.
  - Source 9 (General, Executive Order): "That tech should probably say reveal not draw. Players can play riders etc."
- [Custodia Vigilia (Legendary Planet)] The Custodia Vigilia planet card is gained exhausted. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Council Keleres, Custodia Vigilia as a planet): "It is gained exhausted."
- [Custodia Vigilia (Legendary Planet)] Units cannot be placed on Custodia Vigilia. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Council Keleres, Custodia Vigilia as a planet): "however units cannot be placed on it."
- [Custodia Vigilia (Legendary Planet)] Custodia Vigilia is not on the game board, and does not exist in a system. <sup>4</sup>
  - Edited from: Custodia Vigilia is not adjacent to any system, unit, player or other planet.
  - Source 4 (Council Keleres, Custodia Vigilia as a planet): "This planet is not on the game board, and does not exist in a system."
- [Custodia Vigilia (Legendary Planet)] The Keleres player cannot be eliminated once they control Custodia Vigilia. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Council Keleres, Custodia Vigilia as a planet): "Keleres cannot be eliminated if they control Custodia Vigilia."
- [Custodia Vigilia (Legendary Planet)] Custodia Vigilia may be used to qualify for objectives, if it meets any other requirements listed. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Council Keleres, Custodia Vigilia as a planet): "It counts as a planet for objectives and agendas if it meets the specific criteria of those objectives and agendas."
- [Custodia Vigilia (Legendary Planet)] Custodia Vigilia counts as a planet for agendas if it meets the specific criteria of those agendas. <sup>4</sup>
  - Edited from: Custodia Vigilia may be elected by any “elect planet” agendas. However, Custodia Vigilia may be immune to the effects of the agenda.
  - Source 4 (Council Keleres, Custodia Vigilia as a planet): "It counts as a planet for objectives and agendas if it meets the specific criteria of those objectives and agendas."
- [Custodia Vigilia (Legendary Planet)] Custodia Vigilia only gives command tokens when the Imperial strategy card is used to gain a victory point for controlling Mecatol Rex, not when it is used to score a public objective. <sup>4</sup>
  - Edited from: A player gains victory points from the Imperial strategy card only if they control Mecatol Rex. If they use the Imperial strategy card to score an objective, then they gain victory points from that objective, and not the Imperial strategy card.
  - Source 4 (Council Keleres, Custodia Vigilia and Imperial): "the intent is that the tokens are only gained off of using Imperial’s ability to gain a Victory Point because you control Mecatol Rex."
- [Custodia Vigilia (Legendary Planet)] When the Keleres player uses the Production ability of Custodia Vigilia, it is treated as though it were a unit. <sup>4</sup>
  - Edited from: When the Keleres player uses the Production ability of Custodia Vigilia, it is treated as though the Keleres player was using the Production abilitiy of one of their units on Mecatol Rex.
  - Source 4 (Council Keleres, Custodia Vigilia PRODUCTION): "Yes, Custodia Vigilia should include “as if it were a unit”."
- [Custodia Vigilia (Legendary Planet)] This may trigger the abilities of the Sarween Tools technology, and other similar abilities. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Council Keleres, Custodia Vigilia PRODUCTION): "Does Custodia Vigilia's PRODUCTION count as a unit for sarween tools, etc.? A: Yes"
- [Custodia Vigilia (Legendary Planet)] The Ul player’s Terraform faction promissory note may be attached to Custodia Vigilia. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Council Keleres, Custodia Vigilia as a planet): "Terraform can be placed on it"
- [Custodia Vigilia (Legendary Planet)] If Terraform is attached to Custodia Vigilia, it may be explored. <sup>4</sup>
  - Edited from: If Terraform is attached to Custodia Vigilia, it may be explored. However, Custodia Vigilia may be immune to the effects of some exploration cards.
  - Source 4 (Council Keleres, Custodia Vigilia as a planet): "It may be explored, however units cannot be placed on it."
- [Xander Alexin Victori III (Agent)] Xander Alexin Victori III applies to only a single instance of spending trade goods. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Council Keleres, agent duration): "only lasts for the duration of that spend."
- [Kuuasi Aun Jalatai — Overwing Zeta (Hero)] If a player wishes to place a ship, but there are none of that type left in their reinforcements, they may remove a ship of that type from any system that does not contain one of their command tokens and place that instead. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (23.4a): "When a player would place a unit, if there are none of that type left in their reinforcements, that player can remove a unit from any system that does not contain one of their command tokens and place that unit in their reinforcements."
- [Omniopiares (Mech)] If a planet contains multiple mechs, the invading player must pay one influence for each, as separate payments. <sup>4</sup>
  - Edited from: If a planet contains multiple mechs, the invading player must pay one influence for each, as separate payments. For example, if all four mechs were on a planet, the invading player could only exhaust Meer to pay for one instance of the ability; they would still have three instances of a single influence to pay.
  - Source 4 (Council Keleres, Omniopiares): "Each mech is one instance of spend one influence."

**Restored without a source** (marked * on the site)

- [Law’s Order] If the Keleres player owns the Political Censure law, they will not lose a victory point when it is blanked, and they may use action cards during this turn. <sup>*</sup>
- [Law’s Order] If the Keleres player then uses the Repeal Law action card, targeting the Political Censure law, then it will be discarded without the Keleres player losing the victory point. <sup>*</sup>
- [Keleres Rider (Promissory Note)] A player who cannot vote may still play a Keleres Rider. <sup>*</sup>
- [Keleres Rider (Promissory Note)] A player who cannot play action cards may still play a Keleres Rider. <sup>*</sup>
- [Agency Supply Network (Technology)] The Keleres player may use Custodia Vigilia as the additional Production ability, and when they use Custodia Vigilia as the original Production ability, they may use an additional Production ability. <sup>*</sup>
- [Agency Supply Network (Technology)] The original Production ability must be fully resolved, before the Keleres player may use an additional Production ability. <sup>*</sup>
- [Agency Supply Network (Technology)] The Keleres player cannot pay one resource for two fighters or infantry, then place one with a unit using the original Production ability and one with the unit using the additional Production ability. <sup>*</sup>
- [Executive Order (Technology)] If the Keleres player draws one of the Classified Document Leaks, Judicial Abolishment, Miscount Disclosed or New Constitution agendas, they will discard it if required and reveal a new agenda from the deck. <sup>*</sup>
- [Executive Order (Technology)] If the Miscount Disclosed agenda is resolved, the players will also vote on the elected agenda during the Keleres player’s action. <sup>*</sup>
- [Executive Order (Technology)] If an agenda would give multiple players a victory point, those players gain that victory point in initiative order, starting with the player with the Leadership strategy card (or next lowest initiative value should no player have the Leadership strategy card), regardless of the Keleres player’s initiative. <sup>*</sup>
- [Executive Order (Technology)] If a third law is put into play, the Dictate Policy secret objective cannot be scored until the agenda phase. <sup>*</sup>
- [I.I.H.Q. Modernization (Technology/Breakthrough)] If the Keleres player is neighbors with another player, that player is neighbors with the Keleres player. <sup>*</sup>
- [Custodia Vigilia (Legendary Planet)] The Keleres player may use a command token to perform the secondary of Imperial during the same strategic action that they gained that token. <sup>*</sup>
- [Suffi An (Commander)] The trade good to unlock Suffi An is spent after, and independent of, any trade goods spent while resolving the action card. <sup>*</sup>
- [Suffi An (Commander)] If the Keleres player uses their additional action to perform another component action, they may perform another additional action. They may do this any number of times. <sup>*</sup>
- [Suffi An (Commander)] Suffi An does not trigger from the component action of the action card used that was to unlock her. <sup>*</sup>
- [Suffi An (Commander)] If the Keleres player can perform a second action through some other game effect (such as the Fleet Logistics technology), they may unlock Suffi An by playing an action card with a component action for their first action, then perform a second component action, which will then allow them to perform a third action because of Suffi An. <sup>*</sup>
- [Suffi An (Commander)] If a player’s turn is ended by a game effect, they cannot use Suffi An to perform an additional action. <sup>*</sup>
- [Suffi An (Commander)] A player cannot use Suffi An to pass on the same turn they performed an action. <sup>*</sup>
- [Suffi An (Commander)] If a player’s additional action would be to use a component action to play an action card, and that card is cancelled, they are not required to perform an alternate additional action on that turn. <sup>*</sup>
- [Kuuasi Aun Jalatai — Overwing Zeta (Hero)] The Keleres player must be participating in the combat in order to resolve Overwing Zeta. <sup>*</sup>
- [Kuuasi Aun Jalatai — Overwing Zeta (Hero)] Overwing Zeta may be played in a round following the Artemiris being destroyed. <sup>*</sup>
- [Odlynn Myrr — Operation Archon (Hero)] The additional votes are not cast until the Keleres player casts votes normally. <sup>*</sup>
- [Odlynn Myrr — Operation Archon (Hero)] The Keleres player may vote for a different outcome than the one they predicted. If they do, they will gain one trade good and one command token. <sup>*</sup>
- [Odlynn Myrr — Operation Archon (Hero)] The Keleres player will still receive the trade goods and command tokens if the agenda is discarded and resolved with no effect by the Deadly Plot action card. <sup>*</sup>

### F_letnev.php

**Notes kept**

- [War Funding (Promissory Note)] A player may receive War Funding in a transaction during a combat. If received at the start of a round, that player may play it immediately. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (94.1a): "A player can resolve a transaction at any time during their turn, even during a combat."
  - Source 1 (FAQ (General): card acquired from a transaction during its timing window): "A: Yes. For example, a promissory note with “At the start of your turn:” timing may be immediately played if the transaction occurred within the “start of turn” timing window."
- [War Funding (Promissory Note)] A transaction must involve the active player. As such, the defender will be unable to receive War Funding. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (94.1): "During the active player’s turn, they may resolve up to one transaction with each of their neighbors."
  - Source 1 (29): "During either a space or ground combat, the player who is not the active player is the defender."
- [War Funding Ω (Promissory Note)] A player may receive War Funding Ω in a transaction during a combat. If received after dice are rolled, that player may play it immediately. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (94.1a): "A player can resolve a transaction at any time during their turn, even during a combat."
  - Source 1 (FAQ (General): card acquired from a transaction during its timing window): "A: Yes. For example, a promissory note with “At the start of your turn:” timing may be immediately played if the transaction occurred within the “start of turn” timing window."
- [War Funding Ω (Promissory Note)] A transaction must involve the active player. As such, the defender will be unable to receive War Funding Ω. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (94.1): "During the active player’s turn, they may resolve up to one transaction with each of their neighbors."
  - Source 1 (29): "During either a space or ground combat, the player who is not the active player is the defender."
- [War Funding Ω (Promissory Note)] A player may only reroll combat rolls with War Funding Ω. They cannot reroll anti–fighter barrage rolls and similar. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Barony of Letnev: War Funding Omega): "No, War Funding Omega, War Funding, Munitions Reserves and Crown of Thalnos, are specific to combat rolls."
- [Viscount Unlenn (Agent)] This ability only applies to combat rolls. It does not apply to dice rolls for a unit’s Anti–Fighter Barrage ability. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Barony of Letnev: Viscount Unlenn): "No, the Barony agent only has an effect on combat rolls."
- [Dunlain Reaper (Mech)] A Deploy ability may be resolved only once per timing window. As such, the Letnev player may only place one Dunlain Reaper this way per ground combat round. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (30.3): "A unit’s deploy ability can be resolved only once per timing window."
- [Dunlain Reaper (Mech)] A Deploy ability may only be resolved for units in a player’s reinforcements. If all four Dunlain Reapers are already on the board, no Dunlain Reaper may be deployed. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (30.2, 30.2a): "A player can only resolve a deploy ability to place a unit that is in their reinforcements."

**Removed notes restored**

- [War Funding (Promissory Note)] The active player may perform a transaction with each other player at most once per turn. As such, the active player cannot receive War Funding more than once per turn. <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p.17, Neighbors, Transactions, and Deals): "The active player may negotiate only once with each of their neighbors per turn. After a transaction has been finalized, no other transactions may occur between those players that turn."
- [War Funding Ω (Promissory Note)] The active player may perform a transaction with each other player at most once per turn. As such, the active player cannot receive War Funding Ω more than once per turn. <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p.17, Neighbors, Transactions, and Deals): "The active player may negotiate only once with each of their neighbors per turn. After a transaction has been finalized, no other transactions may occur between those players that turn."
- [War Funding (Promissory Note)] A player may play War Funding when the Letnev player has zero or one trade goods. The Letnev player will lose the single trade good, if applicable, and the other effects will resolve as normal. <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (Vidyaraja, BGG, Sep 18, 2017): "You can still use the Letnev promissory note in the event that the Letnev has 1 or 0 trade goods. In that case, as you have guessed, the Letnev loses up to 2 trade goods."
  - Source 5 (sigmazero13, BGG, 2018-01-17): "I’m inclined to say that it is official at this point. This should prevent situations where the Letnev can easily prevent someone from making use of their promissory note."
- [Gravleash Maneuvers (Breakthrough)] If a ship has its movement value increased by an ability such as the Gravity Drive technology, then other ships will have their movement values increased to match the modified value. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (Barony of Letnev): "Q: Can a fast ship have its movement boosted with Gravity Drive, and then have this modified value copied to a slow ship? A: Yes"
- [Non–Euclidean Shielding (Technology)] If there are multiple hits that can be cancelled, then the Letnev player must cancel two hits whenever one of their units uses its Sustain damage ability; they cannot cancel just one. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (non-euclidean-shielding (Community consensus)): "it cancels 2 hits instead of 1"
- [Non–Euclidean Shielding (Technology)] Say the Letnev player has exactly one hit produced against them remaining, and one of their units uses its Sustain damage ability to cancel it. If additional hits are produced against the Letnev player’s units, such as with the Reflective Shielding action card, the Letnev player cannot retroactively use the previous use of Sustain damage to allow Non–Euclidean Shielding to cancel a second hit. <sup>2</sup>
  - Trimmed from: Say the Letnev player has exactly one hit produced against them remaining, and one of their units uses its Sustain damage ability to cancel it. If additional hits are produced against the Letnev player's units, such as with the Reflective Shielding action card, the Letnev player cannot retroactively use the previous use of Sustain damage to allow Non–Euclidean Shielding to cancel a second hit.
  - Source 2 (non-euclidean-shielding (Community consensus)): "Unused cancellation is lost; it doesn't carry over to a later hit such as Devotion's."
- [Rear Admiral Farran (Commander)] If multiple units use their Sustain Damage ability within a single step, the trade goods are gained one at a time. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (letnev-commander-per-sustain (Community consensus)): "Yes — each use triggers it separately."

### F_lizix.php

**Notes kept**

- [Assimilate] If the L1Z1X player would have to place a structure, but there are none of that type left in their reinforcements, they may remove a structure of that type from any system that does not contain one of their command tokens and place that instead. <sup>1,4</sup>
  - Source 1 (23.4a): "When a player would place a unit, if there are none of that type left in their reinforcements, that player can remove a unit from any system that does not contain one of their command tokens and place that unit in their reinforcements."
  - Source 4 (General: keyword "replace"): "Any instance of “replace” can be considered to say “remove and place” if no units are left in reinforcements, and would be covered by Component Limitations in the LRR."
- [Assimilate] If there are none of a structure’s type in their reinforcements, the L1Z1X player is not forced to replace that structure. <sup>1,4</sup>
  - Edited from: The L1Z1X player must mandatorily replace every structure. However, if there are none of that type in their reinforcements they are not forced to do so.
  - Source 1 (23.4a): "Abilities cannot force a player to remove and place a unit in this manner."
  - Source 4 (General: keyword "replace"): "Any instance of “replace” can be considered to say “remove and place” if no units are left in reinforcements, and would be covered by Component Limitations in the LRR."
- [Harrow] The Planetary Shield ability will prevent the use of the Harrow ability on a planet. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (65.2): "The “Planetary Shield” ability prevents an L1Z1X player from using their “Harrow” faction ability."
- [Harrow] The L1Z1X player cannot use their Harrow ability if they are not the active player. <sup>4</sup>
  - Edited from: The L1Z1X player cannot use their Harrow ability if they are not the active player. This will most commonly occur due to the effect of the N’orr player’s commander, G’hom Sek’kus.
  - Source 4 (L1Z1X Mindnet: Harrow): "Q: Can the L1Z1X use harrow when they're defending during ground combat? A: No, only the active player can use BOMBARDMENT."
- [I48S (Agent)] If a player wishes to place a mech, but there are none left in their reinforcements, they may remove a mech from any system that does not contain one of their command tokens and place that instead. The mech will be placed undamaged. <sup>1,4</sup>
  - Source 1 (23.4a): "When a player would place a unit, if there are none of that type left in their reinforcements, that player can remove a unit from any system that does not contain one of their command tokens and place that unit in their reinforcements."
  - Source 4 (General: keyword "replace"): "Any instance of “replace” can be considered to say “remove and place” if no units are left in reinforcements, and would be covered by Component Limitations in the LRR."
  - Source 4 (General: remove and place, damaged units): "If it is produced, placed, or replaced which would require a remove and place it is no longer damaged."
- [The Helmsman — Dark Space Navigation (Hero)] A future rule change will allow a player’s ships to transport units from systems that contain that player’s command token when those ships move outside of a tactical action. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (General: Transport and Movement Abilities (L1Z1X Hero)): "The LRR will be updated to reflect that transportation of units out of systems that contain your command tokens are only applicable during tactical actions. During Movement abilities, you can transport units out of systems that contain your tokens."
- [The Helmsman — Dark Space Navigation (Hero)] Ships moving out of a gravity rift must roll for removal. <sup>1,4</sup>
  - Source 1 (41.2): "For each ship that would move out of or through a gravity rift, one die is rolled immediately before it exits the gravity rift system; on a result of 1–3, that ship is removed from the board."
  - Source 4 (Anomalies): "Any units moving into, through or out of anomalies must follow the same rules for ships moving into, through or out of anomalies."
- [The Helmsman — Dark Space Navigation (Hero)] Ships cannot move into a supernova, even if it contains one of the L1Z1X player’s command tokens. <sup>1,4</sup>
  - Edited from: Ships cannot move into a nebula or supernova, even if it contains one of the L1Z1X player’s command tokens.
  - Source 1 (86.1): "A ship cannot move through or into a supernova."
  - Source 4 (Anomalies): "Any units moving into, through or out of anomalies must follow the same rules for ships moving into, through or out of anomalies."
- [The Helmsman — Dark Space Navigation (Hero)] Dark Space Navigation may be used to move ships into the wormhole nexus. If the nexus is inactive, this will cause it to activate. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (100.2): "After a player moves or places a unit into the wormhole nexus, or gains control of the planet Mallice, that player flips the wormhole nexus to its active side."

**Removed notes restored**

- [Harrow] The L1Z1X player may use the ability of the X–89 Bacterial Weapon Ω or X–89 Bacterial Weapon ΩΩ technologies whenever they bombard. <sup>10,15</sup>
  - Source 10 (Codex I cards, X-89 Bacterial Weapon (Omega)): "After 1 or more of your units use BOMBARDMENT against a planet, if at least 1 of your opponent’s infantry was destroyed, you may destroy all of your opponent’s infantry on that planet."
  - Source 15 (Codex 4.5 technology card updates, X-89 Bacterial Weapon): "Double the hits produced by your units' BOMBARDMENT and ground combat rolls."

  - Source 5 (sigmazero13, BGG, Feb 19, 2018): "The combat ending doesn’t nullify the end of a round of combat trigger. Harrow, in this case, would still resolve."
  - Source 5 (Clipper, BGG, Feb 20, 2018): "2. Harrow goes off (let’s say it destroys he last unit of the enemy) 3. The winner is determined (a draw)"
- [Harrow] During the Bombardment step, each of the L1Z1X player’s units with the Bombardment ability is assigned only one planet to bombard. However, during ground combat, every unit in the system with the Bombardment ability may use it against the planet the ground combat is taking place on. <sup>1,5</sup>
  - Source 1 (15.1): "The active player chooses which planet each of their units that has a “Bombardment” ability will bombard."
  - Source 5 (sigmazero13, BGG, Feb 16, 2018): "Each ship in the system can be part of Harrow."
- [Cybernetic Enhancements (Promissory Note)] If the L1Z1X player has no command tokens in their strategy pool, Cybernetic Enhancements cannot be played. <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (Reddit email ruling, 2019 (latest on this question)): "The command tokens must be present in order to resolve these PNs, as was the understanding before my recent ruling."
  - Source 5 (sigmazero13, BGG, 2018-01-17): "The L1Z1X one however is not (one ability that can’t fully be resolved means that you can’t resolve it)."

  - Source 2 (structures-destroyed-when-planet-taken (Community consensus)): "L1Z1X's Assimilate replaces them instead, and the new dock can produce that same action."

- [The Helmsman — Dark Space Navigation (Hero)] Ships in systems with one of the L1Z1X player’s command tokens may move. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (ability-movement-rules (Community consensus)): "move values, the command-token restriction and other tactical-action movement rules are ignored"
- [The Helmsman — Dark Space Navigation (Hero)] Ships move directly to their destination system. They may only transport units from their origin system. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (heroes-movement-nexus-invasion (Community consensus)): "The ships can carry units starting with them, but can't pick up along a path"
- [The Helmsman — Dark Space Navigation (Hero)] Ships may travel into an asteroid field only if the L1Z1X player owns the Antimass Deflectors technology. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (ability-movement-rules (Community consensus)): "Anomaly rules still apply"
- [Annihilator (Mech)] An Annihilator may bombard when using the L1Z1X player’s Harrow ability if that mech is not currently participating in ground combat, even if it has been committed to a different planet, and has been or will be involved in another ground combat during the current invasion. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (l1z1x-mech-harrow (Community consensus)): "a mech fighting on a planet can't bombard it, but one on another planet in the system can."

- [Salvage Operations (Technology)] If the Mentak player wishes to place a unit using their Salvage Operations ability, but there are none of that type left in their reinforcements, they can remove a unit of that type from any system that does not contain one of their command tokens and place that instead. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (67.5a): "If a player cannot produce a unit because it is not in their reinforcements, that player can remove a unit from any system that does not contain one of their command tokens and place that unit in their reinforcements."
- [Salvage Operations (Technology)] If the opponent has a faction specific ship, including their flagship, destroyed, the Mentak player may use their Salvage Operations to produce a generic ship of the same type, or their Fourth Moon, as appropriate. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (FAQ appendix, The Mentak Coalition (Salvage Operations)): "Yes, even though the units are technically different, they share the flagship unit type."
- [Salvage Operations (Technology)] The Mentak player cannot produce ground forces using Salvage Operations, even if their opponent has the ability to treat a ground force as a ship. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (FAQ appendix, The Mentak Coalition (Salvage Operations)): "No, the infantry do not count as ships once the combat is over."
- [Salvage Operations (Technology)] The Mentak player cannot produce a war sun unless they have their war sun technology. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (FAQ appendix, The Mentak Coalition (Salvage Operations)): "Without war sun technology, they cannot produce a war sun, even using “Salvage Operations.”"
- [Ipswitch, Loose Cannon — Sleeper Cell (Hero)] If all of the Mentak player’s ships are destroyed, they may still place ships with this ability. If they do, combat will continue. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Mentak Coalition, Sleeper Cell): "Yes, after both players assign hits the Mentak player then places a ship from their reinforcements in the active system and combat continues."
- [Ipswitch, Loose Cannon — Sleeper Cell (Hero)] Both players will choose and destroy one of their own ships in the active system for each hit their opponent produced during each round of combat, before the Mentak player places their ships for the Sleeper Cell ability. <sup>4</sup>
  - Edited from: Both players will choose and destroy one of their own ships in the active system for each hit their opponent produced during each round of combat, before the Mentak player places their ships for the Sleeper Cell ability. As such, the Mentak player may place a ship that was destroyed in the same round of combat, if they destroyed one of their opponent’s ships of the same type, even if they had none of that ship type in their reinforcements.
  - Source 4 (Mentak Coalition, Sleeper Cell): "after both players assign hits the Mentak player then places a ship from their reinforcements in the active system"
- [Ipswitch, Loose Cannon — Sleeper Cell (Hero)] If the Mentak player wishes to place a unit with this ability, but there are none of that type left in their reinforcements, they may remove a unit of that type from any system that does not contain one of their command tokens and place that instead. This unit will be placed undamaged. <sup>1,4</sup>
  - Source 1 (23.4a): "When a player would place a unit, if there are none of that type left in their reinforcements, that player can remove a unit from any system that does not contain one of their command tokens and place that unit in their reinforcements."
  - Source 4 (General, damaged unit removed and placed): "If it is produced, placed, or replaced which would require a remove and place it is no longer damaged."
- [Ipswitch, Loose Cannon — Sleeper Cell (Hero)] If the Fourth Moon is destroyed during combat, but the Mentak player then destroys their opponent’s flagship and places the Fourth Moon back into the combat, they cannot score the Unveil Flagship objective. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Mentak Coalition, Unveil Flagship): "No, the wording on Unveil Flagship would prevent you from scoring it since your flagship was destroyed in the combat, regardless of the fact that it returned."
- [Ipswitch, Loose Cannon — Sleeper Cell (Hero)] The Mentak player cannot place a war sun unless they have their war sun technology. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Mentak Coalition, Sleeper Cell war sun): "be used to place a warsun if you do not own the warsun technology? A: No."

**Removed notes restored**

- [Ipswitch, Loose Cannon — Sleeper Cell (Hero)] Capacity is not checked during combat. As such, the Mentak player may place an unlimited number of fighters into a combat with this ability. <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (ti-k0289_learn_to_play_2020_web.txt p.14): "During combat, a player’s fighters and ground forces can exceed their ships’ capacity"
  - Source 3 (ti-k0289_learn_to_play_2020_web.txt p.24): "Players can exceed their ships’ capacity during combat."
- [Pillage] While the agenda phase allows a player to resolve transactions with all other players, it does not make that player neighbors with the Mentak player. <sup>5</sup>
  - Trimmed from: While the agenda phase and the Hacan player’s Trade Convoys promissory note allow a player to resolve transactions with all other players, they do not make that player neighbors with the Mentak player.
  - Source 5 (doc4.txt CreussEmissary, Jan 17, 2019 (Dane)): "Simply being in the agenda phase does not confer neighbor status to all players. In other words, the Mentak can only pillage their actual neighbors"
- [Pillage] If a player would gain multiple trade goods one at a time, the Mentak player can use their Pillage ability for each trade good. <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (doc4.txt sigmazero13, Aug 15, 2018 (Dane)): "This ability triggers for each instance of a neighbor gaining trade goods or resolving a transaction"
- [Pillage] The Mentak player may use their Pillage ability against both players involved in a transaction. <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (doc4.txt sigmazero13, Aug 15, 2018 (Dane)): "so yes, you would be able to steal from both."
- [Salvage Operations (Technology)] If the space combat ends in a draw, Salvage Operations has no effect. <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (doc4.txt Skootur, 1/25/2019 (Dane)): "A draw is neither a win nor a loss. In both cases, Salvage Operations is not triggered."
- [Corsair (Unit)] The Nekro player cannot place a Valefar token on the Corsair card. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (doc5.txt The Mentak Coalition): "Can Nekro copy Corsair from Mentak? ... A: They cannot copy corsair"
- [Ambush] Game effects that reroll, modify, or otherwise affect combat rolls do not affect dice rolls made when resolving the Ambush ability. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (mentak-ambush-details (Community consensus)): "It isn't a combat roll, so Morale Boost doesn't apply"
- [Pillage] The Mentak player may use their Pillage ability even if the transaction does not involve trade goods. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (mentak-pillage-triggers (Community consensus)): "After each instance of a neighbor gaining trade goods or resolving a transaction, if that neighbor then has 3 or more trade goods"
- [Pillage] If the Mentak player resolves a transaction with another player, they may then use their Pillage ability against that player. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (mentak-pillage-limits (Designer ruling)): "Pillage triggers separately each time a neighbor gains trade goods or resolves a transaction and ends with 3 or more"
- [Promise of Protection (Promissory Note)] If the player with Promise of Protection in their play area resolves a transaction with another player, the Mentak player may still use their Pillage ability on that other player. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (mentak-pillage-triggers (Community consensus)): "if that neighbor then has 3 or more trade goods and no face-up Promise of Protection. Both sides of a transaction between two neighbors can each be pillaged"
- [Promise of Protection (Promissory Note)] Promise of Protection has no effect while it is in a player’s hand. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (unplayed-note-ignores-return-condition (Community consensus)): "But it also doesn't protect you from Pillage until it is face up in your play area."
- [Mirror Computing (Technology)] If an effect specifically requires that trade goods are spent (for example, the Negotiate Trade Routes objective), Mirror Computing does not increase the value of those trade goods. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (mirror-computing-trade-goods (Community consensus)): "still 1 when spent as trade goods, so Bribery and objectives that spend trade goods get no bonus."
- [S’ula Mentarion (Commander)] The Mentak player’s opponent chooses which promissory note they give to the Mentak player. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (target-chooses-promissory-note (Community consensus)): "The target does; the other player can't look at or name a specific note."
- [Ipswitch, Loose Cannon — Sleeper Cell (Hero)] The opponent may still retreat during combat. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (mentak-hero-mid-combat (Community consensus)): "The opponent can limit it by retreating, or escape before any losses with Skilled Retreat"

**Notes added** (rulings that were not on the site before)

- [Pillage] The Mentak player may use their Pillage ability each time the Saar player gains a trade good from their Scavenge faction ability during a single turn, if all of the conditions of Pillage are met. <sup>1</sup>

  - Source 2 (mentak-ambush-and-fourth-moon (Community consensus)): "those ships still roll normally from the first round"

**Restored without a source** (marked * on the site)

- [Ambush] If a cruiser or destroyer is removed before the Mentak player can resolve their Ambush ability, that ship cannot be one of the ships used when they do resolve their Ambush ability. <sup>*</sup>
- [Pillage] Effects that force players to give objects to other players are not transactions. <sup>*</sup>
- [Pillage] If Alice plays Bob’s Trade Agreement promissory note, then the Mentak player may use Pillage on Alice, but not Bob. <sup>*</sup>
- [Pillage] The Mentak player does not decide to use their Pillage ability until after the transaction has been resolved. Any deal made to not use their Pillage ability before the transaction has been resolved is non–binding. <sup>*</sup>
- [Promise of Protection (Promissory Note)] Promise of Protection is returned when the system is activated, even if the active player will perform no hostile acts towards the Mentak player this turn. <sup>*</sup>
- [Promise of Protection (Promissory Note)] Activating a system containing only the Mentak player’s structures will still cause Promise of Protection to be returned. <sup>*</sup>
- [Promise of Protection (Promissory Note)] If an effect other than activating a system during a tactical action places a command counter in a system with the Mentak player’s units (for example, the primary ability of the Diplomacy strategy card), this will not cause Promise of Protection to be returned. <sup>*</sup>
- [S’ula Mentarion (Commander)] Giving a promissory note because of S’ula Mentarion is not resolving a transaction. <sup>*</sup>
- [S’ula Mentarion (Commander)] If the Mentak player resolves their Salvage Operations to place their fourth cruiser faction technology after winning a space combat, they cannot use the ability of S’ula Mentarion from winning that combat. <sup>*</sup>
- [S’ula Mentarion (Commander)] If the Mentak player places their fourth cruiser during combat, such as by the effect of Sleeper Cell, they may unlock and use the ability of S’ula Mentarion at the end of that combat, should they win. <sup>*</sup>
- [S’ula Mentarion (Commander)] The four cruisers need not survive until the end of combat; S’ula Mentarion is unlocked from the placement of the fourth cruiser on the game board. <sup>*</sup>
- [Ipswitch, Loose Cannon — Sleeper Cell (Hero)] The Mentak player can trigger the Sleeper Cell ability, their Ambush ability, or any other “at the start of a space combat” abilities they have in any order. <sup>*</sup>
- [Ipswitch, Loose Cannon — Sleeper Cell (Hero)] If ships are destroyed before the Sleeper Cell ability is triggered, the Mentak player cannot place those units. <sup>*</sup>
- [Ipswitch, Loose Cannon — Sleeper Cell (Hero)] No costs are paid for the placed units. <sup>*</sup>
- [Ipswitch, Loose Cannon — Sleeper Cell (Hero)] When players would use their ships’ Sustain Damage abilities, they do so in alternating order, starting with the attacker. If the Mentak player uses a Direct Hit action card to destroy one of their opponent’s ships, they must then make the choice immediately if they will replace it using the Sleeper Cell ability, before any other ships may use their Sustain Damage ability. Should the Mentak version of the newly placed ship type have a Sustain Damage ability, it may then use it during the same combat round. <sup>*</sup>
- [Ipswitch, Loose Cannon — Sleeper Cell (Hero)] If the Mentak player starts the combat without the Fourth Moon, and places it during the combat, they may score the Unveil Flagship objective if the Fourth Moon is not destroyed. <sup>*</sup>
- [Ipswitch, Loose Cannon — Sleeper Cell (Hero)] If a destroyed unit is a ground force or structure, that the other player is treating as a ship due to some effect, the Mentak player cannot place that unit. <sup>*</sup>
- [Moll Terminus (Mech)] If a player commits a mech to a planet that contains both a Moll Terminus mech and a PDS belonging to the Mentak player, then the committed mech cannot use its Sustain Damage ability to cancel any Space Cannon hits during that invasion. <sup>*</sup>
- [Corsair (Unit)] If the active system contains a non–Mentak player’s units, the Mentak player may move a Corsair through systems containing any other player’s ships, not just those of the player in the active system. <sup>*</sup>
- [Corsair (Unit)] The ability of the Corsair may be triggered even if the Mentak player has some of their own units in the active system. <sup>*</sup>

- [Adjudicator Ba’al — Nova Seed (Hero)] Nova Seed purges all tokens on the replaced system tile other than command tokens and frontier tokens. Any faction–specific tokens, such as Creuss wormhole tokens or Ul sleeper tokens, are returned to the player that owns them instead. <sup>4</sup>

**Restored without a source** (marked * on the site)

- [Star Forge] The Muaat player cannot use Star Forge if the do not have a war sun on the game board. <sup>*</sup>
- [Magmus Reactor (Technology)] The war sun must be in the system prior to the use of Production to gain the trade good. <sup>*</sup>
- [Magmus Reactor (Technology)] The trade good is gained after the use of Production; it cannot be used to pay for the produced units. <sup>*</sup>
- [Magmus Reactor Ω (Technology)] If the Muaat player has a unit in a system containing a supernova, they cannot be eliminated. <sup>*</sup>
- [Umbat (Agent)] If ground forces are produced, they may be placed in the space area or on a planet the player controls in the system with their war sun or flagship. <sup>*</sup>
- [Umbat (Agent)] If the Naalu or Yin players are chosen, and choose to produce fighters or infantry, they will only be able to produce two of those units; their commander will have no effect. <sup>*</sup>
- [Umbat (Agent)] If the Regulated Conscription law is in play, then that player may use their commander to produce two units for one resource when resolving Umbat. <sup>*</sup>
- [Magmus (Commander)] When a command token is spent to resolve the secondary ability of a strategy card, the trade good is gained after resolving the secondary ability. As such, it cannot be spent to pay for costs of the secondary ability. <sup>*</sup>
- [Magmus (Commander)] If the Muaat player spends multiple tokens from their strategy pool (e.g. for the Lead From the Front objective), they gain that many trade goods, one at a time. <sup>*</sup>
- [Magmus (Commander)] Each trade good gained may trigger the Mentak player’s Pillage faction ability. <sup>*</sup>
- [Magmus (Commander)] If the Muaat player wishes to score Lead From the Front and Form a Spy Network during the one status phase, they must do so simultaneously, and both happen before the Mentak player may use their Pillage faction ability. If the Mentak player subsequently uses their agent, Suffi An, when they use their Pillage faction ability on the trade goods the Muaat player gained from Magmus when spending the tokens for Lead From the Front, then the Muaat player cannot discard the drawn action card for Form a Spy Network. <sup>*</sup>
- [Magmus (Commander)] If the Muaat player uses the ability of the Scepter of Emelpar relic, they will be unable to benefit from the ability of Magmus. <sup>*</sup>
- [Magmus (Commander)] The Muaat player must have Magmus unlocked before spending the strategy token in order to gain the trade good. <sup>*</sup>
- [Magmus (Commander)] For example, if the Muaat player spends a strategy token to follow the secondary ability of the Warfare strategy card, and in doing so produces the war sun that unlocks Magmus, they will not gain the trade good from spending that strategy token. <sup>*</sup>
- [Adjudicator Ba’al — Nova Seed (Hero)] Any method of movement is sufficient to trigger this ability, not only tactical action movement. For example, the Muaat player may trigger Nova Seed when they retreat. <sup>*</sup>
- [Adjudicator Ba’al — Nova Seed (Hero)] If the Mahact player moves the Muaat player’s war sun via the use of their Benediction hero ability, the Muaat player cannot trigger Nova Seed. <sup>*</sup>
- [Adjudicator Ba’al — Nova Seed (Hero)] If the war sun is in the target system when it is activated, it must move out of the system, and back in, for Nova Seed to be able to be triggered. <sup>*</sup>
- [Adjudicator Ba’al — Nova Seed (Hero)] If the Muaat player owns Magmus Reactor Ω, and resolves this ability during a tactical action, they will be able to produce units during the Production step, if the Muaat player still has units in the system. <sup>*</sup>
- [Adjudicator Ba’al — Nova Seed (Hero)] Nova Seed cannot target the home system of an eliminated player. <sup>*</sup>
- [Adjudicator Ba’al — Nova Seed (Hero)] Nova Seed may target the Creuss Gate (tile 17) or the Wormhole Nexus (tile 82). <sup>*</sup>
- [Adjudicator Ba’al — Nova Seed (Hero)] The Empyrean player cannot use the ability of their agent, Acamar, on the Muaat player after they use Nova Seed if the original system tile contained planets. <sup>*</sup>
- [Stellar Genesis (Breakthrough)] The Muaat player explores Avernus when they gain it. <sup>*</sup>
- [Stellar Genesis (Breakthrough)] The Muaat player may move Avernus even if another player controls it. <sup>*</sup>
- [Stellar Genesis (Breakthrough)] Avernus may be moved into a system containing another player’s units. <sup>*</sup>
- [Stellar Genesis (Breakthrough)] Structures may be placed on Avernus. <sup>*</sup>
- [Stellar Genesis (Breakthrough)] Any PDS (or other relevant unit) on Avernus may use its Space Cannon ability during the movement step of the same tactical action the planet is moved. <sup>*</sup>
- [Stellar Genesis (Breakthrough)] Any of the Muaat player’s space docks (or other relevant units) on Avernus may use its Production ability during the production step of the same tactical action the planet is moved. <sup>*</sup>
- [Avernus — The Nucleus (Legendary Planet)] If the Muaat player uses The Nucleus, they will not gain a trade good from the ability of their commander, Magmus. <sup>*</sup>
- [Avernus — The Nucleus (Legendary Planet)] If the Muaat player uses The Nucleus, they will still place infantry with their adjacent mechs. <sup>*</sup>
- [Avernus — The Nucleus (Legendary Planet)] If another player controls Avernus, they may use The Nucleus only if they have a war sun on the game board. <sup>*</sup>

**Notes kept**

- [Telepathic] The Naalu player retains the Naalu 0 token, even if an effect such as the Imperial Arbiter law causes them to lose the strategy card it was on. The Naalu player will place the Naalu 0 token on another strategy card in this scenario. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (FAQ (Naalu Collective), p.44): "No. The Naalu “0” token stays with the Naalu or the faction that gained the token through the “Gift of Prescience” promissory note and is placed on any of that player’s strategy cards."
- [Foresight] Ground forces may be transported. <sup>1</sup>
  - Edited from: Fighters are moved without being transported. Ground forces may be transported.
  - Source 1 (FAQ (General), p.41): "Any effect that moves a ship allows that ship to transport units in its system, if it has available capacity."
- [Gift of Prescience (Promissory Note)] The player with Gift of Prescience retains the Naalu 0 token, even if an effect such as the Imperial Arbiter law causes them to lose the strategy card it was on. That player will place the Naalu 0 token on another strategy card in this scenario. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (FAQ (Naalu Collective), p.44): "No. The Naalu “0” token stays with the Naalu or the faction that gained the token through the “Gift of Prescience” promissory note and is placed on any of that player’s strategy cards."
- [Matriarch (Flagship)] The committed fighters are returned to the space area when combat ends, and thus will not be on the planet for the Establish Control step. If the Naalu player does not commit at least one ground force to a planet and have it survive the combat, they will be unable to gain control of that planet, and the ground combat will end in a draw. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (FAQ (Naalu Collective), p.44): "No. The Naalu fighters return to the space area when ground combat ends. If no Naalu ground forces are present, the combat is considered to be a draw, and the Naalu do not gain control of the planet during the “Establish Control” step."
- [Matriarch (Flagship)] The Daxcive Animators technology will not allow the Naalu player to gain control of a planet without committing a ground force. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (FAQ (Naalu Collective), p.44): "No. Because the combat ends in a draw, the “Dacxive Animators” ability is not triggered."
- [Z’eu Ω (Agent)] The chosen player is considered to be the active player. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Naalu Collective, Z’eu Omega): "effectively makes them the active player for the duration of the tactical action"
- [Z’eu Ω (Agent)] If the chosen player is not the Naalu player, it is not considered their turn for game effects. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Naalu Collective, Z’eu Omega): "This DOES NOT count as the tactical action player’s turn"
- [Z’eu Ω (Agent)] If the chosen player is not the Naalu player, they cannot use the Fleet Logistics technology to perform an additional action. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Naalu Collective, Z’eu Omega): "so they cannot utilize fleet logistics"
- [Z’eu Ω (Agent)] The chosen player may use the Master Plan action card or the Minister of War agenda to perform an additional action. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Naalu Collective, Z’eu Omega): "however they could use Master Plan or the Minister of War, as these reference actions and not a player’s turn."
- [Z’eu Ω (Agent)] Any deal between the Naalu player and another player regarding which system will be activated, if made before Z’eu Ω is exhausted, is non–binding. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (28.4): "If the terms of a deal cannot be resolved immediately, it is a non-binding deal."
- [M’aban (Commander)] The Naalu player may choose to produce one fighter for one resource. If they do, they may produce one additional fighter. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Naalu Collective, M’aban): "both of these commanders allow the player to choose to only build a single fighter/infantry for 1 resource and gain an additional unit of that type each time they do."
- [M’aban Ω (Commander)] When the Covert Legislation agenda is revealed during the agenda phase, the Naalu player cannot look at the hidden agenda. <sup>4</sup>
  - Edited from: When the Covert Legislation agenda is revealed during the agenda phase, the Naalu player cannot look at the hidden agenda. Once the speaker has read the hidden agenda, the Naalu player may look at the next card of the agenda deck.
  - Source 4 (Naalu Collective, M’aban Omega): "cannot look at the next card when Covert Legislation is revealed before the speaker draws the top card of the agenda deck."
- [M’aban Ω (Commander)] The Naalu player cannot look at the agenda deck while a player is resolving the primary ability of the Politics strategy card. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Naalu Collective, M’aban Omega): "It also cannot be used to interrupt the primary ability of the Politics strategy card."

**Removed notes restored**

- [Z’eu Ω (Agent)] All other rules applying to tactical actions apply, other than placing a command token. <sup>12</sup>
  - Source 12 (ti_codex_volume_3_vigil_v2_1-compressed.txt p.14, Z’eu card): "that player may perform a tactical action in a non-home system without placing a command token; that system still counts as being activated."
- [Z’eu Ω (Agent)] If a player uses Z’eu Ω to activate a system containing another player’s units, that will count for the purposes of returning promissory notes, and other similar effects. <sup>12</sup>
  - Source 12 (ti_codex_volume_3_vigil_v2_1-compressed.txt p.14, Z’eu card): "that system still counts as being activated."
- [Iconoclast Ω (Mech)] The ability will apply regardless of if the Iconoclast is in the space area or on a planet in the system. <sup>12</sup>
  - Source 12 (ti_codex_volume_3_vigil_v2_1-compressed.txt p.14, Iconoclast card): "Other players cannot use ANTI-FIGHTER BARRAGE against your units in this system."
- [Foresight] If the destination system already contains one of the Naalu player’s command tokens, the command token from the Naalu player’s strategy pool is instead placed in their reinforcements. <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (doc4.txt, JamesG, Jan 19, 2018): "If the answer is Yes, then I assume for Foresight the Naalu player still takes a command token from the their Strategy Pool but they place it in their reinforcements instead of on the map."
  - Source 5 (doc4.txt, JamesG, Jan 19, 2018): "Dane's Answer: That is correct."
- [Foresight] After resolving Foresight, play continues to the Space Cannon Offense step. <sup>5</sup>
  - Trimmed from: After resolving Foresight, play continues to the Space Cannon Offense step. Only the active player’s ships in the active system may be assigned hits.
  - Source 5 (doc4.txt, sigmazero13, Dec 8, 2017): "that is correct, you would trigger foresight before Space Cannon Offense."
- [Matriarch (Flagship)] Any structures on the planet will not be destroyed if the Naalu player committed no ground forces. <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (doc4.txt, sigmazero13, Sep 17, 2018): "Personally, I would say that the invading fighters are never "contained" by the planet, they are just participating in combat."
  - Source 5 (doc4.txt, sigmazero13, Sep 17, 2018): "Dane: The Space dock would not be destroyed, in this instance, for the reason you have stated."
- [Foresight] Using Foresight is not a retreat. As such, it cannot be cancelled with the Intercept action card. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (naalu-foresight-timing-and-destinations (Community consensus)): "Intercept doesn't stop it, as it isn't a combat retreat."
- [M’aban (Commander)] When producing units, the Naalu player must produce all the units they intend to produce before they may unlock M’aban. M’aban cannot be applied to the instance of producing the units that unlocks it. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (naalu-commander-mid-production (Community consensus)): "No — production is one step, so the unlock condition is only met after it finishes; use the commander from your next production."
- [M’aban (Commander)] For example, before production, the Naalu player has ten fighters on the game board. They pay two resources during production. They cannot produce two fighters, unlock M’aban, then produce three more fighters. Instead, they would produce all four fighters, and then unlock M’aban. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (naalu-commander-mid-production (Community consensus)): "No — production is one step, so the unlock condition is only met after it finishes"
- [The Oracle — C–Radium Geometry (Hero)] Each other player chooses which promissory note they give the Naalu player. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (promissory-notes-in-hand (Community consensus)): "With the Naalu hero, each player chooses which note to give."

**Notes added** (rulings that were not on the site before)

- [Z’eu Ω (Agent)] The Minister of Peace agenda and the Mahact player’s Starlancer mech still end the chosen player’s turn, even though it is not considered their turn. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Factions/Naalu Collective): "Minister of Peace and the Mahact Gene-Sorcerers mech, Starlancer ends the turn of the tactical action player, regardless of referencing a “turn”."
- [Matriarch (Flagship)] The text of the Matriarch is changed to: “During an invasion in this system, you may commit fighters to planets as if they were ground forces. When combat ends, return those units to the space area.” <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (Errata: Matriarch): "During an invasion in this system, you may commit fighters to planets as if they were ground forces."
- [Telepathic] Placing the Naalu 0 token is mandatory, unless the Naalu player has given it to another player with their Gift of Prescience promissory note. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (naalu-zero-token-mandatory (Community consensus)): "Yes — Telepathic has no 'may', so the Naalu always go first in initiative unless they've given the token away with Gift of Prescience."
- [Foresight] There is no limit on the number of times Foresight may be used each round, as long as the Naalu player has command tokens in their strategy pool. Foresight cannot be used if another player’s ships only move through the system that contains the Naalu player’s ships. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (naalu-foresight-limits (Community consensus)): "there is no per-round limit"
- [Foresight] The Naalu player may use Foresight to move their ships into a system that contains another player’s structures but no ships, but cannot commit ground forces to planets in that system. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (naalu-foresight-timing-and-destinations (Community consensus)): "including the one the attacker just vacated or one with only enemy structures, but can't land ground forces there"
- [Matriarch (Flagship)] Fighters committed to a planet use their own combat value, including that of any fighter unit upgrade. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (naalu-fighters-in-ground-combat-values (Community consensus)): "Their own fighter combat value, upgrades included"
- [Iconoclast Ω (Mech)] Other players do not roll any anti–fighter barrage dice in the system. Effects that trigger from Anti–Fighter Barrage, such as the Argent player’s Raid Formation faction ability, do not trigger. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (naalu-iconoclast-omega-afb (Community consensus)): "no dice are rolled and effects tied to it, like Argent's, don't trigger"

**Restored without a source** (marked * on the site)

- [Foresight] The command token is not spent. The Naalu player cannot use the Scepter of Emelpar, nor will they gain a trade good if they have the Muuat player’s Alliance promissory note. <sup>*</sup>
- [Foresight] If all ships are removed, the strategy token will still be placed in the destination system. <sup>*</sup>
- [Neuroglaive (Technology)] If the Mahact player only has other players’ command tokens in their fleet pool when they trigger Neuroglaive, they must return one of those command tokens to that player’s reinforcements. <sup>*</sup>
- [Matriarch (Flagship)] The committed fighters may be assigned hits during the Space Cannon Defense step. <sup>*</sup>
- [Z’eu Ω (Agent)] The system cannot already contain a command token for the player performing the tactical action. <sup>*</sup>
- [Z’eu Ω (Agent)] A player may play a Ceasefire promissory note or discard the Minister of Peace law for their effects. <sup>*</sup>
- [Z’eu Ω (Agent)] If the Yssaril player is chosen, and owns their Transparasteel Plating faction technology, other players may still play action cards during the action. <sup>*</sup>
- [Z’eu Ω (Agent)] If the chosen player is not the Naalu player, they may use any “before/after you perform an action” abilities. <sup>*</sup>
- [Z’eu Ω (Agent)] If the chosen player is able to perform a component action, they may then use the ability of Suffi An, the Keleres commander, to perform additional actions. <sup>*</sup>
- [Z’eu Ω (Agent)] If the chosen player is not the Naalu player, and they had previously passed, they are still considered passed during their action. They do not pass at the end of the action. <sup>*</sup>
- [Z’eu Ω (Agent)] The chosen player cannot score the Prove Endurance secret objective at the end of their action. <sup>*</sup>
- [Z’eu Ω (Agent)] If the Yssaril player owns their Transparasteel Plating faction technology, and uses the ability of Ssruu, their agent, to duplicate the ability of Z’eu Ω, choosing a player that has passed, the chosen player cannot play action cards during their action. <sup>*</sup>
- [Z’eu ΩΩ (Agent)] Z’eu ΩΩ may be used whenever a command token is placed in a system. For example, it may be used when a player activates a system, when a player resolves the primary ability of the Diplomacy strategy card, or when a player resolves the Signal Jamming action card. <sup>*</sup>
- [M’aban (Commander)] If the Regulated Conscription law is in play, the Naalu player may produce two fighters for one resource. This will count one towards their Production limit. <sup>*</sup>
- [M’aban (Commander)] If a game effect instructs the Naalu player to produce ships without using the Production ability, they may only produce additional fighters if that game effect allows them to produce fighters. <sup>*</sup>
- [Iconoclast (Mech)] The +1 will not apply to an opponent who has a relic but zero relic fragments. <sup>*</sup>
- [Iconoclast ΩΩ (Mech)] The Naalu player must mandatorily place a mech when another player gains a relic, if they have at least one in their reinforcements. <sup>*</sup>
- [Mindsieve (Breakthrough)] The Naalu player may only give promissory notes from their hand; they cannot give promissory notes that are in their play area. <sup>*</sup>
- [Mindsieve (Breakthrough)] Giving a promissory note because of Mindsieve is not resolving a transaction. <sup>*</sup>

### F_naaz_rokha.php

**Notes kept**

- [Distant Suns] The Naaz–Rokha player must choose to use this ability before seeing the first exploration card. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Naaz-Rokha, Distant Suns): "Before the initial exploration card is drawn."
- [Fabrication] If the relic deck is empty, the Naaz–Rokha player may still purge two relic fragments as an action. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Exploration): "Yes you can purge relic fragments and not gain a relic if there are none left in the deck."
- [Fabrication] If the Naaz–Rokha player has no command tokens in their reinforcements, they may still purge one relic fragment as an action. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Naaz-Rokha): "Yes, you can purge the fragment and not gain a command token if there are none in reinforcements."
- [Black Market Forgery (Promissory Note)] If there are no cards in the relic deck, a player cannot gain a relic. <sup>1,4</sup>
  - Edited from: If there are no cards in the relic deck, a player cannot gain a relic. As such, a player cannot play Black Market Forgery when the relic deck is empty.
  - Source 1 (73.2a): "If there are no cards in the relic deck, they do not gain a relic."
  - Source 4 (Exploration): "Yes you can purge relic fragments and not gain a relic if there are none left in the deck."
- [Supercharge (Technology)] Supercharge does not modify anti–fighter barrage, bombardment or space cannon rolls. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (10.1c): "Game effects that reroll, modify, or otherwise affect combat rolls do not affect anti-fighter barrage rolls."
  - Source 1 (15.1c): "Game effects that reroll, modify, or otherwise affect combat rolls do not affect bombardment rolls."
  - Source 1 (77.3d): "Game effects that reroll, modify, or otherwise affect combat rolls do not affect space cannon rolls."
- [Hesh and Prit — Perfect Synthesis (Hero)] If the Naaz–Rokha player has no command tokens in their reinforcements, they must use a command token from their command sheet when performing the secondary ability of the strategy cards. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Naaz-Rokha, Hesh and Prit): "The LRR will be updated to be more general towards taking off sheet if none are in reinforcements."

- [Pre–Fab Arcologies (Technology)] The planet is not readied until after the planet is explored. <sup>2</sup>
  - Trimmed from: The planet is not readied until after the planet is explored. If the Freelancers exploration card is revealed, then:

  - Source 2 (winnu-and-naaz-rokha-heroes-secondaries (Community consensus)): "The Naaz-Rokha hero resolves the secondaries of up to two readied or unchosen cards"
- [Eidolon /Z–Grav Eidolon (Mech)] If the Naaz–Rokha player had an Eidolon in the space area of the active system, they must mandatorily use its ability to convert it to a Z–Grav Eidolon. <sup>2</sup>

- [Eidolon /Z–Grav Eidolon (Mech)] The mech flips at the start of space combat, resolved in the normal player order for abilities at that timing. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (The Naaz-Rokha Alliance / Z-Grav Eidolon): "Mech Flips at start of Space Combat in player order timing."

**Restored without a source** (marked * on the site)

- [Distant Suns] If the Naaz–Rokha player has multiple Eidolon on the planet they explore, they will draw only one additional exploration card. <sup>*</sup>
- [Distant Suns] If a planet has multiple traits, the additional exploration card must come from the same deck as the first. <sup>*</sup>
- [Fabrication] Either or both of the relic fragments may be Unknown Relic Fragments. <sup>*</sup>
- [Black Market Forgery (Promissory Note)] Either or both of the relic fragments may be Unknown Relic Fragments. <sup>*</sup>
- [Pre–Fab Arcologies (Technology)] If the planet was exhausted before the exploration, its influence or resources cannot be spent to produce the unit. <sup>*</sup>
- [Pre–Fab Arcologies (Technology)] If the planet was readied before the exploration, its influence or resources may be spent to produce the unit by exhausting it. After the unit is produced, the planet will then be readied. <sup>*</sup>
- [Visz El Vir (Flagship)] Each mech will roll an additional die. <sup>*</sup>
- [Visz El Vir (Flagship)] The Visz El Vir ability applies to both Eidolon and Z–Grav Eidolon. <sup>*</sup>
- [Hesh and Prit — Perfect Synthesis (Hero)] The Naaz–Rokha player cannot choose the same strategy card twice. <sup>*</sup>
- [Hesh and Prit — Perfect Synthesis (Hero)] The Naaz–Rokha player must choose which strategy cards they will perform the secondary abilities of before they resolve any of those abilities. <sup>*</sup>
- [Hesh and Prit — Perfect Synthesis (Hero)] When resolving the abilities of two strategy cards, they may be resolved in either order. Game objects affected by the first strategy card ability may be affected by the second. <sup>*</sup>
- [Hesh and Prit — Perfect Synthesis (Hero)] For example, say the Naaz–Rokha player chooses to resolve the secondary abilities of the Diplomacy and Warfare strategy cards. They may resolve the Diplomacy ability first to ready some planets, then exhaust those same planets to pay for the units they produce with the Warfare ability. Alternatively, they may resolve the Warfare ability first, exhausting some of their readied planets to pay for the units they produce, then resolve the Diplomacy ability to ready those same planets. <sup>*</sup>
- [Hesh and Prit — Perfect Synthesis (Hero)] If a player is eliminated, the strategy cards that they had are considered “unchosen”. <sup>*</sup>
- [Hesh and Prit — Perfect Synthesis (Hero)] If the Naaz–Rokha player has the Muaat player’s Alliance promissory note, they will not gain a trade good from it when they use their Perfect Synthesis ability. <sup>*</sup>
- [Eidolon /Z–Grav Eidolon (Mech)] The Naaz–Rokha mechs are only Z–Grav Eidolon during the Space Combat step, only in the active system, and only in the space area. <sup>*</sup>
- [Eidolon /Z–Grav Eidolon (Mech)] If the Naaz–Rokha player owns the Assault Cannon technology, they may count their Z–Grav Eidolon towards the three non–fighter ships, once they resolve its ability. However, if another player then resolves an ability that reduces the number of non–ships the Naaz–Rokha player has in the active system to less than three, the Naaz–Rokha player will no longer be able to resolve the Assault Cannon technology ability. <sup>*</sup>
- [Eidolon /Z–Grav Eidolon (Mech)] Any effect that may target ships or non–fighter ships may target a Z–Grav Eidolon. <sup>*</sup>
- [Eidolon /Z–Grav Eidolon (Mech)] A Z–Grav Eidolon is still a ground force and a mech. <sup>*</sup>
- [Eidolon /Z–Grav Eidolon (Mech)] A Z–Grav Eidolon participating in a space combat may count towards scoring the Demonstrate Your Power secret objective. <sup>*</sup>
- [Absolute Synergy (Breakthrough)] The four mechs can be anywhere in the same system; they need not be all on the same planet, and some or all may be in the space area. <sup>*</sup>
- [Absolute Synergy (Breakthrough)] The mechs may be removed and the card flipped as soon as the four mechs are in the same system. For example, this may be done before space combat starts. <sup>*</sup>
- [Eidolon Maximum (Mech)] When in the space area of a system, the Eidolon Maximum counts towards either of the Naaz–Rokha player’s capacity or fleet pool in that system. <sup>*</sup>
- [Eidolon Maximum (Mech)] If hits are produced by unit abilities against a group of the Naaz–Rokha player’s units that includes the Eidolon Maximum, then these hits must be assigned to the other eligible units in that group, if possible. <sup>*</sup>
- [Eidolon Maximum (Mech)] The Eidolon Maximum only repairs during combats that it is participating in. <sup>*</sup>
- [Eidolon Maximum (Mech)] The Eidolon Maximum is considered a mech for all relevant game effects, such as rolling an additional dice from the effect of the Visz El Vir. <sup>*</sup>
- [Eidolon Maximum (Mech)] The Eidolon Maximum may be destroyed by a Direct Hit action card whenever it uses its Sustain Damage ability, including if it does so during a ground combat. <sup>*</sup>

**Removed notes that the site already covers elsewhere**

- [Eidolon /Z–Grav Eidolon (Mech)] All other players will have the opportunity to resolve an ability between the Naaz–Rokha player resolving their Eidolon ability and any other ability. _(no source)_
  - Covered by [F_naaz_rokha.php](F_naaz_rokha.php) [Eidolon / Z–Grav Eidolon (Mech)]: The mech flips at the start of space combat, resolved in the normal player order for abilities at that timing.
- [Eidolon /Z–Grav Eidolon (Mech)] When a Z–Grav Eidolon reverts back to an Eidolon at the end of combat, it will count towards capacity in the active system. Capacity limits must be met before proceeding to the Invasion step. _(no source)_
  - Covered by [R_capacity.php](R_capacity.php) [Rules Reference]: A player’s fighters and ground forces do not count against capacity during combat. At the end of combat, any excess units are removed.

**Notes removed**

- [Eidolon Maximum (Mech)] The Naaz–Rokha player can never have two or more Eidolon Maximums on the game board. _(no source)_ _(kept out: contradicted by sourced CC item on page: additional Eidolon Maximums may be placed while Articles of War is in play)_
