**Restored without a source** (marked * on the site)

- [Galactic Threat] If the Nekro player has the Xxcha player’s Alliance promissory note, the Nekro player may vote, without losing their ability to predict outcomes for their Galactic Threat ability. <sup>*</sup>
- [Technology Singularity] If the Nekro player gains a technology during a space combat, this does not prevent them from gaining technology during ground combats in the Invasion step of the same tactical action. <sup>*</sup>
- [Technology Singularity] If multiple ground combats happen on separate planets as part of a single Invasion step during one action, the Nekro player may gain a technology during each combat. <sup>*</sup>
- [Technology Singularity] If a unit is removed, but not destroyed, that unit will not trigger the Technology Singularity ability. <sup>*</sup>
- [Technology Singularity] The combat value of a combat dice is fixed as it is rolled, and all combat dice are rolled before any hits are assigned. Gaining a unit upgrade technology will not cause any already rolled combat dice to produce any additional hits due to an improved combat value. The same applies to unit ability dice. <sup>*</sup>
- [Technology Singularity] Destroying an opponent’s unit during the Anti–Fighter Barrage step, and gaining a unit upgrade technology will allow units of that type to use the abilities and attributes of the upgrade for the combat rolls of the same round. <sup>*</sup>
- [Technology Singularity] Destroying an opponent’s unit at the start of a combat, such as with the ability of the Assault Cannon technology, and gaining a unit upgrade technology with an Anti–Fighter Barrage ability will allow units of that type to use that ability during the Anti–Fighter Barrage step of the first round of combat. <sup>*</sup>
- [Technology Singularity] If the Nekro player uses the Direct Hit action card to destroy a unit when it uses its Sustain Damage ability, this will occur before any units are destroyed from being assigned hits. If the Nekro player then gains a technology that gives their units the Sustain Damage ability, they may then use that ability for their units participating in the combat to cancel hits produced by their opponent during that round of combat. <sup>*</sup>
- [Technology Singularity] For example, if the Nekro player uses the ability of the Assault Cannon technology at the start of a space combat to destroy a unit belonging to the Creuss player, and thus place a Valefar token on that player’s Dimensional Splicer faction technology, the Nekro player may immediately use the ability of their Valefar Dimensional Splicer to produce a hit against one of the Creuss player’s ships. <sup>*</sup>
- [Technology Singularity] If the Nekro player gains the Infantry II unit upgrade from their Technology Singularity ability during a combat, any of the Nekro player’s infantry destroyed at the same time as the unit used to trigger the Technology Singularity ability will be returned to their reinforcements. <sup>*</sup>
- [Technology Singularity] If the Nekro player uses a Direct Hit action card to destroy an opponent’s unit, and gain the Infantry II unit upgrade, then any infantry destroyed in that Assign Hits step will roll to be placed on the Infantry II card. This will most commonly occur if the Nekro player has infantry participating in space combat via the ability of their flagship, The Alastor. <sup>*</sup>
- [Technology Singularity] Any infantry destroyed by the Argent player’s Strike Wing Alpha II faction unit ability are destroyed during the Roll Dice substep of the Anti–Fighter Barrage step. The Nekro player will not have the opportunity to gain the Infantry II unit upgrade until the Assign Hits substep immediately following, and so the destroyed infantry will be returned to their reinforcements. <sup>*</sup>
- [Propagation] The Nekro player may still benefit from owning the Minister of Sciences agenda card. <sup>*</sup>
- [Propagation] If an ability triggers “when” a player researches a technology, that ability will still be triggered by the Nekro player. <sup>*</sup>
- [Propagation] If an ability triggers “after” a player researches a technology, that ability will never be triggered by the Nekro player. <sup>*</sup>
- [Antivirus (Promissory Note)] The effect of Antivirus does not prevent the Nekro player gaining a technology from a player via their Galactic Threat ability. <sup>*</sup>
- [Antivirus (Promissory Note)] The player holding Antivirus may only play it at the start of a combat they are participating in. <sup>*</sup>
- [Antivirus (Promissory Note)] Antivirus may be played at the start of a combat that the Nekro player is not participating in. <sup>*</sup>
- [Antivirus (Promissory Note)] Antivirus has no effect while it is in a player’s hand. <sup>*</sup>
- [Antivirus (Promissory Note)] Antivirus is returned when the system is activated, even if the active player will perform no hostile acts towards the Nekro player this turn. <sup>*</sup>
- [Antivirus (Promissory Note)] Activating a system containing only the Nekro player’s structures will still cause Antivirus to be returned. <sup>*</sup>
- [Antivirus (Promissory Note)] If an effect other than activating a system during a tactical action places a command counter in a system with the Nekro player’s units (for example, the primary ability of the Diplomacy strategy card), this will not cause Antivirus to be returned. <sup>*</sup>
- [Valefar Assimilator (Technology)] When copying another technology, Valefar Assimilator will retain its exhausted/readied state. It will not copy the target technology’s exhausted/readied state. <sup>*</sup>
- [Valefar Assimilator (Technology)] The Nekro player may use any ability of the copied technology that does not require exhausting as a cost, even if the Valefar Assimilator card is exhausted. <sup>*</sup>
- [Valefar Assimilator (Technology)] An exhausted Valefar Assimilator will always ready during the Status Phase, even if it is not currently copying a technology with an exhaust ability. <sup>*</sup>
- [Valefar Assimilator (Technology)] If the Nekro player gains a faction–specific infantry unit upgrade technology while they own the generic Infantry II unit upgrade technology and they have infantry on that unit upgrade card that would be placed in their home system at the start of their next turn, then those infantry are transferred to the Valefar Assimilator card that they are using to copy the faction–specific infantry unit upgrade. <sup>*</sup>
- [Valefar Assimilator (Technology)] If the Nekro player has copied certain technology (possibly two or more at different points in time), the following apply: <sup>*</sup>
- [Valefar Assimilator (Technology)] If both the Saar player’s Floating Factory II unit upgrade and the Vuil’raith player’s Vortex technology are copied, and another player blockades a Nekro space dock, the Nekro player returns any captured units, then destroys the blockaded space dock. <sup>*</sup>
- [Valefar Assimilator (Technology)] If both the Muaat player’s Magmus Reactor technology and the Saar player’s Floating Factory II unit upgrade are copied, the Nekro player may move their space docks into supernovae. <sup>*</sup>
- [Valefar Assimilator (Technology)] If the Saar player’s Floating Factory II unit upgrade is copied, both the Nekro player and the Saar player may have their space docks in the same system, if there are no ships in that system. <sup>*</sup>
- [Valefar Assimilator (Technology)] If the N’orr player’s Exotrireme II unit upgrade is copied, and the Nekro player is in a combat with the N’orr player, then the players will alternate when resolving end of combat round abilities, starting with the active player (all players may resolve abilities in initiative order, but it is most common for only the two players involved in the combat to want to resolve abilities). For example, if the attacking player has two Exotriremes II in the system and the defender has four, assuming both players are hostile towards each other, the most likely sequence is as follows: The attacker activates one of their Exotriremes II, leaving them with one and the defender with two; The defender activates one of their Exotriremes II leaving them with one and the attacker with none. <sup>*</sup>
- [Valefar Assimilator (Technology)] If the Deepwrought player’s Radical Advancement technology is copied, the Nekro player may resolve its ability, and will gain the chosen new technology; they will not gain command tokens. <sup>*</sup>
- [Valefar Assimilator (Technology)] The Nekro player may lose a technology if they copy a new one. If they lose certain technologies, the following apply: <sup>*</sup>
- [Valefar Assimilator (Technology)] If the Vuil’raith player’s Dimensional Tear II is lost, the dimensional tear tokens are removed from under the Nekro player’s space docks; the systems are no longer gravity rifts (unless the system tile is a printed gravity rift). <sup>*</sup>
- [Valefar Assimilator (Technology)] The Nekro player may lose a faction–specific infantry unit upgrade technology, while they have infantry on the unit upgrade card that would be placed in their home system at the start of their next turn. If they are moving the Valefar Assimilator token to a different faction–specific infantry unit upgrade technology, the infantry remain on the Valefar Assimilator card. Else, if they own the generic Infantry II unit upgrade technology, the infantry are transferred to that unit upgrade card. Otherwise, the infantry are returned to the Nekro player’s reinforcements. <sup>*</sup>
- [The Alastor (Flagship)] After the Nekro player uses the ability of The Alastor, all other players will have the opportunity to resolve an “at the start of combat” or an “at the start of a round of combat” ability before the Nekro player may resolve another ability. <sup>*</sup>
- [The Alastor (Flagship)] For example, say the Nekro player owns the Assault Cannon technology, and uses the ability of The Alastor to bring the total number of non–fighter ships in the combat to three (or more). Other players may then resolve one ability each. If their opponent uses an ability that destroys ships, such as from their own Assault Cannon, to reduce the number of non–fighter ships the Nekro player has in the combat to two (or fewer), then the Nekro player will be unable to resolve the ability of their Assault Cannon <sup>*</sup>
- [The Alastor (Flagship)] Some abilities may destroy The Alastor at the start of a combat before the Nekro player has used its ability, such as the Assault Cannon technology. <sup>*</sup>
- [The Alastor (Flagship)] If the Nekro player copies another player’s flagship unit upgrade technology with one of their Valefar Assimilator technologies during a space combat, any ground forces in that combat remain in that combat. If the Nekro player starts the space combat copying another player’s flagship unit upgrade technology, ground forces cannot participate in that combat, unless the Nekro player stops copying that flagship unit upgrade technology during the “start of combat” window. <sup>*</sup>
- [The Alastor (Flagship)] If the Nekro player has one of their Valefar Assimilator tokens on the Ul player’s Hel Titan II faction unit upgrade technology, they may use The Alastor to have their PDS in the active system participate in the space combat. <sup>*</sup>
- [The Alastor (Flagship)] A ground force participating in a space combat may count towards scoring the Demonstrate Your Power secret objective. <sup>*</sup>
- [The Alastor (Flagship)] If the Nekro player loses their last ground force during a space combat and consequently meets the requirements for elimination, they are immediately eliminated. They will not be given the opportunity to score any objectives from winning the combat or destroying certain units at the same time their last ground force was destroyed. <sup>*</sup>
- [The Alastor (Flagship)] If the Nekro player uses a Direct Hit action card to destroy an opponent’s flagship, they may score the Destroy their Greatest Ship secret objective, even if there are some hits remaining that will cause the Nekro player to be eliminated once they are assigned. If this would bring the Nekro player to ten victory points, they will instead win the game before they are eliminated. <sup>*</sup>
- [Nekro Malleon (Agent)] If the chosen player is the Muaat player with their commander, Magmus, unlocked, they will gain a trade good from it if they spend a token from their strategy pool when resolving this ability. <sup>*</sup>
- [Nekro Malleon (Agent)] That trade good will be gained separately from the other two. <sup>*</sup>
- [Nekro Acidos (Commander)] When the Nekro places a Valefar Assimilator token on a technology, they are not gaining a technology. <sup>*</sup>
- [UNIT.DSGN.FLAYESH — Polymorphic Algorithm (Hero)] When the other player’s units are destroyed, this does not trigger the Nekro player’s Technology Singularity ability. <sup>*</sup>
- [Mordred (Mech)] A Mordred will apply +2 against a player with both Valefar Assimilator tokens, and not +4. <sup>*</sup>
- [Valefar Assimilator Z (Breakthrough)] If the Nekro player places a Valefar Assimilator X or Y token on the Nomad player’s Memoria II unit upgrade technology card, their flagship would still gain each ability granted to them by Valefar Assimilator Z from the flagships of other players. <sup>*</sup>
- [Valefar Assimilator Z (Breakthrough)] The Nekro player cannot place multiple Valefar Assimilator Z tokens on the same player’s faction sheet. <sup>*</sup>
- [Valefar Assimilator Z (Breakthrough)] If the Nekro player has a Valefar Assimilator Z token on the Mahact player’s faction sheet, they will always apply the +2 to the combat rolls for The Alastor. <sup>*</sup>
- [Valefar Assimilator Z (Breakthrough)] If the Nekro player has a Valefar Assimilator Z token on the Vuil’raith player’s faction sheet, they will capture destroyed units. <sup>*</sup>
- [Valefar Assimilator Z (Breakthrough)] If the Nekro player has a Valefar Assimilator Z token on the Firmament player’s faction sheet, The Alastor will lose the ability of Heaven’s Eye when that player converts to the Obsidian components. <sup>*</sup>

**Removed notes that the site already covers elsewhere**

- [Technology Singularity] Players resolve abilities in initiative order, starting from the active player, until all players decline to resolve an ability consecutively; players who declined to resolve an ability previously may choose to resolve an ability if another player does so. While every player has the opportunity to resolve an ability, it is most common for only the two players involved in the combat to do so. Say the Nekro player does not have the Dreadnought II unit upgrade. If they use the Sustain Damage ability of one of their dreadnoughts, then their opponent may destroy it with a Direct Hit action card. If the Nekro player does not use the Sustain Damage ability (or any other ability within the same timing window), then their opponent may choose to use the Sustain Damage ability of one of their units (or any other ability within the same timing window). If they do not, then the timing window advances, and no more units may use their Sustain Damage abilities to cancel any of the remaining hits. If the opponent does, however, use the Sustain Damage ability of one of their units, the Nekro player may then destroy it with a Direct Hit action card, if it is an eligible target. After that, the Nekro player may choose to use the Sustain Damage ability of one of their units, even if they had previously declined to do so; if they gained the Dreadnought II unit upgrade when they destroyed their opponent’s non–dreadnought unit with the Direct Hit action card, then their opponent can no longer destroy the Nekro player’s with their own Direct Hit action card. _(no source)_
  - Covered by [R_abilities.php](R_abilities.php) [Notes]: A player may decline to resolve an ability during a timing window, but later resolve one if another player resolves an ability after
- [Propagation] If the Nekro player resolves an ability that instructs them to “gain” a technology, instead of “research” that technology, they will get that technology instead of the command tokens. _(no source)_
  - Covered by [R_technology.php](R_technology.php) [Rules Reference]: If an ability instructs a player to gain a technology, they do not research it
- [Valefar Assimilator (Technology)] If a unit upgrade that provides that unit with the Sustain Damage ability is lost, any damaged units will remain damaged, until either the status phase or another effect repairs them. _(no source)_
  - Covered by [R_status_phase.php](R_status_phase.php) [Notes]: All damaged units will be repaired, even if a game effect has caused those units to no longer have Sustain Damage
- [The Alastor (Flagship)] A mech in the space combat may be targeted with the Direct Hit action card if it uses its Sustain Damage ability. _(no source)_
  - Covered by [F_nekro.php](F_nekro.php) [The Alastor (Flagship)]: Any effect that may target ships or non-fighter ships may target a ground force participating in space combat

### F_nomad.php

**Notes kept**

- [Future Sight] If the Deadly Plot action card is played, the Nomad will not gain a trade good from Future Sight. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Agendas, Deadly Plot): "“Resolved with no effect” is not an outcome that could have been predicted, so no prediction abilities can trigger."
- [Temporal Command Suite (Technology)] Temporal Command Suite may allow the Nomad player to perform a second transaction with another player during one turn. <sup>4</sup>
  - Edited from: Temporal Command Suite may allow the Nomad player to perform a second transaction with another player during one turn, before or after the regular transaction.
  - Source 4 (Nomad, Temporal Command Suite): "Yes, Temporal Command Suite’s transaction does not affect performing a second transaction with the same player that turn."
- [Navarch Feng (Commander)] Commanders cannot become locked after being unlocked. If the Nomad player has only one scored secret objective, and it is elected by the Classified Document Leaks agenda, this will have no effect on Navarch Feng. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (51.6d): "A commander cannot flip to its locked side after it is unlocked, even if its owner no longer meets the unlock conditions."
- [Ahk–Syl Siven — Probability Matrix (Hero)] The Memoria may transport ground forces from systems containing one of the Nomad player’s command tokens while the ability of Ahk–Syl Siven is active. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Nomad, Ahk-Syl Siven): "Does the Nomad’s Hero, Ahk-Syl Siven, allow their flagship to pick up groundforces in systems that contain their tokens? A: Yes."
- [Quantum Manipulator (Mech)] During a space combat, A Quantum Manipulator cannot be repaired by the Duranium Armor technology, as it is not participating in the combat. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Nomad, Duranium Armor): "No, Duranium Armor only affects units participating (rolling dice) in a combat."

**Removed notes restored**

- [Future Sight] The Nomad player may only predict agenda outcomes via game effects that allow them to do so, e.g. rider action cards. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (nomad-future-sight-predictions (Community consensus)): "Only when an ability lets you predict, usually a rider."
- [Artuno the Betrayer (Agent)] When a player gains trade goods that were on a strategy card, they do not gain them from the supply. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (nomad-agent-artuno (Community consensus)): "Trade goods gained from the supply ... and as written neither do trade goods taken off strategy cards."
- [Quantum Manipulator (Mech)] Effects which directly destroy a ship cannot be prevented with the ability of a Quantum Manipulator. <sup>2</sup>
  - Trimmed from: Effects which directly destroys a ship cannot be prevented with the ability of a Quantum Manipulator.
  - Source 2 (sustain-damage-vs-destroy-effects (Community consensus)): "Sustain Damage only cancels hits, and these effects destroy units without producing hits."

**Notes added** (rulings that were not on the site before)

- [Artuno the Betrayer (Agent)] Converting commodities to trade goods is not gaining trade goods from the supply, and does not trigger Artuno the Betrayer. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (nomad-agent-artuno (Community consensus)): "Converting commodities doesn't count"
- [The Thundarian (Agent)] The Thundarian may be used during a combat that the Nomad player is not participating in. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (thundarian-other-combats (Community consensus)): "it has no participation requirement"

**Citations added to existing items**

- [Ahk–Syl Siven — Probability Matrix (Hero)] The Memoria may transport ground forces from systems containing one of the Nomad player’s command tokens while the ability of Ahk–Syl Siven is active. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (nomad-hero-memoria-pickups (Community consensus)): "the hero lets the flagship and the units it transports leave command-token systems, overriding the normal pickup ban."

**Restored without a source** (marked * on the site)

- [Future Sight] If the Nomad player predicts multiple different outcomes, and one of those outcomes is resolved, they will gain the trade good. <sup>*</sup>
- [Future Sight] If the Nomad player predicts an outcome and votes for another outcome (via the Xxcha player’s Alliance promissory note), and one of those outcomes is resolved, they will gain the trade good. <sup>*</sup>
- [The Cavalry (Promissory Note)] One ship is chosen. That ship retains the flagship’s values and abilities until it is destroyed or the combat ends. <sup>*</sup>
- [The Cavalry (Promissory Note)] If the chosen ship does not usually have the Sustain Damage ability, and is damaged during combat, it will remain damaged even after losing the Sustain Damage ability. <sup>*</sup>
- [The Cavalry (Promissory Note)] The damaged ship may be chosen again if The Cavalry is played by the same player during a future combat, regaining the Sustain Damage ability. As it is already damaged, it will be unable to use its Sustain Damage ability again. <sup>*</sup>
- [The Cavalry (Promissory Note)] The damaged ship will be repaired during the status phase, regardless of if it currently has the Sustain Damage ability. <sup>*</sup>
- [The Cavalry (Promissory Note)] In a future combat, the damaged ship may be repaired by the Duranium Armor technology. It will be unable to be damaged again unless it has regained the Sustain Damage ability. <sup>*</sup>
- [The Cavalry (Promissory Note)] If the Emergency Repairs action card is played, the damaged ship will not be repaired unless it currently has the Sustain Damage ability. <sup>*</sup>
- [Temporal Command Suite (Technology)] The Nomad player may perform a transaction with another player without being neighbors with that player. <sup>*</sup>
- [Temporal Command Suite (Technology)] The Nomad player may perform a transaction with another player even if neither player is the active player. <sup>*</sup>
- [Temporal Command Suite (Technology)] Temporal Command Suite may allow the Nomad player to perform a transaction at a time they usually could not. For example, if the Mentak player exhausts their agent, Suffi An, during the strategy phase when another player gains the trade goods on the strategy card they chose, the Nomad player may use Temporal Command Suite and then perform a transaction with the Mentak player. <sup>*</sup>
- [Memoria (Flagship)] Only the Memoria is adjacent to systems with a Quantum Manipulator. Other ships cannot move between the Memoria’s system and a system containing a Quantum Manipulator using this ability. <sup>*</sup>
- [Memoria (Flagship)] Other players cannot use the Deep Space Cannon ability of units in the same system as a Quantum Manipulator against the Memoria, unless those units are adjacent using another adjacency method. <sup>*</sup>
- [Memoria (Flagship)] The Memoria cannot retreat to a system containing a Quantum Manipulator, unless it is adjacent to that system using another adjacency method. <sup>*</sup>
- [Memoria (Flagship)] The Intimidate Council objective requires the system to be adjacent to Mecatol Rex. As such, the Nomad player cannot use the Memoria’s ability to score this objective. A similar prohibition applies to the Learn the Secrets of the Cosmos and Threaten Enemies objectives. <sup>*</sup>
- [Memoria (Flagship)] The Memoria is adjacent to the system that the Quantum Manipulator is in before movement, regardless of if that Quantum Manipulator is transported during that movement. <sup>*</sup>
- [Artuno the Betrayer (Agent)] If the Nomad player would gain trade goods from multiple effects, they may only put the trade goods from one of those effects on Artuno the Betrayer. <sup>*</sup>
- [Artuno the Betrayer (Agent)] For example, if the Nomad player successfully predicts the outcome of an agenda via the Trade Rider action card, they could put either the trade goods gained from the Trade Rider, or from Future Sight, but not both. <sup>*</sup>
- [Artuno the Betrayer (Agent)] When the Nomad player gains trade goods that were on Artuno the Betrayer, they do not gain them from the supply. <sup>*</sup>
- [Field Marshal Mercer (Agent)] The ground forces may be from a system with that players command token in it. <sup>*</sup>
- [Field Marshal Mercer (Agent)] The ground forces may be on a planet or in a space area. <sup>*</sup>
- [Field Marshal Mercer (Agent)] The ground forces may be from different systems. <sup>*</sup>
- [Field Marshal Mercer (Agent)] The ground forces may be placed on one or two planets. <sup>*</sup>
- [Field Marshal Mercer (Agent)] Any damaged mechs remain damaged. <sup>*</sup>
- [The Thundarian (Agent)] The dice are rerolled in the same round. Any effects that apply for a single round of combat remain in effect. <sup>*</sup>
- [The Thundarian (Agent)] This includes the Magen Defense Grid technology, the Fighter Prototype and Morale Boost action cards, the Letnev Munitions Reserves faction ability, the Naaz–Rokha Supercharge faction technology, the Letnev War Funding promissory note, the Letnev agent, Viscount Unlenn, and the Sol agent, Evelyn DeLouis. <sup>*</sup>
- [The Thundarian (Agent)] The Roll Dice step occurs after the start of a round of combat. Any effects that may be played at the start or end of a round of combat cannot be played until the next round of combat. <sup>*</sup>
- [The Thundarian (Agent)] This includes the ability of the Duranium Armor or Magen Defense Grid technologies, the Fighter Prototype or Morale Boost action cards, the L1Z1X Harrow or the Letnev Munitions Reserves faction abilities, the Naaz–Rokha Supercharge faction technology, the Letnev War Funding promissory note, the Letnev flagship, the Arc Secundus, the Letnev mech, a Dunlain Reaper, the N’orr Exotrireme II dreadnought ability, the Keleres Overwing Zeta hero ability, the Letnev agent, Viscount Unlenn, or the Sol agent, Evelyn DeLouis. <sup>*</sup>
- [The Thundarian (Agent)] The Thundarian is played at the end of the “Roll Dice” step, after effects that occur “when/after you roll dice” or similar. <sup>*</sup>
- [The Thundarian (Agent)] If The Thundarian is used after the Hacan player has spent trade goods for the ability of their flagship, the Wrath of Kenara, those trade goods remain spent, but the +1 to combat rolls will not be applied for the subsequent dice rolls. The Hacan player may spend trade goods after the subsequent dice roll to use the ability of the Wrath of Kenara for the new results. <sup>*</sup>
- [The Thundarian (Agent)] If The Thundarian is used after a player has used the ability of The Crown of Thalnos relic, any units that did not produce hits and so were destroyed remain destroyed, but the +1 to combat rolls will not be applied for the subsequent dice rolls. That player may use the ability of The Crown of Thalnos on the subsequent dice roll. <sup>*</sup>
- [The Thundarian (Agent)] If The Thundarian is used after a player has played the Fire Team action card, it will be discarded without effect on the subsequent roll. <sup>*</sup>
- [The Thundarian (Agent)] If The Thundarian is used after a player has played the Letnev War Funding Ω promissory note, it will be returned without effect on the subsequent roll. <sup>*</sup>
- [The Thundarian (Agent)] If the N’orr player’s Valkyrie Particle Weave faction technology would produce a hit, that hit is not assigned if The Thundarian is used. <sup>*</sup>
- [The Thundarian (Agent)] If a game effect readies The Thundarian when it is used, its effect may be applied again at the end of the same round of combat. <sup>*</sup>
- [Navarch Feng (Commander)] The flagship still has a cost of 8. <sup>*</sup>
- [Navarch Feng (Commander)] The flagship cannot be produced with abilities that are limited by the cost of units, such as the Integrated Economy technology or the Muaat player’s agent, Umbat. <sup>*</sup>
- [Navarch Feng (Commander)] If the flagship is chosen for the Scuttle action card, the player gains 8 trade goods. <sup>*</sup>
- [Navarch Feng (Commander)] The objective elected by the Classified Document Leaks agenda is a public objective, not a secret objective. Navarch Feng cannot be unlocked by scoring it. <sup>*</sup>
- [Navarch Feng (Commander)] If the Classified Document Leaks agenda is discarded, the elected objective is neither a public objective nor a secret objective. Navarch Feng cannot be unlocked by having scored it. <sup>*</sup>
- [Ahk–Syl Siven — Probability Matrix (Hero)] The game round ends after the agenda phase (or the status phase if the custodians token is yet to be removed from Mecatol Rex). <sup>*</sup>
- [Quantum Manipulator (Mech)] When a Quantum Manipulator uses its Sustain Damage ability to cancel a hit produced against a ship, the Direct Hit and Reflective Shielding action cards cannot be played, as the Quantum Manipulator is not a ship. <sup>*</sup>
- [Quantum Manipulator (Mech)] A Quantum Manipulator may use its Sustain Damage ability to cancel any hit produced during combat against the Nomad player’s ships, not just hits produced by combat rolls. For example, hits produced by anti–fighter barrage rolls may be cancelled. <sup>*</sup>
- [Quantum Manipulator (Mech)] Hits that are produced outside of combat cannot be cancelled with the ability of a Quantum Manipulator. For example, hits produced by space cannon rolls cannot be canceled. <sup>*</sup>
- [Thunder’s Paradox (Breakthrough)] The readied agent can belong to any player. It need not belong to the Nomad player nor the active player. <sup>*</sup>

  - Source 9 (General: Crimson Commander): "A:Yes to both."

  - Trimmed from: Active breaches cannot be removed in this manner. If every breach token is on the game board as an active breach, the Rebellion player cannot resolve abilities that would place additional breach tokens.

  - Trimmed from: (originally a child of 'A system may have any number of breaches in it.', which is unsupported; restored at top level)
  - Source 6 (Crimson Rebellion): "Q: Incursion (Ability): If a system contains multiple breaches during the status phase, how many can be removed in that single status phase? A: All active breaches can be removed"
- [Subatomic Splicer (Technology)] During a space combat in the Rebellion player’s home system, they cannot produce ships there while another player’s ships are present. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (Crimson Rebellion): "“A player cannot produce ships in a system that contains other players’ ships”. Does this apply to Subatomic Splicer? A: It does apply."
- [Exile (Unit)] The destroyer must be on the game board when the combat ends in order to place the breach. If the destroyer was in the active system, and was destroyed in the space combat, it cannot be used to place a breach. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (crimson-breaches (Community consensus)): "A breach goes in the combat's system at the end of combat, whoever won, if one of your destroyers is in range then; it needn't have fought."
- [Ahk Ravin (Agent)] If the Rebellion player transports ground forces during the swap, those ground forces will be placed in the space area of their destination system. They cannot be committed to planets in that system until and unless a tactical action is resolved in that system. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (crimson-agent-swaps-and-component-moves (Community consensus)): "A swap is a component action, not a tactical action, so there's no invasion unless the ability says so."
- [Resonance Generator (Breakthrough)] The passive, movement ability of Resonance Generator is still in effect when the card is exhausted. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (breakthroughs-not-technologies (Community consensus)): "Their passive abilities keep working while exhausted."

**Notes added** (rulings that were not on the site before)

- [Sundered] Sundered only prevents the Rebellion player’s ships from moving through wormholes other than epsilon wormholes. Other wormholes still make systems adjacent for the Rebellion player for all other purposes, such as Space Cannon, neighbors, objectives, action cards, and the ability of the Exile. <sup>9</sup>
  - Source 9 (General / Using Wormholes): "They can't move through them. Other things are fine."
- [Exile (Unit)] The Rebellion player may place a breach with the ability of an Exile at the end of a combat against neutral units. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (Crimson Rebellion): "Can the Crimson destroyer, Exile, place a breach at the end of a combat with neutral units?"
- [Sundered] The Rebellion player may use the Creuss player’s Creuss IFF promissory note, but their ships still cannot move through Creuss wormholes. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (Crimson Rebellion): "Yes, they still may not move through the Creuss wormholes though."
- [Sundered] The Rebellion player may use the Creuss player’s agent, Emissary Taivra, and the Lost Star Chart action card. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (Crimson Rebellion): "Can they use the Creuss agent or the Lost Star Charts action card?"
- [Sundered] The Wormhole Reconstruction agenda does not override Sundered. However, the systems it makes adjacent are adjacent for movement, and the Rebellion player’s ships do not need to use the wormholes to move between them. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (Crimson Rebellion): "No, but those systems are adjacent for movement, they do not need to use the worm holes so functionally it overrides Sundered."
- [Sundered] Sundered is a state–based effect, and resolves before another player would gain control of Ahk Creuxx, even if that player is the active player. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (Crimson Rebellion): "Sundered is a state-based effect which would trigger prior to gain control."
- [Sever (Promissory Note)] Sever only prevents movement through the wormhole. Adjacency, Space Cannon, the Creuss player’s Quantum Entanglement and Slipstream faction abilities, the Ghost Ship action card and the Become the Gatekeeper objective are unaffected. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (Crimson Rebellion / Sever): "Blocks movement. Adjacency, PDS, Ghost Ship, Become the Gatekeeper, SLIPSTREAM are all unaffected."
- [Sever (Promissory Note)] Sever affects all wormholes in the system, not just the one the token is placed on. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (Crimson Rebellion / Sever): "All wormholes in the system."
- [Incursion] If the Rebellion player is eliminated, breach tokens remain in play, and active breaches remain adjacent to each other. Inactive breaches may be removed from the game board. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (Elimination): "Breach tokens also remain in play and active breaches remain adjacent. Inactive breaches may be removed as they only serve as clutter at this point."
- [Homesick Phantom — Fragment Reality (Hero)] Fragment Reality cannot be used during a combat between two other players. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (crimson-rebellion-hero-combats (Community consensus)): "it is meant for combats you are part of"

**Citations added to existing items**

- [Sundered] Sundered only prevents the Rebellion player’s ships from moving through wormholes other than epsilon wormholes. Other wormholes still make systems adjacent for the Rebellion player for all other purposes, such as Space Cannon, neighbors, objectives, action cards, and the ability of the Exile. now also cites <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (Crimson Rebellion): "Crimson are unable to move through wormholes. All other uses are permitted including PDS, Neighbors, placing Breaches, etc."
- [Ahk Ravin (Agent)] Ahk Ravin is a swap, not a move. This means units will not trigger gravity rift rolls and the ability cannot be used to swap with a Saar Spacedock. now also cites <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (Crimson Rebellion): "Q: How does the agent interact with swapping out of a Gravity Rift? Do you have to roll? A: Swapping is not movement, so no roll is required."
- [Ahk Siever (Commander)] Ahk Siever triggers off of combats with neutral units. now also cites <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (Crimson Rebellion): "Q: Does the Crimson commander,Ahk Siever, work on combats with neutral units? A: Yes, the commander triggers on any combat involving players (which is all combats)."
- [Sundered] Sundered only prevents the Rebellion player’s ships from moving through wormholes other than epsilon wormholes. Other wormholes still make systems adjacent... <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (crimson-cannot-use-wormholes (Community consensus)): "it only stops them moving through wormholes ... Adjacency still counts for neighbors, breach placement, Space Cannon and objectives."
- [Incursion] If a player has a ship in a system containing multiple breaches at the end of the status phase, they may remove any or all of them. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (crimson-breaches (Community consensus)): "At the end of the status phase a player with ships there may remove any or all active breaches"

**Restored without a source** (marked * on the site)

- [Incursion] Breaches are not wormholes. <sup>*</sup>
- [Subatomic Splicer (Technology)] The produced ships must still be paid for. <sup>*</sup>
- [Exile (Unit)] A breach may be placed after a space combat and/or a ground combat. <sup>*</sup>
- [Quietus (Flagship)] The Quietus removes only the unit abilities from other players’ units; any text abilities are unaffected. <sup>*</sup>
- [Quietus (Flagship)] Text abilities that rely on unit abilities, such as the space dock II text ability that defines “X” in that unit’s Production X ability, will have no effect. <sup>*</sup>
- [Quietus (Flagship)] If a unit loses its Deploy ability, then the text that describes how that unit’s Deploy ability is used will have no effect. <sup>*</sup>
- [Ahk Siever (Commander)] The Rebellion player does not have to be a participant in the combat to gain or convert commodities. <sup>*</sup>
- [Ahk Siever (Commander)] If there are multiple combats in one turn, the Rebellion player may gain or convert a commodity for each. This includes for each ground combat on a separate planet. <sup>*</sup>
- [Homesick Phantom — Fragment Reality (Hero)] The Rebellion player may only start placing ships on Homesick Phantom once the hero has been unlocked. <sup>*</sup>
- [Revenant (Mech)] The Rebellion player may only Deploy one mech per tactical action, regardless of the number of planets in the active system. <sup>*</sup>

- [Incursion] A system may have any number of breaches in it. _(no source)_

If the Rebellion player purges Fragment Reality and places fighters and/or ground forces in a system, they will not need to remove any fighters or ground forces from the space area to satisfy their capacity limit until after the combat has been resolved. _(no source)_

### F_saar.php

**Notes kept**

- [Scavenge] If the Saar player gains control of multiple planets during one invasion, the trade goods are gained one at a time. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (FAQ (Mentak): Pillage and Scavenge): "A: Yes. The Mentak can trigger “Pillage” each time the Saar gain control of a planet, if all the conditions of “Pillage” are met."
- [Chaos Mapping (Technology)] The produced unit must be paid for. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (FAQ (Production)): "A: Yes, a unit that is produced must always be paid for."
- [Chaos Mapping (Technology)] A unit may be produced on each of the Saar player’s turns. <sup>1</sup>
  - Edited from: A unit may be produced on each of the Saar player’s turns; Chaos Mapping is not exhausted.
  - Source 1 (FAQ (Clan of Saar): Chaos Mapping): "A: Yes, “Chaos Mapping” can be used as many times as you have turns during the action phase."
- [Chaos Mapping (Technology)] A unit may be produced on the turn the Saar player passes. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (FAQ (Clan of Saar): Chaos Mapping): "A: Yes, “Chaos Mapping” can be used on the turn that a player passes."
- [Floating Factory (Unit)] Hits produced by space cannon rolls cannot be assigned to a Floating Factory. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (FAQ (Clan of Saar): Floating Factories and PDS): "A: No, “Floating Factories” cannot be the target of PDS fire."
- [Floating Factory (Unit)] A Floating Factory moving through or out of a gravity rift must roll for removal. It will receive the +1 to its movement. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Anomalies): "Any units moving into, through or out of anomalies must follow the same rules for ships moving into, through or out of anomalies."
- [Floating Factory (Unit)] If a Floating Factory is in a system that contains none of the Saar player’s ships, and another player moves ships into that system, the Floating Factory is immediately destroyed. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (79.4a): "The Clan of Saar’s “Floating Factory” faction-specific space dock is destroyed when it is blockaded; that is to say, when it is in a system with another player’s ships and none of the Clan of Saar’s ships."
- [Captain Mendosa (Agent)] The effect of Captain Mendosa occurs when the system is activated. <sup>4</sup>
  - Edited from: The effect of Captain Mendosa occurs when the system is activated. The move value will be set to the chosen ship’s move value during this window.
  - Source 4 (Clan of Saar: Mendosa and movement bonuses): "Clan of Saar’s agent, Mendosa, will get an errata to “WHEN you activate a system.” This means other bonuses would be applied after Mendosa takes effect."
- [Captain Mendosa (Agent)] Move value modifying effects that trigger after a system is activated, such as the Flank Speed action card or the Gravity Drive technology will not be included in Captain Mendosa’s effect. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Clan of Saar: Mendosa and movement bonuses): "This means other bonuses would be applied after Mendosa takes effect."
- [Captain Mendosa (Agent)] The nebula effect of setting the move value of all ships in that system to one will be overwritten by Captain Mendosa’s effect. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Clan of Saar: Mendosa and Nebula): "Mendosa would be treated as a bonus and would override the Nebula’s movement value rule."
- [Gurno Aggero — Armageddon Relay (Hero)] A unit is not adjacent to the system it is in. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (6.2, 6.2a): "A unit or planet is adjacent to all system tiles that are adjacent to the system tile that contains that unit or planet. a A system is not adjacent to itself."

**Removed notes restored**

- [Floating Factory (Unit)] Game effects that affect ship movement, such as the Gravity Drive technology, the Flank Speed action card, the Light/Wave Deflector technology, the Antimass Deflectors technology, etc, may affect Floating Factories. <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (iswearihaveajob, BGG, Jan 18, 2018): "Floating Factories are affected by abilities that affect movement (Gravity Drive, Flank Speed, Light/Wave Deflectors, In the Silence of Space, Antimass Deflectors, and so on)."
- [Floating Factory (Unit)] If the Saar player announces a retreat during a space combat, but all their ships are destroyed that round, any Floating Factories in that system are destroyed without retreating. <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (garfielder, BGG, Sep 19, 2017): "As a rule, in any situation where a Floating Factory is alone with enemy ships, it is destroyed before it can retreat."
- [Floating Factory (Unit)] When resolving an ability of the Construction strategy card, the Saar player must control a planet in the system they place a Floating Factory in. <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (sigmazero13, BGG, Aug 1, 2018): "You still follow the rules of the Construction SC to the letter. Then, when you would place it, you place it in the space area instead. So while it is never placed on the planet, an eligible planet does need to exist."
- [Floating Factory (Unit)] This will happen before the Space Cannon Offense step. The Floating Factory is destroyed, even if all of the other player’ ships are destroyed during this step. <sup>5</sup>
  - Trimmed from: This will happen before the Space Cannon Offense step. The Floating Factory is destroyed, even if all of the other player’ ships are destroyed during this step. Additionally, the Saar player cannot use that Floating Factory to resolve a space cannon roll enabled by the Experimental Battlestation action card.
  - Source 5 (garfielder, BGG, Sep 19, 2017): "if the Saar Space dock was alone when the ships move in, it is destroyed, though the space cannons can certainly attempt to avenge it."

  - Source 6 (The Clans of Saar): "the targeted player uses Sustain Damage when the hit is produced against that mech and cancels the hit"
- [Deorbit Barrage (Breakthrough)] The Saar player may assign multiple hits to the same unit. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (The Clans of Saar): "this allows another hit that was produced to be used against that mech."
- [Ragh’s Call (Promissory Note)] All of the Saar player’s ground forces must be placed on the same planet. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (saar-raghs-call (Community consensus)): "moves the Saar ground forces from one planet to another single planet"
- [Floating Factory (Unit)] A floating Factory does not count towards the Saar player’s fleet pool. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (saar-floating-factory-not-a-ship (Designer ruling)): "They don't count against your fleet pool"
- [Floating Factory (Unit)] When a Floating Factory produces ground forces, they may be placed in the space area or on a planet they control in that system. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (where-produced-ground-forces-go (Community consensus)): "If the producing unit is in space, like a Saar Floating Factory ... they can go in that space area or on any planet you control in the system."
- [Scavenger Zeta (Mech)] If the Saar player gains control of multiple planets, they may deploy one Scavenger Zeta to each. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (saar-mech-per-planet (Community consensus)): "Yes — each planet gained is its own timing window."

**Notes added** (rulings that were not on the site before)

- [Floating Factory (Unit)] If the Saar player’s last ship in a system is destroyed, any Floating Factories in that system are blockaded and destroyed before the Yin player’s agent, Brother Milor, can be resolved to place fighters. <sup>6</sup>

**Restored without a source** (marked * on the site)

- [Scavenge] When the Saar player gains control of a planet that is not already controlled by another player, they will explore it before gaining the trade good from this ability. <sup>*</sup>
- [Scavenge] If the Saar player is to gain control of multiple planets not already controlled by another player, they will gain and explore one planet and gain a trade good before gaining and exploring the next. <sup>*</sup>
- [Scavenge] If the Saar player has the Naaz–Rokha player’s Alliance promissory note, and they gain control of a planet that was controlled by another player, they may explore it or gain a trade good in either order. <sup>*</sup>
- [Ragh’s Call (Promissory Note)] Playing Ragh’s Call will prevent ground combat from occurring on that planet. <sup>*</sup>
- [Ragh’s Call (Promissory Note)] Any PDS on the planet remain. They might produce hits during the Space Cannon Defense step. <sup>*</sup>
- [Chaos Mapping (Technology)] The produced unit may move later that same turn, if the Saar player performs a tactical action. <sup>*</sup>
- [Chaos Mapping (Technology)] A player may still use abilities such as action cards or Deep Space Cannon that affect the Saar player’s units located in asteroid fields. <sup>*</sup>
- [Chaos Mapping (Technology)] If an asteroid field contains only non–ship units belonging to the Saar player, it may still be activated by other players. <sup>*</sup>
- [Floating Factory (Unit)] If neither player has ships in the active system after the final round of combat, the Floating Factory is not destroyed, and does not retreat. <sup>*</sup>
- [Floating Factory (Unit)] If the Saar player has their last ship destroyed during combat by a Direct Hit action card, a Floating Factory in the system will be blockaded and destroyed, even if the Saar player produced enough hits to destroy their opponent’s remaining ships during that round of combat. <sup>*</sup>
- [Floating Factory (Unit)] Players alternate using the Sustain Damage ability of their units, one at a time, starting with the active player, and continuing until both players decline, in a row, to use the Sustain Damage of one of their units. If both the Saar player and their opponent have a Direct Hit, then the first unit to use Sustain Damage will be the first unit that may be destroyed by a Direct Hit. If the Saar player’s unit is the last to be destroyed, and leaves no other ships in the system, then a Floating Factory in that system will not be blockaded nor destroyed. <sup>*</sup>
- [Floating Factory (Unit)] If, at the end of the combat, the Saar player has no ships, an their opponent has only fighters, then any Floating Factories in the system will be blockaded, and thus destroyed, before the fighters are removed due to lack of capacity. <sup>*</sup>
- [Floating Factory (Unit)] If the Nekro player has only ground forces participating in the combat as ships due to the effect of their flagship, the Alastor, those ground forces will blockade and destroy any Floating Factories, even if those ground forces are on planets instead of in the space area. <sup>*</sup>
- [Floating Factory (Unit)] The Saar player cannot place a Floating Factory in a system if the only planet they control in that system has the Demilitarized Zone cultural exploration card attached. <sup>*</sup>
- [Floating Factory (Unit)] If an effect allows a Floating Factory to move through a system that contains another player’s ships (such as the Light/Wave Deflectors technology), it will not be blockaded in systems it moves through. <sup>*</sup>
- [Floating Factory (Unit)] If all of the other player’s ships are removed due to a gravity rift, they will not arrive in the active system. The Floating Factory will not be destroyed. <sup>*</sup>
- [Floating Factory (Unit)] A Floating Factory cannot count towards the Improve Infrastructure or Protect the Border objectives. <sup>*</sup>
- [Captain Mendosa (Agent)] Gravity rifts apply the +1 during movement. This modifier will not be included in Captain Mendosa’s effect. <sup>*</sup>
- [Rowl Sarring (Commander)] If another player has the Saar player’s Alliance promissory note, this does not allow them to produce fighters at a blockaded space dock, so as to place them elsewhere. <sup>*</sup>
- [Scavenger Zeta (Mech)] The Saar player may perform the Deploy ability or their Scavenge ability in either order. If they perform their Scavenge ability first, they may pay for the Deploy ability with the gained trade good. <sup>*</sup>
- [Scavenger Zeta (Mech)] When the Saar player gains control of a planet that is not already controlled by another player, they will explore it before the Deploy ability will be able to trigger. <sup>*</sup>
- [Deorbit Barrage (Breakthrough)] The Saar player must choose how many resources to spend before rolling any dice. <sup>*</sup>

### F_sol.php

**Notes kept**

- [Military Support (Promissory Note)] A player may receive Military Support in a transaction during the Sol player’s turn. If received at the start of the Sol player’s turn, that player may play it immediately. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (FAQ appendix, General): "a promissory note with “At the start of your turn:” timing may be immediately played if the transaction occurred within the “start of turn” timing window."
  - Source 1 (94.1a): "A player can resolve a transaction at any time during their turn, even during a combat."

**Removed notes restored**

- [Genesis (Flagship)] Placing the infantry during the status phase is mandatory. <sup>3</sup>
  - Trimmed from: Placing the infantry during the status phase is mandatory. After, the Sol player might need to remove an infantry or fighter to meet capacity limits.
  - Source 3 (ti-k0289_learn_to_play_2020_web.txt p.4): "At the end of the status phase, place 1 infantry from your reinforcements in this system’s space area."
- [Military Support (Promissory Note)] Military Support may be played when the Sol player has no command tokens in their strategy pool. <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (doc4.txt reddit faction promissory notes answer (c. May 2019, Dane)): "the line ‘if able’ is extraneous"
  - Source 5 (doc4.txt same): "Each of the effects of these should be resolvable whether or not the affected faction has a command token available."
- [Military Support (Promissory Note)] If a player received Military Support on a previous turn, they may play it at the start of the Sol player’s turn, and immediately perform a transaction with the Sol player to regain it. However, Military Support cannot be played twice in one timing window. The active player cannot play Military Support again until the Sol player’s next turn. <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (doc4.txt x3n d0g, 08/31/2018 / Clipper, Jun 6, 2018 (Dane)): "that PN cannot be traded and resolved multiple times during the same window (in the case of the Federation of Sol’s case, for example)."
- [Claire Gibson (Commander)] If the Sol player has no ground forces on a planet they control, ground combat will not occur, and so they cannot place an infantry on that planet. This includes if they lose the last of their ground forces during the Bombardment step of the invasion. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (sol-commander-needs-ground-combat (Community consensus)): "No — it triggers at the start of ground combat, which only happens if a defending ground force (a mech counts; structures don't) survives to that point."

**Notes added** (rulings that were not on the site before)

- [Versatile] If the Sol player owns the Hyper Metabolism technology, they gain four command tokens during the status phase. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (hyper-metabolism-misprint (Community consensus)): "It stacks with Sol's extra token, so Sol with it gains 4."
- [Orbital Drop] Orbital Drop may be used multiple times each round, once for each command token spent from the Sol player’s strategy pool. Each use is a separate action. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (sol-orbital-drop (Community consensus)): "It can be used as many times as you have tokens in your strategy pool, each use as a separate action."

**Citations added to existing items**

- [Military Support (Promissory Note)] A player may receive Military Support in a transaction during the Sol player’s turn. If received at the start of the Sol player’s turn, that player may play it immediately. now also cites <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (doc4.txt x3n d0g, 08/31/2018 (Dane)): "You can trade a promissory note and have it be immediately used during the start of turn window. That is allowed."
- [Military Support (Promissory Note)] Military Support may be played when the Sol player has no command tokens in their strategy pool. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (sol-military-support-rules (Community consensus)): "It works without a token — the note only spends Sol's strategy token if able."
- [Military Support (Promissory Note)] If a player received Military Support on a previous turn, ... The active player cannot play Military Support again until the Sol player’s next turn. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (military-support-once-per-sol-turn (Community consensus)): "If Sol trades it out again that turn, the start of that turn has passed, so it waits until Sol's next turn."

**Restored without a source** (marked * on the site)

- [Military Support (Promissory Note)] Military Support is played before the Sol player may use Orbital Drop. <sup>*</sup>
- [Military Support (Promissory Note)] Military Support may be played the turn the Sol player passes. <sup>*</sup>
- [Evelyn DeLouis (Agent)] This ability only applies to combat rolls. <sup>*</sup>
- [Evelyn DeLouis (Agent)] This ability does not allow one of the L1Z1X player’s Annihilator mechs to roll an additional Bombardment dice when resolving their Harrow ability. <sup>*</sup>
- [Claire Gibson (Commander)] If an invasion involves ground combat on multiple planets, an infantry will be placed on each. <sup>*</sup>
- [Bellum Gloriosum (Breakthrough)] If the Sol player produces multiple ships simultaneously, the combined capacity is used to determine how many fighters and ground forces do not count towards the Production limit. <sup>*</sup>
- [Bellum Gloriosum (Breakthrough)] The additional fighters and ground forces are produced simultaneously with any other fighters and ground forces, and the resources paid will be determined by their combined cost. <sup>*</sup>
- [Bellum Gloriosum (Breakthrough)] For example, say that the Sol player has Production 2, and wishes to produce a dreadnought and two infantry. They would pay five resources for this, as they would pay a single resource for the pair of infantry. <sup>*</sup>

**Removed notes that the site already covers elsewhere**

- [Military Support (Promissory Note)] The active player may perform a transaction with each other player at most once per turn. As such, a player cannot receive Military Support more than once per turn. _(no source)_
  - Covered by [R_transactions.php](R_transactions.php) [Rules Reference]: During the active player’s turn, they may resolve up to one transaction with each of their neighbors.
- [Claire Gibson (Commander)] The start of ground combat occurs after the Space Cannon Defense step. If all of the ground forces committed to a planet are destroyed in that step, then the ground combat will be skipped on that planet, and this ability will not trigger. _(no source)_
  - Covered by [R_invasion.php](R_invasion.php) [Rules Reference]: Step 3 – Space Cannon Defense ... Step 4 – Ground Combat: If the active player has ground forces on a planet ... that contains another player’s ground forces, those players resolve a ground combat

### F_ul.php

**Notes kept**

- [Awaken] If the Ul player wishes to place a PDS, but there are none left in their reinforcements, they may remove a PDS from any system that does not contain one of their command tokens and place that instead. The PDS will be placed undamaged. <sup>1,4</sup>
  - Source 1 (23.4a): "When a player would place a unit, if there are none of that type left in their reinforcements, that player can remove a unit from any system that does not contain one of their command tokens and place that unit in their reinforcements."
  - Source 4 (General, damaged unit removed and placed): "If it is produced, placed, or replaced which would require a remove and place it is no longer damaged."
- [Coalescence] If the Ul player’s units exist in the same location as another player’s units, effects that end the Ul player’s turn cannot prevent the combat from occuring. <sup>4</sup>
  - Edited from: If the Ul player’s units exist in the same location as another player’s units, no game effect can prevent the combat from occuring, including effects that end the Ul player’s turn.
  - Source 4 (Titans of Ul, turn ending after Coalescence): "Coalescence forces combat steps to occur. No other steps of the tactical action occur, and abilities can only be used within combat."
- [Coalescence] Only the active player may use the Bombardment ability of their units during an invasion. <sup>4</sup>
  - Edited from: Only the active player may use the Bombardment ability of their units during an invasion. As such, any ships in the active system will be unable to use their Bombardment ability during the Ul player’s turn, unless they belong to the Ul player.
  - Source 4 (L1Z1X Mindnet, Harrow when defending): "No, only the active player can use BOMBARDMENT."
- [Coalescence] This prevents the L1Z1X player from using their Harrow ability. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (L1Z1X Mindnet, Harrow when defending): "Can the L1Z1X use harrow when they're defending during ground combat? A: No, only the active player can use BOMBARDMENT."
- [Terraform (Promissory Note)] Once played, Terraform counts as being in the play area of the player who controls the planet. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Titans of Ul, Terraform and objectives): "when Terraform is attached to a planet it counts as being in that planet owner’s play area."
- [Hel–Titan (Unit)] When multiple units use their Production ability, the Production value is pooled. As such, if the Ul player has two Hel–Titans in a system, they may produce two infantry or two fighters for one resource, rather than two resources. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (FAQ appendix, The Arborec; 68.1a): "Production value is totaled when the “Production” ability of units in a system is used."
- [Hel–Titan (Unit)] Effects that move ground forces, such as the Ghost Squad action card or the ability of the N’orr player’s commander, G’hom Sek’kus, (via the Alliance promissory note), cannot be used to move a Hel–Titan to another planet. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Titans of Ul, Hel-Titan movement): "No, structures cannot move."
- [Tungstantus (Commander)] The trade good may be spent on the units produced by the Production ability that triggered Tungstantus. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Titans of Ul, Tungstantus): "The gain and spend are simultaneous, so cannot be pillaged."
- [Tungstantus (Commander)] The trade good may be spent as it is gained. The number of trade goods the Ul player has after producing units is used to determine if the Mentak player may use their Pillage ability. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Titans of Ul, Tungstantus): "The gain and spend are simultaneous, so cannot be pillaged."
- [Hecatoncheires (Mech)] A Deploy ability may only be resolved for units in a player’s reinforcements. If all four of the Hecatoncheires are already on the board, no Hecatoncheires may be deployed. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (30.2): "A player can only resolve a deploy ability to place a unit that is in their reinforcements."
- [Hecatoncheires (Mech)] The Ul player cannot place a PDS on a planet that already has two of their PDS on it. As such, they are unable to place a Hecatoncheires on a planet with two of their PDS using its Deploy ability. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Titans of Ul, 63.3 and DEPLOY): "You cannot place a structure on a planet with the maximum number of your structures, which prevents using the DEPLOY ability on a planet with 2 PDS of yours"
- [Hecatoncheires (Mech)] The Ul player must have at least one PDS in their reinforcements to place in order to use the Deploy ability of a Hecatoncheires. However, when they would place a PDS, they may remove a PDS from any system that does not contain one of their command tokens and put it in their reinforcements. They may then use the Deploy ability of a Hecatoncheires. <sup>1,4</sup>
  - Source 1 (23.4a): "When a player would place a unit, if there are none of that type left in their reinforcements, that player can remove a unit from any system that does not contain one of their command tokens and place that unit in their reinforcements."
  - Source 4 (Titans of Ul, 63.3 and DEPLOY): "You also cannot DEPLOY a mech if you have no PDS in reinforcements, but could remove a PDS from the board and then DEPLOY your mech to an eligible target planet"
- [Slumberstate Computing (Breakthrough)] The Ul player does not have to be neighbors with the player that agrees to have a sleeper token placed on their planet. <sup>9</sup>
  - Source 9 (Twilight's Fall, Titans Breakthrough): "There is no real timing window or other requirement, it is something that can easily be worked into a transaction or deal with friendly players."

**Removed notes restored**

- [Terraform (Promissory Note)] If a planet has multiple traits, the player exploring the planet chooses which of the corresponding exploration decks to draw from. <sup>7</sup>
  - Source 7 (te_rulebook_web.txt p.11): "When exploring one of these planets with the Prophecy of Kings expansion, the exploring player can choose to draw a card matching either of the planet’s traits (but not both)."
- [Tungstantus (Commander)] Other effects that produce units without a unit using its Production ability will not trigger Tungstantus. <sup>14</sup>
  - Source 14 (ti_codex_2_cards.txt p.3): "When 1 or more of your units use PRODUCTION: You may gain 1 trade good."
- [Awaken] Only sleeper tokens present in the system when it is activated may be replaced with PDS. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (titans-awaken-timing (Community consensus)): "Right after activating a system that already held your sleeper token; a sleeper placed later in that activation, say by Scanlink exploration, can't be awakened then."
- [Awaken] A sleeper token that is placed during the Activation step, most commonly by using the Scanlink Drone Network technology and the Terragenesis ability, cannot be replaced via the Awaken ability during the same tactical action. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (titans-awaken-timing (Community consensus)): "a sleeper placed later in that activation, say by Scanlink exploration, can't be awakened then."
- [Awaken] If the Ul player places a PDS on a planet controlled by another player, and that player has ground forces on that planet, then a ground combat will be resolved during the Invasion step of the tactical action. <sup>2</sup>
  - Trimmed from: If the Ul player places a PDS on a planet controlled by another player, and that player does not have any ground forces on that planet, the Ul player will destroy all of the other player’s structures, and gain control of that planet immediately. If the other player has ground forces, then a ground combat will be resolved during the Invasion step of the tactical action.
  - Source 2 (titans-awaken-on-taken-planet (Community consensus)): "the sleeper stays until Awaken, and if enemy ground forces are there a ground combat follows, the winner keeping the planet."

  - Trimmed from: ... using their flagship or Awaken ability.
  - Source 2 (titans-awaken-timing (Community consensus)): "Ceasefire only stops movement, so Awaken still works."
- [Terraform (Promissory Note)] Once played, Terraform is never returned to the Ul player. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (titans-terraform-note (Community consensus)): "once attached it can't be played again or traded."
- [Hel–Titan (Unit)] Effects that remove ground forces, and then place them on the game board without transporting them, such as the Decoy Operation action card or the Transit Diodes technology, may be used on a Hel–Titan. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (transit-diodes-hel-titans (Community consensus)): "Hel-Titans yes: they are ground forces, and Transit Diodes removes and places units rather than transporting them."
- [Ouranos (Flagship)] Only PDS present in the system when it is activated may be replaced with the Ouranos. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (titans-flagship-deploy (Community consensus)): "But the PDS must be there when you activate"
- [Ouranos (Flagship)] A PDS that is placed during the activation step, most commonly by using the Awaken ability, cannot be replaced with the Ouranos during the same tactical action. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (titans-flagship-deploy (Community consensus)): "so one placed by Awaken during that activation doesn't qualify."

**Notes added** (rulings that were not on the site before)

- [Slumberstate Computing (Breakthrough)] There is no timing window or other requirement for another player allowing the Ul player to place a sleeper token on a planet they control; it may be included as part of a transaction or deal. <sup>9</sup>
  - Source 9 (General / Titans Breakthrough): "There is no real timing window or other requirement, it is something that can easily be worked into a transaction or deal with friendly players."

  - Source 4 (Factions/Titans of Ul): "No other steps of the tactical action occur, and abilities can only be used within combat."
- [Awaken] The Ul player may place a PDS on a planet that contains two of another player’s PDS. They cannot place a PDS on a planet that already contains two of their own PDS. <sup>4</sup>

  - Source 6 (Titans of Ul / Slumberstate Computing): "No, the ability is specifically Status Phase Step 3 DrawAction Cards."

- [Slumberstate Computing (Breakthrough)] A planet controlled by another player may contain at most one sleeper token. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (Titans of Ul / Slumberstate Computing): "One per planet"
- [Slumberstate Computing (Breakthrough)] When another player agrees to allow the Ul player to place a sleeper token, the agreement includes which planet the token will be placed on. <sup>6</sup>

- [Terraform (Promissory Note)] If Terraform is attached to a planet in The Fracture, that planet may be explored. <sup>6</sup>

- [Terraform (Promissory Note)] Terraform may be attached to Thunder’s Edge. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (Expedition): "Can Terraform be attached to Thunder's Edge?"
- [Terragenesis] A planet cannot contain more than one sleeper token. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (titans-terragenesis-limits (Community consensus)): "so a planet holds at most one"
  - Source 2 (titans-sleeper-details (Community consensus)): "A planet holds one sleeper"
- [Awaken] If the Ul player activates a system containing their sleeper tokens and the Xxcha player’s ships, the Ul player, as the active player, may resolve Awaken before the Xxcha player resolves the Nullification Field technology. Any resulting ground combat still occurs. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (titans-awaken-timing (Community consensus)): "the active Titans go first, so they can awaken before their turn is ended; the resulting ground combat still happens"
- [Awaken] A sleeper token is not removed when another player gains control of the planet it is on. The Ul player may still replace it using Awaken. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (titans-hel-titan-and-sleepers (Community consensus)): "it stays on a captured planet and can be awakened later"
  - Source 2 (titans-awaken-on-taken-planet (Community consensus)): "the sleeper stays until Awaken"
- [Hecatoncheires (Mech)] The Ul player may use the Deploy ability of a Hecatoncheires when placing a PDS with the Construction strategy card, including for each PDS placed with the primary ability. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (titans-construction-mech-deploy (Community consensus)): "Construction places PDS, so the Titans' deploy works there, even twice with the primary"
- [Awaken] If the Ul player retreats into a system containing their sleeper token, Awaken is not triggered, as the system is not activated. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (titans-retreat-no-awaken (Community consensus)): "a retreat places a command token but doesn't activate the system"
- [Hel–Titan (Unit)] A Hel–Titan is a structure, and so cannot be targeted by the Vuil’raith player’s Vortex faction technology. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (hel-titan-structure-and-production (Community consensus)): "the Vuil'raith vortex, which needs a non-structure, can't take it"
