### F_vuilraith.php

**Notes kept**

- [Devour] When an opponent’s Infantry II is destroyed during combat, the Vuil’raith player captures an infantry token, and the opponent rolls for resurrection, placing the destroyed infantry on the Infantry II unit upgrade card if successful. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Technology: Infantry 2 and Capture): "Q: What is the interaction between Infantry 2 and Capture? A: Both happen"
- [Crucible (Promissory Note)] Each gravity rift will still provide its usual +1 to each ship’s move value. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Vuil’raith Cabal: The Crucible): "the bonus would apply to all ships that can make it to the active system, including the bonuses from the promissory and the rift they are passing through."
- [Crucible (Promissory Note)] If a ship could move from its current system to the active system through a gravity rift if its move value were +2, it may do so using Crucible. This is true even if that ship could not reach the gravity rift without Crucible. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Vuil’raith Cabal: The Crucible): "Q: Can a ship benefit from the Vuil'raith Cabal promissory note, The Crucible, if it would not be able to reach a gravity rift on the way to the active system without it? A: Yes"
- [Crucible (Promissory Note)] For example, consider a series of systems X–S–G–Y. Only systems connected by a “–” are adjacent. System “G” is a gravity rift. Systems “X”, “S” and “Y” are standard systems with no movement restrictions. A ship with a move value of one is in system “X”. Were it to have +2 to its movement value, it could reach system “Y”. Currently, that ship may reach only system “S”. Despite this, if its owner activated system “Y” and played Crucible, the ship could move to that system. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Vuil’raith Cabal: The Crucible): "once a system has been activated and The Crucible has been played, the bonus would apply to all ships that can make it to the active system"
- [Vortex (Technology)] If a player has all their units of a particular type on the board, other than fighters or infantry, that type of unit belonging to that player cannot be targeted. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Vuil’raith Cabal: Vortex): "Q: Can Vortex be used on a ship if a player doesn't have any of those ships in their reinforcements? A: No, since they cannot fully resolve Vortex."
- [Dimensional Tear (Unit)] A system containing a Dimensional Tear is an anomaly. <sup>4</sup>
  - Edited from: This system is a gravity rift, and thus an anomaly.
  - Source 4 (Vuil’raith Cabal: Dimensional Tears): "Yes, any game effect that references an anomaly includes systems containing Dimensional Tears."
- [Dimensional Tear (Unit)] If a ship moves through or out of the same gravity rift multiple times, each instance will provide a +1 to movement. <sup>1</sup>
  - Edited from: If a ship moves through or out of multiple gravity rifts, and/or the same gravity rift multiple times, each instance will provide a +1 to movement.
  - Source 1 (41.3): "A gravity rift can affect the same ship multiple times during a single movement."
- [Dimensional Tear (Unit)] Multiple Dimensional Tears in a single system have no additional effects. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (41.4): "A system that contains multiple gravity rifts is treated as a single gravity rift."
- [The Terror Between (Flagship)] When The Terror Between is destroyed, it still captures units that were destroyed at the same time. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Vuil’raith Cabal: flagship): "Q: Does the Cabal Flagship capture other units that are destroyed in the same timing window in which it is destroyed? A: Yes."
- [The Stillness of Stars (Agent)] If a player loses their commodities immediately after replenishing them, most commonly via that player’s Trade Agreement promissory note, the Vuil’raith player may still target them. If they do, they still use that player’s full commodity value to determine which units may be captured. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Vuil’raith Cabal: agent and Trade Agreement): "Yes, the commodities would not be there but the agent could still be used to capture a ship up to the player’s commodity value."
- [The Stillness of Stars (Agent)] When The Stillness of Stars converts a player’s commodities to trade goods, those trade goods are not treated as being gained for the purpose of triggering other abilities. In particular, the Mentak player’s Pillage faction ability is not triggered by this ability. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Vuil’raith Cabal: agent and Pillage): "No, whenever commodities are converted to a player’s own trade good area, they are not considered gained."
- [Reanimator (Mech)] If the Vuil’raith player owns the Infantry II unit upgrade technology, and one is destroyed during ground combat on a planet with a Reanimator, the Vuil’raith player captures an infantry token, and they roll for resurrection, placing the destroyed infantry on the Infantry II unit upgrade card if successful. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Technology: Infantry 2 and Capture): "Q: What is the interaction between Infantry 2 and Capture? A: Both happen"
- [Al’raith Ix Ianovar (Breakthrough)] When The Fracture is brought into play by Al’raith Ix Ianovar, the Vuil’raith player places ingress tokens according to the synergy on the Cabal breakthrough. <sup>9</sup>
  - Edited from: When The Fracture is brought into play by Al’raith Ix Ianovar, the Vuil’raith player places ingress tokens according to the synergy on the Cabal breakthrough. For each color of technology in the synergy, they choose up to three planets with a matching technology specialty and place an ingress token in each of those planets’ systems.
  - Source 9 (General: Cabal Breakthrough): "A: According to cabal BT colors"
- [Al’raith Ix Ianovar (Breakthrough)] This uses the cabal breakthrough synergy colors method, not the one planet per color method. <sup>9</sup>
  - Source 9 (General: Cabal Breakthrough): "should cabal place them according to cabal synergy, or should they place them according to the same logic as Nekro breakthrough and other non breakthrough affects? A: According to cabal BT colors"

**Removed notes restored**

- [Dimensional Tear (Unit)] If the Dimensional Tear plastic figure is destroyed, the Dimensional Tear token is also removed. <sup>8</sup>
  - Trimmed from: If the Dimensional Tear plastic figure is destroyed or removed, the Dimensional Tear token is also removed.
  - Source 8 (p.16, Clarifications, Dimensional Tear Tokens): "If a space dock that has a dimensional tear token under it is destroyed, the dimensional tear token is removed from the board."
- [Amalgamation] If the Vuil’raith player produces multiple units, their Amalgamation ability may be applied to each. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (vuilraith-captured-units (Community consensus)): "Each captured unit or token gives one unit"
- [Amalgamation] Amalgamation does not change the cost of the produced units, only the resources spent. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (vuilraith-captured-units (Community consensus)): "produce one unit of that type without paying ... its printed cost still counts toward limits like Integrated Economy's."
- [Amalgamation] If the Vuil’raith player uses the ability of the Integrated Economy technology, Amalgamation will have no effect on the limit to the units they may build. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (vuilraith-captured-units (Community consensus)): "its printed cost still counts toward limits like Integrated Economy's."
- [Amalgamation] The Vuil’raith player produces one fighter or infantry without spending resources for each captured fighter or infantry they spend. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (vuilraith-captured-units (Community consensus)): "Each captured unit or token gives one unit, even fighters or infantry"
- [Dimensional Tear (Unit)] This system qualifies for the Make History and similar such objectives. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (vuilraith-normal-gravity-rifts (Community consensus)): "Those dock systems are anomalies, which counts for objectives like Making History."
- [Dimensional Tear (Unit)] If a Dimensional Tear is in a system that is normally a gravity rift (e.g. the Cormund system), the Vuil’raith player will not have to roll for removal when moving out of or through that system. There are no additional effects. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (vuilraith-dimensional-tear-rifts (Community consensus)): "No roll: a system with more than one rift counts as one gravity rift, and Dimensional Tear says your ships don't roll for that system's rift."
- [The Terror Between (Flagship)] Using the Sustain Damage ability of units is done before remaining hits are assigned. As such, if The Terror Between is destroyed by a Direct Hit action card, units destroyed by being assigned hits in the same round of combat, or from the same pool of Space Cannon hits, will not be captured. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (cabal-fleet-destroyed-by-yin-flagship (Community consensus)): "If the flagship was destroyed earlier, it isn't there to capture later losses."
- [The Terror Between (Flagship)] If ships are destroyed outside of combat, those ships will still be captured by The Terror Between. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (vuilraith-flagship-scope (Community consensus)): "Every other non-structure unit destroyed in its system, the Cabal's own included, even outside combat"
- [It Feeds on Carrion — Dimensional Anchor (Hero)] Units captured while resolving Dimensional Anchor are not destroyed. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (total-war-variant (Community consensus)): "Units captured without being destroyed, as by the Vuil'raith hero, add nothing."
- [It Feeds on Carrion — Dimensional Anchor (Hero)] Each non–fighter ship affected will roll only once, regardless of how many Dimensional Tears it is adjacent to. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (vuilraith-hero-one-roll (Community consensus)): "each non-fighter ship in or next to a dimensional tear rolls once, however many tears it touches."

**Notes added** (rulings that were not on the site before)

- [Al’raith Ix Ianovar (Breakthrough)] The Vuil’raith player cannot choose to roll for The Fracture when they gain Al’raith Ix Ianovar; the breakthrough’s ability replaces the roll. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (Vuil’raith Cabal / Al’raith Ix Ianovar): "No, the breakthrough replaces the roll with its own ability"
- [Al’raith Ix Ianovar (Breakthrough)] Ingress tokens cannot be placed in The Fracture. The Vuil’raith player cannot move an ingress token into a system in The Fracture, even if they have a space dock in that system. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (Vuil’raith Cabal / Al’raith Ix Ianovar): "No, ingress tokens cannot be placed in the Fracture."
- [Devour] Units destroyed by Space Cannon or Bombardment rolls are not destroyed during combat, and are not captured by Devour. Units destroyed by Anti–Fighter Barrage are destroyed during combat, and are captured. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (vuilraith-devour-not-cannon (Community consensus)): "those happen outside space and ground combat, so Devour doesn't see them; Anti-Fighter Barrage is part of combat and counts"
- [Amalgamation] A captured faction–specific unit counts as a unit of its base type; for example, a captured Prototype War Sun counts as a war sun. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (vuilraith-captured-units (Community consensus)): "Any captured unit of the base type works, a Prototype War Sun counting as a war sun"
- [Riftmeld] The returned captured unit may belong to any player, regardless of whether that player owns the corresponding unit upgrade. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (vuilraith-riftmeld-any-captured (Community consensus)): "any captured unit of the matching type lets you ignore that upgrade's prerequisites"
- [Amalgamation] The Vuil’raith player cannot produce a war sun using Amalgamation unless they own their war sun unit upgrade technology. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (vuilraith-captured-war-sun (Community consensus)): "you need the War Sun technology"

**Citations added to existing items**

- [Al’raith Ix Ianovar (Breakthrough)] When The Fracture is brought into play by Al’raith Ix Ianovar, the Vuil’raith player places ingress tokens according to the synergy on the Cabal breakthrough. now also cites <sup>6,9</sup>
  - Source 6 (Vuil’raith Cabal): "Cabal BT will place Fracture as if it were rolled for."
- [Crucible (Promissory Note)] Each gravity rift will still provide its usual +1 to each ship’s move value. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (stacking-movement-and-end-of-turn (Community consensus)): "Yes to both: movement bonuses stack"
- [Dimensional Tear (Unit)] A system containing a Dimensional Tear is an anomaly. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (vuilraith-dimensional-tear-rifts (Community consensus)): "it is simply a gravity rift, and counts as an anomaly for objectives."
- [Dimensional Tear (Unit)] Multiple Dimensional Tears in a single system have no additional effects. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (vuilraith-dimensional-tear-rifts (Community consensus)): "Two tears in one system don't stack the bonus either"
- [The Terror Between (Flagship)] When The Terror Between is destroyed, it still captures units that were destroyed at the same time. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (cabal-fleet-destroyed-by-yin-flagship (Community consensus)): "it captures every other unit destroyed in the same timing window, even if it is destroyed there too"

**Restored without a source** (marked * on the site)

- [Devour] The Vuil’raith player cannot capture the Ul player’s Hel Titan PDS. <sup>*</sup>
- [Amalgamation] If the Vuil’raith player has captured their own units, they may use their Amalgamation ability when producing a unit of that type, even of they have no other units of that type in their reinforcements. <sup>*</sup>
- [Amalgamation] If the Vuil’raith player has the Naalu or Yin player’s Alliance promissory note, they may spend one resource for one fighter or infantry, but spend a captured unit instead of that resource, then get one additional fighter or infantry for no cost, which will not count towards their production limit. <sup>*</sup>
- [Crucible (Promissory Note)] Crucible will provide an additional +1 to each ship’s move value, which will not increase if that ship moves through two or more gravity rifts. <sup>*</sup>
- [Crucible (Promissory Note)] A ship that moves through or out of no gravity rifts will apply +0 to its move value. <sup>*</sup>
- [Crucible (Promissory Note)] A ship that moves through or out of two gravity rifts will apply +3 to its move value. <sup>*</sup>
- [Crucible (Promissory Note)] A ship that moves through or out of three gravity rifts will apply +4 to its move value. <sup>*</sup>
- [Crucible (Promissory Note)] And so on. <sup>*</sup>
- [Crucible (Promissory Note)] If a player plays both Crucible and the Nav Suite action card during the same tactical action, they will still apply +1 to the move value of their ships that move through or out of a gravity rift. <sup>*</sup>
- [Vortex (Technology)] Vortex cannot be used if there are no units that can be targeted. <sup>*</sup>
- [Vortex (Technology)] If another player is blockading a Dimensional Tear, their units cannot be targeted with Vortex. <sup>*</sup>
- [Dimensional Tear (Unit)] If a Dimensional Tear is in a system with a Nebula, then the +1 to move values will be applied after the nebula sets each ship’s move value to 1. <sup>*</sup>
- [The Stillness of Stars (Agent)] The Vuil’raith player cannot capture a unit without a cost. Notably, they cannot capture a PDS, a space dock, or a war sun of a player without their war sun unit upgrade. <sup>*</sup>
- [The Stillness of Stars (Agent)] If the Vuil’raith player chooses to capture a fighter or infantry, they will capture one, not two. <sup>*</sup>
- [The Stillness of Stars (Agent)] When the primary ability of the Trade strategy card is resolved, the Vuil’raith player must choose if they will use The Stillness of Stars or not after the active player has replenished their commodities, but before players are chosen to perform the secondary ability without spending a command token. <sup>*</sup>
- [The Stillness of Stars (Agent)] When the secondary ability of the Trade strategy card is resolved, the Vuil’raith player must choose if they will use The Stillness of Stars or not after the current player has replenished their commodities, but before the next player has decided if they will spend a command token to perform the secondary. <sup>*</sup>
- [It Feeds on Carrion — Dimensional Anchor (Hero)] If a player’s units are blockading one of the Vuil’raith player’s Dimensional Tears, dice will not be rolled for that player’s units when resolving Dimensional Anchor. <sup>*</sup>
- [It Feeds on Carrion — Dimensional Anchor (Hero)] The player that owns the ground forces and fighters chooses which are removed. They are not assigned to particular ships beforehand. <sup>*</sup>
- [It Feeds on Carrion — Dimensional Anchor (Hero)] If the Nekro player has used a Valefar Assimilator faction technology to copy Dimensional Tear II, ships in systems containing or adjacent to the Nekro player’s space docks will also have to roll for capture when resolving Dimensional Anchor. This includes the Nekro player’s own ships. <sup>*</sup>
- [Reanimator (Mech)] If the Vuil’raith player’s infantry on a planet with a Reanimator are destroyed outside of combat, such as with the Plague action card, those infantry will be captured. <sup>*</sup>
- [Al’raith Ix Ianovar (Breakthrough)] When Al’raith Ix Ianovar causes The Fracture to enter play, all the ingress tokens will be placed before the Vuil’raith player chooses which tokens they wish to move into gravity rifts. <sup>*</sup>
- [Al’raith Ix Ianovar (Breakthrough)] The Vuil’raith player may move the ingress tokens into systems that contain their Dimensional Tears. <sup>*</sup>

Systems “A”, “B” and “C” have dimensional tears, while system “M” does not. The Vuil’raith player has a carrier with move one in system “C” and a ground force in system “A”. They could activate system “M” and move the carrier along the path “C” → “B” → “A” → “B” → “C” → “M”, picking up the ground force from system “A”. This path would make the carriers move value 1+5, which is more than enough for this movement. _(no source)_

### F_winnu.php

**Notes kept**

- [Lazax Gate Folding (Technology)] The Winnu player may become neighbors with other players via Lazax Gate Folding. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (FAQ (Mentak Coalition), p.44): "Can the Mentak Coalition use the “Pillage” faction ability to steal trade goods when they are neighbors with another faction as a result of the “Lazax Gate Folding” faction technology"
- [Salai Sai Corian (Flagship)] During a combat against the Nekro player in a system containing each player’s flagships, the Salai Sai Corian will count the Nekro player’s infantry participating in the combat when determining how many dice to roll. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (FAQ (Nekro Virus), p.43): "Yes. The “Salai Sai Corian” would get one additional die per infantry."
- [Rickar Rickani (Commander)] If a system meets two (or more) of the conditions listed (such as by attaching the Nano–Forge relic to Mecatol Rex), Rickar Rickani will only apply +2 to combat rolls, not +4 (or +6). <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Winnu, Rickar Rickani): "No, the commander only triggers once no matter how many conditions are met, +2 is the max."

**Removed notes restored**

- [Acquiescence (Promissory Note)] If either strategy card had trade goods on it at the start of the strategy phase, those trade goods remain with the player that originally chose the strategy card. <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (doc4.txt, Milty, 10/30/2018): "In both the situations you mentioned there (Quantum Datahub Node and Acquiescence) the player who picked the strategy card originally would get the trade goods."
- [Lazax Gate Folding (Technology)] While Lazax Gate Folding is exhausted, the wormhole passive effect still applies if its conditions are met. <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (doc4.txt, Falcone1983, Jun 7, 2018 (also wekker, 09/06/2018)): "Since the passive portion of LGF doesn’t require exhausting the card as part of a cost, you can still use it."
- [Lazax Gate Folding (Technology)] Lazax Gate Folding may cause the Mecatol Rex system to be adjacent to other systems containing an alpha or beta wormhole for all players during the Winnu player’s tactical actions. <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (doc4.txt, Vinci, 12/11/2018): "There was a question the other day as to whether only Winnu get the advantages of their Lazax Gate Folding Tech during their tactical actions."
  - Source 5 (doc4.txt, Vinci, 12/11/2018): "rules as written, the Mentak would be able to pillage the transaction. Note that this is not the case for a similar question that has often arisen with Creuss."
  - Source 5 (doc4.txt, Vinci, 12/11/2018): "2. Xxcha can also fire. Same idea as above."
- [Lazax Gate Folding (Technology)] Other players may use the Deep Space Cannon ability of their units in systems containing alpha or beta wormholes during the Space Cannon Offense step of the Winnu player’s turn if the Mecatol Rex system is the active system. <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (doc4.txt, Vinci, 12/11/2018): "PDS: Xxcha hold Mecatol. Winnu has PDS2 on Quann, Xxcha has PDS2 on Lodor. Winnu activates Mecatol. Does only Winnu get to fire or does Xxcha get to also?"
  - Source 5 (doc4.txt, Vinci, 12/11/2018): "2. Xxcha can also fire."
- [Lazax Gate Folding (Technology)] A player may retreat to a system containing an alpha or beta wormhole from the Mecatol Rex system during the Winnu player’s tactical action. <sup>5</sup>
  - Trimmed from: A player may retreat to a system containing an alpha or beta wormhole from the Mecatol Rex system, or vice versa, during the Winnu player’s tactical action.
  - Source 5 (doc4.txt, Vinci, 12/11/2018): "could Creuss retreat to Lodor or use Dimensional Splicer?"
  - Source 5 (doc4.txt, Vinci, 12/11/2018): "But yes - they can also retreat to Lodor."
- [Reclamation] Placing the structure will occur after the Production step. If the Winnu player places a Space Dock, they cannot produce out of it during the same action. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (winnu-mech-hopes-end (Community consensus)): "Likewise, a dock placed by Winnu's Reclamation comes after the tactical action, too late to produce in it."
- [Salai Sai Corian (Flagship)] If the Winnu player’s opponent has only fighters participating in the combat, the Salai Sai Corian will roll no dice. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (winnu-flagship-dice (Community consensus)): "it rolls one die per enemy non-fighter ship"
- [Mathis Mathinus — Imperial Seal (Hero)] A player chosen to perform the secondary ability must still spend a command token from their strategy pool to do so, except for the Leadership strategy card and potentially the Trade strategy card. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (winnu-and-naaz-rokha-heroes-secondaries (Community consensus)): "players who follow pay the secondary's normal costs."

**Notes added** (rulings that were not on the site before)

- [Hegemonic Trade Policy (Technology)] The text of Hegemonic Trade Policy is changed to: “Exhaust this card when 1 or more of your units use Production; swap the resource and influence values of 1 planet you control during that use of Production.” <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (Errata: Hegemonic Trade Policy): "swap the resource and influence values of 1 planet you control during that use of ‘Production.’"
- [Lazax Gate Folding (Technology)] The action ability of Lazax Gate Folding cannot be used if the Winnu player does not control Mecatol Rex. <sup>3,5</sup>
  - Source 5 (Falcone1983, Apr 23, 2018): "The intent is that the action is unusable if you do no control Mecatol Rex."
  - Source 3 (Component Actions example card): "ACTION: If you control Mecatol Rex, exhaust this card to place 1 infantry"
- [Reclaimer (Mech)] If the Winnu player places a Reclaimer with the Imperial Arms Vault ability of Hope’s End, it cannot use its ability to place a structure that turn, as that happens at the end of the turn, after the tactical action has been resolved. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (winnu-mech-hopes-end (Community consensus)): "Hope's End resolves at the end of your turn, after the window where the mech's ability triggers"

**Citations added to existing items**

- [Lazax Gate Folding (Technology)] The Winnu player may become neighbors with other players via Lazax Gate Folding. now also cites <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (doc4.txt, Vinci, 12/11/2018): "Though not necessarily thematically (or mechanically) intended, rules as written, the Mentak would be able to pillage the transaction."
- [Lazax Gate Folding (Technology)] While Lazax Gate Folding is exhausted, the wormhole passive effect still applies if its conditions are met. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (lazax-gate-folding-winnu (Community consensus)): "The passive part ... doesn't need the card ready, so it works while exhausted."
- [Lazax Gate Folding (Technology)] The action ability of Lazax Gate Folding cannot be used if the Winnu player does not control Mecatol Rex. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (lazax-gate-folding-winnu (Community consensus)): "The action needs you to control Mecatol Rex, so it can't be used as a stall."
- [Salai Sai Corian (Flagship)] During a combat against the Nekro player in a system containing each player’s flagships, the Salai Sai Corian will count the Nekro player’s infantry participating in the combat when determining how many dice to roll. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (nekro-flagship-combat-details (Community consensus)): "they count as non-fighter ships for things like the Winnu flagship's extra dice (per the LRR FAQ)"

**Notes kept**

- [Peace Accords] A planet is adjacent to both the system it is in, and every system adjacent to that. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (6.2): "A unit or planet is adjacent to all system tiles that are adjacent to the system tile that contains that unit or planet."
  - Source 1 (6.3): "A planet is treated as being adjacent to the system that contains that planet."
  - Source 1 (FAQ (Xxcha Kingdom), p.43): "Yes, a planet is treated as being adjacent to its own system."
- [Nullification Field (Technology)] Once the Xxcha player resolves the ability of Nullification Field, the active player cannot use any “after you activate a system” abilities. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Mahact Gene Sorcerers, Il Na Viroset (question names Nullification Field)): "Any ability that ends your turn should be treated as ending your turn when they occur, and no further abilities during that same trigger window can take place."
- [Nullification Field (Technology)] Other players, including the Xxcha player, cannot use any “after another player activates a system that…” abilities. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Mahact Gene Sorcerers, Il Na Viroset (question names Nullification Field)): "no further abilities during that same trigger window can take place."
- [Nullification Field (Technology)] The active player may still use any “at the end of your turn” abilities. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Mahact Gene Sorcerers, Il Na Viroset (question names Nullification Field)): "End of turn abilities can still be used."
- [Ggrocuto Rinn (Agent)] A planet is adjacent to both the system it is in, and every system adjacent to that. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (6.2): "A unit or planet is adjacent to all system tiles that are adjacent to the system tile that contains that unit or planet."
  - Source 1 (6.3): "A planet is treated as being adjacent to the system that contains that planet."
- [Ggrocuto Rinn (Agent)] A planet must be exhausted to be targeted by Ggrocuto Rinn. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Xxcha Kingdom, Ggrocuto Rinn): "The target planet must be exhausted."
- [Xxekir Grom — Political Data Nexus (Hero)] If the Xxcha player draws the Covert Legislation agenda, they will only draw a hidden agenda if they choose to reveal it. If the Xxcha player is not the speaker, the speaker will view the hidden agenda. <sup>4</sup>
  - Edited from: If the Xxcha player draws the Covert Legislation agenda, they will only draw a hidden agenda if they choose to reveal it. If the Xxcha player is not the speaker, the speaker will view the hidden agenda, but the Xxcha player will not see it until it is either discarded from Quash, or resolved.
  - Source 4 (Xxcha Kingdom, hero): "Xxcha would only get to see the agenda tied to Covert Legislation if it was one of the 2 agendas selected to resolve and they are the speaker, otherwise the speaker would see the agenda."
- [Xxekir Grom — Political Data Nexus (Hero)] When the Xxcha player chooses and reveals an agenda, they may then use their Quash ability. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Xxcha Kingdom, Xxekir Grom): "Yes, the Xxcha player can play riders, and use their quash ability during their hero"
- [Xxekir Grom — Political Data Nexus (Hero)] After the Xxcha player chooses and reveals an agenda, they may play any rider action cards on the revealed agenda. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Xxcha Kingdom, Xxekir Grom): "Yes, the Xxcha player can play riders"
- [Xxekir Grom — Political Data Nexus (Hero)] When an agenda outcome with an immediate effect resolves, all players resolve the effect. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Xxcha Kingdom, Xxekir Grom): "The intent is that players still resolve agendas that the Xxcha player chooses off of their Hero."
- [Xxekir Grom — Political Data Nexus (Hero)] If an agenda would give multiple players a victory point, those players gain that victory point in initiative order, regardless of the Xxcha player’s initiative. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Xxcha Kingdom, hero): "Initiative order determines the winner. Initiative order is always the lowest initiative player onwards, regardless of who the active player is."
- [Xxekir Grom — Political Data Nexus (Hero)] The effect of the Checks and Balances agenda that occurs “at the end of this agenda phase” is ignored. <sup>4</sup>
  - Edited from: Effects from agenda outcomes that occur “at the end of this agenda phase” are ignored.
  - Source 4 (Xxcha Kingdom, Checks and Balances): "This effect does not trigger if it happens during the Xxcha Hero."
- [Xxekir Grom — Political Data Nexus Ω(Hero)] During the status phase, public and secret objectives are scored simultaneously. The Xxcha player cannot score a public objective, unlock Xxekir Grom, and then use Political Data Nexus Ω in order to score a secret objective, or vice versa. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Xxcha Kingdom, Political Data Nexus Omega): "Scoring in the status phase is done all at once, the unlock condition of heroes is not checked until the score objectives step of the status phase is complete."
- [Xxekir Grom — Political Data Nexus Ω(Hero)] The combined value may be spent as either influence or resources, not both. <sup>4</sup>
  - Edited from: The combined value may be spent as either influence or resources, not both, and cannot be split between the two.
  - Source 4 (Xxcha Kingdom, Political Data Nexus Omega): "the Xxcha Kingdom player chooses to spend those as one or the other, not both."
- [Xxekir Grom — Political Data Nexus Ω(Hero)] Political Data Nexus Ω does not change the value used by abilities that reference a planet’s resource value; the printed resource value of the planet is used. <sup>4</sup>
  - Edited from: Political Data Nexus Ω only changes the spendable influence and resources. It does not change the value for any other game effect.
  - Source 4 (Xxcha Kingdom, Uprising): "When using an ability that references “resource value”, the printed resource value of the planet is used."

  - Trimmed from: If Quash is used after any Political Secret promissory notes have been played, those are immediately returned and will have no effect on the replacement agenda.
  - Source 5 (doc4.txt, sigmazero13, Jun 6, 2018): "Dane: It counts as being resolved."
  - Source 5 (doc4.txt, sigmazero13, Jun 6, 2018): "Political Secret says the effects last until the Agenda is resolved."
  - Source 1 (lrr.txt FAQ p.44): "Yes. It is a new agenda and thus the effect of the player’s “Political Secret” is ended."
- [Quash] Each agenda is considered separate for the purpose of limiting each pair of players to one transaction per agenda. <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (doc4.txt, sigmazero13, Jun 19, 2018): "If players (for some reason) made transactions prior to the Quash, does the new agenda "reset" this?"
  - Source 5 (doc4.txt, sigmazero13, Jun 19, 2018): "I would also say that they could perform new transactions"
- [Quash] Quash may be used on the replacement agenda. <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (doc4.txt, sigmazero13, Jun 19, 2018): "Dane: Yes, the other Agenda can be Quashed."
- [Political Favor (Promissory Note)] If the Xxcha player has no command tokens in their strategy pool, Political Favor cannot be played. <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (doc4.txt, reddit faction promissory notes thread (2019, final follow-up superseding the earlier reversal)): "The command tokens must be present in order to resolve these PNs, as was the understanding before my recent ruling."
- [Instinct Training (Technology)] If a player has a second copy of an action card, they may play it if the first was cancelled by Instinct Training. <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (doc4.txt, sigmazero13, Jan 11, 2018 (question names "Xxcha Nullification Field", i.e. the Xxcha action-card-cancelling tech, Instinct Training)): "If an action card is cancelled with "Sabotage" (or the Xxcha Nullification Field), can another copy of the same action card be played?"
  - Source 5 (doc4.txt, sigmazero13, Jan 11, 2018): "Because the card was cancelled, yes, you can play another copy of the same action card."
- [Quash] Quash, Political Favor, the Political Secret promissory note, and the Veto action card are all played in the same timing window, before the rider timing window. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (when-effects-before-after-effects (Community consensus)): "'when' effects (Quash, Veto, Political Favor, Political Secret) resolve first, then 'after' effects (Riders, Assassinate Representative, Galactic Threat), then voting."
- [Political Favor (Promissory Note)] Quash, Political Favor, the Political Secret promissory note, and the Veto action card are all played in the same timing window, before the rider timing window. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (when-effects-before-after-effects (Community consensus)): "'when' effects (Quash, Veto, Political Favor, Political Secret) resolve first, then 'after' effects (Riders, Assassinate Representative, Galactic Threat), then voting."
- [Instinct Training (Technology)] Instinct Training may cancel a Sabotage action card. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (instinct-training (Community consensus)): "it cancels any other player's action card, Sabotage included"
- [Loncara Ssodu (Flagship)] During the Space Cannon Offense supstep of a tactical action, the active player resolves the Space Cannon abilities of their units first. If the Xxcha player is not the active player, and the Loncara Ssodu is destroyed by another player’s space cannon roll, it will not resolve its own Space Cannon ability. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (space-cannon-one-player-at-a-time (Community consensus)): "so a unit destroyed earlier, such as an Xxcha flagship, never gets to shoot."
- [Elder Qanoj (Commander)] A planet with zero influence may be used to cast one additional vote. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (xxcha-commander-vs-cannot-vote (Community consensus)): "Each planet you exhaust to vote gives 1 extra vote, so even a 0-influence planet gives 1."
- [Elder Qanoj (Commander)] The Xxcha player may play rider action cards and vote on the same agenda. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (xxcha-commander-vs-cannot-vote (Community consensus)): "so Xxcha can vote despite a rider or Political Secret."

  - Source 2 (xxcha-hero-follow-up-effects (Community consensus)): "A player elected for Public Execution can still vote in the next agenda phase."
- [Xxekir Grom — Political Data Nexus (Hero)] Other players may still perform one transaction total with the Xxcha player during this turn, if they are neighbors. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (xxcha-hero-follow-up-effects (Community consensus)): "Transactions during the hero's action still need neighbors, since it isn't the agenda phase."
- [Xxekir Grom — Political Data Nexus (Hero)] The Drive the Debate objective cannot be scored while resolving Political Data Nexus. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (xxcha-hero-follow-up-effects (Community consensus)): "Agenda-phase secret objectives such as Drive the Debate can't be scored from it, since it isn't the agenda phase."
- [Xxekir Grom — Political Data Nexus Ω(Hero)] A space dock will not add the influence value of the planet it is on to its Production value. <sup>2</sup>
  - Trimmed from: A space dock will not add the influence value of the planet it is on to its Production value.
  - Source 2 (xxcha-combined-values-ability (Community consensus)): "It doesn't change printed values, so it doesn't raise a space dock's Production."
- [Indomitus (Mech)] During the Space Cannon Offense supstep of a tactical action, the active player resolves the Space Cannon abilities of their units first. If the Xxcha player is not the active player, and their ships are removed by another player’s space cannon roll, they must immediately remove units to meet their capacity limit. They will not resolve the Space Cannon abilities of any of their removed mechs. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (space-cannon-one-player-at-a-time (Community consensus)): "one player at a time, starting with the active player and then the others in order."
  - Source 2 (capacity-checked-outside-combat (Community consensus)): "Immediately whenever it isn't combat, for example after each player's Space Cannon Offense volley, before the next player fires."

**Restored without a source** (marked * on the site)

- [Instinct Training (Technology)] If an action card is cancelled by Instinct Training, no costs are paid. <sup>*</sup>
- [Instinct Training (Technology)] A player playing an action card announces the following before Instinct Training may be played: <sup>*</sup>
- [Instinct Training (Technology)] Any targeted planets, system, units, players, cards, outcomes, and/or other such objects. <sup>*</sup>
- [Instinct Training (Technology)] The value of any variable cost to be paid. <sup>*</sup>
- [Instinct Training (Technology)] Any dice are rolled and any cards are drawn only after all other players has declined to play Instinct Training. <sup>*</sup>
- [Instinct Training (Technology)] If an action card instructs a player to research a technology, that player need not announce what technology they are researching until all other players has declined to play Instinct Training. <sup>*</sup>
- [Instinct Training (Technology)] If an action card is played that will have an effect later, such as a rider, that card may only be cancelled by Instinct Training when it is originally played. <sup>*</sup>
- [Instinct Training (Technology)] If the action card that was cancelled by Instinct Training was to be used to perform a component action, the active player must perform a different action, or pass. <sup>*</sup>
- [Instinct Training (Technology)] If the component action was to be the second action the active player was to perform on their turn, through an effect such as the Fleet Logistics technology, the active player may end their turn without performing a second action and without passing. <sup>*</sup>
- [Xxekir Grom — Political Data Nexus (Hero)] If the Xxcha player draws, reveals and resolves the Miscount Disclosed agenda, they cast one vote for an outcome of the elected law, and resolve it. <sup>*</sup>
- [Xxekir Grom — Political Data Nexus (Hero)] The Xxcha player chooses the order the two agendas are resolved. <sup>*</sup>
- [Xxekir Grom — Political Data Nexus (Hero)] The two agendas are revealed before either is resolved. <sup>*</sup>
- [Xxekir Grom — Political Data Nexus (Hero)] The Xxcha player will resolve all abilities that trigger when or after an agenda is revealed for the first agenda before revealing the second agenda. <sup>*</sup>
- [Xxekir Grom — Political Data Nexus (Hero)] If the Representative Government law is in play, it will have no effect on the Xxcha player as they resolve Political Data Nexus. <sup>*</sup>
- [Xxekir Grom — Political Data Nexus (Hero)] If a third law is put into play, the Dictate Policy objective cannot be scored until the agenda phase. <sup>*</sup>
- [Xxekir Grom — Political Data Nexus (Hero)] Effects from agenda outcomes that occur “at the start of the next strategy phase” will still occur. <sup>*</sup>
- [Xxekir Grom — Political Data Nexus Ω(Hero)] If the Xxcha player owns a planet with three influence and three resources, they cannot score the Amass Wealth objective by exhausting just it and spending three trade goods. <sup>*</sup>
- [Xxekir Grom — Political Data Nexus Ω(Hero)] The resource values of the planets the Xxcha player controls will not contribute to unlocking Elder Qanoj. <sup>*</sup>
- [Xxekir Grom — Political Data Nexus Ω(Hero)] Political Data Nexus Ω does not apply when scoring the Establish Hegemony or Hoard Raw Materials objectives. <sup>*</sup>
- [Xxekir Grom — Planetary Defense Nexus ΩΩ(Hero)] The units may be placed on a readied planet. <sup>*</sup>
- [Xxekir Grom — Planetary Defense Nexus ΩΩ(Hero)] Multiple units may be placed on the same planet. <sup>*</sup>
- [Archon’s Gift (Breakthrough)] A source of both influence and resources, such as a planet, may be spent for one or the other, but not both. <sup>*</sup>
- [Archon’s Gift (Breakthrough)] For example, Archon Tau will provide one resource or one influence, not two. <sup>*</sup>
- [Archon’s Gift (Breakthrough)] For example, if the Xxcha player wishes to score the Amass Wealth objective, each planet they exhaust will contribute to either the resource requirement or the influence requirement, but cannot partially contribute to both. <sup>*</sup>
- [Archon’s Gift (Breakthrough)] Archon’s Gift only changes how a planet’s influence and resources may be spent. It does not change the value for any other game effect. <sup>*</sup>
- [Archon’s Gift (Breakthrough)] A space dock cannot use the influence value of the planet it is on to calculate its Production value. <sup>*</sup>
- [Archon’s Gift (Breakthrough)] The influence value of a planet will not increase the number of units the Xxcha player may produce when using the Integrated Economy technology. <sup>*</sup>
- [Archon’s Gift (Breakthrough)] The resource values of the planets the Xxcha player controls will not contribute to unlocking Elder Qanoj. <sup>*</sup>
- [Archon’s Gift (Breakthrough)] Archon’s Gift does not apply when scoring the Establish Hegemony or Hoard Raw Materials objectives. <sup>*</sup>
- [Archon’s Gift (Breakthrough)] The Xxcha player cannot use the influence value of a planet when they gain trade goods with the Mining Initiative action card. Other players cannot use the influence value when they gain trade goods from the Uprising action card if they choose to exhaust one of the Xxcha player’s planets. <sup>*</sup>

### F_yin.php

**Notes kept**

- [Devotion] When resolving Devotion, the Yin player chooses which ship is assigned the hit. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (Errata, Devotion): "to produce 1 hit and assign it to 1 of your opponent’s ships in that system."
- [Devotion] The Yin cannot choose their own ships as targets. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (Errata, Devotion): "assign it to 1 of your opponent’s ships in that system."
- [Devotion] The Shields Holding action card may be used to cancel the hit. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (FAQ appendix, Action Cards (Shields Holding)): "Can the “Shields Holding” action card be used to cancel hits from abilities that occur during combat, such as “Ambush,” “Dimensional Splicer,” and “Devotion?” A: Yes."
- [Greyfire Mutagen Ω (Promissory Note)] A player may receive Greyfire Mutagen Ω in a transaction during a ground combat. If received at the start of ground combat, that player may play it immediately. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (94.1a): "A player can resolve a transaction at any time during their turn, even during a combat."
  - Source 1 (FAQ appendix, General): "a promissory note with “At the start of your turn:” timing may be immediately played if the transaction occurred within the “start of turn” timing window."
- [Brother Milor (Agent)] If all of a player’s ships are destroyed during combat, they may still place ships with this ability. If they do, combat will continue. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Yin Brotherhood, Brother Milor): "Does the Yin Brotherhood agent, Brother Milor, keep combat going after the last ship is destroyed? A: Yes."
- [Brother Milor (Agent)] If all ships in the system are destroyed by hits produced from a space cannon roll, the player that produced those hits may score the Turn Their Fleets to Dust secret objective before the new fighters are placed. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Objectives, when secret objectives are scored): "If the last ship in a system is destroyed, TTFTD could be scored for destroying the last ship, then after the Yin agent would trigger."
- [Brother Milor Ω (Agent)] Brother Milor Ω may only be used during the action phase. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Yin Brotherhood, Brother Milor Omega in Agenda Phase): "Brother Milor Omega can only be used during the action phase."
- [Brother Milor Ω (Agent)] If all ships in the system are destroyed by hits produced from a space cannon roll, the player that produced those hits may score the Turn Their Fleets to Dust secret objective before the new fighters are placed. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Objectives, when secret objectives are scored): "If the last ship in a system is destroyed, TTFTD could be scored for destroying the last ship, then after the Yin agent would trigger."
- [Brother Milor Ω (Agent)] If the Yin player uses Brother Milor Ω when a unit is destroyed that is both a ground force and a ship due to some game effect, that unit’s owner may place two fighters or two infantry. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Yin Brotherhood, Brother Milor Omega and flagships): "The owner of the unit can choose whether to place 2 infantry or 2 fighters when using Brother Milor Omega"
- [Brother Milor Ω (Agent)] If placed this way during a space combat, any newly placed infantry cannot participate. If placed this way during a ground combat, any newly placed fighters cannot participate. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Yin Brotherhood, Brother Milor Omega and flagships): "units placed this way can only continue to participate in space combat if fighters are placed, and can only continue to participate in ground combat if infantry are placed"
- [Brother Omar (Commander)] The Yin player may choose to produce one infantry for one resource. If they do, they may produce one additional infantry. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Yin Brotherhood, Brother Omar): "both of these commanders allow the player to choose to only build a single fighter/infantry for 1 resource and gain an additional unit of that type each time they do."
- [Dannel of the Tenth Ω — Quantum Dissemination Ω (Hero)] Only ground combats are resolved on the chosen planets, not the full steps of an invasion. <sup>4</sup>
  - Edited from: Only the Commit Ground Forces, Ground Combat and Establish Control steps of an invasion are resolved.
  - Source 4 (Yin Brotherhood, Quantum Dissemination Omega): "should indicate to resolve ground combats on those planets, not full invasion steps."
- [Dannel of the Tenth Ω — Quantum Dissemination Ω (Hero)] The Parley action card may be used on one planet when the Yin player resolves Quantum Dissemination. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (Yin Brotherhood, Quantum Dissemination Omega): "Parley can be played on one of the planets."
- [Moyin’s Ashes (Mech)] A Deploy ability may only be resolved for units in a player’s reinforcements. If all four Moyin’s Ashes are already on the board, no more may be deployed. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (30.2): "A player can only resolve a deploy ability to place a unit that is in their reinforcements."

However, Greyfire Mutagen Ω cannot be played twice in one timing window. The active player cannot play Greyfire Mutagen Ω again during the same ground combat. <sup>*</sup>
- [Greyfire Mutagen Ω (Promissory Note)] If an invasion involves ground combat on multiple planets, Greyfire Mutagen Ω may be played at the start of each of them. <sup>*</sup>
- [Impulse Core (Technology)] When resolving Impulse Core, the Yin player’s opponent chooses which ship is assigned the hit. <sup>*</sup>
- [Yin Spinner Ω (Technology)] The two infantry must be placed together. <sup>*</sup>
- [Van Hauge (Flagship)] When the Van Hauge is destroyed, it will not destroy any of the Saar player’s Floating Factories present in the system. <sup>*</sup>
- [Van Hauge (Flagship)] The Van Hauge will not destroy ground forces in the system. However, each player must then remove ground forces, if necessary, from the space area of that system to meet capacity limits. <sup>*</sup>
- [Brother Milor (Agent)] If all ships in the system are destroyed, and there are excess hits that have not been assigned to a ship, those hits will lapse, and cannot be assigned to the newly placed fighters. <sup>*</sup>
- [Brother Milor (Agent)] If a ship uses its Sustain Damage ability, and is then destroyed by a Direct Hit action card, then any remaining hits may be assigned to any placed fighters. <sup>*</sup>
- [Brother Milor Ω (Agent)] If all units in the combat are destroyed, and there are excess hits that have not been assigned to a unit, those hits will lapse, and cannot be assigned to the newly placed units. <sup>*</sup>
- [Brother Milor Ω (Agent)] If a ship uses its Sustain Damage ability, and is then destroyed by a Direct Hit action card, then any remaining hits may be assigned to any placed fighters. <sup>*</sup>
- [Brother Milor Ω (Agent)] If all ground forces on a planet are destroyed by hits produced from a bombardment roll, the player that produced those hits may score the Make an Example of Their World secret objective before the new infantry are placed. <sup>*</sup>
- [Brother Omar (Commander)] If the Regulated Conscription law is in play, the Yin player may produce two infantry for one resource. This will count one towards their Production limit. <sup>*</sup>
- [Brother Omar (Commander)] If a game effect instructs the Yin player to produce units without using the Production ability, they may only produce infantry if that game effect allows them to produce infantry. <sup>*</sup>
- [Brother Omar Ω (Commander)] The faction abilities to unlock Brother Omar are Indoctrination or Devotion. <sup>*</sup>
- [Brother Omar Ω (Commander)] If another player owns a faction specific unit upgrade, it cannot be chosen in order to gain the generic version of that unit upgrade by using Brother Omar. <sup>*</sup>
- [Brother Omar Ω (Commander)] If another player has the Yin player’s Alliance promissory note, they cannot use it to research a faction specific unit upgrade. <sup>*</sup>
- [Dannel of the Tenth — Spinner Overdrive (Hero)] The Yin player may ready a planet they control containing zero infantry. <sup>*</sup>
- [Dannel of the Tenth Ω — Quantum Dissemination Ω (Hero)] The Yin player may commit infantry to Mallice even if the wormhole nexus has not been flipped to its active side. Doing so will cause the wormhole nexus to flip. <sup>*</sup>
- [Dannel of the Tenth Ω — Quantum Dissemination Ω (Hero)] The Yin player commits all infantry before resolving any combats. <sup>*</sup>
- [Dannel of the Tenth Ω — Quantum Dissemination Ω (Hero)] The Yin player may use their Indoctrination ability and their mech’s Deploy ability. <sup>*</sup>
- [Dannel of the Tenth Ω — Quantum Dissemination Ω (Hero)] The Yin player does not activate the systems containing the planets that they are committing infantry to. As such, any effects that trigger “when/after a player activates a system” do not trigger. <sup>*</sup>
- [Dannel of the Tenth Ω — Quantum Dissemination Ω (Hero)] If the Yin player has no ships with capacity in the planet’s system, then the infantry will be removed from the board. <sup>*</sup>
- [Dannel of the Tenth Ω — Quantum Dissemination Ω (Hero)] If the Yin player does have ships with capacity in the planet’s system, then the infantry will be placed in the space area of the system. The Yin player might then need to remove infantry and/or fighters from the system to satisfy the capacity limit. <sup>*</sup>
- [Moyin’s Ashes (Mech)] If a Moyin’s Ashes is destroyed during combat, another may be deployed in a later combat during the same invasion. <sup>*</sup>
- [Moyin’s Ashes (Mech)] The removed unit must still be an infantry. <sup>*</sup>
- [Moyin’s Ashes (Mech)] The Deploy ability has a total cost of three influence. The Yin player may exhaust a single planet with three or more influence to pay this cost. <sup>*</sup>

### F_yssaril.php

**Notes kept**

- [Scheming] Scheming applies whenever the Yssaril player draws action cards. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (FAQ (General): Neural Motivator and Scheming): "The Yssaril’s “Scheming” ability, however, is triggered each time that action cards are drawn."
- [Spy Net (Promissory Note)] A player may receive Spy Net in a transaction during their turn. If received at the start of that player’s turn, that player may play it immediately. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (94.1a): "A player can resolve a transaction at any time during their turn, even during a combat."
  - Source 1 (FAQ (General): card acquired from a transaction during its timing window): "A: Yes. For example, a promissory note with “At the start of your turn:” timing may be immediately played if the transaction occurred within the “start of turn” timing window."

**Removed notes restored**

- [Spy Net (Promissory Note)] The active player may perform a transaction with each other player at most once per turn. As such, the active player cannot receive Spy Net more than once per turn. <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p.17, Neighbors, Transactions, and Deals): "The active player may negotiate only once with each of their neighbors per turn. After a transaction has been finalized, no other transactions may occur between those players that turn."
- [Scheming] The Yssaril player will draw only one additional action card, regardless of how many action cards they are instructed to draw. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (Ral Nel Consortium (Kan Kip Rel copied by Yssaril)): "Draw 3 instead of 2"
- [Scheming] The discarded action card may be any card in the Yssaril player’s hand; it does not have to be one of the cards they just drew. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (Ral Nel Consortium (Kan Kip Rel copied by Yssaril)): "discard 1 from the 3 drawn or hand to scheming"
- [Scheming] Effects that give the Yssaril player action cards without drawing them, such as The Codex relic or the Reverse Engineer action card, will not trigger Scheming. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (yssaril-scheming-and-discards (Community consensus)): "Scheming only triggers when you draw action cards from the deck, not when you take or receive them from a player."
- [Crafty] The effect of the Executive Sanctions law does not affect the Yssaril player. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (public-execution-effects (Community consensus)): "Crafty does beat effects that cap hand size, such as Executive Sanctions."
- [Mageon Implants (Technology)] When resolving Mageon Implants, the Yssaril player is not drawing a card. As such, Scheming will not trigger. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (yssaril-scheming-and-discards (Community consensus)): "not when you take or receive them from a player."
- [Mageon Implants (Technology)] The Yssaril player may claim orally what action cards they saw. <sup>2</sup>
  - Trimmed from: The Yssaril player may claim orally what action cards they saw; they may do so truthfully or deceitfully.
  - Source 2 (sharing-information-from-peeking (Community consensus)): "Yes — nothing in the rules stops you from sharing or trading that information."
- [Kyver, Blade and Key — Guild of Spies (Hero)] Taking action cards from a player using Guild of Spies will not trigger the Yssaril player’s Scheming ability. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (yssaril-scheming-and-discards (Community consensus)): "not when you take or receive them from a player."

**Notes added** (rulings that were not on the site before)

- [Deepgloom Executable (Breakthrough)] The Yssaril player may allow another player to use one of their faction abilities whenever that ability would be used. That player may use it for the duration of that ability. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (Yssaril Tribes): "Whenever that ability would be used, for the duration of that ability."
- [Stall Tactics] Stall Tactics is a faction ability, not an action card, and so cannot be cancelled by the Sabotage action card. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (yssaril-stall-tactics (Community consensus)): "It is a faction ability, not an action card, so Sabotage cannot cancel it."
- [Crafty] Crafty does not prevent the Yssaril player from being made to discard action cards by other effects. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (yssaril-scheming-and-discards (Community consensus)): "Ignoring the hand limit doesn't stop effects that make you discard."

**Citations added to existing items**

- [Spy Net (Promissory Note)] A player may receive Spy Net in a transaction during their turn. If received at the start of that player’s turn, that player may play it immediately. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p.17, Neighbors, Transactions, and Deals): "During the active player’s turn, they may negotiate a transaction with one or more of their neighbors, even during a combat."
- [Scheming] Scheming applies whenever the Yssaril player draws action cards. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (yssaril-scheming-and-discards (Community consensus)): "Scheming only triggers when you draw action cards from the deck"

**Restored without a source** (marked * on the site)

- [Scheming] No other abilities may resolve until the Yssaril player has discarded the action card. <sup>*</sup>
- [Spy Net (Promissory Note)] The player that plays Spy Net must look at the Yssaril player’s hand of action cards. They do not have to read or memorize what they look at. <sup>*</sup>
- [Mageon Implants (Technology)] The Yssaril player cannot show the other player’s hand of action cards to any other players. <sup>*</sup>
- [Transparasteel Plating (Technology)] Other players may resolve faction abilities, leader abilities or technology abilities during the Yssaril player’s turns. <sup>*</sup>
- [Y’sia Y’ssrila (Flagship)] If the Yssaril player owns the Light/Wave Deflector technology, it will have no additional effect on the Y’sia Y’ssrila <sup>*</sup>
- [Ssruu (Agent)] If the Yssaril player duplicates an agent that allows a unit to roll an additional die, and both the duplicated agent and Ssruu target the same unit, that unit will roll two additional dice. <sup>*</sup>
- [Ssruu (Agent)] If the Yssaril player duplicates the Saar player’s Captain Mendosa agent, they may do so before or after other effects are used to modify any ship’s move value. This includes the Saar player’s Captain Mendosa agent effect. <sup>*</sup>
- [Ssruu (Agent)] If both the Yssaril player and the Vuil’raith player wish to target the same player with the Vuil’raith The Stillness of Stars agent ability, then they will both be able to capture a ship, resolving in initiative order from the active player. Both players will still use the target player’s full commodity value to determine which units they may capture. Should the first player to resolve capture the last of a type of unit from the target player’s reinforcements, the latter player cannot capture a unit of the same type. <sup>*</sup>
- [Ssruu (Agent)] If the Yssaril player duplicates the Mentak player’s Suffi An agent, then the Yssaril player and the player targeted by the Mentak player’s Pillage ability will draw action cards. The Mentak player will not. <sup>*</sup>
- [Ssruu (Agent)] Duplicating the effect of the Argent player’s Trillossa Aun Mirik agent, the Creuss player’s Emissary Taivra agent or the Jol–Nar player’s Doctor Sucaban agent during the same timing window as that agent is used will have no additional effect. <sup>*</sup>
- [Ssruu (Agent)] If either the Yssaril player or the Nomad player resolve the effect of the Nomad player’s The Thundarian agent, the other will be unable to resolve the same effect immediately. They must wait until dice are rolled again before they may resolve the effect. <sup>*</sup>
- [Kyver, Blade and Key — Guild of Spies (Hero)] Each other player chooses which action card they show the Yssaril player. <sup>*</sup>
- [Deepgloom Executable (Breakthrough)] The Yssaril player may perform a transaction with another player without being neighbors with that player. <sup>*</sup>
- [Deepgloom Executable (Breakthrough)] The Yssaril player may perform a transaction with another player even if neither player is the active player. <sup>*</sup>
- [Deepgloom Executable (Breakthrough)] Deepgloom Executable may allow the Yssaril player to perform a transaction at a time they usually could not. For example, if the Mentak player exhausts their agent, Suffi An, during the strategy phase when another player gains the trade goods on the strategy card they chose, the Yssaril player may allow either of those players to use their Scheming ability, and then perform a transaction with that player. <sup>*</sup>

**Removed notes that the site already covers elsewhere**

- [Spy Net (Promissory Note)] If the active player received Spy Net on a previous turn, they may play it and immediately perform a transaction with the Yssaril player to regain it. However, Spy Net cannot be played twice in one timing window. The active player cannot play Spy Net again until their next turn. _(no source)_
  - Covered by [R_abilities.php](R_abilities.php) [Notes]: An ability from a single physical object cannot be resolved more than once in one timing window
- [Spy Net (Promissory Note)] Any deal between the Yssaril player and another player regarding which action card will be chosen, if made before Spy Net is exchanged, is non–binding. _(no source)_
  - Covered by [R_deals.php](R_deals.php) [Rules Reference]: If the terms of a deal cannot be resolved immediately, it is a non-binding deal
- [Mageon Implants (Technology)] The Yssaril player must target a player with at least one action card in their hand when they resolve Mageon Implants. _(no source)_
  - Covered by [R_component_action.php](R_component_action.php) [Notes]: A component action cannot be performed if its ability cannot be completely resolved.
- [So Ata (Commander)] The Yssaril player cannot unlock So Ata if they are yet to discard a card for their Scheming ability. _(no source)_
  - Covered by [R_leaders.php](R_leaders.php) [Notes]: A commander’s unlock conditions cannot be met while an ability or game effect is being resolved

### R_abilities.php

**LRR section corrections**

- **after 1.26**: not in LRR v2.0; moved to Notes (supported by DQA)
  - Before: Whenever a game effect uses or grants a unit ability, treat it as if a unit were using or having that unit ability. (nested: This means abilities that reference unit abilities, such as the Argent Commander, combo with these effects...)
  - After: (removed)

**Notes removed (owner review)**

- [Notes] Multiple action cards with the same name cannot be played during a single timing window to affect the same units or game effect. See the action cards page for more details.
  - Reason: an action-card rule, not a general ability rule; already stated as LRR 2.6b on [R_action_cards.php](R_action_cards.php).

**Notes kept**

- [Notes] An ability may be triggered during the timing window it was gained, if applicable. For example, if a player receives the Creuss player's Creuss Iff promissory note at the start of their turn, they may use it immediately. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (FAQ section (General)): "Can a card (such as a promissory note) with a specified timing of a certain window that is acquired from a transaction during that window be played immediately? A: Yes."
- [Notes] During the action phase, abilities are resolved in the current relative turn order, starting with the active player. For example, Trade (5), then Warfare (6), then Technology (7)... <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (1.19): "each player takes a turn resolving an ability in initiative order, beginning with the active player."
- [Notes] If a player has multiple abilities they wish to resolve, they must be resolved one at a time. Between each ability being resolved, each other player will have the opportunity to resolve one ability. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (1.19): "each player takes a turn resolving an ability in initiative order, beginning with the active player. This process continues until each player has resolved each ability that they wish to resolve during that window."
- [Notes] For example, Alice ... The order of resolution would be: Alice #1; Bob #1; Cheng #1; Alice #2; Cheng #2; Alice #3; Alice #4. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (1.19): "each player takes a turn resolving an ability in initiative order, beginning with the active player."
- [Notes] The secondary abilities of strategy cards are resolved in clockwise order, after the primary ability. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (82.1): "After the active player resolves the primary ability on their strategy card, each other player, beginning with the player to the left of the active player and proceeding clockwise, may resolve that strategy card’s secondary ability."
- [Notes] A player may resolve “at the start of your turn” and “at the end of your turn” abilities on the turn that they pass. <sup>1,4</sup>
  - Source 1 (3.3a): "During a turn that a player passes, they can resolve transactions and “at the start of your turn” abilities."
  - Source 4 (General: end of turn abilities on the turn you pass): "Can you resolve end of turn abilities on the turn you pass? A: Yes."
- [Notes] All abilities that occur “when” an event occurs all trigger before any abilities that occur “after” the same event occurs. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (1.16): "Effects that occur “when” an event happens take priority over effects that occur “after” an event happens."
- [Notes] All abilities that occur “after” an event occurs all trigger before any abilities that occur “before” the next event occurs. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (General: after x vs before y): "They are distinct. “After x” happens before “before y”"
- [Notes] Whenever a game effect uses or grants a unit ability, treat it as if a unit were using or having that unit ability. <sup>9</sup>
  - Source 9 (Unit Abilities imply Units?): "Should these things be treated as if they were units while using those unit abilities, and thus combo with things like Argent commander, and be shut down by things like Crimson flagship?"
  - Source 9 (Unit Abilities imply Units?): "A: Yes I'd say let them combo and be shut down."
- [Notes] This means abilities that reference unit abilities, such as the Argent Commander, combo with these effects. Similarly, effects that shut down unit abilities, such as the Crimson Flagship, will affect these abilities as well. <sup>9</sup>
  - Source 9 (Unit Abilities imply Units?): "A: Yes I'd say let them combo and be shut down."

**Removed notes restored**

- [Notes] An ability from a single physical object cannot be resolved more than once in one timing window. For example, if a player starts their turn with the Creuss player’s Creuss Iff promissory note in their hand (having received it on a previous turn) and uses it, they will not be able to use it a second time this turn, if they receive it again as part of a transaction. <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (DR, BGG Clipper, Jun 6, 2018): "that PN cannot be traded and resolved multiple times during the same window"
- [Notes] Once every player has consecutively declined to resolve an ability during a timing window, no more abilities may be resolved during that window. <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (DR, BGG 0 hr, Jul 19, 2018): "The answer is A) As soon s every player in order has passed, regardless of seating."
  - Source 5 (DR, BGG 0 hr, Jul 19, 2018): "Once someone has played an ability, every other player will have exactly one chance to continue."
- [Notes] A player may decline to resolve an ability during a timing window, but later choose to resolve an ability during that same timing window, but only if another player chooses to resolve an ability after the player declined. <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (DR, BGG Clipper, May 10, 2018): "You keep going around the circle/sequence until everybody passes simultaneously."
  - Source 5 (DR, BGG Clipper, May 10, 2018): "Dane: Regarding your question, option 2 is the intended method of resolution."
  - Source 5 (DR, BGG 0 hr, Jul 19, 2018): "Once someone has played an ability, every other player will have exactly one chance to continue."
- [Notes] Note that some triggers check their conditions when they trigger, while some check their conditions when they would resolve.
  - Source 2 (titans-awaken-timing (Community consensus)): "a sleeper placed later in that activation, say by Scanlink exploration, can't be awakened then."
  - Source 2 (assault-cannon-order-and-targets (Community consensus)): "with each trigger re-checked when its turn comes"
- [Notes] The Ul player's Awaken ability is an example of an ability that checks its condition when it triggers; activating a system without a sleeper token will not trigger Awaken, even if a sleeper token is later added during the activation step of that tactical action. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (titans-awaken-timing (Community consensus)): "Right after activating a system that already held your sleeper token; a sleeper placed later in that activation, say by Scanlink exploration, can't be awakened then."
- [Notes] The Assault Cannon technology is an example of an ability that checks its condition when it would resolve; a player without three or more non-fighter ships in the system cannot use Assault Cannon, even if they previously had more ships. <sup>2,5</sup>
  - Source 2 (assault-cannon-order-and-targets (Community consensus)): "So the attacker's Assault Cannon can push the defender below 3 non-fighter ships and deny the defender's own Assault Cannon"
  - Source 5 (DR, reddit livestrongbelwas, Feb 08, 2018): "Dane: 2a) The second player doesn't get to use his Assault Cannons"
- [Notes] Each unit on the board is its own separate physical object. For example, two or more of the N'orr player's Exotrireme II in a system may use their ability to destroy themselves and other ships, as the ability is linked to the units on the game board, and not the unit upgrade technology card. <sup>*</sup>
- [Notes] Following on from the above example, had Alice declined to resolve "Alice #2", she could still resolve "Alice #3", as Cheng resolved "Cheng #2", breaking the series of consecutive declinations. However, if Alice had instead declined to resolve "Alice #3", she would be unable to resolve "Alice #4", as then each player would have consecutively declined to resolve an ability. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (passing-in-a-timing-window (Community consensus)): "if anyone plays something after you passed, you get another chance. The window only closes once every player passes in a row."

**Notes added** (rulings that were not on the site before)

- [Notes] Once an ability has been resolved, it cannot be undone or withdrawn, even if another player then resolves an ability in response. The player may instead respond by resolving another ability when they next have the opportunity during that timing window. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (resolved-abilities-cannot-be-undone (Community consensus)): "No — anything already resolved stays resolved."
- [Notes] Each paragraph on a card is a separate ability, and is resolved independently of the others. For example, a promissory note’s final paragraph instructing the player to return the card is still resolved, even if an earlier paragraph had no effect. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (separate-paragraphs-are-separate-abilities (Community consensus)): "Yes — each paragraph is its own ability and resolves on its own."
- [Notes] “At the start of your turn” abilities are resolved before the player chooses their action or passes, and so before a system is activated. Such abilities can only be resolved during the action phase, as players do not take turns during other phases. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (start-of-turn-abilities (Community consensus)): "Before you choose your action or pass, so they come before activating a system and before anything activation triggers, like Ceasefire."
- [Notes] An ability that refers to “a player” may be used on the player resolving it. Only an ability that refers to “another player” excludes that player. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (agents-and-a-player (Community consensus)): "'A player' includes you; only 'another player' excludes you"

### R_action_cards.php

**Notes kept**

- [Notes] A player may choose to reveal any or all of the action cards in their hand, if they so choose. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (FAQ section (General): reveal hidden information): "Can you intentionally reveal hidden information to another player, such as an action card from your hand or your secret objective? A: Yes."
- [Notes] A player cannot target themselves with offensive action cards, such as Lucky Shot. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (FAQ section (Action Cards): Lucky Shot): "Can abilities that destroy units, such as the “Lucky Shot” action card, be used by a player against their own units or planets? A: No. “Lucky Shot” and other similar effects can only be used against other player’s units and planets."
- [Notes] If the action card deck is depleted, immediately shuffle the discard pile to form a new action card deck. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (23.5): "CARDS: When a deck is depleted, players shuffle the deck’s discard pile and place it facedown to create a new deck."
- [Notes] If a player's action card is cancelled, usually via a Sabotage action card, then if that player has a second copy of that action card, they may play it. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (2.6b): "Multiple action cards with the same name cannot be played during a single timing window to affect the same units or game effect. Canceled cards are not treated as being played."
- [Notes] If a player has more than seven action cards, they must discard the excess. <sup>1</sup>
  - Edited from: If a player has more than seven action cards, they must discard the excess immediately. They cannot play them to get down to seven, and the Hacan player cannot trade them.
  - Source 1 (2.4): "If a player ever has more than seven action cards, that player must choose seven cards to keep and discard the rest."

**Removed notes restored**

- [Notes] If an action card targets “each” of a particular type of object, that action card may target zero of those objects. As such, these cards may be played even if they would cause no effect. <sup>5</sup>
  - Trimmed from: If an action card targets “any number”, “up to”, or “each” of a particular type of object, that action card may target zero of those objects. As such, these cards may be played even if they would cause no effect.
  - Source 5 (DR, x3n d0g, 1/25/2019): "the ability to exhaust (or ready) all planets (in this case 0) is fully resolved, whether or not any game state is changed."
  - Source 5 (DR, x3n d0g, 1/25/2019): "the rule present in 21.3 does more to prohibit using actions that don't have legal targets than it does to prevent actions that don't result in the game state being changed."
- [Notes] If an action card targets a specific number of a particular type of object, that action card cannot be played if those objects do not currently exist. For example, Repeal Law cannot be played if there are no laws in play. <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (DR, x3n d0g, 1/25/2019): "'No, you can't just play an action card that has no legal target in order to skip a turn' (think Repeal Law when there are no laws in play)"
- [Notes] Players start the game with zero action cards. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (no-starting-commodities (Community consensus)): "nobody starts with commodities, trade goods or action cards."
- [Notes] Action cards are dealt out in initiative order. <sup>2</sup>
  - Trimmed from: During the action phase, action cards are dealt out in initiative order. (children on Neural Motivator / Yssaril Scheming not restored: no RP support)
  - Source 2 (action-card-draw-order (Per the rulebook — 3. Status Phase)): "In initiative order, though it rarely matters in practice."

**Notes added** (rulings that were not on the site before)

- [Notes] Action cards are discarded faceup. Players may look through the action card discard pile. <sup>4,5</sup>
  - Source 5 (x3n d0g 1/25/2019): "Action cards are discarded faceup and players may look through the discard deck."
  - Source 4 (The Codex relic): "the discard is public knowledge"

**Citations added to existing items**

- [Rules Reference] Action cards provide players with various abilities that they can resolve as described on the cards. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (Learn to Play p.17): "Players can use action cards to resolve powerful one-time abilities."
- [Rules Reference] Each player draws one action card during each status phase. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (Learn to Play p.11): "3. DRAW ACTION CARDS: Each player draws one card from the top of the action card deck."
- [Rules Reference] Players can draw action cards by resolving the primary and secondary abilities of the Politics strategy card. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (Learn to Play p.7): "Spend 1 token from your strategy pool to draw 2 action cards."
- [Rules Reference] When a player draws an action card, they take the top card from the action card deck and add it to their hand of action cards. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (Learn to Play p.11): "Each player draws one card from the top of the action card deck."

### R_action_phase.php

**Notes kept**

**Citations added to existing items**

- [Rules Reference] During the action phase, each player takes a turn in initiative order. During a player’s turn, they perform a single action.   - Source 3 (Learn to Play p.9): "During the action phase, players take turns in initiative order. While a player is taking a turn, they are the active player, and they can perform one action. After each player has taken a turn, player turns begin again in initiative order."
