  - Source 3 (Learn to Play p.9): "There are three types of actions: tactical actions, strategic actions, and component actions."
- [Rules Reference] After a player has passed, they have no further turns and cannot perform additional actions during that action phase. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (Learn to Play p.9): "After a player passes, their turn is skipped for the remainder of the action phase."
- [Rules Reference] A player that has passed can still resolve the secondary ability of other players’ strategy cards. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (Learn to Play p.10): "A player who has passed during the action phase can still resolve the secondary ability of other players’ strategy cards."
- [Rules Reference] A player cannot pass until they have performed the strategic action of their strategy card. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (Learn to Play p.9): "A player cannot pass until they have performed their strategic action"
- [Rules Reference] During a three–player or four–player game, a player cannot pass until they have exhausted both of their strategy cards. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (Learn to Play p.12): "PASSING: A player cannot pass during the action phase unless both of their strategy cards are exhausted."
- [Rules Reference] After all players have passed, play proceeds to the status phase. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (Learn to Play p.9): "After each player has passed, the game round continues to the status phase."
- [Rules Reference] During a player's turn, they may perform one of the following three types of actions ... <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (one-action-per-turn (Per the rulebook — 2. Action Phase)): "Exactly one action per turn — strategic, tactical or component — or you pass."
- [Rules Reference] A player that has passed can still resolve the secondary ability of other players' strategy cards. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (secondaries-after-passing (Per the rulebook — 2. Action Phase)): "passing ends your turns, not your ability to follow secondaries by spending a strategy token."
- [Rules Reference] A player cannot pass until they have performed the strategic action of their strategy card. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (one-action-per-turn (Per the rulebook — 2. Action Phase)): "you can't pass until you have used your strategy card"
- [Rules Reference] During a three-player or four-player game, a player cannot pass until they have exhausted both of their strategy cards. <sup>2</sup>

  - Source 3 (p. 11, Agenda Phase): "After the custodians token has been removed from Mecatol Rex, a new phase is added to each round"
- [Rules Reference] Reveal Agenda: The speaker draws one agenda card from the top of the agenda deck and reads it aloud to all players, including all of its possible outcomes. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p. 20, Agenda Phase): "The speaker draws one agenda card from the top of the agenda deck and reads it aloud to all players"
- [Rules Reference] Vote: Each player, starting with the player to the left of the speaker and continuing clockwise, can cast votes for an outcome of the current agenda. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p. 20, Agenda Phase): "Each player, starting with the player to the left of the speaker and continuing clockwise, casts votes in favor of a single outcome."
- [Rules Reference] Resolve Outcome: Players tally each vote that was cast and resolve the outcome that received the most votes. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p. 20, Agenda Phase): "Players count votes and resolve the outcome with the most votes."
- [Rules Reference] Step 2 – Second Agenda: Players repeat the First Agenda step of this phase for a second agenda. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p. 21, Agenda Phase): "Players resolve a second agenda following the same rules and steps for step 1"
- [Rules Reference] Step 3 – Ready Planets: Each player readies each of their exhausted planets. Then, a new game round begins starting with the strategy phase. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p. 21, Agenda Phase): "Each player readies all of their planet cards. Then, the agenda phase ends and players begin a new game round"
- [Voting] To cast votes, a player exhausts any number of their planets and chooses an outcome. The number of votes cast for that outcome is equal to the combined influence values of the planets that the player exhausts. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p. 20, Agenda Phase): "they may exhaust any number of their planets. Each planet contributes a number of votes equal to its influence value."
- [Voting] A player cannot cast votes for multiple outcomes of the same agenda. Each vote a player casts must be for the same outcome. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p. 20, Agenda Phase): "A player can only vote for one outcome per agenda."
- [Voting] Some agendas have “For” and “Against” outcomes. When a player casts votes on such an agenda, that player must cast their votes either “For” or “Against”. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p. 20, Agenda Phase): "The player commits their votes “For” or “Against” the agenda."
- [Voting] When electing a planet, a player must cast votes for a planet that is controlled by a player. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p. 20, Agenda Phase): "That planet must be controlled by a player unless the agenda specifies otherwise."
- [Voting] When casting votes, a player must declare aloud the outcome for which their votes are being cast. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p. 20, Agenda Phase): "When casting votes, the player announces the outcome they are voting for aloud."
- [Voting] A player may choose to abstain by not casting any votes. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p. 20, Agenda Phase): "They may, however, choose to abstain from the vote entirely."
- [Outcomes] If there is a tie for the outcome that received the most votes, or if no outcome receives any votes, the speaker decides which of the tied outcomes to resolve. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p. 21, Agenda Phase): "If multiple outcomes receive the same number of votes after all players have voted, the speaker decides which of the tied"
- [Outcomes] If an “Elect” or “For” outcome of a law was resolved, that card remains in play and permanently affects the game. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p. 21, Agenda Phase): "if a “For” outcome received the most votes, or if the law requires an election, the law’s effect becomes a permanent part of the game."
- [Outcomes] If a directive or an “Against” outcome of a law was resolved, that card is placed in the agenda discard pile. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p. 20, Agenda Phase): "When resolving a directive, players resolve the outcome that received the most votes and discard the agenda card"
  - Source 3 (p. 21, Agenda Phase): "If an “Against” outcome received the most votes, players resolve the text effect of the outcome and discard the agenda"
- [Notes] Each pair of players may resolve one transaction during each agenda. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p. 20, Agenda Phase): "Each player may negotiate up to one transaction with each other player while resolving the vote for each agenda."
- [Notes] A player may cast votes with space stations, The Triad, and Oceans. now also cites <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (Space Stations): "Yes, Space Stations are used for voting but may not be elected."
  - Source 6 (Relics): "Q: Can you vote using The Triad relic?"
  - Source 6 (Deepwrought Scholarate): "Oceans do not count as planets for scoring. They may be spent as planet cards."
- [Notes] Casting zero votes for an outcome is the same as abstaining. A player that casts zero votes gains no positive or negative effects of voting for that outcome. now also cites <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (Clipper, Mar 2, 2018): "Nope, you are not allowed to cast zero votes. Consider zero votes to be mechanically the same as abstaining."
- [Voting] Some game effects allow a player to cast additional votes for an outcome. These votes cannot be cast for a different outcome than other votes cast by that player. now also cites <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (Skootur, 1/25/2019): "It should specify that you are casting 1 additional vote for the outcome that you voted for."
  - Source 5 (Skootur, 1/25/2019): "It was not intended to circumvent any other rules or allow a player to vote from multiple angles."
- [Voting] If a player cannot vote on an agenda because of a game effect, that player cannot cast votes for that agenda by exhausting planets or through any other game effect. now also cites <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (sigmazero13, Jun 11, 2018): "you can’t use it if another effect is stopping you from casting votes."
- [Rules Reference] Players skip the agenda phase during the early portion of each game. After the custodians token is removed from Mecatol Rex, the agenda phase is added to each game round. To resolve the agenda phase, players perform the following steps:. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (agenda-phase-timing-and-readying (Per the rulebook — 4. Agenda Phase)): "Once the custodians token is off Mecatol Rex, the agenda phase follows the status phase every round"
- [Rules Reference] Vote: Each player, starting with the player to the left of the speaker and continuing clockwise, can cast votes for an outcome of the current agenda. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (how-voting-works (Per the rulebook — 4. Agenda Phase)): "Each player votes once per agenda, openly, starting to the speaker's left and ending with the speaker"
- [Rules Reference] Step 3 – Ready Planets: Each player readies each of their exhausted planets. Then, a new game round begins starting with the strategy phase. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (agenda-phase-timing-and-readying (Per the rulebook — 4. Agenda Phase)): "Planets ready again at the end of the agenda phase for the next action phase"

  - Source 2 (vote-with-part-of-planet-influence (Community consensus)): "exhausting a planet casts all of its influence as votes"

  - Source 2 (elect-planet-agendas (Community consensus)): "Only planets some player controls are eligible"

  - Source 2 (trade-goods-cannot-vote (Per the rulebook — 4. Agenda Phase)): "trade goods count as influence for everything except voting"
- [Voting] A player may choose to abstain by not casting any votes. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (abstaining-and-zero-votes (Community consensus)): "You can always abstain, whether or not you have votes available"
- [Outcomes] If there is a tie for the outcome that received the most votes, or if no outcome receives any votes, the speaker decides which of the tied outcomes to resolve. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (ties-and-everyone-abstaining (Per the rulebook — 4. Agenda Phase)): "The speaker picks which tied outcome resolves; at 0 to 0 that means any eligible outcome"
- [Outcomes] The speaker’s decision is not a vote. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (ties-and-everyone-abstaining (Per the rulebook — 4. Agenda Phase)): "The speaker's choice is not a vote"
- [Outcomes] If an “Elect” or “For” outcome of a law was resolved, that card remains in play and permanently affects the game. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (laws-versus-directives (Per the rulebook — 4. Agenda Phase)): "If a law's For (or elect) outcome wins, the card stays in play as a lasting effect"

  - Source 2 (laws-versus-directives (Per the rulebook — 4. Agenda Phase)): "A law's Against outcome, and either outcome of a directive, resolves once and the card is discarded"
- [Outcomes] Some game effects instruct a player to predict an outcome. To predict an outcome, a player declares aloud the outcome they think will receive the most votes. That player must make this prediction after the agenda is revealed but before any votes have been cast. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (nomad-future-sight-predictions (Community consensus)): "Predictions are declared after the agenda is revealed and before any votes"

  - Source 2 (agenda-phase-transactions-non-neighbors (Designer ruling)): "while each agenda is being resolved, from its reveal until its outcome resolves, every pair of players may make one transaction"
- [Notes] Casting zero votes for an outcome is the same as abstaining. A player that casts zero votes gains no positive or negative effects of voting for that outcome. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (abstaining-and-zero-votes (Community consensus)): "Casting zero votes is the same as abstaining"

### R_anti_fighter_barrage.php

**Notes kept**

- [Notes] A non-fighter ship cannot use its Sustain Damage ability to cancel a hit produced by an anti-fighter barrage roll. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (87.4a): "a player cannot use a dreadnought’s “Sustain Damage” ability to cancel a hit from “Anti-Fighter Barrage.”"

**Removed notes restored**

- [Notes] The "0" side of the d10 represents a result of 10. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (LRR v2.0 FAQ section, General (p. 40)): "A: Yes, the “0” face is a “10” result."
- [Notes] Effects such as the Shields Holding action card, which trigger on hits produced during space combat, may be used to cancel a hit produced by an anti–fighter barrage roll. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (shields-holding-which-hits (Community consensus)): "Hits during space combat, including Anti-Fighter Barrage in the first round"

**Citations added to existing items**

- [Rules Reference] A unit with the Anti–Fighter Barrage ability may be able to destroy an opponent’s fighters at the onset of a space battle. During the Anti–Fighter Barrage step of the first round of space combat, players perform the following steps: now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p. 19, Unit Abilities): "A player uses this ability during the “Anti-Fighter Barrage” step of the first round of space combat."
- [Rules Reference] Step 1: Each player rolls dice for each of their units in the combat that has the Anti–Fighter Barrage ability; this is called an anti–fighter barrage roll. A hit is produced for each die roll that is equal to or greater than the unit’s Anti–Fighter Barrage value. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p. 19, Unit Abilities): "These abilities are always followed by a number that determines the minimum die result required to produce a hit."
- [Rules Reference] The Anti–Fighter Barrage ability is displayed as Anti–Fighter Barrage X (×Y). The X is the minimum value needed for a die to produce a hit, and Y is the number of dice rolled. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p. 19, Unit Abilities): "Some of these abilities are followed by a second number presented inside parentheses."
- [Rules Reference] This ability can still be used if no fighters are present; hits produced may be used to trigger specific abilities. now also cites <sup>8</sup>
  - Source 8 (p. 16, Clarifications): "step can occur even if a player’s opponent has no fighters in the combat."
- [Rules Reference] Step 2: Each player must choose and destroy one of their fighters in the active system for each hit their opponent’s anti–fighter barrage roll produced. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p. 19, Unit Abilities): "These hits can only be assigned to fighters."
- [Rules Reference] Game effects that reroll, modify, or otherwise affect combat rolls do not affect anti–fighter barrage rolls. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (what-is-a-combat-roll (Community consensus)): "Anti-Fighter Barrage, Space Cannon, Bombardment ... are ability rolls, so Morale Boost ... and effects that reroll combat rolls don't touch them"
- [Rules Reference] This ability can still be used if no fighters are present; hits produced may be used to trigger specific abilities. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (argent-raid-formation-no-fighters (Community consensus)): "Argent fire barrage even when the opponent has no fighters"
- [Notes] The “0” side of the d10 represents a result of 10. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (zero-on-die-is-ten (Community consensus)): "10 — the Living Rules Reference FAQ confirms the 0 face is a 10"

- [Rules Reference] Planets that contain a unit with the Planetary Shield ability cannot be bombarded. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (x-89-omega-rules (Community consensus)): "Planetary Shield, by blocking Bombardment, blocks it too"
- [Notes] The “0” side of the d10 represents a result of 10. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (zero-on-die-is-ten (Community consensus)): "10 — the Living Rules Reference FAQ confirms the 0 face is a 10"
- [Notes] A single planet must be chosen for each unit with the Bombardment ability; any hits generated by that unit will be assigned to units on that planet. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (bombardment-assignment (Community consensus)): "a unit bombards a single planet with all its dice"

- [Notes] Say a player had three dreadnoughts in the active system, and owned the Plasma Scoring technology. They would be able to roll their choice of zero, three, or four dice when resolving their Bombardment ability. <sup>*</sup>

### R_breakthroughs.php

**Removed notes restored**

- [Notes] A breakthrough is a faction specific card. <sup>7</sup>
  - Trimmed from: A breakthrough is a faction specific card. Players start the game without their faction’s breakthrough.
  - Source 7 (p. 8, Breakthroughs and Synergy): "A breakthrough is a new type of faction-specific component"
- [Notes] A breakthrough is commonly gained through an expedition. There are other game effects that can gain a player their faction’s breakthrough. <sup>7</sup>
  - Trimmed from: A breakthrough is commonly gained through an expedition, or the Thunder’s Edge legendary planet ability card. There are other game effects that can gain a player their faction’s breakthrough.
  - Source 7 (p. 8, Breakthroughs and Synergy): "most commonly gained by interacting with Thunder’s Edge."
  - Source 7 (p. 8, Thunder’s Edge Expedition): "The first time a player claims one of the expedition slices, they gain their faction’s breakthrough."
  - Source 7 (p. 8, Breakthroughs and Synergy): "When a player gains their breakthrough, regardless of the source,"
- [Notes] When a player gains their faction’s breakthrough, they perform a breakthrough roll, which may cause The Fracture to enter play. <sup>7</sup>
  - Source 7 (p. 8, Breakthroughs and Synergy): "When a player gains their breakthrough, regardless of the source, if The Fracture is not already in play, they roll one die. If their die roll is equal to 1 or 10, they put The Fracture into play."
- [Notes] A breakthrough has 1 or more abilities, and a synergy (other than for the Nekro player). <sup>7</sup>
  - Source 7 (p. 8, Breakthroughs and Synergy): "A breakthrough will give each faction a unique new ability and grants synergy between two technology colors."
  - Source 7 (p. 9, The Fracture): "a breakthrough that does not have synergy (as is the case with the Nekro Virus faction)"
- [Notes] If a breakthrough has a passive ability and an exhaust ability, the passive ability always remains in effect, even when the breakthrough is exhausted. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (breakthroughs-not-technologies (Community consensus)): "Their passive abilities keep working while exhausted."
- [Notes] A breakthrough itself is not a technology; it alone cannot be used to meet a prerequisite when researching a technology, nor can it alone be used to meet the technology requirement of an objective. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (breakthroughs-not-technologies (Community consensus)): "They aren't technologies, so a breakthrough ... doesn't count as a unit upgrade or for anything that cares about technologies"

**Notes added** (rulings that were not on the site before)

- [Notes] The Rebellion player gains their breakthrough as a starting component, which triggers a breakthrough roll during setup; The Fracture may be in play from the start of the game. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (crimson-starting-breakthrough-fracture (Community consensus)): "the roll triggers whenever a player gains a breakthrough from any source"

### R_capture.php

**LRR section corrections**

- **17.4**: LRR v2.0 has this as top-level 17.4 with sub-items a-c; restored structure so numbering matches
  - Before: (17.4 text was nested as a sub-item of 17.3; displayed 17.4 was 'When a captured fighter or infantry is returned, it is placed in the supply.')
  - After: Captured fighters and infantry do not belong to any player and are returned only when an ability instructs the capturing player to do so.
- **17.4c**: LRR v2.0 has this as 17.4c, not a top-level item
  - Before: When a captured fighter or infantry is returned, it is placed in the supply. (top-level item, shown as 17.4)
  - After: When a captured fighter or infantry is returned, it is placed in the supply. (sub-item c of 17.4)
- **17.4a/17.4b**: LRR v2.0 structure
  - Before: nested under 17.3
  - After: nested under 17.4

**Notes kept**

- [Notes] Units are returned as soon as a space dock is blockaded. <sup>1</sup>
  - Edited from: Units are returned as soon as a space dock is blockaded. If this occurs at the end of the Space Combat step of a tactical action, the units will be returned before the Invasion step, in which the space dock could potentially be destroyed.
  - Source 1 (14.2): "When a player blockades another player’s space dock, if the blockaded player has captured any of the blockading player’s units, those units are returned to the blockading player’s reinforcements."
- [Notes] A captured unit may only be returned to the player that originally owned it, and not to another player. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (17.1): "When such a unit is returned, it is placed into the reinforcements of the original owner."
- [Notes] If a player is eliminated, any of their units that are captured remain with the player that captured them. When the capturing player would return them, the units are instead returned to the game box. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (General, captured units when owner eliminated): "Captured units remain on the sheet of the player that captured them. If they would ever be returned to the eliminated player, they are returned to the game box instead"
- [Notes] If a player has all of their units of one type on the game board or captured ... remove a unit from any system that does not contain one of their command tokens and place it in reinforcements before placing. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (23.4a): "When a player would place a unit, if there are none of that type left in their reinforcements, that player can remove a unit from any system that does not contain one of their command tokens and place that unit in their reinforcements."
- [Notes] A player cannot capture fighter or infantry tokens corresponding to units belonging to a player that is blockading one of their space docks. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (17.6): "If one or more of a player’s space docks is being blockaded, that player cannot capture units from the blockading players."
  - Source 1 (14.2a): "While a player is blockading another player, the blockaded player cannot capture any of the blockading player’s units."

  - Edited from: If only one player has units on a planet that was in coexistence, the coexistence ends, and that player gains control of that planet if they were the coexisting player.
  - Source 9 (Coexist: Control Default (With Multiple Coexisting Players)): "Control defaults to the next player in order as per ability resolution order by phase"
- [Notes] A player is considered to control a planet they are coexisting on when scoring an objective. <sup>9</sup>
  - Edited from: A player is considered to control a planet they are coexisting on solely when scoring an objective. For any other game ability or effect, they are not considered to control that planet.
  - Source 9 (Coexist: Perspective During Scoring): "the coexisting player sees both themselves and the controlling player as controlling that planet when scoring objectives."

**Removed notes restored**

- [Notes] Some game effects allow two or more players’ units to exist on a planet without triggering combat; this is coexistence. <sup>7</sup>
  - Source 7 (p.11 Coexist): "Some game effects allow a player’s units to coexist with other units on a planet. When a unit or units coexist with another player’s units, they do not trigger combat."
- [Notes] One player controls the planet; all other players are coexisting on that planet. <sup>7</sup>
  - Source 7 (p.11 Coexist): "The player whose units triggered coexistence does not gain or retain control of the planet; if they already controlled it, the player they are now coexisting with gains control of it instead, exhausted."
- [Notes] If a game effect instructs a player to coexist on a planet they do not control, the original controller of that planet retains control. <sup>7</sup>
  - Source 7 (p.11 Coexist): "The player whose units triggered coexistence does not gain or retain control of the planet"
- [Notes] If a game effect instructs a player to coexist on a planet they do control, then another player will gain control of that planet (which will exhaust that planet). <sup>7</sup>
  - Source 7 (p.11 Coexist): "if they already controlled it, the player they are now coexisting with gains control of it instead, exhausted"
- [Notes] If additional units are added to those already coexisting, by, for example, committing additional ground forces during an invasion, or resolving an effect that allows a unit to be placed directly on a planet, the added units immediately coexist. <sup>7</sup>
  - Source 7 (p.11 Coexist): "If the coexisting player places, produces, or moves additional units onto that planet, those units also coexist."
- [Notes] When a player uses the Bombardment ability of 1 of their units against a planet in coexistence, they choose which player’s units on that planet will have the hits assigned. <sup>7</sup>
  - Source 7 (p.11 Coexist): "Coexisting units can be bombarded. When a player makes a bombardment roll against a planet, they choose which of their units with bombardment are bombarding which other player’s units, rolling against each player separately."
- [Notes] If that player has multiple units with the Bombardment ability, they make this choice independently for each unit. <sup>7</sup>
  - Source 7 (p.11 Coexist): "they choose which of their units with bombardment are bombarding which other player’s units"
- [Notes] If that player produces a surplus of hits above the number of units of the player they have chosen, the extra hits cannot be assigned to the units of a different player on that planet. <sup>7</sup>
  - Source 7 (p.11 Coexist): "rolling against each player separately"
- [Notes] A player who controls a planet may start a ground combat against a coexisting player during the invasion step of a tactical action. <sup>7</sup>
  - Source 7 (p.11 Coexist): "Coexisting units can have combat initiated against them by units being committed to the planet that contains them, including units that they were already coexisting with."
- [Notes] A player who is coexisting on a planet may start a ground combat against the player that controls that planet during the invasion step of a tactical action. <sup>7</sup>
  - Source 7 (p.11 Coexist): "a coexisting player may choose to end their coexistence by activating the coexisting unit’s system and committing the coexisting units against the planet they are coexisting on. If they win the ground combat, they cease coexisting and gain control of the planet as normal."
- [Notes] A player who had no units on a planet, but commits 1 or more ground forces during the invasion step of a tactical action must start a ground combat against the player that controls that planet (unless they have an ability that would allow them to coexist). <sup>7</sup>
  - Source 7 (p.11 Coexist): "The activating player may choose not to engage the coexisting units, however, and leave the coexisting units in a state of coexistence."
  - Source 7 (p.11 Coexist): "they may optionally engage a coexisting player’s units after winning a combat against the planet’s owner"
- [Notes] Should a player win the ground combat on a planet resulting from one of these aforementioned methods, they gain control of that planet, if they were not in control of it already. Then, they may start an additional ground combat against another coexisting player, if present, and may continue to do so until they decline to start another ground combat or there are no more coexisting players. Any coexisting players that they do not resolve a ground combat against remain coexisting. <sup>7</sup>
  - Source 7 (p.11 Coexist): "If a player does wish to engage coexisting units, they may optionally engage a coexisting player’s units after winning a combat against the planet’s owner, initiating separate combats against any coexisting player as desired."

**Notes added** (rulings that were not on the site before)

- [Notes] If multiple players are coexisting on a planet and the player that controls that planet no longer has units on it, control passes to the next coexisting player in the order used to resolve abilities in the current phase: initiative order during the action phase, otherwise clockwise order. <sup>9</sup>
  - Source 9 (Coexist / Coexistence Control Default (With Multiple Coexisting Players)): "Control defaults to the next player in order as per ability resolution order by phase (initiative order during action phase, otherwise clockwise)"
- [Notes] When scoring an objective, the player that controls a planet does not count a coexisting player as also controlling it; the coexisting player considers both themselves and the controlling player to control that planet. <sup>9</sup>
  - Source 9 (Coexist / Coexistence, Perspective During Scoring): "The player the coexisting player is coexisting with does not count the coexisting player as also controlling that planet"
- [Notes] A player may score public objectives even if they coexist on, but do not control, each planet in their home system. <sup>9</sup>
  - Source 9 (Coexist / Scoring Public Objectives Coexisting At Home): "Yes, you may score public objectives even if you coexist on but do not outright control each planet in your home system."
- [Notes] A player must control a planet, not merely coexist on it, to explore it. A player cannot spend another player’s coexisting units to pay the cost of an exploration card, such as Volatile Fuel Source. <sup>9</sup>
  - Source 9 (Coexist / Coexist and Exploration): "You must control a planet outright to explore it. You cannot spend other player’s units to pay for explore cards’ costs."
- [Notes] During an invasion, if the last of the controlling player’s units on a planet are destroyed, such as by Bombardment, control does not pass to the coexisting player until the Establish Control step. The invading player may land ground forces and gain control of the planet, and the coexisting player remains in coexistence. <sup>9</sup>
  - Source 9 (Coexist / Coexist Control Default (During Invasions)): "During invasion, control default due to coexistence does not occur until the establish control step."
- [Notes] Coexisting units may use their Production ability to produce ground forces, but cannot produce ships. <sup>9</sup>
  - Source 9 (Coexist / Coexistence and PRODUCTION): "Coexisting units can produce ground forces but are always blockaded and cannot produce ships."
- [Notes] Structures without ground forces may maintain control of a planet while another player’s ground forces coexist on it. Structures without ground forces may coexist on a planet by themselves. <sup>9</sup>
  - Source 9 (Coexist / Coexistence and Structures): "Structures without ground forces may maintain control of a planet with coexisting ground forces. Structures without ground forces may coexist by themselves."
- [Notes] All coexisting units are blockaded, including units that are not structures, such as mechs with the Production ability. <sup>6,9</sup>
  - Source 6 (Coexistence): "Yes, coexisting units are always blockaded."
  - Source 9 (Coexistence and PRODUCTION): "Coexisting units can produce ground forces but are always blockaded and cannot produce ships."
- [Notes] If multiple players may choose to coexist on a planet during the same timing window, the active player chooses first; if they decline, the other player may then choose to coexist. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (Coexistence): "Both coexistences happen in the same timing window, so it will go by active player order, the active player is given the opportunity to coexist first, and if they decline, then the other player may choose to coexist."
- [Notes] Outside of the Invasion step of a tactical action, a coexisting player gains control of a planet immediately when they become the only player with units on it, such as when the controlling player moves all of their units off that planet. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (Coexistence): "At all other times, control is exchanged immediately after the coexisting player becomes the only player with units on the planet."
- [Notes] A player who enters coexistence on a planet they control when ground forces are committed to it may still use Space Cannon against those ground forces during the Space Cannon Defense step. They do not lose control of the planet until the Establish Control step, and if they are then the only player with units on the planet, they are no longer coexisting and retain control. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (Coexistence): "You may fire PDS defense against the active player’s committed ground forces after entering coexistence. If you have the only units on a planet you exit coexistence and you do not lose control of the planet."
- [Notes] When a player ends their coexistence by starting a ground combat, all of their units on that planet, including structures, stop coexisting, even if they do not win the ground combat. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (Coexistence): "When you end coexistence, you end coexistence for all of your units on that planet, including structures."
- [Notes] A unit with Planetary Shield on a planet protects all units on that planet, including those of the controlling player and coexisting players. All PDS on a planet, including coexisting PDS, may use Space Cannon during the Space Cannon Defense step against ground forces committed by the active player. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (Coexistence): "Planetary Shield from any units on the planet applies to the planet itself and thus protects all units on the planet."

**Citations added to existing items**

  - Source 7 (p.11 Coexist): "Coexisting structures are always blockaded."

### R_combat.php

**Notes kept**

- [Notes] The "0" side of the d10 represents a result of 10. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (LRR v2.0 FAQ section, General (p. 40)): "A: Yes, the “0” face is a “10” result."

**Notes added** (rulings that were not on the site before)

- [Notes] Abilities that trigger “at the start of a combat”, other than those on agents, can only be resolved during a combat in which the player resolving them is participating. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (General): "No, any non-agent “at the start of a combat” abilities must be played during a combat you are participating in."
- [Notes] A player only wins a combat if a space combat or ground combat occurred. Destroying all opposing ships with the Space Cannon ability, destroying all opposing ground forces with the Bombardment ability, landing ground forces on a planet without opposing ground forces, or the opposing player avoiding the combat with the Naalu player’s Foresight faction ability does not count as winning a combat. A planet containing only another player’s structures does not cause a ground combat. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (what-counts-as-winning-a-combat (Community consensus)): "No — a combat is a space combat or a ground combat, and you win when your units remain and the opponent's don't."

**Citations added to existing items**

- [Rules Reference] During combat, if a unit’s combat roll produces a result equal to or greater than its combat value, it produces a hit. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p.14 Make Combat Rolls): "If the result of a unit’s die roll is equal to or greater than that unit’s combat value shown on its faction sheet, that roll produces a hit."
- [Rules Reference] If a unit’s combat value contains two or more burst icons, instead of rolling a single die, the player rolls one die for each burst icon when making that unit’s combat rolls. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p.14 Make Combat Rolls): "If a unit’s combat value contains two or more burst icons, the player rolls this number of dice instead"
- [Rules Reference] During combat, if a unit’s combat roll produces a result equal to or greater than its combat value, it produces a hit. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (no-critical-hits (Community consensus)): "A roll hits when the result, after modifiers, equals or beats the unit's combat value"
- [Rules Reference] If a unit’s combat value contains two or more burst icons, instead of rolling a single die, the player rolls one die for each burst icon when making that unit’s combat rolls. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (faction-sheet-arrows-and-dots (Per the rulebook — Unit Attributes)): "Each dot or burst by a combat value is one die the unit rolls"
- [Notes] The “0” side of the d10 represents a result of 10. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (zero-on-die-is-ten (Community consensus)): "10 — the Living Rules Reference FAQ confirms the 0 face is a 10"

### R_command_sheet.php

**Notes kept**

- [Notes] When a command token is gained, it may be placed in any of the three pools if no specific pool is specified by the gaining effect. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (20.2): "When a player gains a command token, they choose which of their three pools to place it in."

**Citations added to existing items**

- [Rules Reference] The pools on the command sheet are where players place their command tokens. Command tokens in a player’s pools are used by that player to perform strategic and tactical actions and to increase the number of ships that player can have in each system. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p.10 Key Concept: Command Sheet): "When a player gains a command token, they place it in any one of three pools: the tactic pool, the fleet pool, or the strategy pool."
  - Source 3 (p.10 Tactic Pool): "players may spend command tokens from their tactic pool to perform tactical actions"
- [Notes] When a command token is gained, it may be placed in any of the three pools if no specific pool is specified by the gaining effect. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p.10 Key Concept: Command Sheet): "When a player gains a command token, they place it in any one of three pools: the tactic pool, the fleet pool, or the strategy pool."
- [Notes] When a command token is gained, it may be placed in any of the three pools if no specific pool is specified by the gaining effect. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (command-tokens-in-status-phase (Per the rulebook — 3. Status Phase)): "Newly gained tokens may go in any pool."

### R_command_tokens.php

**Notes added** (rulings that were not on the site before)

- [Notes] If an effect instructs a player to spend a command token from their reinforcements, that player must have a command token in their reinforcements to do so. The token remains in their reinforcements, unless the effect places it on the game board. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (spend-token-from-reinforcements (Community consensus)): "You need a token in reinforcements to pay; it isn't purged or moved to your sheet"

**Citations added to existing items**

- [Rules Reference] Each player begins the game with eight tokens on their command sheet: three in their tactic pool, three in their fleet pool, and two in their strategy pool. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p.6 First-Game Setup): "Each player places three command tokens in their tactic pool, three command tokens in their fleet pool (ship silhouette side up), and two command tokens in their strategy pool."
- [Rules Reference] Command tokens in the fleet pool are placed with the ship silhouette faceup. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p.10 Fleet Pool): "Players place command tokens in their fleet pool with the ship silhouette faceup."
- [Rules Reference] When a player gains a command token, they choose which of their three pools to place it in. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p.10 Key Concept: Command Sheet): "When a player gains a command token, they place it in any one of three pools"
- [Rules Reference] During the action phase, a player can perform a tactical action by spending a command token from their tactic pool; they place the command token in a system. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p.13 Activation): "They activ ate that system by taking a command token from their tactic pool and placing it on that system."
- [Rules Reference] After a player performs a strategic action during the action phase, each other player can resolve the secondary ability of that strategy card by spending a command token from their strategy pool. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p.10 Strategy Pool): "Most of the secondary abilities on strategy cards require a player to spend a token from their strategy pool to resolve the ability."
- [Rules Reference] When a player gains a command token, they choose which of their three pools to place it in. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (command-tokens-in-status-phase (Per the rulebook — 3. Status Phase)): "Newly gained tokens may go in any pool."
- [Rules Reference] If a player would gain a command token but has none available in their reinforcements, that player cannot gain that command token. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (command-tokens-are-limited (Community consensus)): "You don't gain it. Your 16 command tokens are a hard limit."
- [Rules Reference] If a game effect would place a player’s command token from their reinforcements and none are available, that player must take a token from a pool on their command sheet, unless the token would be placed into a system that already contains one of their command tokens. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (must-place-command-token-none-in-reinforcements (Community consensus)): "You take one of your choice from your command sheet instead."
- [Rules Reference] If a game effect would place a player’s command token in a system where they already have one, they place the token in their reinforcements instead. Any effects that resolve by placing that token are resolved as normal. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (never-two-own-tokens-in-system (Community consensus)): "if an effect would place your token in a system that already has one, you don't place a second. Construction says the spent token goes to your reinforcements instead, and other effects work the same way."
- [Rules Reference] A player does not spend a command token to resolve the secondary ability of the Leadership strategy card. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (strategy-primary-costs-no-token (Per the rulebook — Strategic Action)): "Secondaries cost a strategy pool token, except Leadership's"
- [Rules Reference] After a player performs a strategic action during the action phase, each other player can resolve the secondary ability of that strategy card by spending a command token from their strategy pool. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (strategy-primary-costs-no-token (Per the rulebook — Strategic Action)): "Secondaries cost a strategy pool token, except Leadership's"
- [Rules Reference] During the action phase, a player can perform a tactical action by spending a command token from their tactic pool; they place the command token in a system. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (one-system-per-tactical-action (Community consensus)): "Each tactical action spends one tactic token to activate one system."

### R_commodities.php

**Removed notes restored**

- [Notes] A player starts the game with zero commodities. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (no-starting-commodities (Community consensus)): "nobody starts with commodities, trade goods or action cards"
- [Notes] If a player has their maximum number of commodities, and is instructed to replenish their commodities, they will take no commodities. However, they will still trigger any “when [this] player replenishes commodities” effects, most notably the Trade Agreement promissory note. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (minister-cards-details (Community consensus)): "Minister of Commerce still pays 1 trade good per neighbor when your commodities were already full, since you still replenished"

**Citations added to existing items**

- [Rules Reference] Commodities represent goods that are plentiful for their own faction and are desired by other factions. A commodity has no inherent game effects, but converts into a trade good if given to or received from another player. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p. 17, Commodities): "Commodities have no inherent value but become trade goods when given to another player."
- [Rules Reference] Commodities and trade goods are represented by opposite sides of the same token. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p. 17, Commodities): "Both trade goods and commodities are represented by opposite sides of the same token"
- [Rules Reference] The commodity value on a player’s faction sheet indicates the maximum number of commodities that player can have. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p. 17, Commodities): "A player cannot have more commodities than that printed value."
- [Rules Reference] When an effect instructs a player to replenish commodities, that player takes the number of commodity tokens necessary so that the amount of commodities that player has equals the commodity value on their faction sheet. Then, those tokens are placed faceup in the commodity area of that player’s faction sheet. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p. 17, Commodities): "that player takes commodity tokens from the supply until they have a number of tokens equal to the commodities value on their faction sheet."
- [Rules Reference] When a player replenishes commodities, that player takes the commodity tokens from the supply. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p. 17, Commodities): "that player takes commodity tokens from the supply until they have a number of tokens equal to the commodities value on their faction sheet."
- [Rules Reference] Players can trade commodities following the rules for transactions. When a player receives a commodity from another player, the player who received that token converts it into a trade good by placing it in the trade good area of their command sheet with the trade good side faceup. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p. 17, Trade): "When a player gives another player a commodity, that commodity converts into a trade good; the player receiving the commodity flips the token to its trade good side."
- [Rules Reference] Any game effect that instructs a player to give a commodity to another player causes that commodity to be converted into a trade good. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p. 17, Trade): "When a player gives another player a commodity, that commodity converts into a trade good"
- [Rules Reference] Players can trade commodities following the rules for transactions. When a player receives a commodity from another player, the player who received that token converts it into a trade good by placing it in the trade good area of their command sheet with the trade good side faceup. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (commodities-become-trade-goods (Community consensus)): "A commodity becomes a trade good the moment another player receives it"
- [Rules Reference] Any game effect that instructs a player to give a commodity to another player causes that commodity to be converted into a trade good. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (commodities-become-trade-goods (Community consensus)): "whether by transaction, Pillage or another effect"

### R_component_action.php

**Notes kept**

- [Notes] Action cards without the "Action" header are not used to perform component actions. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (22.1): "Each component action is indicated by an “Action” header."

**Notes added** (rulings that were not on the site before)

- [Notes] There is no limit to how many component actions a player may perform during a round, other than any limit stated on the component itself. Each component action uses that player’s action for the turn. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (component-actions-no-round-limit (Community consensus)): "No — each one simply uses your action for the turn."

**Citations added to existing items**

- [Rules Reference] Component actions can be found on various game components, including action cards, technology cards, leaders, exploration cards, relics, promissory notes, and faction sheets. Each component action is indicated by an “Action” header. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p.10 Component Actions): "A component action is an action that is printed on a game component."
  - Source 3 (p.10 Component Actions): "Each of these effects is preceded by the word “Action.”"
- [Rules Reference] A component action cannot be performed if its ability cannot be completely resolved. now also cites <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (x3n d0g, 1/25/2019): "'A player cannot resolve a component action if he cannot completely resolve this ability.' Which was a line that I included to basically say 'No, you can't just play an action card that has no legal target in order to skip a turn'"
- [Rules Reference] A component action cannot be performed if its ability cannot be completely resolved. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (component-action-must-fully-resolve (Community consensus)): "a component action can only be performed if you can carry out the whole ability"
- [Rules Reference] If a component action is canceled, it does not use that player’s action. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (sabotaged-action-card-turn-not-used (Community consensus)): "a cancelled card counts as not played, so you still take an action"

### R_component_limitations.php

**LRR section corrections**

- **23.4**: Owner decision: only fighters and infantry have tokens (LRR 23.4b); mechs are limited to their plastic pieces. LRR v2.0 itself says "ground forces".
  - Before: Units: Units are limited to those included in the game, except for fighters and ground forces.
  - After: Units: Units are limited to those included in the game, except for fighters and infantry. <sup>1,2</sup>

**Notes kept**

- [Notes] Players may swap between three value tokens and one value tokens as desired. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (21.8, 36.4, 46.4, 93.7): "Trade good tokens come in values of one and three. A player can swap between these tokens as necessary."
- [Notes] A player may only resolve a deploy ability to place a unit that is in their reinforcements. A player cannot remove a unit from the board to use its deploy ability. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (30.2): "A player can only resolve a deploy ability to place a unit that is in their reinforcements."
  - Source 1 (30.2a): "If there are no units that have a deploy ability in a player’s reinforcements, the deploy ability cannot be used."
- [Notes] When a discard pile is shuffled to form a new deck, any cards that have been purged are not included. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (70.1-70.2): "Purged components cannot be used or otherwise returned to the game by any means."
- [Notes] If a player removes a unit in order to place it, because they have none of that unit type in their reinforcements, that unit is placed undamaged. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (General (removed and placed)): "If it is produced, placed, or replaced which would require a remove and place it is no longer damaged."
- [Notes] If a player is instructed to "replace" one unit with another, and they have none of the replacement unit type in their reinforcements, they may remove a unit of that type from any system that does not contain one of their command tokens and place that unit instead. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (General (keyword replace)): "Any instance of “replace” can be considered to say “remove and place” if no units are left in reinforcements, and would be covered by Component Limitations in the LRR."

**Removed notes restored**

- [Notes] Each faction has sixteen command and seventeen control tokens included in the game. <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p. 6, First-Game Setup, step 3): "17 control tokens"
  - Source 3 (p. 6, First-Game Setup, step 3): "16 command tokens"
- [Notes] As each player only has ten plastic fighter figures and twelve plastic infantry figures, a player cannot have fighters in more than ten systems, and cannot have infantry on more than twelve planets or being carried in more than twelve space areas, or any combination thereof. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (fighter-and-infantry-tokens (Community consensus)): "each stack of tokens must sit with at least one plastic piece of the same type. So your plastic fighters and infantry limit how many places you can have them"
- [Notes] Players may also swap infantry and fighter plastic pieces for tokens at any time. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (fighter-and-infantry-tokens (Community consensus)): "You may swap a plastic piece on the board for a token at any time to free the plastic for use elsewhere"

**Citations added to existing items**

- [Rules Reference] When a player would place a unit, if there are none of that type left in their reinforcements, that player can remove a unit from any system that does not contain one of their command tokens and place that unit in their reinforcements. A player can remove any number of their units in this way; however, any units that are removed must be placed immediately. Abilities cannot force a player to remove and place a unit in this manner. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p. 16, Production): "that player may remove one of their units of that type from a system that does not contain one of their command tokens and return it to their reinforcements."
- [Rules Reference] When producing a fighter or infantry unit, a player can use a fighter or infantry token, as appropriate, from the supply instead of a plastic piece. These tokens must be accompanied by at least one plastic piece of the same type; players can swap infantry and fighter tokens for plastic pieces at any time. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p. 16, Production): "they must be accompanied by at least one plastic figure of that type that matches their color."
- [Notes] A player may only resolve a deploy ability to place a unit that is in their reinforcements. A player cannot remove a unit from the board to use its deploy ability. now also cites <sup>8</sup>
  - Source 8 (p. 10, Mechs): "These abilities can only be resolved to place a unit that is in a player’s reinforcements"
- [Rules Reference] When a player would place a unit, if there are none of that type left in their reinforcements, that player can remove a unit from any system that does not contain one of their command tokens and place that unit in their reinforcements. A player can remove any number of their units in this way; however, any units that are removed must be placed immediately. Abilities cannot force a player to remove and place a unit in this manner. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (taking-units-from-board-when-out (Community consensus)): "the rules let you remove a unit from the board to place it elsewhere, but you are not required to"
- [Rules Reference] When producing a fighter or infantry unit, a player can use a fighter or infantry token, as appropriate, from the supply instead of a plastic piece. These tokens must be accompanied by at least one plastic piece of the same type; players can swap infantry and fighter tokens for plastic pieces at any time. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (fighter-and-infantry-tokens (Community consensus)): "each stack of tokens must sit with at least one plastic piece of the same type"

### R_construction.php

**LRR section corrections**

- **intro**: Owner decision: use the Thunder's Edge revised strategy card.
  - Before: The Construction strategy card allows players to construct structures on planets they control.
  - After: The Construction strategy card allows players to place structures on planets they control. <sup>13</sup>
- **24.2**: Owner decision: use the Thunder's Edge revised strategy card.
  - Before: …may place either one PDS or one space dock on a planet they control. Then, that player may place an additional PDS on a planet they control.
  - After: …may either place one structure on a planet they control, or use the Production ability of one of their space docks. Then, that player may place one structure on a planet they control. <sup>13</sup>
- **24.3**: Owner decision: use the Thunder's Edge revised strategy card.
  - Before: …may spend one command token from their strategy pool and place that command token in any system… Then, that player places either one PDS or one space dock on a planet they control in that system.
  - After: …may spend one command token from their strategy pool to place one structure on a planet they control. The command token is not placed in any system. <sup>13</sup>
- **24.4**: Owner decision: use the Thunder's Edge revised strategy card.
  - Before: When a player places either a PDS or space dock using the Construction strategy card, they take that PDS or space dock from their reinforcements.
  - After: When a player places a structure using the Construction strategy card, they take that structure from their reinforcements. <sup>13</sup>

**Notes kept**

- [Notes] A player may have a maximum of one space dock on each planet. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (79.3): "Each planet can have a maximum of one space dock."
- [Notes] A player may have a maximum of two PDS units on each planet. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (85.5): "A player can have a maximum of two PDS units on each planet."

**Notes added** (rulings that were not on the site before)

- [Notes] Placing structures with the Construction strategy card is not producing units; the structures have no cost, and production rules do not apply. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (construction-structures-free (Community consensus)): "No — space docks and PDS have no cost."
- [Notes] Resolving the secondary ability of the Construction strategy card does not activate a system, and it does not matter whether the system has already been activated. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (te-construction-card (Community consensus)): "It doesn't activate the system or care whether it was activated."

**Citations added to existing items**

- [Notes] A player may have a maximum of one space dock on each planet. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p. 24, Rules Summary): "Players are limited to two PDS units and one space dock on each planet."
- [Notes] A player may have a maximum of two PDS units on each planet. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p. 24, Rules Summary): "Players are limited to two PDS units and one space dock on each planet."
- [Rules Reference] If a player does not have the unit in their reinforcements, that player can remove a unit from any system that does not contain one of their command tokens and place that unit in their reinforcements. Then, that player must place the unit on the game board as instructed by the effect that is placing the unit. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (moving-structures-when-out (Community consensus)): "if none are in reinforcements, you may take one from a system without your command token and place it where the effect directs"
- [Notes] A player may have a maximum of one space dock on each planet. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (structures-not-produced (Per the rulebook — Control, Structures, and the Custodians Token)): "A planet holds at most one space dock and two PDS"
- [Notes] A player may have a maximum of two PDS units on each planet. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (structures-not-produced (Per the rulebook — Control, Structures, and the Custodians Token)): "A planet holds at most one space dock and two PDS"

**Restored without a source** (marked * on the site)

- [Notes] Structures cannot be placed on the planet with the Demilitarized Zone exploration card attached. <sup>*</sup>

### R_control.php

**Notes kept**

- [Notes] Control tokens are not component limited. <sup>1</sup>
  - Edited from: Control tokens are not component limited; a player may control an unlimited number of planets.
  - Source 1 (23.2): "TOKENS: Tokens are limited to those included in the game, except for the following: • Control Tokens"

**Notes added** (rulings that were not on the site before)

- [Notes] Different players may control different planets in the same system. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (different-players-planets-same-system (Community consensus)): "each planet is controlled separately and nobody controls the space area"
- [Notes] If a player is given another player’s planet card, such as with the Hacan player’s mech, Pride of Kenara, they gain control of that planet. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (planet-card-transfer-control (Community consensus)): "control and holding the planet card go together, so the receiver controls the planet"

**Citations added to existing items**

- [Rules Reference] When a player gains control of a planet, they take the planet card that corresponds to that planet and place it in their play area; that card is exhausted. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (Learn to Play p.15): "When a player gains control of a planet, they gain its corresponding planet card and place it in their play area exhausted."
- [Rules Reference] When a player gains control of a planet that is not already controlled by another player, they explore that planet. now also cites <sup>8</sup>
  - Source 8 (Prophecy of Kings Rulebook p.11): "When a player takes control of a planet that is not already controlled by another player, they explore that planet."
- [Rules Reference] During the Invasion step of a tactical action, control is determined during the Establish Control step instead. now also cites <sup>5,6</sup>
  - Source 5 (DR, BGG Skootur, Oct 12, 2017): "This bullet is not intended to supersede the invasion timing as it pertains to establishing control of a planet"
  - Source 6 (CC, Coexistence): "During the Invasion step of a tactical action, control is not exchanged until the Establish Control step."
- [Rules Reference (intro)] Each player begins the game with control of each planet in their home system. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (home-planets-controlled-at-start (Community consensus)): "You control every home planet from the start, empty or not"
- [Rules Reference] When a player gains control of a planet, they take the planet card ... that card is exhausted. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (legendary-ability-card-ready (Community consensus)): "The planet card arrives exhausted as usual"
- [Rules Reference] While a player controls a planet, that planet's card remains in their play area until they lose control of that planet. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (keeping-control-of-planets (Community consensus)): "you control a planet while you hold its card"
- [Rules Reference] A player can control a planet that they do not have any units on; that player places a control token ... <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (keeping-control-of-planets (Community consensus)): "with no units there, mark it with a control token."
- [Rules Reference] A player can lose control of a planet through some game effects. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (keeping-control-of-planets (Community consensus)): "You only lose control when another player gains it, by invading or an effect that says so."
- [Rules Reference] A player loses control of a planet if they no longer have units on it and another player has units on it. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (destroying-ground-forces-not-control (Community consensus)): "destroying defenders never changes control"

### R_cost.php

**Notes kept**

- [Notes] Whenever a unit is produced, its cost must be paid, unless the effect that is producing the unit explicitly says otherwise. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (26.1): "To produce a unit, a player must spend a number of resources equal to or greater than the cost of the unit they are producing."
- [Notes] A player does not have to pay a unit's cost to resolve that unit's Deploy ability. However, the Deploy ability itself may have a cost that must be paid. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (30.1a): "A player does not have to spend resources to deploy a unit unless otherwise specified."

**Citations added to existing items**

- [Rules Reference] To produce a unit, a player must spend a number of resources equal to or greater than the cost of the unit they are producing. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p. 16, Production): "they may choose to produce any of the units on their faction sheet by spending resources equal to the chosen unit’s cost."
- [Rules Reference] If the cost is accompanied by two icons – typically for fighters and ground forces – a player produces two of that unit for that cost. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p. 16, Production): "If a unit’s cost is accompanied by two icons, such as the cost values of fighters and infantry, the player receives two units for the indicated cost."
- [Rules Reference] Structures do not have costs and are usually placed by resolving the Construction strategy card. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (construction-structures-free (Community consensus)): "space docks and PDS have no cost"
- [Notes] Whenever a unit is produced, its cost must be paid, unless the effect that is producing the unit explicitly says otherwise. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (produce-vs-place (Community consensus)): "An effect that says 'produce' means you pay the cost unless it says otherwise"

### R_custodians_token.php

**Citations added to existing items**

- [Rules Reference] The custodians token begins each game on Mecatol Rex. The token represents the caretakers that safeguard the seat of the empire until such time as the galactic council can be reconvened. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p. 20, Custodians Token): "The custodians token represents the caretakers that safeguard Mecatol Rex until one of the great races can claim the throne."
- [Rules Reference] Units can move into the system that contains Mecatol Rex following normal rules; however, players cannot commit ground forces to land on Mecatol Rex until the custodians token is removed from the planet. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p. 20, Custodians Token): "Players may freely move units into the Mecatol Rex system, but cannot land ground forces on the planet while the custodians token is present."
- [Rules Reference] Before the Commit Ground Forces step of an invasion, the active player can remove the custodians token from Mecatol Rex by spending six influence. Then, that player must commit at least one ground force to land on the planet. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p. 20, Custodians Token): "To remove this token, the active player must spend six influence immediately before landing ground forces on the planet."
- [Rules Reference] When a player removes the custodians token from Mecatol Rex, they take the token from the game board and place it in their play area. Then, they gain one victory point. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p. 20, Custodians Token): "When a player removes the custodians token, they place it in their play area and gains one victory point."
- [Rules Reference] After a player removes the custodians token from Mecatol Rex, the agenda phase is added to all subsequent game rounds, including the game round during which the custodians token was removed from Mecatol Rex. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p. 20, Custodians Token): "the agenda phase is added as the last phase of each game round, including the round during which a player gained control of Mecatol Rex."
- [Rules Reference] Before the Commit Ground Forces step of an invasion, the active player can remove the custodians token from Mecatol Rex by spending six influence. Then, that player must commit at least one ground force to land on the planet. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (custodians-token-mecatol (Per the rulebook — Control, Structures, and the Custodians Token)): "during invasion, before committing ground forces, spend 6 influence to remove the custodians token"
- [Rules Reference] When a player removes the custodians token from Mecatol Rex, they take the token from the game board and place it in their play area. Then, they gain one victory point. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (custodians-token-mecatol (Per the rulebook — Control, Structures, and the Custodians Token)): "gaining it and 1 victory point"
- [Rules Reference] After a player removes the custodians token from Mecatol Rex, the agenda phase is added to all subsequent game rounds, including the game round during which the custodians token was removed from Mecatol Rex. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (agenda-phase-timing-and-readying (Per the rulebook — 4. Agenda Phase)): "Once the custodians token is off Mecatol Rex, the agenda phase follows the status phase every round"

**Restored without a source** (marked * on the site)

- [Notes] The custodians token is not an attachment. <sup>*</sup>

### R_deals.php

**Removed notes restored**

- [Notes] In general, only the terms of the deal that a player can immediately perform, even without the deal taking place, are binding. <sup>5</sup>
  - Trimmed from: In general, only the terms of the deal that a player can immediately perform, even without the deal taking place, are binding. For example:
  - Source 5 (Milty, 10/02/2018): "The terms need to be legal at the time of the transaction."
  - Source 5 (x3n d0g, 10/13/2018): "This would be non-binding, because when the deal is made, the non-Ghost player does not technically qualify to even be able to perform his side of the deal (he doesn’t have the IFF). If he already had the IFF, it could be a binding transaction."
- [Notes] The following are examples of non-binding deals: <sup>5</sup>
  - Trimmed from: The following are further examples of non-binding deals:
  - Source 5 (x3n d0g, 10/13/2018): "This would be non-binding, because when the deal is made, the non-Ghost player does not technically qualify to even be able to perform his side of the deal (he doesn’t have the IFF). If he already had the IFF, it could be a binding transaction."
  - Source 5 (Skootur, Oct 19, 2017 (BGG)): "—Non-Binding: You get to refresh for free now, but must trade me 2 for 1 after the trade card resolves."
- [Notes] Making a deal to use a promissory note in a specific way, before the promissory note has been transacted. <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (x3n d0g, 10/13/2018): "This would be non-binding, because when the deal is made, the non-Ghost player does not technically qualify to even be able to perform his side of the deal (he doesn’t have the IFF). If he already had the IFF, it could be a binding transaction."
- [Notes] Making a deal to trade commodities in exchange for the active player to replenish another player's commodities during the resolution of the primary ability of the Trade strategic action. <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (Skootur, Oct 19, 2017 (BGG)): "—Non-Binding: You get to refresh for free now, but must trade me 2 for 1 after the trade card resolves."
- [Notes] Making a deal to not make use of a unit’s Space Cannon ability during a tactical action, before ships have been moved. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (when-is-a-deal-binding (Community consensus)): "taking a trade good not to fire Space Cannon at the moment you decide whether to fire binds you not to fire. Promises about future actions [...] are non-binding"
  - Source 2 (deal-not-to-attack (Community consensus)): "pay for a specific immediate act, such as choosing not to fire Space Cannon right now"
- [Notes] Making a deal for a player to vote on an agenda in a certain way, when it is not yet that player’s opportunity to vote. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (vote-deals-binding (Community consensus)): "Only for a player about to cast votes right now. [...] a promise to vote a certain way later can still be broken."
- [Notes] Any deal that will resolve after dice are rolled. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (when-is-a-deal-binding (Community consensus)): "Only when its terms resolve immediately [...] You can bind yourself to an act, but not to its result"

**Citations added to existing items**

- [Rules Reference] If the terms of a deal can be resolved immediately, it is a binding deal. When a deal is binding, a player must adhere to the terms of the agreement and whatever transactions, if any, were agreed upon. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p.17 Neighbors, Transactions, and Deals): "Because the effect can be resolved immediately, this deal is a binding deal. When a deal is binding, a player must honor their end of the bargain."
- [Rules Reference] If the terms of a deal cannot be resolved immediately, it is a non–binding deal. When a deal is non–binding, a player does not have to adhere to any part of the agreement. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p.17 Neighbors, Transactions, and Deals): "Because the effect cannot be resolved immediately, this deal is a non-binding deal."
  - Source 3 (p.17 Neighbors, Transactions, and Deals): "is not required to honor their end of the bargain"
- [Rules Reference] If the terms of a deal can be resolved immediately, it is a binding deal. When a deal is binding, a player must adhere to the terms of the agreement and whatever transactions, if any, were agreed upon. now also cites <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (Skootur, Oct 19, 2017 (BGG)): "The “immediate” requirement for binding deals is satisfied only when all aspects of the deal can be acted upon during the same game effect"
- [Rules Reference] The results of playing an action card, including the act of successfully resolving a card, are not instantaneous and cannot be guaranteed. They cannot be part of a binding deal. now also cites <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (QuantumOctopus, 05/16/2019): "the result of an action card (including, such as in this case, simply successfully resolving that action card in any way) cannot be part of a binding deal."
- [Rules Reference] Players can make deals with each other at any time, even if they are not neighbors. However, deals that include a transaction must follow the rules for transactions, including that the players be neighbors. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (who-can-transact-and-when (Per the rulebook — The Economy: Resources, Trade Goods, and Commodities)): "Deals that don't exchange components can be made with anyone at any time."
- [Rules Reference] If the terms of a deal can be resolved immediately, it is a binding deal. When a deal is binding, a player must adhere to the terms of the agreement and whatever transactions, if any, were agreed upon. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (when-is-a-deal-binding (Community consensus)): "Only when its terms resolve immediately"
- [Rules Reference] The results of playing an action card, including the act of successfully resolving a card, are not instantaneous and cannot be guaranteed. They cannot be part of a binding deal. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (when-is-a-deal-binding (Community consensus)): "You can bind yourself to an act, but not to its result, such as a card that might be Sabotaged."
- [Rules Reference] If the terms of a deal cannot be resolved immediately, it is a non–binding deal. When a deal is non–binding, a player does not have to adhere to any part of the agreement. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (when-is-a-deal-binding (Community consensus)): "Promises about future actions, and if-then conditions, are non-binding and can be broken."
- [Notes] In general, only the terms of the deal that a player can immediately perform, even without the deal taking place, are binding. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (when-is-a-deal-binding (Community consensus)): "Only when its terms resolve immediately"

**Removed notes that the site already covers elsewhere**

- [Notes] Production-step dreadnought example (binding). _(no source (interpretive example))_
  - Covered by [R_deals.php](R_deals.php) [Notes]: In general, only the terms of the deal that a player can immediately perform, even without the deal taking place, are binding.

  - Covered by [R_deals.php](R_deals.php) [Notes]: In general, only the terms of the deal that a player can immediately perform, even without the deal taking place, are binding.
