### R_deploy.php

**Notes added** (rulings that were not on the site before)

- [Notes] Using a Deploy ability is always optional, even if the ability’s text does not include the word “may”. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (Naalu Collective / Iconoclast): "Deploy being a unit ability is always a may."

**Citations added to existing items**

- [Rules Reference] Some units have deploy abilities. Deploy abilities are indicated by the Deploy header and provide the means to place specific units on the game board without producing them as normal. now also cites <sup>8</sup>
  - Source 8 (Prophecy of Kings Rulebook p.10): "Deploy abilities provide an alternative way to place units on the game board."
- [Rules Reference] A player can only resolve a Deploy ability to place a unit that is in their reinforcements. now also cites <sup>8</sup>
  - Source 8 (Prophecy of Kings Rulebook p.10): "These abilities can only be resolved to place a unit that is in a player’s reinforcements"
- [Rules Reference] A unit’s Deploy ability can be resolved only once per timing window. now also cites <sup>8</sup>
  - Source 8 (Prophecy of Kings Rulebook p.10): "each deploy ability can be resolved only once per timing window."
- [Rules Reference (intro)] Some units have deploy abilities ... place specific units on the game board without producing them as normal. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (mechs-are-ground-forces (Community consensus)): "Deploy places a unit without producing it"

### R_destroyed.php

**Citations added to existing items**

- [Rules Reference] Various game effects can cause a unit to be destroyed. When a player’s unit is destroyed, it is removed from the game board and returned to their reinforcements. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p. 14, Space Combat): "A player removes destroyed ships from the game board and places them in their reinforcements."
- [Rules Reference] When a player assigns hits that were produced against their units, that player chooses a number of their units to be destroyed equal to the number of hits produced against those units. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p. 14, Space Combat): "Each player must choose and destroy one of their ships for each hit their opponent produced."
- [Rules Reference] If a player’s unit is removed from the board by a game effect, it is not treated as being destroyed; effects that trigger when a unit is destroyed are not triggered. now also cites <sup>10</sup>
  - Source 10 (p. 14, Rules Updates: Gravity Rift): "units that fail to survive the roll are removed from the board and returned to players’ reinforcements rather than being destroyed—meaning that abilities that trigger when a unit is destroyed are not resolved."
- [Rules Reference] If a player’s unit is removed from the board by a game effect, it is not treated as being destroyed; effects that trigger when a unit is destroyed are not triggered. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (units-not-tied-to-ships-after-moving (Community consensus)): "Units removed for lack of capacity are removed, not destroyed, so Infantry II doesn't trigger"

### R_diplomacy.php

**Removed notes restored**

- [Notes] The Diplomacy token represents a command token from each player other than the player with the Diplomacy strategy card. It may be used to simplify play when no player is expected to interact with the command tokens placed by the primary ability. <sup>7</sup>
  - Trimmed from: The Diplomacy token represents a command token from each player other than the player with the Diplomacy strategy card. It may be used to simplify play when no player is expected to interact with the command tokens placed by the primary ability, especially during early rounds.
  - Source 7 (p. 12, Diplomacy Token): "This token is a player aid included to facilitate ease of play when resolving simple uses of the “Diplomacy” strategy card’s primary ability. It represents a command token from each player."
- [Notes] A player cannot increase the number of tokens they have access to from the use of the Diplomacy token. <sup>7</sup>
  - Trimmed from: In particular, a player cannot increase the number of tokens they have access to from the use of the Diplomacy token. After a player has played Diplomacy, should they use the Diplomacy token, then each other player must keep a command token available in their reinforcements that corresponds to the command token represented by the Diplomacy token.
  - Source 7 (p. 12, Diplomacy Token): "It cannot be used to bring a player above the component limit for command tokens"
- [Notes] Game effects that can remove a command token from a system may still be used to remove a command token from the system containing the Diplomacy token. Should this happen, players may first wish to replace the Diplomacy token with the corresponding command tokens, then remove the required command token, leaving the rest in the system. <sup>7</sup>
  - Source 7 (p. 12, Diplomacy Token): "should not be used when interacting with abilities that remove command tokens."
- [Notes] The system that contains the Diplomacy token should be treated as containing a command token of the relevant players for all game effects. <sup>7</sup>
  - Trimmed from: The system that contains the Diplomacy token should be treated as containing a command token of the relevant players for all game effects. Primarily this means that the system cannot be activated by those players, nor can they move ships or transport units out of it. Other relevant effects include preventing a second command token from being placed in that system should a player resolve a Skilled Retreat action card to move ships into that system, or allowing the Argent player to move ships into that system with Helix Protocol, their hero ability.
  - Source 7 (p. 12, Diplomacy Token): "It represents a command token from each player."
- [Notes] If the player with Diplomacy controls fewer than two exhausted planets, they may still perform a strategic action. They will ready as many planets as possible. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (diplomacy-revised-card (Community consensus)): "lets the primary player also ready up to 2 exhausted planets they control"

### R_elimination.php

**Notes kept**

  - Source 4 (Exploration, relics when eliminated): "Relics are purged, relic fragments discarded."

  - Source 4 (General, captured units when owner eliminated): "Captured units remain on the sheet of the player that captured them. If they would ever be returned to the eliminated player, they are returned to the game box instead"

  - Source 5 (Vidyaraja, Sep 18, 2017 (BGG), answer 6): "the Nekro player takes that tech and places it in his play area until such time as the game ends or he moves that token"
- [Rules Reference] A player is eliminated when they meet all of the following three conditions: <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (elimination-conditions (Per the rulebook — Elimination)): "Only when all three are true: no ground forces on the board, no units with Production, and no planets controlled."

- [Notes] A unit in an entropic scar cannot use unit abilities. <sup>7</sup>

### R_expedition.php

**Removed notes restored**

- [Notes] A player may perform an expedition, which will unlock their breakthrough, and potentially put The Fracture and/or Thunder’s Edge into play. <sup>7</sup>
  - Source 7 (p.8 Thunder's Edge Expedition): "Players may venture to Thunder’s Edge to unlock powerful new abilities and potentially earn the right to claim the planet of Thunder’s Edge for their faction."
  - Source 7 (p.8 Breakthroughs and Synergy): "Each time a breakthrough is gained, there is a possibility that the fracture will come into play."
- [Notes] At the end of their turn, a player may perform an expedition. To do so they choose one of the unclaimed slices on the expedition token. They pay the indicated cost, and place one of their control tokens in the indicated area to claim it. <sup>7</sup>
  - Source 7 (p.8 Thunder's Edge Expedition): "At the end of a player’s turn, they may commit to the expedition. To do so, they choose an unclaimed slice of the expedition and pay the indicated cost, placing one of their control tokens in that slice to indicate that it has been claimed."
- [Notes] When a player performs an expedition, they gain their faction’s breakthrough if they do not already have it. This will trigger a breakthrough roll to possibly place The Fracture into play. <sup>7</sup>
  - Source 7 (p.8 Thunder's Edge Expedition): "The first time a player claims one of the expedition slices, they gain their faction’s breakthrough."
  - Source 7 (p.8 Breakthroughs and Synergy): "When a player gains their breakthrough, regardless of the source, if The Fracture is not already in play, they roll one die."
- [Notes] The costs to perform an expedition are: <sup>7</sup>
  - Trimmed from: The costs to perform an expedition are, in clockwise order from the top of the expedition token:
  - Source 7 (p.8 Thunder's Edge Expedition): "The expedition costs are as follows:"
- [Notes] Spend five resources; <sup>7</sup>
  - Source 7 (p.8 Thunder's Edge Expedition): "Spend 5 Resources"
- [Notes] Discard two action cards; <sup>7</sup>
  - Source 7 (p.8 Thunder's Edge Expedition): "Discard 2 Action Cards"
- [Notes] Spend five influence; <sup>7</sup>
  - Source 7 (p.8 Thunder's Edge Expedition): "Spend 5 Influence"
- [Notes] Discard one unscored secret objective; <sup>7</sup>
  - Source 7 (p.8 Thunder's Edge Expedition): "Discard 1 Unscored Secret Objective"
- [Notes] Exhaust a planet that has a technology speciality; or <sup>7</sup>
  - Source 7 (p.8 Thunder's Edge Expedition): "Exhaust 1 Technology Specialty Planet"
- [Notes] Spend three trade goods. <sup>7</sup>
  - Source 7 (p.8 Thunder's Edge Expedition): "Spend 3 Trade Goods"
- [Notes] One player may claim multiple slices. A single slice cannot be claimed multiple times (neither by the same or different players). <sup>7</sup>
  - Trimmed from: One player may claim multiple slices, but no more than one slice per turn. A single slice cannot be claimed multiple times (neither by the same or different players).
  - Source 7 (p.8 Thunder's Edge Expedition): "A player can claim multiple expedition slices in a game, but must choose a different unclaimed slice each time they do so."
  - Source 7 (p.8 Thunder's Edge Expedition): "Once claimed, that slice cannot be claimed by another player"
- [Notes] If a player already has their breakthrough when they claim a slice, no additional effect will trigger, other than for the sixth and final slice. <sup>7</sup>
  - Source 7 (p.8 Thunder's Edge Expedition): "The first time a player claims one of the expedition slices, they gain their faction’s breakthrough."
- [Notes] Once the sixth and final slice has been claimed, Thunder’s Edge will enter play. <sup>7</sup>
  - Source 7 (p.8 Thunder's Edge Expedition): "When all slices are claimed, the expedition is complete; the player who claimed the final slice flips Thunder’s Edge to its planet side"
- [Notes] The player who claimed the sixth and final slice flips the expedition token to the Thunder’s Edge side, and places it in a system on the game board. They must choose a system that does not contain a planet, a supernova, or a printed wormhole, and is not in The Fracture, should it be in play. <sup>7</sup>
  - Trimmed from: Then, the player who claimed the sixth and final slice flips the expedition token to the Thunder’s Edge side, and places it in a system on the game board. They must choose a system that does not contain a planet, a supernova, or a printed wormhole, and is not in The Fracture, should it be in play.
  - Source 7 (p.8 Thunder's Edge Expedition): "places it in a system of their choice that does not contain a planet, a supernova, or a printed wormhole"
  - Source 7 (p.8 Thunder's Edge Expedition): "Thunder’s Edge cannot be placed in The Fracture."
- [Notes] Finally, the player who had claimed the most slices of the expedition token places a number of infantry equal to the number of slices they had claimed on to Thunder’s Edge. If multiple players are tied for the most number of slices, the player placing Thunder’s Edge chooses one of those players to place the infantry; they may choose themself. <sup>7</sup>
  - Trimmed from: Finally, the player who had claimed the most slices of the expedition token places a number of infantry equal to the number of slices they had claimed on to Thunder’s Edge. If multiple players are tied for the most number of slices, the player placing Thunder’s Edge chooses one of those players to place the infantry; they may choose themself. The player placing the infantry then gains control of Thunder’s Edge.
  - Source 7 (p.8 Thunder's Edge Expedition): "the player with the most control tokens on the expedition places that many infantry on Thunder’s Edge. In the case of a tie, the player who claimed the final slice chooses which tied player places infantry on Thunder’s Edge."
- [Notes] If Thunder’s Edge is place in a system containing a frontier token, that token is not removed. <sup>7</sup>
  - Trimmed from: If Thunder’s Edge is place in a system containing a frontier token, that token is not removed. It may be explored by a player with the Dark Energy Tap technology at a later point in time.
  - Source 7 (p.16 Clarifications: Thunder's Edge): "When Thunder’s Edge is placed into a system that contains a frontier token, do not remove the frontier token; it can still be explored as normal."

**Notes added** (rulings that were not on the site before)

  - Source 8 (p.11 Exploration): "Planets that do not have a type cannot be explored."
- [Rules Reference] If a planet has multiple traits, the player exploring the planet chooses which of the corresponding exploration decks to draw from. now also cites <sup>7</sup>
  - Source 7 (p.11 Dual Planet Traits): "the exploring player can choose to draw a card matching either of the planet’s traits (but not both)"
- [Rules Reference] If a player gains control of multiple planets or resolves multiple explore effects at the same time, they choose the order in which they resolve those explorations, completely resolving each exploration card before resolving the next. now also cites <sup>8</sup>
  - Source 8 (p.11 Exploration): "If a player gains control of multiple planets at the same time, they choose the order in which they explore those planets, drawing and resolving each planet’s exploration card before exploring the next planet."
- [Rules Reference] Players can explore space areas that contain frontier tokens if they own the Dark Energy Tap technology or if another game effect allows them to. now also cites <sup>8</sup>
  - Source 8 (p.11 Exploration): "Players that have the “Dark Energy Tap” technology can explore frontier tokens."
  - Source 8 (p.16 Clarifications): "If an ability instructs a player to explore a frontier token, they may do so even if they do not have the “Dark Energy Tap” technology."
- [Rules Reference] When a player explores a frontier token, they draw and resolve a card from the frontier exploration deck. now also cites <sup>8</sup>
  - Source 8 (p.11 Exploration): "When a player explores a frontier token, they discard the token and draw a card from the top of the frontier exploration deck."
- [Rules Reference] After a frontier token is explored, it is discarded and returned to the supply. now also cites <sup>8</sup>
  - Source 8 (p.11 Exploration): "When a player explores a frontier token, they discard the token"
- [Rules Reference] To resolve an exploration card, a player reads the card, makes any necessary decisions, and resolves its ability. If the card was not a relic fragment or an attachment, it is discarded into its respective discard pile. now also cites <sup>8</sup>
  - Source 8 (p.11 Exploration): "Then, the card is discarded unless it is a relic fragment or has an “Attach” ability"
- [Rules Reference] If a player resolves an exploration card that has an “attach” header, they attach that card to the planet card of the planet being explored. now also cites <sup>8</sup>
  - Source 8 (p.11 Attached Cards): "When a player draws an exploration card that includes the “Attach” header, they attach it to the explored planet’s card"
- [Rules Reference] If a player resolves an exploration card that has “relic fragment” in the title, they place that card faceup in their play area. now also cites <sup>8</sup>
  - Source 8 (p.11 Relic Fragments and Relics): "When a player draws an exploration card that contains “relic fragment” in the title, they place it faceup in their play area."
- [Rules Reference] Players can resolve the ability of relic fragments that are in their play area. Resolving these abilities allows players to draw cards from the relic deck. now also cites <sup>8</sup>
  - Source 8 (p.11 Relic Fragments and Relics): "three relic fragments of the same type can be purged to gain a relic"
  - Source 8 (p.11 Relic Fragments and Relics): "When a player gains a relic, they draw a card from the top of the relic deck"
- [Rules Reference] Relic fragments can be exchanged as part of transactions. now also cites <sup>8</sup>
  - Source 8 (p.11 Relic Fragments and Relics): "Relic fragments can be exchanged as part of a transaction."
- [Notes] If a player is to gain multiple planets in a system, they choose the order in which they gain them, and explore each planet as they gain it before gaining the next. now also cites <sup>8</sup>
  - Source 8 (p.11 Exploration): "If a player gains control of multiple planets at the same time, they choose the order in which they explore those planets"
- [Rules Reference] Frontier tokens are placed in systems during setup and by specific abilities. now also cites <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (The Fracture): "Frontier tokens are placed during setup and the fracture is not in play at this time. The Empyrean Hero will place frontier tokens into the empty systems of the Fracture if it is in play."
- [Rules Reference] When a player takes control of a planet that is not already controlled by another player, they explore that planet. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (exploration-basics (Community consensus)): "When you gain control of a planet nobody controlled, draw a card from the exploration deck matching its trait"
- [Rules Reference] When a player explores a planet, they draw and resolve a card from the exploration deck that corresponds to that planet’s trait. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (exploration-basics (Community consensus)): "When you gain control of a planet nobody controlled, draw a card from the exploration deck matching its trait"
- [Rules Reference] Planets that do not have traits, such as Mecatol Rex and planets in home systems, cannot be explored. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (titans-terragenesis-limits (Community consensus)): "Mecatol Rex and home planets have no trait and can't be explored"
- [Rules Reference] If a planet has multiple traits, the player exploring the planet chooses which of the corresponding exploration decks to draw from. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (explore-multi-trait-planet (Community consensus)): "You choose one of the matching trait decks and draw a single card from it."
- [Rules Reference] To resolve an exploration card, a player reads the card, makes any necessary decisions, and resolves its ability. If the card was not a relic fragment or an attachment, it is discarded into its respective discard pile. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (exploration-cards-public (Community consensus)): "relic fragments are kept face up and attachments go on planets, while other cards are discarded. When a deck runs out, shuffle its discards into a new deck"
- [Rules Reference] If there are no cards in an exploration deck, its discard pile is shuffled to form a new exploration deck. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (exploration-cards-public (Community consensus)): "relic fragments are kept face up and attachments go on planets, while other cards are discarded. When a deck runs out, shuffle its discards into a new deck"

  - Source 2 (exploration-cards-public (Community consensus)): "relic fragments are kept face up and attachments go on planets, while other cards are discarded. When a deck runs out, shuffle its discards into a new deck"

  - Source 2 (relic-fragments-tradeable (Community consensus)): "relic fragments can be included in transactions by either side."

### R_fleet_pool.php

**Removed notes restored**

- [Notes] Fighters and ground forces do not count towards capacity during combat. When combat ends however, units will need to be removed to meet capacity requirements. <sup>1,3</sup>
  - Trimmed from: Fighters and ground forces do not count towards capacity during combat. As such, any number of Fighter II may be in a system during combat, regardless of capacity and fleet pool. This will usually only be caused by effects that place units in a system during combat. When combat ends however, units will need to be removed to meet capacity and fleet pool requirements.
  - Source 1 (LRR 16.3c): "A player’s fighters and ground forces do not count against capacity during combat. At the end of combat, any excess units are removed"
  - Source 3 (Learn to Play p.14): "During combat, a player’s fighters and ground forces can exceed their ships’ capacity, but at the end of the combat, any excess units are destroyed."
- [Notes] Ships may be moved into or produced in a system even if doing so would exceed the fleet pool limit. However, some of those ships must immediately be removed to satisfy the limit. <sup>5,6</sup>
  - Trimmed from: Ships may be moved into, produced in or placed in a system even if doing so would exceed the fleet pool limit. However, some of those ships must immediately be removed to satisfy the limit.
  - Source 5 (DR, BGG garfielder, Sep 28, 2017): "you can destroy any of the ships in the system and still keep the fighters, it is a legal move as long as you respect fleet supply once you’ve moved. For #2, you could build 3 dreadnoughts and destroy the destroyer that was there initially."
  - Source 6 (CC, The Emirates of Hacan): "with zero in fleet you can produce 3 ships, gain the fleet token, then remove 2 ships to fleet pool."
- [Notes] During movement, a ship may move through a system regardless of how many ships are in that system relative to the fleet pool limit. <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (DR, BGG Crikrunner, Sep 27, 2017): "the fleet supply doesn’t count while you’re moving, it only cares about where you’ve stopped."
  - Source 5 (DR, email Bocks, Mar 17, 2018): "In neither instance do you need to destroy any ships due to fleet supply"
- [Notes] If some of those ships are fighters II, they may instead count towards that player's capacity in that system. If capacity is exceeded, fighters or ground forces must be removed to meet the limit. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (fighter-ii-moving-alone (Community consensus)): "If ships in the destination have room for them, they don't count against your fleet pool."
  - Source 2 (fighters-without-capacity (Community consensus)): "Fighter IIs that don't fit in capacity count against your fleet pool like other ships."

**Citations added to existing items**

- [Rules Reference] The fleet pool is an area of a player’s command sheet. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (Learn to Play p.7): "These pools are located on the player’s command sheet."
- [Rules Reference] The number of command tokens in a player’s fleet pool indicates the maximum number of non–fighter ships that a player can have in a system. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (Learn to Play p.10): "the number of tokens in a player’s fleet pool is the maximum number of ships, excluding fighters, that they can have in each system."
- [Rules Reference] Players place command tokens in their fleet pools with the ship silhouette faceup. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (Learn to Play p.10): "Players place command tokens in their fleet pool with the ship silhouette faceup."
- [Rules Reference] If at any time the number of a player’s non–fighter ships in a system exceeds the number of tokens in that player’s fleet pool, they choose and remove excess ships in that system, returning those units to their reinforcements. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (Learn to Play p.10): "If a player ever has more ships in a system than they have tokens in their fleet pool, they must return ships from that system to their reinforcements"
- [Rules Reference] Players do not spend command tokens from this pool unless a game effect specifically allows it. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (Learn to Play p.10): "Players do not spend these command tokens like the command tokens in their other pools."
- [Rules Reference] The number of command tokens in a player's fleet pool indicates the maximum number of non-fighter ships that a player can have in a system. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (fleet-pool-when-checked (Community consensus)): "any non-fighter ships over your fleet pool are removed straight away"
- [Rules Reference] If at any time the number of a player's non-fighter ships in a system exceeds ... they choose and remove excess ships ... <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (exceeding-fleet-pool-deliberately (Community consensus)): "you just remove the excess right away, choosing which."
- [Notes] Fighters and ground forces do not count towards capacity during combat. When combat ends however, units will need to be removed to meet capacity requirements. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (capacity-checked-outside-combat (Community consensus)): "During combat fighters and ground forces may exceed capacity and keep fighting; the excess is removed when the space combat ends"
- [Notes] Ships may be moved into or produced in a system even if doing so would exceed the fleet pool limit. However, some of those ships must immediately be removed ... <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (exceeding-fleet-pool-deliberately (Community consensus)): "Yes — nothing stops you; you just remove the excess right away, choosing which."
- [Notes] During movement, a ship may move through a system regardless of how many ships are in that system relative to the fleet pool limit. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (moving-ships-simultaneous (Community consensus)): "Fleet pool isn't checked in systems you pass through, only at the end"

**Notes removed**

- [Notes] Fighters and ground forces do not count towards capacity during combat. As such, any number of Fighter II may be in a system during combat ... When combat ends however, units will need to be removed to meet capacity and fleet pool requirements. _(no source)_ _(kept out: contradicted by RP (rp_logs conflict: fleet pool checked at all times; unsupported Fighter IIs count against fleet pool); remaining capacity part duplicates the kept sourced note)_

### R_fracture.php

**Removed notes restored**

- [Notes] The Fracture consists of additional systems beyond the regular bounds of the game map. <sup>7</sup>
  - Source 7 (p. 9, The Fracture): "The Fracture is an enigmatic area of space that is not connected to the rest of the galaxy."
  - Source 7 (p. 9, The Fracture): "places it along any edge of the game board"
- [Notes] When a player gains their breakthrough, they roll a dice. On a result of 1 or 10, The Fracture enters play. Other game effects may also bring The Fracture into play. <sup>7</sup>
  - Source 7 (p. 8, Breakthroughs and Synergy): "If their die roll is equal to 1 or 10, they put The Fracture into play."
  - Source 7 (p. 9, The Fracture): "If The Fracture was brought into play by another ability"
- [Notes] When The Fracture enters play, it is placed against the edge of the regular game map. <sup>7</sup>
  - Source 7 (p. 9, The Fracture): "the player that brought it into play places it along any edge of the game board"
- [Notes] The placement location of The Fracture is arbitrary, and should have no mechanical effect on the game state. <sup>7</sup>
  - Trimmed from: The placement location of The Fracture is arbitrary, and should have no mechanical effect on the game state. The Fracture may be moved if required at a later point during the game.
  - Source 7 (p. 9, The Fracture): "Regardless of where The Fracture is placed, its systems are not adjacent to the systems it is touching, and each of its systems is considered to be on the edge of the game board."
- [Notes] All systems in The Fracture are considered to be on the edge of the game board. <sup>7</sup>
  - Trimmed from: All systems in The Fracture, as well as the systems of the regular game map that they are touching, are considered to be on the edge of the game board.
  - Source 7 (p. 9, The Fracture): "each of its systems is considered to be on the edge of the game board."
- [Notes] When The Fracture is brought into play, neutral units are placed on the planets in The Fracture as well as the space area of those planets’ systems, as indicated on the reverse side of The Fracture tiles. <sup>7</sup>
  - Source 7 (p. 9, The Fracture): "They then place neutral units as indicated on the back of The Fracture’s tiles."
- [Notes] When The Fracture is brought into play, several ingress tokens will be placed on the game board. Several systems in The Fracture contain a printed egress. Each ingress is adjacent to each egress, and vice versa. An ingress is not adjacent to an ingress and an egress is not adjacent to an egress. <sup>7</sup>
  - Source 7 (p. 9, The Fracture): "A system that contains an ingress is adjacent to each system in The Fracture that contains an egress. However, ingress systems are not adjacent to other ingress systems, and egress systems are not adjacent to other egress systems."
- [Notes] If The Fracture was brought into play as a result of a player rolling a dice upon gaining their breakthrough, they will place ingress tokens according to the synergy on their breakthrough. For each color of technology in their breakthrough’s synergy, they choose three planets with a matching technology specialty, and place an ingress token in that planet’s system. <sup>7</sup>
  - Source 7 (p. 9, The Fracture): "If The Fracture was brought into play by a breakthrough roll, the rolling player places ingress tokens on the game board. For each synergy color on their breakthrough, that player must choose three systems that contain matching technology specialties, if able, and place ingress tokens in those systems."
- [Notes] If there are fewer than three planets with a technology specialty of a given color, as many planets as possible are chosen. <sup>7</sup>
  - Source 7 (p. 9, The Fracture): "that player must choose three systems that contain matching technology specialties, if able,"
- [Notes] If a different game effect places The Fracture into play, or The Fracture enters play because of the Nekro player’s breakthrough (which does not have a synergy), then the player that caused The Fracture to enter play chooses one planet with a technology specialty for each of the four colors of technology, and places ingress tokens in each of those planets’ systems. <sup>7</sup>
  - Source 7 (p. 9, The Fracture): "If The Fracture was brought into play by another ability, or by a breakthrough that does not have synergy (as is the case with the Nekro Virus faction), the player chooses four planets and places an ingress token in those planets’ systems. Each planet must be in a different system and must have a different technology specialty."
- [Notes] If one system contains two planets with a technology specialty, only one of those planets may be chosen when placing ingress tokens. <sup>7</sup>
  - Source 7 (p. 9, The Fracture): "Each planet must be in a different system"
  - Source 7 (p. 9, The Fracture): "A system cannot have more than one ingress token"
- [Notes] After ingress tokens are placed with either of these two methods, one additional ingress token is placed. If Thunder’s Edge is on the game board, then an ingress token is place into its system. Otherwise, an ingress token is placed into the Mecatol Rex system. <sup>7</sup>
  - Source 7 (p. 9, The Fracture): "Finally, the players place an ingress token in the Thunder’s Edge system, if it is in play, or in the Mecatol Rex system, if the expedition has not been completed."
- [Notes] A system cannot contain two or more ingress tokens. <sup>7</sup>
  - Source 7 (p. 9, The Fracture): "A system cannot have more than one ingress token"
- [Notes] When a player gains control of a planet in The Fracture that is not already controlled by another player, they draw one relic card. <sup>7</sup>
  - Source 7 (p. 9, The Fracture): "Each planet in the fracture has a relic icon."
  - Source 7 (p. 10, Relics): "When a player gains a planet card from the planet deck that has a relic icon, or when a game effect tells them to draw a relic, they draw the top card of the relic deck"
- [Notes] The "0" side of the d10 represents a result of 10. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (LRR v2.0 FAQ section, General (p. 40)): "A: Yes, the “0” face is a “10” result."
- [Notes] With sufficient movement, a ship could move from a system containing an ingress in the regular game map, into a system containing an egress within The Fracture, and then out to a different system containing an ingress in the regular game map. A ship could also do the reverse to travel from an egress to a different egress via an ingress. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (fracture-ingress-movement (Community consensus)): "they can go in through one ingress and out via an egress to another ingress system if their move allows"
  - Source 2 (fracture-ingress-egress-both-ways (Community consensus)): "ingress and egress adjacency works both ways, like wormholes"

**Notes added** (rulings that were not on the site before)

- [Notes] While The Fracture is not in play, its systems, such as the one containing Styx, are not legal targets for abilities such as those of the Yin player’s and L1Z1X player’s heroes. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (The Fracture): "No. The Fracture is not in play and not a legal target."
- [Notes] If The Fracture enters play as a result of the expedition that also places Thunder’s Edge, Thunder’s Edge is placed first, and then the final ingress token is placed in its system. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (The Fracture): "Thunder’s Edge is placed, then you place the final Ingress in the Thunder’s Edge system."
- [Notes] Attachments, such as the Nano–Forge relic and the Ul player’s Terraform promissory note, may be attached to planets in The Fracture. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (The Fracture): "Can Nano-Forge and/or Terraform be attached to planets in The Fracture?"

  - Source 6 (Vuil’raith Cabal): "No, the rules state that a system may not contain more than 1 ingress token."

### R_ground_combat.php

**Notes kept**

- [Notes] A player may score up to one secret objective per ground combat. <sup>1</sup>
  - Edited from: A player may score up to one secret objective per ground combat. If there is combat on multiple planets, a player may score a secret objective in each.
  - Source 1 (61.7): "they can only score one objective during or after each combat."
- [Notes] A player may use the Sustain Damage ability of a unit involved in a combat, usually a mech, to cancel a hit produced by their opponent. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (87.4): "A unit can use its “Sustain Damage” ability any time a hit is produced against it. This includes hits produced during combat"

**Removed notes restored**

- [Notes] If ground combat is to happen on multiple planets during a single invasion step, they will be resolved planet by planet, after the Space Cannon Defense step has been resolved on all planets and before the Establish Control step is resolved on any planet. The active player chooses the order combats are fought in. <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p. 15, Invasion): "Ground combats on multiple planets are resolved in the order of the active player’s choice."
  - Source 3 (p. 15, Invasion): "Players resolve an invasion by performing the following steps in"
- [Notes] The "0" side of the d10 represents a result of 10. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (LRR v2.0 FAQ section, General (p. 40)): "A: Yes, the “0” face is a “10” result."
- [Notes] The “start of combat” and “start of combat round” windows occur before the Roll Dice step. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (magen-defense-grid-disabled-pds (Community consensus)): "That hit lands at the start of ground combat, before dice are rolled, so the destroyed unit never rolls"

**Citations added to existing items**

- [Rules Reference] During the Ground Combat step of an invasion, if the active player has ground forces on a planet that contains another player’s ground forces, those players resolve a ground combat on that planet. To resolve a ground combat, players perform the following steps: now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p. 15, Invasion): "If multiple players have ground forces on the same planet, those players resolve a ground combat."
- [Rules Reference] Step 1 – Roll Dice: Each player rolls one die for each ground force they have on the planet; this is a combat roll. If a unit’s combat roll produces a result that is equal to or greater than that unit’s combat value, that roll produces a hit. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p. 14, Space Combat): "If the result of a unit’s die roll is equal to or greater than that unit’s combat value shown on its faction sheet, that roll produces a hit."
  - Source 3 (p. 15, Invasion): "following the same rules as the space combat steps of the same name"
- [Rules Reference] If a unit’s combat value contains two or more burst icons, the player rolls one die for each burst icon instead. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p. 14, Space Combat): "If a unit’s combat value contains two or more burst icons, the player rolls this number of dice instead"
  - Source 3 (p. 15, Invasion): "following the same rules as the space combat steps of the same name"
- [Rules Reference] Step 2 – Assign Hits: Each player in the combat must choose one of their own ground forces on the planet to be destroyed for each hit result their opponent produced. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p. 14, Space Combat): "Each player must choose and destroy one of their ships for each hit their opponent produced."
  - Source 3 (p. 15, Invasion): "following the same rules as the space combat steps of the same name"
- [Rules Reference] After assigning hits, if both players still have ground forces on the planet, players resolve a new combat round starting with the Roll Dice step. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p. 15, Invasion): "if multiple players have units remaining on the planet, they resolve another round of ground combat starting with the “Make Combat Rolls” step."
- [Rules Reference] Ground combat ends when only one player (or neither player) has ground forces on the planet. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p. 15, Invasion): "After all units on one or both sides of the combat have been destroyed, proceed to the next step."
- [Rules Reference] If neither player has a ground force remaining, there is no winner; the combat ends in a draw. now also cites <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (Skootur, Oct 12, 2017): "6. Neither player has units remaining on the planet"
  - Source 5 (Skootur, Oct 12, 2017): "3. The combat is considered to be a draw"
  - Source 5 (Skootur, 1/25/2019): "A draw is neither a win nor a loss."
- [Rules Reference] During the Ground Combat step of an invasion, if the active player has ground forces on a planet that contains another player’s ground forces, those players resolve a ground combat on that planet. To resolve a ground combat, players perform the following steps:. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (ground-combat-needs-both-sides (Per the rulebook — Invasion and Ground Combat)): "ground combat only happens if both players still have ground forces on the planet"
- [Rules Reference] During the first round of a combat, “start of combat” and “start of combat round” effects occur during the same timing window. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (start-of-combat-timing (Community consensus)): "Yes — they are the same window"
- [Rules Reference] After a combat ends, the player with one or more ground forces remaining on the planet is the winner of the combat; the other player is the loser of the combat. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (what-counts-as-winning-a-combat (Community consensus)): "you win when your units remain and the opponent's don't"
- [Rules Reference] If neither player has a ground force remaining, there is no winner; the combat ends in a draw. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (shard-of-the-throne-draw (Community consensus)): "if neither player has ground forces left, nobody won the combat"
- [Notes] A player may score up to one secret objective per ground combat. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (action-phase-secret-objectives (Per the rulebook — Objectives and Victory Points)): "only one per combat or step"
- [Notes] The “0” side of the d10 represents a result of 10. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (zero-on-die-is-ten (Community consensus)): "10 — the Living Rules Reference FAQ confirms the 0 face is a 10"

**Restored without a source** (marked * on the site)

- [Notes] The "end of combat" and "end of combat round" windows occur after the Assign Hits step. <sup>*</sup>
- [Notes] No player may retreat from a ground combat. <sup>*</sup>

### R_infantry_tokens.php

**LRR section corrections**

- **46.3a**: match LRR v2.0 wording
  - Before: If the player cannot replace the token, the unit is destroyed.
  - After: If that player cannot replace the token, the unit is destroyed.

**Notes kept**

- [Notes] Infantry tokens are not component limited. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (23.2): "Tokens are limited to those included in the game, except for the following:"
- [Notes] If a player has an infantry token that is not accompanied by a plastic infantry and cannot replace it, the token is removed instead of destroyed. <sup>4</sup>
  - Edited from: A future rule change will have any unaccompanied infantry tokens removed, instead of destroyed.
  - Source 4 (General (exceeding plastic infantry/fighters)): "A: Removed."

**Removed notes restored**

- [Notes] As each player only has twelve plastic infantry figures, a player cannot have infantry on more than twelve planets or being transported in more than twelve space areas, or any combination thereof. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (fighter-and-infantry-tokens (Community consensus)): "your plastic fighters and infantry limit how many places you can have them, not how many you have"

**Citations added to existing items**

- [Rules Reference] An infantry token functions as a plastic infantry unit for all game purposes. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p. 16, Production): "These tokens function identically to plastic figures of that type"
- [Rules Reference] When producing an infantry unit, a player can use an infantry token from the supply instead of a plastic piece. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p. 16, Production): "that player can use fighter or infantry tokens from the supply instead."
- [Rules Reference] Players can replace their plastic infantry with tokens at any time. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (fighter-and-infantry-tokens (Community consensus)): "You may swap a plastic piece on the board for a token at any time"
- [Rules Reference] If a player ever has an infantry token on a planet that does not contain one of their plastic infantry or in the space area of a system that does not contain one of their plastic infantry, that player must replace it with one of their plastic infantry from their reinforcements. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (fighter-and-infantry-tokens (Community consensus)): "each stack of tokens must sit with at least one plastic piece of the same type"
- [Notes] Infantry tokens are not component limited. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (fighter-and-infantry-tokens (Community consensus)): "Tokens are unlimited"

**Restored without a source** (marked * on the site)

- [Notes] A player may remove a plastic infantry figure from a planet or space area, along with any accompanying infantry tokens, if doing so allows them to swap it into the active system and allows them to commit ground forces to and fight ground combats on multiple planets during the Invasion step ... when they could otherwise not do so. <sup>*</sup>

**Removed notes that the site already covers elsewhere**

- [Notes] Players may also swap infantry tokens for plastic pieces at any time. _(no source (LRR 46.2 only states plastic to tokens))_
  - Covered by [R_component_limitations.php](R_component_limitations.php) [Rules Reference]: ... players can swap infantry and fighter tokens for plastic pieces at any time.

### R_influence.php

**Citations added to existing items**

- [Rules Reference] Influence represents a planet’s political power. Players spend influence to gain command tokens using the Leadership strategy card, and the influence values of planets are used to cast votes during the agenda phase. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p.5 Planets): "Players spend influence to gain command tokens and to vote during the agenda phase."
- [Rules Reference] A planet’s influence is the rightmost value (surrounded by a blue border) found on the planet’s system tile and planet card. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p.5 Planets): "two values: resources on the left in yellow and influence on the right in blue"
- [Rules Reference] A player can spend a planet’s influence by exhausting that planet’s card. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p.16 Key Concept: Spending Resources and Influence): "To spend a planet’s resources or influence, a player exhausts that planet’s planet card."
- [Rules Reference] A player can spend a trade good as if it were one influence. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p.17 Trade Goods and Commodities): "A player may spend a trade good as either one resource or one influence."
- [Rules Reference] A player can spend a planet’s influence by exhausting that planet’s card. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (spending-planets-one-use (Community consensus)): "exhausting a planet spends either its resources or its influence"
- [Rules Reference] A player can spend a trade good as if it were one influence. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (trade-goods-cannot-vote (Per the rulebook — 4. Agenda Phase)): "trade goods count as influence for everything except voting"
- [Rules Reference] Players cannot spend trade goods to cast votes during the agenda phase. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (trade-goods-cannot-vote (Per the rulebook — 4. Agenda Phase)): "trade goods count as influence for everything except voting"

### R_invasion.php

**Notes kept**

- [Notes] If a player gains control of an uncontrolled planet during the Establish Control step, they explore it. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (35.1): "When a player takes control of a planet that is not already controlled by another player, they explore that planet."
- [Notes] If a player gains control of a legendary planet, they gain the legendary planet ability card in addition to the planet card. <sup>1</sup>
  - Edited from: If a player gains control of a legendary planet, they gain the legendary planet ability card in addition to the planet card. The ability card will not be exhausted if it was readied.
  - Source 1 (53.2): "When a player gains control of a legendary planet, they also place its legendary planet ability card in their play area."
- [Notes] If Mecatol Rex has the custodians token on it, a player must remove it before they may commit ground forces to it. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (27.1): "players cannot commit ground forces to land on Mecatol Rex until the custodians token is removed from the planet."

**Notes added** (rulings that were not on the site before)

- [Notes] Unless an ability states otherwise, ground forces can only land on a planet by being committed during the Commit Ground Forces step, even if the player already controls that planet. Abilities that move ships as part of a component action do not allow ground forces to land on planets. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (landing-only-in-invasion-step (Community consensus)): "No — ground forces land on planets only by being committed in the invasion step of a tactical action"

**Citations added to existing items**

- [Rules Reference] Invasion is a step of the tactical action during which the active player can land ground forces on planets to gain control of those planets. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p.15 Invasion): "The active player can invade planets in the active system."
- [Rules Reference] To resolve an invasion, players perform the following steps: now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p.15 Invasion): "Players resolve an invasion by performing the following steps in order"
- [Rules Reference] Step 1 – Bombardment: The active player may use the Bombardment ability of any of their units in the active system. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p.15 Invasion): "the active player may use the “Bombardment” abilities of any of their units in that system"
- [Rules Reference] Step 2 – Commit Ground Forces: If the active player has ground forces in the space area of the active system, that player may commit any number of those ground forces to land on any of the planets in that system. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p.15 Invasion): "The active player decides which ground forces they wish to land on planets."
- [Rules Reference] To commit a ground force to a planet, the active player places that ground force unit on that planet. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p.15 Invasion): "places each one on the planet they wish to invade"
- [Rules Reference] Step 3 – Space Cannon Defense: If the active player commits any ground forces to a planet that contains units that have the Space Cannon ability, those Space Cannon abilities can be used against the committed ground forces. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p.15 Invasion): "If another player has a PDS on any of the planets the active player has committed ground forces to, the player who has a PDS may be able to use its “Space Cannon” ability"
- [Rules Reference] Step 4 – Ground Combat: If the active player has ground forces on a planet in the active system that contains another player’s ground forces, those players resolve a ground combat on that planet. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p.15 Invasion): "If multiple players have ground forces on the same planet, those players resolve a ground combat."
- [Rules Reference] If players must resolve a combat on more than one planet, the active player chooses the order in which those combats are resolved. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p.15 Invasion): "Ground combats on multiple planets are resolved in the order of the active player’s choice."
- [Rules Reference] Step 5 – Establish Control: The active player gains control of each planet they committed ground forces to if that planet still contains at least one of their ground forces. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p.15 Invasion): "The active player gains control of each invaded planet that still contains at least one of their ground forces."
- [Rules Reference] When a player gains control of a planet, any structures on the planet that belong to other players are immediately destroyed. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p.15 Invasion): "if the planet contains structures that belong to another player, those structures are destroyed"
- [Rules Reference] When a player gains control of a planet, they gain the planet card that matches that planet and exhaust that card. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p.15 Invasion): "they gain its corresponding planet card and place it in their play area exhausted"
- [Notes] If a player gains control of an uncontrolled planet during the Establish Control step, they explore it. now also cites <sup>8</sup>
  - Source 8 (p.11 Exploration): "When a player takes control of a planet that is not already controlled by another player, they explore that planet."
- [Notes] If a player gains control of a legendary planet, they gain the legendary planet ability card in addition to the planet card. now also cites <sup>7,8</sup>
  - Source 8 (p.10 Legendary Planets): "When a player takes control of a legendary planet, they also place its legendary planet ability card in their play area."
  - Source 7 (p.10 Legendary Planets): "When a player takes control of a legendary planet, they also place its legendary planet ability card in their play area."
- [Notes] If Mecatol Rex has the custodians token on it, a player must remove it before they may commit ground forces to it. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p.20 Custodians of Mecatol Rex): "cannot land ground forces on the planet while the custodians token is present"
- [Rules Reference] If there was a combat, and all units belonging to both players were destroyed, the player who was the defender retains control of the planet and places one of their control tokens on the planet. now also cites <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (aegiscruiser, Oct 4, 2017 / Skootur, Oct 12, 2017 (BGG)): "Neither player has units remaining on the planet, the defender retains control of the planet (44.5)"
- [Rules Reference] Step 1 – Bombardment: The active player may use the Bombardment ability of any of their units in the active system. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (bombardment-optional (Community consensus)): "The Bombardment step always happens, but using the ability is optional: the active player may bombard."
- [Rules Reference] Step 2 – Commit Ground Forces: If the active player has ground forces in the space area of the active system, that player may commit any number of those ground forces to land on any of the planets in that system. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (invade-several-planets-one-action (Community consensus)): "in the invasion step you commit ground forces to any or all planets in the active system"
  - Source 2 (commit-from-planet-to-another-planet (Community consensus)): "Only ground forces in the space area can be committed"
- [Rules Reference] If the active player does not wish to commit ground forces, that player proceeds to the Production step of the tactical action. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (invasion-optional (Community consensus)): "committing ground forces is optional. You can leave your ships in space and go straight to production"
- [Rules Reference] Step 3 – Space Cannon Defense: If the active player commits any ground forces to a planet that contains units that have the Space Cannon ability, those Space Cannon abilities can be used against the committed ground forces. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (space-cannon-defense-which-pds (Community consensus)): "Only PDS on the planet being invaded."
- [Rules Reference] Step 4 – Ground Combat: If the active player has ground forces on a planet in the active system that contains another player’s ground forces, those players resolve a ground combat on that planet. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (ground-combat-needs-both-sides (Per the rulebook — Invasion and Ground Combat)): "ground combat only happens if both players still have ground forces on the planet after those steps"
- [Rules Reference] Step 5 – Establish Control: The active player gains control of each planet they committed ground forces to if that planet still contains at least one of their ground forces. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (two-planets-separate-combats (Per the rulebook — Invasion and Ground Combat)): "you take only the planets where your ground forces remain and the defender's don't"
- [Rules Reference] When a player gains control of a planet, any structures on the planet that belong to other players are immediately destroyed. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (structures-destroyed-when-planet-taken (Community consensus)): "They are destroyed when another player's ground forces take control of the planet with none of the owner's ground forces left."
- [Rules Reference] When a player gains control of a planet, they gain the planet card that matches that planet and exhaust that card. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (legendary-ability-card-ready (Community consensus)): "The planet card arrives exhausted as usual"
- [Rules Reference] If there was a combat, and all units belonging to both players were destroyed, the player who was the defender retains control of the planet and places one of their control tokens on the planet. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (two-planets-separate-combats (Per the rulebook — Invasion and Ground Combat)): "If both sides lose all their ground forces on a planet, the defender keeps control."
- [Notes] If a player gains control of an uncontrolled planet during the Establish Control step, they explore it. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (exploration-basics (Community consensus)): "When you gain control of a planet nobody controlled, draw a card from the exploration deck matching its trait"
- [Notes] If Mecatol Rex has the custodians token on it, a player must remove it before they may commit ground forces to it. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (custodians-token-mecatol (Per the rulebook — Control, Structures, and the Custodians Token)): "during invasion, before committing ground forces, spend 6 influence to remove the custodians token"

**Removed notes that the site already covers elsewhere**

### R_leader_sheet.php

**Citations added to existing items**

- [Rules Reference] Each player has a leader sheet that contains slots for their faction’s three leader cards as well as their faction’s mech unit card. now also cites <sup>8</sup>
  - Source 8 (Prophecy of Kings Rulebook p.8): "from top slot to bottom slot, they place their agent, commander, and hero leader cards and their mech unit card on the leader sheet."
- [Rules Reference] The leader slots of the leader sheet are where players place their three leader cards during setup. Each slot displays the name of the type of leader that is placed in that slot (agent, commander, and hero) as well as a symbol in the upper–right that helps players quickly determine which side of those leaders begins the game faceup. now also cites <sup>8</sup>
  - Source 8 (Prophecy of Kings Rulebook p.8): "All leaders are placed showing the side that has the slot icon in the upper-right corner."
- [Rules Reference] The mech slot of the leader sheet is where players place their mech unit cards during setup. now also cites <sup>8</sup>
  - Source 8 (Prophecy of Kings Rulebook p.8): "they place their agent, commander, and hero leader cards and their mech unit card on the leader sheet."

### R_leaders.php

**Removed notes restored**

- [Notes] A commander’s ability cannot be applied to the instance of the effect that unlocked it. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (leader-unlock-after-effect (Community consensus)): "unlock conditions are checked only after the current effect fully resolves, so the commander isn't unlocked until after that third technology"
- [Notes] A commander may be unlocked between two abilities that occur in the same timing window. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (commanders-unlock-immediately (Community consensus)): "As soon as its condition is met, mid-turn if need be ... It is checked only after the current effect fully resolves"

**Notes added** (rulings that were not on the site before)

- [Notes] Using an agent’s ability on behalf of another player is not a transaction, and does not require the players to be neighbors. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (agents-not-transactions (Community consensus)): "No to both — it is just an ability"

**Citations added to existing items**

- [Rules Reference] Each player has several faction–specific leader cards that represent characters with unique abilities. now also cites <sup>8</sup>
  - Source 8 (p. 10, Leaders): "Each faction has three leaders with unique abilities"
- [Rules Reference] Each faction has three leaders; one agent, one commander, and one hero. now also cites <sup>8</sup>
  - Source 8 (p. 10, Leaders): "Each faction has three leaders with unique abilities"
  - Source 8 (p. 10, Leaders): "There are three types of leaders:"
- [Rules Reference] A player’s leaders are placed on their leader sheet during setup. now also cites <sup>8</sup>
  - Source 8 (p. 10, Leaders): "Leaders are placed on their corresponding leader slots during setup."
- [Rules Reference] Each leader card is placed on the slot that matches its type. The leader cards are placed so that the hash mark symbols in the upper right are faceup and match the slot that the card is placed on. now also cites <sup>8</sup>
  - Source 8 (p. 10, Leaders): "All leaders must be placed showing the side that has the slot icon in the upper-right corner."
- [Agents] An agent does not need to be unlocked and begins the game in a readied state. They can be exhausted by resolving their abilities, and they ready during the Ready Cards step of the status phase. now also cites <sup>8</sup>
  - Source 8 (p. 10, Leaders): "Each agent ability exhausts that leader. Agents are readied along with all other exhausted cards during the “Ready Cards” step."
  - Source 8 (p. 10, Leaders): "Agent abilities are available from the beginning of the game"
- [Commanders] A commander must be unlocked to use its abilities. A player unlocks their commander if they fulfill the conditions listed after the “Unlock” header. now also cites <sup>8</sup>
  - Source 8 (p. 10, Leaders): "commander and hero abilities begin the game locked."
  - Source 8 (p. 10, Leaders): "When the goal on a leader card is fulfilled, the player flips the card and the ability on the revealed side is now unlocked and available for the player to use."
- [Commanders] After a player fulfills the unlock condition of their commander, they flip it over to its unlocked side. now also cites <sup>8</sup>
  - Source 8 (p. 10, Leaders): "When the goal on a leader card is fulfilled, the player flips the card"
- [Commanders] The Alliance promissory note allows a player to share their commander’s ability with another player. now also cites <sup>8</sup>
  - Source 8 (p. 10, Leaders): "This ability can be shared with another faction by trading the “Alliance” promissory card."
- [Heroes] A hero needs to be unlocked to use their abilities. A player unlocks their hero if they fulfill the conditions listed after the “Unlock” header. now also cites <sup>8</sup>
  - Source 8 (p. 10, Leaders): "commander and hero abilities begin the game locked."
- [Heroes] After a player fulfills the unlock condition of their hero, they flip it to its unlocked side. now also cites <sup>8</sup>
  - Source 8 (p. 10, Leaders): "When the goal on a leader card is fulfilled, the player flips the card"
- [Rules Reference] The Nomad’s The Company faction ability grants them two additional agents, for a total of five leaders. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (nomad-three-agents (Community consensus)): "their faction ability The Company puts the two extra agents beside their faction sheet at setup"
- [Commanders] A commander’s unlock conditions cannot be met while an ability or game effect is being resolved. That is, pending abilities or partially resolved game effects must be completed before checking if conditions are met. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (commanders-unlock-immediately (Community consensus)): "It is checked only after the current effect fully resolves"

**Notes removed**

- [Notes] For notes about a leader of a specific faction, see that faction's page. _(no source (navigation link))_

### R_legendary_planets.php

**Notes kept**

- [Notes] If a player wishes to resolve the Imperial Arms Vault ability of Hope's End, but they have no mechs left in their reinforcements, they may remove a mech from any system that does not contain one of their command tokens and place that instead. The mech will be placed undamaged. <sup>1,4</sup>

### R_movement.php

**Notes kept**

- [Notes] When an effect moves a unit to an adjacent system, modifying that unit's move value will have no effect. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (58.9): "neither a unit’s move value nor the rules specified above apply."
- [Notes] When an ability moves a player's ships outside of a tactical action, those ships may transport units out of systems that contain that player's command tokens; this restriction only applies during tactical actions. <sup>1,4</sup>
  - Edited from: An ability may move a player's ship out of a system containing one of the player's faction's command tokens. However, the transport rules prevent a player's units from being transported from systems containing one of that player's command tokens, other than the active system. An ability that moves a player's ship must also explicitly allow it to transport units from non-active systems containing that player's faction's command token for it to be able to do so. (original contradicted by FAQ; replaced with designer's answer)
  - Source 1 (FAQ section (General): transport with abilities that move ships): "Any effect that moves a ship allows that ship to transport units in its system, if it has available capacity."
  - Source 4 (General: Transport and Movement Abilities): "transportation of units out of systems that contain your command tokens are only applicable during tactical actions. During Movement abilities, you can transport units out of systems that contain your tokens."
- [Notes] Ships only move “into” the destination system. A ship may move “through” other systems. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (General: moving into systems): "Only the destination system is considered moved “into,” other systems are moved “through.”"
- [Notes] Fighters alone will block other player's ships from moving through that system, whether they are accompanied by a Space Dock or they are Fighters II. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (58.4b): "The ship cannot move through a system that contains ships that are controlled by another player."
  - Source 1 (FAQ section (General)): "Can fighters block ship movement? A: Yes, fighters can block ship movement"

**Removed notes restored**

- [Notes] During a retreat, units may be transported from the active system. <sup>10</sup>
  - Source 10 (Twilight Codex Vol. I p.14): "Instead, when a ship moves as part of a retreat, it can transport ground forces that are on planets in its system as normal."
- [Notes] A ship that can both move and be transported (i.e. Fighter II) cannot do both by “meeting” a ship with capacity partway through a tactical action movement, as all movement is simultaneous. <sup>1,5</sup>
  - Source 5 (DR, FFG Boards FrinkiacVIII, December 13, 2017): "Because there is no partial movement, the Advanced Fighters can either reach the active system from their current system or they cannot. It is not possible to move them part of the way and have a carrier do the rest of the work."

### R_neighbors.php

**Notes kept**

- [Notes] A player may make a deal with any player, however, these deals may only include a transaction if the two players are neighbors. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (28.1): "Players can make deals with each other at any time, even if they are not neighbors. However, deals that include a transaction must follow the rules for transactions, including that the players be neighbors."
- [Notes] A player may resolve one transaction with each other player per each agenda during the agenda phase, however, the agenda phase does not make all players neighbors. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (94.6): "While resolving each agenda during the agenda phase, a player may perform one transaction with each other player."
  - Source 1 (94.6a): "Players do not need to be neighbors to perform these transactions."

**Notes added** (rulings that were not on the site before)

- [Notes] Ships that move through a system do not make their owner neighbors with players who have units in or adjacent to that system, as those ships are never in that system. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (who-are-neighbors (Per the rulebook)): "Ships moving through systems don't create neighbors on the way, since they are never in those systems."

**Citations added to existing items**

- [Rules Reference] Two players are neighbors if they both have a unit or control a planet in the same system. They are also neighbors if they both have a unit or control a planet in systems that are adjacent to each other. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (Learn to Play p.17): "If a player has a unit or controls a planet in a system that is adjacent to a system that contains a unit or planet that another player controls, those two players are neighbors."
- [Rules Reference] Players can resolve transactions with their neighbors. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (Learn to Play p.17): "they may negotiate a transaction with one or more of their neighbors"
- [Notes] A player may resolve one transaction with each other player per each agenda during the agenda phase, however, the agenda phase does not make all players neighbors. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (Learn to Play p.20): "During each vote, players may freely negotiate transactions with other players, even if they are not neighbors with those players."
- [Notes] A player may resolve one transaction with each other player per each agenda during the agenda phase, however, the agenda phase does not make all players neighbors. now also cites <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (DR, CreussEmissary, Jan 17, 2019): "Simply being in the agenda phase does not confer neighbor status to all players."
  - Source 5 (DR, BGG sigmazero13, Jun 19, 2018): "I would also say that they could perform new transactions"
- [Rules Reference (intro)] Two players are neighbors if they both have a unit or control a planet in the same system ... or adjacent systems. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (who-are-neighbors (Per the rulebook — The Economy)): "Players with a unit or controlled planet in the same system or adjacent systems, wormholes included"
- [Rules Reference] Players can resolve transactions with their neighbors. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (who-can-transact-and-when (Per the rulebook — The Economy)): "only the active player can transact, and only with neighbors"
- [Rules Reference] Players are neighbors if the adjacency of systems is granted by a wormhole. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (wormholes-are-optional-adjacency (Per the rulebook — Movement Details)): "Systems with matching wormholes are adjacent for all purposes, movement, Space Cannon and neighbors included."
- [Notes] A player may make a deal with any player, however, these deals may only include a transaction if the two players are neighbors. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (who-can-transact-and-when (Per the rulebook — The Economy)): "Deals that don't exchange components can be made with anyone at any time."
- [Notes] A player may resolve one transaction with each other player per each agenda during the agenda phase, however, the agenda phase does not make all players neighbors. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (agenda-phase-transactions-non-neighbors (Designer ruling)): "every pair of players may make one transaction, neighbors or not. That doesn't make them neighbors for anything else"

### R_neutral_units.php

**Removed notes restored**

- [Notes] Neutral units are placed in some system within The Fracture when it enters play. Several other game effects also place neutral units. <sup>7,11</sup>
  - Source 7 (p. 9, The Fracture): "They then place neutral units as indicated on the back of The Fracture’s tiles."
  - Source 11 (p. 15, Ixthian Artifacts: Minor Factions): "player places 3 neutral infantry on that system’s planets"
- [Notes] If a player has ships in a space area that contains neutral units, they will resolve a space combat against those units. <sup>7</sup>
  - Source 7 (p. 10, Neutral Units): "Neutral units are non-player forces that engage a player in combat if the player moves units to the planet or space area that those neutral units occupy."
- [Notes] If a player has ground forces on a planet that contains neutral units, they will resolve a ground combat against those units. <sup>7</sup>
  - Source 7 (p. 10, Neutral Units): "Neutral units are non-player forces that engage a player in combat if the player moves units to the planet or space area that those neutral units occupy."
- [Notes] Any player other than the active player may roll the combat and unit ability dice during a combat involving neutral units. The combat values and unit abilities are found on the neutral unit reference card. <sup>7</sup>
  - Source 7 (p. 10, Neutral Units): "Neutral units’ combat stats are indicated on the neutral unit reference card, and their rolls are made by any player other than the active player."
- [Notes] Neutral units will always use each and every unit ability that they can. <sup>7</sup>
  - Source 7 (p. 10, Neutral Units): "Neutral units always use unit abilities when they can"
- [Notes] Neutral units do not take turns, own technology, or draw action cards, and so on. <sup>7</sup>
  - Trimmed from: Neutral units do not take turns, own technology, or draw action cards, and so on. They cannot retreat from combat.
  - Source 7 (p. 10, Neutral Units): "Neutral units do not take turns or perform any other game function unless explicitly stated by rule or ability text."
- [Notes] When a hit is assigned against a group of neutral units, it is assigned to the unit that is lowest on the neutral unit reference card. <sup>7</sup>
  - Trimmed from: When a hit is assigned against a group of neutral units, it is assigned to the unit that is lowest on the neutral unit reference card; generally, this corresponds to the unit with the lowest cost.
  - Source 7 (p. 10, Neutral Units): "hits are assigned to neutral units in the order presented on the neutral unit reference, prioritizing units lower on the reference card first"
- [Notes] Neutral units are considered to be another player’s ships for abilities and other game effects. However, there is no neutral player. <sup>7</sup>
  - Source 7 (p. 10, Neutral Units): "Neutral units count as other player’s units for the purpose of resolving players’ abilities and other game effects. There is, however, no “neutral player,”"

**Notes added** (rulings that were not on the site before)

- [Notes] Neutral units with Sustain Damage use it to cancel hits before any remaining hits are assigned. For example, if a neutral destroyer and a neutral dreadnought take one hit, the dreadnought uses Sustain Damage to cancel it. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (Neutral Units): "Sustain window occurs before assign hits and all units with SUSTAIN will use this to cancel hits before then assigning hits to neutral units"
- [Notes] The speaker makes any decisions for neutral units other than assigning hits during combat, such as assigning hits produced by Space Cannon. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (Neutral Units): "Speaker decides any decisions for the neutral units that are not hits during combat."
- [Notes] If there are no neutral units of a given type left in the supply, and one would be placed, it is not placed. <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (Neutral Units): "They are not placed."

**Citations added to existing items**

- [Notes] When a hit is assigned against a group of neutral units, it is assigned to the unit that is lowest on the neutral unit reference card. now also cites <sup>6</sup>
  - Source 6 (Neutral Units): "assigning hits to neutral units in the order presented on the neutral unit reference, prioritizing units lower on the reference card first"

**Removed notes that the site already covers elsewhere**

### R_objective_cards.php

**Notes kept**

  - Source 1 (61.5a): "they must fulfill the requirement on the card during the “Score Objectives” step of the status phase to score that objective."
- [Notes] A player may score an action phase secret objective when they are not the active player. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (61.5b): "When a player scores an objective during the action phase, they can do so at any time during that phase."

  - Source 4 (Objectives (Impersonation)): "Yes, you could draw an additional secret but would then need to return it and shuffle the secret objective deck"

**Removed notes restored**

- [Notes] Any number of players may score a given public objective during the status phase. <sup>3</sup>
  - Trimmed from: Any number of players may score a given public objective during the status phase. Players are not blocked from scoring an objective if another player earlier in initiative order scores it first, unless the earlier player achieved victory and ended the game by doing so.
  - Source 3 (p. 12, Winning the Game): "Any number of players can score each of these objectives."
- [Notes] The Bombardment and Space Cannon steps happen outside of combat. <sup>2</sup>
  - Trimmed from: The Bombardment and Space Cannon steps happen outside of combat; any number of secret objectives may be scored during those steps, and do not prevent another secret objective being scored during combat that turn.
  - Source 2 (what-counts-as-winning-a-combat (Community consensus)): "Destroying ships with Space Cannon during movement, bombarding away all defenders, or landing unopposed involves no combat"
  - Source 2 (space-cannon-wipes-attacker-no-combat (Community consensus)): "Space Cannon Offense happens at the end of movement, outside space combat"
- [Notes] The Anti–Fighter Barrage step, however, is a step during combat. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (nekro-singularity-what-counts (Community consensus)): "Anti-Fighter Barrage is part of combat and counts"
  - Source 2 (vuilraith-devour-not-cannon (Community consensus)): "Anti-Fighter Barrage is part of combat and counts"

- [Notes] If two players could each score an action phase objective during the same combat, the player whose condition is met first scores first; for example, a flagship or war sun is destroyed during a combat round, before the combat ends and has a winner. If both conditions are met at the same moment, the active player scores first. <sup>2</sup>

### R_politics.php

**Notes added** (rulings that were not on the site before)
