- [Notes] Other players may see whether each agenda card is placed on the top or the bottom of the agenda deck. Although the active player cannot show the cards, they may tell other players what the cards are, truthfully or not. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (politics-top-or-bottom-public (Community consensus)): "Yes — everyone can see where each card goes; only the faces stay secret."

**Citations added to existing items**

- [Rules Reference] The active player chooses any player that does not have the speaker token. The active player may choose themselves as long as they do not have the speaker token. The chosen player places the speaker token in their play area; they are now the speaker. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p. 7, Politics strategy card): "Choose a player other than the speaker."
  - Source 3 (p. 7, Politics strategy card): "That player gains the speaker token."
- [Rules Reference] The active player draws two action cards. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p. 7, Politics strategy card): "Draw 2 action cards."
- [Rules Reference] The active player secretly looks at the top two cards of the agenda deck. Then, that player places each card on either the top or the bottom of the deck. If they place both cards on either the top or bottom, they can place them in any order. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p. 7, Politics strategy card): "Look at the top 2 cards of the agenda deck."
  - Source 3 (p. 7, Politics strategy card): "on the top or bottom of the deck in any order."
- [Rules Reference] After the active player resolves the primary ability of the Politics strategy card, each other player, beginning with the player to the left of the active player and proceeding clockwise, may spend one command token from their strategy pool to draw two action cards. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p. 7, Politics strategy card): "strategy pool to draw 2 action cards."
- [Rules Reference] The active player chooses any player that does not have the speaker token. The active player may choose themselves as long as they do not have the speaker token. The chosen player places the speaker token in their play area; they are now the speaker. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (politics-choosing-speaker (Per the rulebook — 1. Strategy Phase)): "it must be someone other than the current speaker; that can be you if you aren't already the speaker"

**Restored without a source** (marked * on the site)

- [Notes] If there are few cards remaining in the action card deck, they will be dealt out in clockwise order from the active player. After those players have discarded down to their seven card hand limit, if necessary, the discard pile will be shuffled to form a new deck. The remaining players ... will then be dealt their action cards. <sup>*</sup>

### R_producing_units.php

**Notes kept**

- [Notes] Whenever a unit is produced, its cost must be paid, unless the effect that is producing the unit explicitly says otherwise. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (67.1): "To produce a unit, a player must spend a number of resources equal to or greater than the cost value of the unit they are producing."
- [Notes] A player cannot produce one fighter and one infantry for one resource. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (67.2): "If the cost is accompanied by two icons—typically for fighters and infantry—a player produces two of that unit for that cost."
- [Notes] If a player removes a unit in order to place it, because they have none of that unit type in their reinforcements, that unit is placed undamaged. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (General (removed and placed)): "If it is produced, placed, or replaced which would require a remove and place it is no longer damaged."

**Removed notes restored**

- [Notes] If an effect allows a player to produce a unit of a specific type, then factional variations do not prevent that player from producing that type of unit. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (faction-units-count-as-base-type (Community consensus)): "a faction unit counts as its base unit type for every purpose"

**Citations added to existing items**

- [Rules Reference] Each unit that a player can produce has a cost value presented on its faction sheet or technology card. To produce a unit, a player must spend a number of resources equal to or greater than the cost value of the unit they are producing. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p. 16, Production): "they may choose to produce any of the units on their faction sheet by spending resources equal to the chosen unit’s cost."
- [Rules Reference] Any resources spent in excess of a unit’s cost are lost. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p. 16, Spending Resources and Influence): "The player could exhaust a planet that has more resources, but the excess resources are lost."
- [Rules Reference] If a player is producing multiple units at a time, that player can add the cost of each unit they are producing to create a total cost before they spend any resources. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p. 16, Production): "When producing multiple units at a time, the cost values of those units are added together to determine the total cost."
- [Rules Reference] If the cost is accompanied by two icons – typically for fighters and infantry – a player produces two of that unit for that cost. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p. 16, Production): "If a unit’s cost is accompanied by two icons, such as the cost values of fighters and infantry, the player receives two units for the indicated cost."
- [Rules Reference] Each of the two units counts toward the total number of units a player can produce. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p. 16, Production): "each individual unit counts against the production limit."
- [Rules Reference] If a player cannot produce a unit because it is not in their reinforcements, that player can remove a unit from any system that does not contain one of their command tokens and place that unit in their reinforcements. Then, that player can produce that unit. A player can remove any number of their units in this way; however, any units that are removed must be produced immediately. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p. 16, Production): "that player may remove one of their units of that type from a system that does not contain one of their command tokens and return it to their reinforcements."
- [Rules Reference] When producing a fighter or infantry unit, a player can use a fighter or infantry token, as appropriate, from the supply instead of a plastic piece. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p. 16, Production): "that player can use fighter or infantry tokens from the supply instead."
- [Rules Reference] A player cannot produce ships in a system that contains other players’ ships. now also cites <sup>5,6</sup>
  - Source 5 (eumaies, Feb 21, 2018): "You can build ships normally, but if enemy ships are present, you cannot."
  - Source 6 (Crimson Rebellion): ""A player cannot produce ships in a system that contains other players’ ships". Does this apply to Subatomic Splicer?"
  - Source 6 (Crimson Rebellion): "It does apply."
- [Rules Reference] Spent resources must come from planets or trade goods that are controlled by the player who is producing the units. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (pay-with-any-planets (Community consensus)): "spend resources from any planets you control, wherever they are, plus trade goods"
- [Rules Reference] Each of the two units counts toward the total number of units a player can produce. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (production-limits-units-not-cost (Community consensus)): "Each fighter or infantry counts as one unit"
- [Rules Reference] When a player produces a unit through the use of their units’ Production abilities during a tactical action, that player follows the rules of the Production ability to determine where in the active system the units can be placed. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (where-produced-ground-forces-go (Community consensus)): "On a planet that holds a unit that used Production, never on other planets in the system"
- [Rules Reference] If a player cannot produce a unit because it is not in their reinforcements, that player can remove a unit from any system that does not contain one of their command tokens and place that unit in their reinforcements. Then, that player can produce that unit. A player can remove any number of their units in this way; however, any units that are removed must be produced immediately. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (taking-plastic-for-production (Community consensus)): "you may remove them from systems without your command token and produce them"
- [Rules Reference] A player cannot produce ships in a system that contains other players’ ships. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (blockade-production (Per the rulebook — Producing Units)): "a dock ... in a system with another player's ships and none of yours is blockaded and can only produce ground forces"
- [Rules Reference] Ground forces can still be produced. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (blockade-production (Per the rulebook — Producing Units)): "can only produce ground forces"
- [Notes] Whenever a unit is produced, its cost must be paid, unless the effect that is producing the unit explicitly says otherwise. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (produce-vs-place (Community consensus)): "An effect that says 'produce' means you pay the cost unless it says otherwise"

### R_production.php

**LRR section corrections**

- **68 (intro)**: missing final period vs LRR
  - Before: ...in the active system to produce units
  - After: ...in the active system to produce units.

**Notes kept**

- [Notes] A unit's Production value is the maximum number of units that may be produced by that unit, regardless of cost. For example, a space dock with Production 6 could produce six dreadnoughts or six fighters. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (68.1): "This value is the maximum number of units that this unit can produce."
  - Source 1 (68.1b): "When producing fighters or infantry, each individual unit counts toward the producing unit’s production limit."
- [Notes] Placement of produced units is not limited by a unit's Production value, only by the location of the producing units. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (68.1a): "that player can produce a number of units up to the combined total of their units’ production values in that system."
  - Source 1 (68.3): "When a player produces ground forces, that player must place those unit on planets that contain a unit that used its “Production” ability."
- [Notes] For example, tile 75 with Space Dock I on Abaddon and Ashtroth but not Loki: seven infantry may be placed on Abaddon, Ashtroth, or split, but not on Loki. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (68.3): "must place those unit on planets that contain a unit that used its “Production” ability."

**Removed notes restored**

- [Notes] If an effect allows a player to produce a ship of a specific type, then factional variations do not prevent that player from producing that type of ship. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (faction-units-count-as-base-type (Community consensus)): "a faction unit counts as its base unit type for every purpose, so the Prototype War Sun is a war sun."

**Notes added** (rulings that were not on the site before)

- [Notes] A player cannot produce ground forces on a planet that contains another player’s ground forces. <sup>4</sup>

- [Rules Reference] When producing fighters or infantry, each individual unit counts toward the producing unit’s production limit. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (Learn to Play p.16): "When producing these units, each individual unit counts against the production limit."
- [Rules Reference] When a player produces ships by using Production that player must place them in the active system. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (Learn to Play p.16): "Players always place ships in the space area of the system in which they were produced."
- [Rules Reference] When a player produces ground forces, that player must place those units on planets that contain a unit that used its Production ability. now also cites <sup>3</sup>

  - Source 5 (DR, BGG kaiteinomen, Sep 20, 2017): "you can put both of the Letani warriors on the same planet, if you wish, as long as one of the units that used Production is located there."
- [Rules Reference (intro)] During the Production step of a tactical action, the active player can resolve the Production ability of each of their units that are in the active system ... <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (produce-only-in-active-system (Community consensus)): "the production step only uses units in the system you just activated."

  - Source 2 (production-limits-units-not-cost (Community consensus)): "The number of units."
- [Rules Reference] ... can produce a number of units up to the combined total of their units' production values in that system. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (production-pooled-in-system (Community consensus)): "all your Production in the active system is pooled into one production: two space docks of 4 and 3 give 7"

### R_promissory_notes.php

**Notes kept**

- [Notes] A player may choose to reveal any or all of the promissory notes in their hand, if they so choose. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (FAQ section (General): reveal hidden information): "This information is kept hidden by default, but it is permissible to reveal it to another player or players as a strategic option."

**Notes added** (rulings that were not on the site before)

- [Notes] If a player receives a card, such as a promissory note, in a transaction during that card’s timing window, they may play it immediately. For example, a promissory note with “At the start of your turn:” timing may be played immediately if the transaction occurred during the “start of turn” timing window. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (FAQ General): "a promissory note with “At the start of your turn:” timing may be immediately played"
- [Notes] Returning a promissory note to its owner as part of resolving it is not a transaction. The note is returned even if the two players are not neighbors. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (returning-used-note-not-transaction (Community consensus)): "returning it is part of resolving the card, so it needs no agreement and happens even if you are no longer neighbors"

**Citations added to existing items**

- [Rules Reference] Each promissory note contains timing text and ability text. A player can resolve any of their promissory note cards by following the text on the card. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (Learn to Play p.21): "Each promissory note contains text that describes the card’s effect and indicates when the card can be resolved."
- [Rules Reference] A player cannot play their color’s or faction’s promissory notes. Since the cards are only valuable to other players, promissory notes can be traded as powerful negotiation tools. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (Learn to Play p.21): "A player cannot resolve their own promissory notes, but they can resolve other players’ notes that they receive from a transaction."
- [Rules Reference] If a promissory note is returned to a player, that player may give it to other players again as part of a future transaction. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (Learn to Play p.21): "a promissory note is usually returned to its original owner and may again be offered by that player as part of a transaction."
- [Rules Reference] When resolving a transaction, a player can trade a maximum of one promissory note from their hand to another player, even if that card originally belonged to another player. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (Learn to Play p.21): "A player cannot trade more than one promissory note during a single transaction. Players can also exchange promissory notes that they have received from other players."
- [Notes] If a player receives a card, such as a promissory note, in a transaction during that card’s timing window, they may play it immediately... now also cites <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (DR, BGG Clipper, Jun 6, 2018): "You can trade a promissory note and have it be immediately used during the start of turn window."
- [Rules Reference] Promissory notes are not mandatory unless otherwise specified. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (promissory-notes-optional-to-play (Community consensus)): "promissory notes are never mandatory unless the note says to play it immediately or place it face up."
- [Rules Reference] An unrevealed promissory note is not subject to effects in its ability text that return the card if certain conditions are met. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (unplayed-note-ignores-return-condition (Community consensus)): "a note you have not played face up ignores its own return conditions."
- [Rules Reference] When resolving a transaction, a player can trade a maximum of one promissory note from their hand ... even if that card originally belonged to another player. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (trading-received-promissory-notes (Community consensus)): "any note in your hand can be traded on"
  - Source 2 (what-can-be-traded (Per the rulebook — The Economy)): "plus one promissory note from each side"
- [Rules Reference] Promissory notes in the play area cannot be traded. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (trading-received-promissory-notes (Community consensus)): "Notes face up in your play area, like Support for the Throne, can't be traded or handed back voluntarily."
- [Notes] A player may choose to reveal any or all of the promissory notes in their hand, if they so choose. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (showing-hidden-cards (Community consensus)): "you may reveal your own hidden cards to anyone at any time, and they still count as hidden afterwards."
- [Notes] If a player receives a card, such as a promissory note, in a transaction during that card's timing window, they may play it immediately ... <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (creuss-iff-start-of-turn-transaction (Community consensus)): "it is still the start of your turn until you actually take an action, so you can trade for the note and then resolve its start-of-turn ability."

**Restored without a source** (marked * on the site)

- [Notes] The number of promissory notes in a player's hand is public information. <sup>*</sup>
- [Notes] When two players make a trade for a promissory note, the specific promissory note that was traded may be hidden from other players. <sup>*</sup>
- [Notes] However, it is public information that a promissory note was traded. <sup>*</sup>
- [Notes] The Alliance and Support for the Throne promissory notes must be played immediately when received. As such, trading either of these notes cannot be kept hidden. <sup>*</sup>

**Removed notes that the site already covers elsewhere**

- [Notes] For notes about specific generic promissory notes, see the promissory notes notes page. _(no source (navigation link, not a sourced rule))_
  - Covered by [index.php](index.php) [Components nav]: Promissory Notes (C_promissory_notes)
- [Notes] For notes about a promissory note of a specific faction, see that faction's notes page. _(no source (navigation text, not a sourced rule))_
  - Covered by [index.php](index.php) [Factions nav]: faction pages (F_*)

### R_reinforcements.php

**Notes kept**

  - Source 1 (23.4a): "When a player would place a unit, if there are none of that type left in their reinforcements, that player can remove a unit from any system that does not contain one of their command tokens and place that unit in their reinforcements."

- [Notes] Command tokens on a player's command sheet are not in that player's reinforcements. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (must-place-command-token-none-in-reinforcements (Community consensus)): "What if an effect makes me place a command token from my reinforcements ... and I have none there? You take one of your choice from your command sheet instead."
  - Source 2 (command-tokens-are-limited (Community consensus)): "Tokens you spend, such as for a secondary ability, go back to your reinforcements, not to your command sheet."

**Citations added to existing items**

- [Notes] If a player wishes to place a unit, but there are none of that type left in their reinforcements, they may remove a unit of that type from any system that does not contain one of their command tokens and place that instead. now also cites <sup>3</sup>

### R_space_combat.php

**Notes kept**

- [Notes] A player's fighters and ground forces do not count against capacity during combat. At the end of combat, any excess units are removed and returned to that player's reinforcements. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (16.3c): "A player’s fighters and ground forces do not count against capacity during combat."
- [Notes] While retreating, a player cannot transport more fighters and/or ground forces than they have capacity in the retreating ships. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (95 (intro)): "When a ship moves, it may transport any combination of fighters and ground forces, but the number of units it transports cannot exceed that ship’s capacity value."
- [Notes] Capacity is checked after the winner of a space combat is determined. <sup>1</sup>
  - Edited from: Capacity is checked after the winner of a space combat is determined. As such, it is possible to win a space combat with only fighters remaining, before removing those fighters due to lack of capacity.
  - Source 1 (78.10a): "If the winner of the combat has fighters or ground forces in the space area of the active system and those units exceed the capacity of that player’s ships in that system, that player must choose and remove any excess units."
- [Notes] The "0" side of the d10 represents a result of 10. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (LRR v2.0 FAQ section, General (p. 40)): "A: Yes, the “0” face is a “10” result."

**Removed notes restored**

- [Notes] The Dark Energy Tap technology allows a player to retreat into a system that does not contain their ships or a planet they control. <sup>8</sup>
  - Source 8 (p.7 Dark Energy Tap card): "Your ships can retreat into adjacent systems that do not contain other players’ units, even if you do not have units or control planets in that system."
- [Notes] While retreating, a player may transport zero or more ground forces from planets they control in the active system. The player need not decide which ground forces they transport until they execute the retreat. <sup>10</sup>
  - Trimmed from: While retreating, a player may transport zero or more ground forces from planets they control in the active system. The player need not decide which fighters and ground forces they transport until they execute the retreat.
  - Source 10 (p.14 Rules Updates: Retreating with Infantry): "Players no longer need to move ground forces from a planet to the space area during the “Announce Retreats” step. Instead, when a ship moves as part of a retreat, it can transport ground forces that are on planets in its system as normal."
- [Notes] Modifying the move value of a ship will have no effect when retreating. Retreats are limited to adjacent systems. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (retreat-destinations (Per the rulebook — Space Combat)): "Movement bonuses don't matter, as a retreat always goes to an adjacent system."

**Notes added** (rulings that were not on the site before)

- [Notes] When a player retreats, their fighters that remain in the space area of the active system are removed, even if that system contains one of their space docks. <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (sigmazero13, Jul 18, 2018): "does this mean the left-behind fighters are destroyed even if the system has a Space Dock?"
  - Source 5 (sigmazero13, Jul 18, 2018): "2b) They’d be destroyed."
- [Notes] Abilities that resolve at the start of a space combat, such as the Assault Cannon technology and the Mentak player’s Ambush faction ability, are resolved before the Anti–Fighter Barrage step. <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (livestrongbelwas, reddit, Feb 08, 2018): "Assault Cannon and Mentak’s Ambush happen before Anti-Fighter Barrage, which is its own distinct timing (essentially the first step of combat)"
- [Notes] If a space combat reaches a state where neither player can win, the attacker must retreat. If the attacker cannot retreat, their units in that combat are destroyed. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (combat-stalemate (Community consensus)): "The Living Rules Reference FAQ says the attacker must retreat."
- [Notes] Ships that have announced a retreat still roll dice during the Roll Dice step of that combat round, then retreat during the Retreat step. Retreating this way avoids abilities that resolve after the combat round, such as the N’orr player’s Exotrireme II. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (retreating-ships-still-roll (Community consensus)): "Yes — announcing a retreat doesn't stop you firing; you roll normally and then leave in the retreat step."
- [Notes] Ground forces transported by retreating ships, or moved with the Skilled Retreat action card, cannot land on planets in the system they move to; they remain in the space area. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (retreated-ground-forces-cannot-land (Community consensus)): "No — landing only happens in the invasion step of a tactical action in the active system, and a retreat doesn't activate anything."

**Citations added to existing items**

- [Rules Reference] After resolving the Space Cannon Offense step of a tactical action, if two players have ships in the active system, those players must resolve a space combat. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p.14 Space Combat): "If multiple players have ships in the active system, they must resolve a space combat in that system."
- [Rules Reference] Step 1 – Anti–Fighter Barrage: If this is the first round of a space combat, the players may simultaneously use the Anti–Fighter Barrage ability of any of their units in the active system. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p.14 Space Combat): "ANTI-FIGHTER BARRAGE: Each player’s units can use their “Anti-Fighter Barrage” abilities."
- [Rules Reference] This step still occurs if no fighters are present. now also cites <sup>8</sup>
  - Source 8 (p.16 Clarifications): "The “Anti-Fighter Barrage” step can occur even if a player’s opponent has no fighters in the combat."
- [Rules Reference] A retreat will not occur immediately; the units retreat during the Retreat step. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p.14 Space Combat): "A retreat will not happen immediately; the units will retreat at the end of the combat round."
- [Rules Reference] Step 3 – Roll Dice: Each player rolls one die for each ship they have in the active system; this is called a combat roll. If a unit’s combat roll produces a result that is equal to or greater than that unit’s combat value, that result produces a hit. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p.14 Space Combat): "Each player rolls one die for each ship they have in the active system. If the result of a unit’s die roll is equal to or greater than that unit’s combat value shown on its faction sheet, that roll produces a hit."
- [Rules Reference] If a unit’s combat value contains two or more burst icons, the player rolls one die for each burst icon instead. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p.14 Space Combat): "If a unit’s combat value contains two or more burst icons, the player rolls this number of dice instead"
- [Rules Reference] If a player has an ability that rerolls a die or affects a die after it is rolled, that player must resolve such an ability immediately after rolling all of their dice. now also cites <sup>10</sup>
  - Source 10 (p.14 Rules Updates: Rerolls During Combat): "a player can roll dice for all of their units in the combat before deciding which—if any—to reroll"
- [Rules Reference] Step 4 – Assign Hits: Each player in the combat must choose and destroy one of their own ships in the active system for each hit their opponent produced. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p.14 Space Combat): "Each player must choose and destroy one of their ships for each hit their opponent produced."
- [Rules Reference] When a unit is destroyed, the player who controls that unit removes it from the board and places it in their reinforcements. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p.14 Space Combat): "A player removes destroyed ships from the game board and places them in their reinforcements."
- [Rules Reference] Step 5 – Retreat: If a player announced a retreat during step 2, and there is still an eligible system for their units to retreat to, they must retreat. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p.15 Retreat): "If a player announced a retreat during the first step of the combat round, they retreat."
- [Rules Reference] To retreat, a player takes all of their ships with a move value in the combat and moves them to a single system that is adjacent to the active system. That player’s fighters and ground forces in the space area of the active system that are unable to move or be transported are removed. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p.15 Retreat): "To retreat, the player takes all of their ships from the combat and places them in an adjacent system."
- [Rules Reference] The system that a player’s units retreat to must contain one or more of that player’s units, a planet they control, or both. Additionally, the system cannot contain ships controlled by another player. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p.15 Retreat): "The chosen system cannot contain ships that belong to another player and must contain either a planet that the retreating player controls or at least one of their units"
- [Rules Reference] If any of a player’s units successfully retreat and are moved into an adjacent system, that player must place a command token from their reinforcements in the system to which their units retreated. If that system already contains one of their command tokens, that player does not place an additional token there. If the player has no command tokens in their reinforcements, that player must use one from their command sheet instead. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p.15 Retreat): "If the chosen system does not contain one of that player’s command tokens, the player must place one token from their reinforcements in that system when they retreat."
- [Rules Reference] After the Retreat step, if both players still have ships in the active system, those players resolve another round of space combat beginning with the Announce Retreats step. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p.15 End of Space Combat): "they resolve another round of combat starting with the “Announce Retreat” step"
- [Rules Reference] After a combat ends, the player with one or more ships remaining in the system is the winner of the combat; the other player is the loser of the combat. If neither player has a ship remaining, the combat ends in a draw and there is no winner. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p.15 End of Space Combat): "a player has won a space combat if they are the only player with ships remaining in the active system when the combat has ended"
- [Rules Reference] If a player announced a retreat during the Announce Retreats step, but their opponent has no ships remaining in the system, the combat immediately ends and the retreat does not occur. now also cites <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (kkohlm, Dec 12, 2017 (BGG)): "you cannot retreat in this situation. The combat immediately ends when your opponent no longer has ships in a system and the “Retreat” step never occurs."
- [Rules Reference] To retreat, a player takes all of their ships with a move value in the combat and moves them to a single system that is adjacent to the active system. That player's fighters and ground forces in the space area of the active system that are unable to move or be transported are removed. now also cites <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (0 hr, Jul 18, 2018 (BGG)): "That rule is only meant to apply to ground forces in the space area. The ground forces on the planets are just fine."
  - Source 5 (sigmazero13, Jul 18, 2018 (BGG)): "2b) They’d be destroyed."
- [Rules Reference] After a combat ends, the player with one or more ships remaining in the system is the winner of the combat; the other player is the loser of the combat. If neither player has a ship remaining, the combat ends in a draw and there is no winner. now also cites <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (Skootur, 1/25/2019): "A draw is neither a win nor a loss."
- [Notes] A player's fighters and ground forces do not count against capacity during combat. At the end of combat, any excess units are removed and returned to that player's reinforcements. now also cites <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (Milty, 08/02/2018): "During a combat, the fighters would persist until the end of combat"
- [Notes] While retreating, a player cannot transport more fighters and/or ground forces than they have capacity in the retreating ships. now also cites <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (Milty, 10/31/2018 / 0 hr, Oct 31, 2018 (BGG)): "the number you can attempt to move out of the system is still limited by your ships capacity in the same way that it is when you move"
- [Rules Reference] After resolving the Space Cannon Offense step of a tactical action, if two players have ships in the active system, those players must resolve a space combat. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (combat-is-mandatory (Per the rulebook — Space Combat)): "when two players have ships in the same space area [...] combat happens"
- [Rules Reference] During the first round of a combat, “start of combat” and “start of combat round” effects occur during the same timing window. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (start-of-combat-timing (Community consensus)): "Yes — they are the same window, before Anti-Fighter Barrage"
- [Rules Reference] Players cannot resolve Anti–Fighter Barrage abilities during any rounds of space combat other than the first round. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (what-is-a-combat-roll (Community consensus)): "Anti-Fighter Barrage happens only in the first round."
- [Rules Reference] This step still occurs if no fighters are present. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (argent-raid-formation-no-fighters (Community consensus)): "Argent fire barrage even when the opponent has no fighters"
- [Rules Reference] Step 2 – Announce Retreats: Each player may announce a retreat, beginning with the defender. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (retreat-announcement-rules (Community consensus)): "Either player can announce a retreat, the attacker included, but the defender announces first, and if the defender retreats the attacker can't that round. You can only announce one if you have a legal system to retreat to"
- [Rules Reference] If the defender announces a retreat, the attacker cannot announce a retreat during that combat round. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (retreat-announcement-rules (Community consensus)): "Either player can announce a retreat, the attacker included, but the defender announces first, and if the defender retreats the attacker can't that round. You can only announce one if you have a legal system to retreat to"
- [Rules Reference] A player cannot announce a retreat if there is not at least one eligible system to retreat to. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (retreat-announcement-rules (Community consensus)): "Either player can announce a retreat, the attacker included, but the defender announces first, and if the defender retreats the attacker can't that round. You can only announce one if you have a legal system to retreat to"
- [Rules Reference] A retreat will not occur immediately; the units retreat during the Retreat step. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (retreating-ships-still-roll (Community consensus)): "you roll normally and then leave in the retreat step"
- [Rules Reference] If a player has ships that have different combat values in the active system, that player rolls these dice separately. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (rolling-dice-by-combat-value (Per the rulebook — Space Combat)): "ships with different values roll separately"
- [Rules Reference] If a player has an ability that rerolls a die or affects a die after it is rolled, that player must resolve such an ability immediately after rolling all of their dice. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (rerolls-after-all-dice (Community consensus)): "rerolls and modifiers are applied after you have rolled all your dice"
- [Rules Reference] Before assigning hits, players may use their units’ Sustain Damage abilities to cancel hits. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (sustain-damage-basics (Per the rulebook — Space Combat)): "Before hits are assigned, a unit with Sustain Damage may cancel one hit"
- [Rules Reference] If a player announced a retreat during the Announce Retreats step, but their opponent has no ships remaining in the system, the combat immediately ends and the retreat does not occur. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (retreat-announcement-rules (Community consensus)): "If your opponent has no ships left after the round, the combat simply ends and your retreat doesn't happen"
- [Rules Reference] To retreat, a player takes all of their ships with a move value in the combat and moves them to a single system that is adjacent to the active system. That player’s fighters and ground forces in the space area of the active system that are unable to move or be transported are removed. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (units-left-behind-after-retreat (Community consensus)): "All your ships with a move value retreat together. Fighters and ground forces in the space area that the retreating ships can't carry are destroyed"
- [Rules Reference] The system that a player’s units retreat to must contain one or more of that player’s units, a planet they control, or both. Additionally, the system cannot contain ships controlled by another player. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (retreat-destinations (Per the rulebook — Space Combat)): "To an adjacent system with no other player's ships that contains your units or a planet you control"
- [Rules Reference] If any of a player’s units successfully retreat and are moved into an adjacent system, that player must place a command token from their reinforcements in the system to which their units retreated. If that system already contains one of their command tokens, that player does not place an additional token there. If the player has no command tokens in their reinforcements, that player must use one from their command sheet instead. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (skilled-retreat-own-command-token (Community consensus)): "A normal retreat [...] may go into a system that already has your command token; you just don't place a second one."
  - Source 2 (must-place-command-token-none-in-reinforcements (Community consensus)): "What if an effect makes me place a command token from my reinforcements, such as Diplomacy or a retreat, and I have none there? You take one of your choice from your command sheet instead."
- [Rules Reference] Space combat ends when only one player – or neither player – has a ship in the space area of the active system. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (combat-only-two-players (Per the rulebook — Space Combat)): "it continues until only one player's ships remain or one side retreats"
- [Rules Reference] After a combat ends, the player with one or more ships remaining in the system is the winner of the combat; the other player is the loser of the combat. If neither player has a ship remaining, the combat ends in a draw and there is no winner. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (what-counts-as-winning-a-combat (Community consensus)): "you win when your units remain and the opponent's don't"
- [Rules Reference] If the winner of the combat has fighters or ground forces in the space area of the active system and those units exceed the capacity of that player’s ships in that system, that player must choose and remove any excess units. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (capacity-during-combat (Community consensus)): "When combat ends, each player checks capacity and removes fighters and ground forces in space that are no longer supported."
- [Notes] A player’s fighters and ground forces do not count against capacity during combat. At the end of combat, any excess units are removed and returned to that player’s reinforcements. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (capacity-during-combat (Community consensus)): "capacity isn't checked during combat [...] When combat ends, each player checks capacity and removes fighters and ground forces in space that are no longer supported."
- [Notes] The Dark Energy Tap technology allows a player to retreat into a system that does not contain their ships or a planet they control. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (retreat-destinations (Per the rulebook — Space Combat)): "Dark Energy Tap drops the second requirement."
- [Notes] While retreating, a player may transport zero or more ground forces from planets they control in the active system. The player need not decide which ground forces they transport until they execute the retreat. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (retreat-with-ground-forces (Community consensus)): "retreating ships move and transport units like any other movement, so they may pick up ground forces from planets there within their capacity"
- [Notes] While retreating, a player cannot transport more fighters and/or ground forces than they have capacity in the retreating ships. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (retreat-with-ground-forces (Community consensus)): "within their capacity"
- [Notes] The “0” side of the d10 represents a result of 10. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (zero-on-die-is-ten (Community consensus)): "the 0 face is a 10"
- [Notes] When a player retreats, their fighters that remain in the space area of the active system are removed, even if that system contains one of their space docks. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (units-left-behind-after-retreat (Community consensus)): "are destroyed, even if a space dock could have supported them"
- [Notes] Abilities that resolve at the start of a space combat, such as the Assault Cannon technology and the Mentak player’s Ambush faction ability, are resolved before the Anti–Fighter Barrage step. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (start-of-combat-timing (Community consensus)): "before Anti-Fighter Barrage"
  - Source 2 (mentak-ambush-details (Community consensus)): "At the start of space combat, before Anti-Fighter Barrage"

**Notes kept**

- [Notes] A player gains control of a space station when they are the only player with ships in that space station’s system. <sup>7</sup>
  - Trimmed from: A player gains control of a space station when they are the only player with units in that space station’s system.
  - Source 7 (p.10 Space Stations): "A player gains control of a space station from the deck or from another player when they are the only player that has ships in its system."

  - Source 7 (p.10 Space Stations): "A player gains control of a space station from the deck or from another player when they are the only player that has ships in its system."
  - Source 7 (p.5 Space Stations summary): "Players gain control when only their ships are in its space area."

  - Source 7 (p.10 Space Stations): "They do not lose control of the station if those ships move out of its system."
- [Notes] Each space station has a corresponding planet card. The space station may be exhausted for resources or influence as though it were a planet. The space station will be readied during the status phase as though it were a planet, or by other game effects that can ready planets. <sup>7</sup>
  - Source 7 (p.10 Space Stations): "Each space station has a corresponding planet card, which is gained exhausted and is spent, readied as if it were a planet."

  - Source 7 (p.10 Space Stations): "structures and ground forces cannot be placed on or committed to space stations"
- [Notes] Space Stations do not count as planets for the purpose of scoring objectives, and a player may still score public objectives even if another player controls a space station in their home system. <sup>7</sup>
  - Source 7 (p.10 Space Stations): "they do not count as planets for the purpose voting, objectives, or controlling a home system"
- [Notes] For each space station a player controls, their commodity value is increased by one. <sup>7</sup>
  - Source 7 (p.10 Space Stations): "A player’s commodity value is increased by 1 for each space station they control"
- [Notes] Players may place a space station commodity token in the commodity area of their faction sheet as a reminder of their increased commodity value. <sup>7</sup>

  - Source 7 (p.5 Space Stations summary): "Increases commodity value by 1 (put space station token in commodity pool as a reminder)."
- [Notes] A player who controls one or more space stations may resolve transactions with other players who control one or more space stations. <sup>7</sup>
  - Source 7 (p.10 Space Stations): "A player that controls a space station can resolve transactions with other players that control a space station, even if they are not neighbors."
- [Notes] Players who resolve transactions in this manner need not be neighbors. <sup>7</sup>
  - Trimmed from: Players who resolve transactions in this manner need not be neighbors. However, the space stations will not make those players neighbors for other game effects.
  - Source 7 (p.10 Space Stations): "even if they are not neighbors"
- [Notes] A player may exhaust a space station at any time to convert any commodities that they have into trade goods. <sup>7</sup>
  - Source 7 (p.10 Space Stations): "players can exhaust a space station at any time to convert their commodities to trade goods"
- [Notes] If a system tile contains a space station, but no planets, then a frontier token will be placed in that system during game setup. <sup>7</sup>
  - Source 7 (p.16 Clarifications: Space Stations): "A system that contains a space station and no planets gets a frontier token during setup when playing with Prophecy of Kings."

  - Source 3 (p.13 Activation): "That system is the active system for the remainder of the tactical action."
- [Rules Reference] Other players’ command tokens do not prevent a player from activating a system. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p.13 Activation): "they may activate a system that contains other players’ command tokens"
- [Rules Reference] Step 2 – Movement: The active player may move any number of ships that have a sufficient move value from any number of systems that do not contain one of their command tokens into the active system, following the rules for movement. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p.13 Movement): "A player cannot move units out of a system that contains one of their command tokens."
- [Rules Reference] Ships that have capacity values can transport ground forces and fighters when moving. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p.13 Movement): "When such a ship moves, it may transport a number of fighters and ground forces"
- [Rules Reference] After the Move Ships step, all players can use the Space Cannon abilities of their units in the active system. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p.19 Space Cannon): "After the “Movement” step of a tactical action, all players can use the “Space Cannon” abilities of their units that are in the active system."
- [Rules Reference] Step 3 – Space Combat: If two players have ships in the active system, those players must resolve a space combat. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p.14 Space Combat): "If multiple players have ships in the active system, they must resolve a space combat in that system."
- [Rules Reference] Step 4 – Invasion: The active player may use their Bombardment abilities, commit units to land on planets, and resolve ground combat against other players’ units. now also cites <sup>3</sup>

  - Source 3 (p.16 Production): "The active player can produce units using their space docks in the active system."

  - Source 3 (p.24 Frequently Overlooked Rules): "Players can produce units at a space dock in the active system during their tactical actions, even if they did not move ships or invade planets."
- [Rules Reference] Step 1 – Activation: The active player must activate a system that does not contain one of their command tokens. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (cannot-activate-system-with-own-token (Per the rulebook — Tactical Action)): "you can't activate that system again until the token is removed"
- [Rules Reference] To activate a system, the active player places a command token from their tactic pool in that system. That system is the active system. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (one-system-per-tactical-action (Community consensus)): "Each tactical action spends one tactic token to activate one system."
- [Rules Reference] The player may choose to not move any ships. <sup>2</sup>

- [Rules Reference] After the Move Ships step, all players can use the Space Cannon abilities of their units in the active system. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (who-fires-space-cannon-offense (Community consensus)): "every player with Space Cannon in range of the active system may fire, the active player first"
- [Rules Reference] Step 3 – Space Combat: If two players have ships in the active system, those players must resolve a space combat. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (combat-is-mandatory (Per the rulebook — Space Combat)): "when two players have ships in the same space area [...] combat happens"
- [Notes] An ability that ends a player’s turn ends that turn as soon as it is resolved. No further abilities may be resolved during that same timing window. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (minister-of-peace-timing (Community consensus)): "Once it ends the active player's turn, no other abilities in that window can be resolved, per the developer's later FAQ ruling."
  - Source 2 (xxcha-nullification-field-timing (Community consensus)): "Once the turn ends, nothing more happens in it"

### R_technology.php

**Notes kept**

- [Notes] If a player is instructed to research a technology by any game effect, that player must meet the prerequisites for the technology they research. <sup>1,4</sup>
  - Source 1 (90.12): "When researching technology, a player must satisfy each of a technology’s prerequisites to research it."
  - Source 4 (Technology, researching via action card): "If an ability instructs you to “research” a technology, you require the prerequisites on that technology to do so."
- [Notes] If a player is instructed to gain a technology, that player does not have to meet the prerequisites. <sup>1,4</sup>
  - Edited from: If a player is instructed to gain a technology, that player does not have to meet the prerequisites, although most game effects that do this will specify what technologies may be gained by that effect.

  - Source 4 (Technology, researching via action card): "If you are instructed to “gain” or “replace” a technology, you do not require prerequisites."

  - Source 2 (what-can-be-traded (Per the rulebook — The Economy)): "A transaction may be lopsided, even a gift."
- [Rules Reference] While resolving each agenda during the agenda phase, a player may perform one transaction with each other player. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (agenda-phase-transactions-non-neighbors (Designer ruling)): "while each agenda is being resolved, from its reveal until its outcome resolves, every pair of players may make one transaction"
- [Rules Reference] Players do not need to be neighbors to perform these transactions. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (agenda-phase-transactions-non-neighbors (Designer ruling)): "neighbors or not."
- [Notes] If a player may perform multiple actions on their turn, they may still only resolve one transaction with each of their neighbors. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (one-transaction-per-turn-not-round (Community consensus)): "Per turn. ... a turn is one player's turn in the action phase."
- [Notes] Players cannot resolve transactions during the strategy phase or the status phase. Players may still negotiate ... not binding. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (no-transactions-strategy-status (Community consensus)): "transactions happen only in the action phase (active player with neighbors) and the agenda phase (anyone). Players can still talk and make non-binding deals at any time"

### R_transport.php

**Notes kept**

- [Notes] A ship may transport units in its system as it retreats or is otherwise moved out of the active system. <sup>1</sup>
  - Edited from: A ship may transport as it retreats or is otherwise moved out of the active system, as the units it transports will be picked up from the active system.
  - Source 1 (LRR v2.0 FAQ section, General (p. 41)): "Any effect that moves a ship allows that ship to transport units in its system, if it has available capacity."
  - Source 1 (78.7b): "That player’s fighters and ground forces in the space area of the active system that are unable to move or be transported are removed."
- [Notes] A ship cannot pick up more units from a planet than it has capacity. <sup>1</sup>
  - Edited from: A ship cannot pick up more units from a planet than it has capacity. However, a ship may pick up any units (including none) in a system as it transports, even if doing so would cause units to be removed due to capacity limits.
  - Source 1 (95 (intro)): "the number of units it transports cannot exceed that ship’s capacity value."
- [Notes] A future rule change will allow a player's ships to transport units from systems that contain that player's command token when those ships move outside of a tactical action. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (General, Transport and Movement Abilities): "The LRR will be updated to reflect that transportation of units out of systems that contain your command tokens are only applicable during tactical actions. During Movement abilities, you can transport units out of systems that contain your tokens."

**Removed notes restored**

- [Notes] A ship that can both move and be transported (i.e. Fighter II) cannot do both by "meeting" a ship with capacity partway through a tactical action movement, as all movement is simultaneous. <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (FrinkiacVIII, December 13, 2017 (FFG response)): "Because there is no partial movement, the Advanced Fighters can either reach the active system from their current system or they cannot. It is not possible to move them part of the way and have a carrier do the rest of the work."
- [Notes] For example, say a carrier (with capacity 4) is in the space area of a system along with four fighters. On the only planet in that system are eight infantry. There are no other units in the system. When the carrier moves out of the system, it obeys the following: <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (Milty, 10/31/2018): "You could in fact leave the system with 4 infantry, causing those fighters to die due to lack of capacity in the system."
  - Source 5 (CreussEmissary (Dane), Oct 31, 2018 (BGG)): "You could not, however, attempt to transport more units than the moving ships have capacity for in an attempt to destroy the excess."
- [Notes] The carrier may transport four of the eight infantry, leaving behind the four remaining infantry in the system. Now that the system has zero capacity, all four of the fighters will be removed. <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (Milty, 10/31/2018): "You could in fact leave the system with 4 infantry, causing those fighters to die due to lack of capacity in the system."
- [Notes] The carrier cannot attempt to pick up all eight infantry, even if it immediately removes four of them (and the fighters). <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (CreussEmissary (Dane), Oct 31, 2018 (BGG)): "You could not, however, attempt to transport more units than the moving ships have capacity for in an attempt to destroy the excess."
  - Source 5 (sigmazero13, Oct 30, 2018 (BGG)): "No, you cannot exceed a unit’s capacity to intentionally destroy units. You would have to leave some of them on the planet in this case."
- [Notes] A ship may pick up ground forces from a planet in the active system, usually to invade a different planet in the same system. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (commit-from-planet-to-another-planet (Community consensus)): "Only if a ship with capacity picked them up into the space area during the movement step."
  - Source 2 (moving-ground-forces-between-planets (Community consensus)): "a ship with capacity, already there or moving in, picks them up during movement, and they land on the other planet in the invasion step"
- [Notes] The carrier may transport the four fighters, leaving behind all eight of the infantry in the system. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (capacity-what-it-covers (Per the rulebook — Fleet Pool, Capacity, and Transport)): "Ground forces on planets need no capacity."
  - Source 2 (over-capacity-to-destroy-own-units (Designer ruling)): "you can load ground forces and leave fighters or infantry already in space behind"
- [Notes] The carrier may transport two of the eight infantry and two of the four fighters, leaving behind the six remaining infantry in the system. Now that the system has zero capacity, the two remaining fighters will be removed. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (over-capacity-to-destroy-own-units (Designer ruling)): "you can load ground forces and leave fighters or infantry already in space behind; capacity is a system total, so those left over are removed if what remains can't hold them"

### R_units.php

**Notes kept**

- [Notes] Units are component limited. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (23.4): "UNITS: Units are limited to those included in the game, except for fighters and ground forces."
- [Notes] Fighters and infantry are semi-limited, via the use of tokens. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (23.4b): "When producing a fighter or infantry unit, a player can use a fighter or infantry token, as appropriate, from the supply instead of a plastic piece. These tokens must be accompanied by at least one plastic piece of the same type"

**Removed notes restored**

- [Notes] If an effect allows a player to produce a ship of a specific type, then factional variations do not prevent that player from producing that type of ship. <sup>2</sup>
  - Trimmed from: If an effect allows a player produce a ship ... (missing 'to' fixed)
  - Source 2 (faction-units-count-as-base-type (Community consensus)): "a faction unit counts as its base unit type for every purpose, so the Prototype War Sun is a war sun."

**Notes added** (rulings that were not on the site before)

- [Notes] A faction–specific unit counts as its base unit type for all purposes. For example, the Muaat player’s Prototype War Sun is a war sun. Only the researched unit upgrade card is a technology; the unit printed on a faction sheet is not. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (faction-units-count-as-base-type (Community consensus)): "Yes — a faction unit counts as its base unit type for every purpose, so the Prototype War Sun is a war sun."
- [Notes] A player cannot remove their own units from the game board at will; units are only removed by game effects, such as being destroyed or captured. The exception is that a player may remove a unit from the board in order to place it when there are none of that type in their reinforcements. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (removing-own-units (Community consensus)): "No — units leave the board only through the game (destroyed, captured and so on)."

**Citations added to existing items**

- [Rules Reference] 4 Mechs now also cites <sup>8</sup>
  - Source 8 (Prophecy of Kings Rulebook p.8): "4 mech units"
- [Rules Reference] There are three types of units: ships, ground forces, and structures. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (pds-and-space-docks-are-structures (Per the rulebook — Components and Key Concepts)): "PDS and space docks are structures, a separate unit type. In the base game, infantry are the only ground forces."
- [Notes] Fighters and infantry are semi-limited, via the use of tokens. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (fighter-and-infantry-tokens (Community consensus)): "Tokens are unlimited, but each stack of tokens must sit with at least one plastic piece of the same type."

### R_victory_points.php

**Citations added to existing items**

- [Rules Reference] The first player to gain 10 victory points wins the game. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p.12 Winning the Game): "A game of Twilight Imperium immediately ends when one player has gained 10 victory points."
- [Rules Reference] Players gain victory points in a variety of ways. A common way that a player can gain victory points is by scoring objectives. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p.12 Winning the Game): "Players gain victory points by completing objectives."
- [Rules Reference] Each player places one of their control tokens on space “0” of the victory point track during setup. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p.7 First-Game Setup): "each player places one of their control tokens on space “0” of the track"
- [Rules Reference] When a player gains a victory point, they advance their control token a number of spaces along the victory point track equal to the number of victory points gained. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p.12 Scoring Objectives): "the player advances their token on the victory point track a number of spaces equal to the value of the objective card"
- [Rules Reference] If the game ends because the speaker cannot reveal an objective card, the player with the most victory points is the winner. If one or more players are tied for having the most victory points, the tied player who is first in initiative order is the winner. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p.12 Imperium Rex): "When the speaker would reveal an objective but cannot, the game immediately ends and the player with the most victory points wins the game. If there is a tie, the player among the tied players who is earliest in initiative order wins the game."
- [Rules Reference] If a player gains a victory point from a law, and that law is discarded, that player does not lose that victory point. now also cites <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (alercah, Sep 14, 2017 (BGG)): "Because the losing of the victory points is tied to the combat and not the losing of the card, the former owner would keep the victory point in both cases."
- [Rules Reference] The game ends immediately when one player has 10 victory points. If multiple players would simultaneously gain their 10th victory point, the player who is earliest in initiative order among those players is the winner; if this occurs when players do not have strategy cards, the player who is nearest the speaker (including the speaker) in clockwise order is the winner. now also cites <sup>5</sup>
  - Source 5 (alercah, Nov 22, 2017 (BGG)): "The intended tiebreaker when there is no initiative order is the one you mentioned: speaker, then clockwise."
- [Rules Reference] If the players are using the 14–space side of the victory point track, the game ends and a player wins when they have 14 victory points instead of 10. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (fourteen-point-game (Per the rulebook — Object of the Game)): "flip the victory point track to its 14-point side and play to 14 instead of 10"
- [Rules Reference] If an ability refers to the player with the “most” or “fewest” victory points, and more than one player is tied in that respect, the effect applies to all of the tied players. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (tied-for-most-or-fewest-points (Community consensus)): "All of them — every tied player counts."
- [Rules Reference] If a player gains a victory point from a law, and that law is discarded, that player does not lose that victory point. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (law-victory-points-kept-when-discarded (Community consensus)): "a point from these laws is lost only through the condition printed on the card. If the law is discarded some other way [...] the old owner keeps the point"
- [Rules Reference] The game ends immediately when one player has 10 victory points. If multiple players would simultaneously gain their 10th victory point, the player who is earliest in initiative order among those players is the winner; if this occurs when players do not have strategy cards, the player who is nearest the speaker (including the speaker) in clockwise order is the winner. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (two-players-reach-10-in-status-phase (Per the rulebook — Object of the Game)): "The first one in initiative order."
  - Source 2 (simultaneous-10-points-agenda-phase (Community consensus)): "Start with the speaker and go clockwise"
  - Source 2 (winning-during-action-phase (Per the rulebook — Winning the Game)): "the game ends the moment anyone reaches the goal"

### R_warfare.php

**LRR section corrections**

- **intro**: Owner decision: use the Thunder's Edge revised strategy card.
  - Before: The Warfare strategy card allows a player to remove a command token from the board and redistribute their command tokens…
  - After: The Warfare strategy card allows a player to perform a tactical action without placing a command token, and to redistribute their command tokens… <sup>2,13</sup>
- **99.1**: Owner decision: use the Thunder's Edge revised strategy card.
  - Before: Step 1: The active player removes any one of their command tokens from the game board. Then, that player gains that command token…
  - After: The active player performs a tactical action in any system without placing a command token, even if the system already has their command token in it; that system still counts as being activated. <sup>2,13</sup>
- **99.2**: Owner decision: use the Thunder's Edge revised strategy card.
  - Before: Step 2: The active player can redistribute their command tokens.
  - After: The active player may redistribute their command tokens before and after this tactical action. <sup>2,13</sup>
- **99.3**: Owner decision: use the Thunder's Edge revised strategy card.
  - Before: …may spend one command token from their strategy pool to resolve the Production ability of one space dock in their home system.
  - After: …may spend one command token from their strategy pool to resolve the Production abilities of units in their home system. <sup>2,13</sup>

**Notes added** (rulings that were not on the site before)

- [Notes] Resolving the secondary ability of Warfare does not activate the player’s home system. It may be resolved even if that system already contains one of their command tokens. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (warfare-secondary-home-system (Community consensus)): "It doesn't activate the system and works even if your home system already has your token"
- [Notes] If a tactical action that is part of the Warfare primary ability is cancelled, or the resolving player's turn is ended, the rest of the strategy card is still resolved. <sup>7</sup>
  - Source 7 (Clarifications, Warfare (Strategy Card)): "If a tactical action that is part of the Warfare primary is canceled, or the resolving player’s turn is ended, the rest of the strategy card is still resolved."
- [Notes] Ships may move into a system that has already been activated during the tactical action of the Warfare primary ability, but ships cannot move out of a system that has already been activated. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (te-warfare-card (Community consensus)): "You can move ships into an already-activated system that way, but not out of one."

**Notes removed**

- [Notes] If the player with Warfare has no command tokens on the game board, they may still perform a strategic action. However, they will not gain a command token. _(applies only to the original Warfare card)_

  - Covered by [R_wormhole_nexus.php + R_movement.php](R_wormhole_nexus.php + R_movement.php) [Rules Reference]: When a ship moves into the wormhole nexus, the nexus becomes active at the end of the Movement step. / Step 2 - Space Cannon Offense is a step of Movement
- [Notes] If the Creuss player moves their Hil Colish flagship into the inactive wormhole nexus, the wormhole nexus will not flip before they move any other ships... _(no source)_
  - Covered by [R_wormhole_nexus.php](R_wormhole_nexus.php) [Rules Reference]: When a ship moves into the wormhole nexus, the nexus becomes active at the end of the Movement step.

### R_wormholes.php

**Notes kept**

- [Notes] A system cannot be adjacent to itself, even if it has multiple wormholes in it. <sup>1</sup>
  - Source 1 (6.2a): "A system is not adjacent to itself."
- [Notes] A player chooses the path of adjacent systems each ship moves through during movement. <sup>4</sup>
  - Edited from: A player chooses the path of adjacent systems each ship moves through during movement. If two systems on that path are adjacent because of a wormhole, that ship moves through that wormhole.
  - Source 4 (General (moving through wormholes)): "The player moving the ships chooses the path their ships move through."
- [Notes] If the two systems are adjacent because of a wormhole and because of a shared edge or another reason, the player may choose whether or not the ship moves through the wormhole. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (General (moving through wormholes)): "you can choose to use those wormholes, a different set of wormholes that are adjacent, or regular adjacency."
- [Notes] If the two systems are adjacent because of two types of wormholes, the player chooses which type of wormhole the ship moves through. <sup>4</sup>
  - Source 4 (General (moving through wormholes)): "you can choose to use those wormholes, a different set of wormholes that are adjacent, or regular adjacency."

**Removed notes restored**

- [Notes] A system with a wormhole is not an anomaly. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (which-systems-are-anomalies (Community consensus)): "Empty systems and wormhole systems are not anomalies unless bordered"
- [Notes] A player may move a ship back and forth through a wormhole between two systems any number of times, if its movement value is high enough. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (move-out-and-back-into-active-system (Community consensus)): "a ship that starts in the active system may move out and back in if its move value allows, and a ship may pass back through a system it already crossed"

**Citations added to existing items**

- [Rules Reference] Some systems contain wormholes. Systems that contain identical wormholes are adjacent. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p. 14, Wormholes): "Systems that contain identical wormholes are adjacent to one another for all purposes."
- [Rules Reference] There are two basic types of wormholes: alpha and beta. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p. 14, Wormholes): "There are two types of basic wormholes–alpha and beta"
- [Rules Reference] If a player has a PDS unit upgrade technology, they can use the Space Cannon abilities of their PDS units through wormholes. now also cites <sup>3</sup>
  - Source 3 (p. 24, Rules Summary): "Players with upgraded PDS units in the same system as a wormhole can use those units’ “Space Cannon” abilities to fire through the wormhole."
- [Rules Reference] Some systems contain wormholes. Systems that contain identical wormholes are adjacent. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (wormholes-are-optional-adjacency (Per the rulebook — Movement Details)): "Systems with matching wormholes are adjacent for all purposes"
- [Rules Reference] Players can be neighbors and perform transactions through wormholes. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (who-are-neighbors (Per the rulebook — The Economy: Resources, Trade Goods, and Commodities)): "Players with a unit or controlled planet in the same system or adjacent systems, wormholes included"
- [Notes] A system cannot be adjacent to itself, even if it has multiple wormholes in it. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (system-not-adjacent-to-itself (Community consensus)): "A system is never adjacent to itself"
- [Notes] If the two systems are adjacent because of a wormhole and because of a shared edge or another reason, the player may choose whether or not the ship moves through the wormhole. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (ion-storm-flipping (Community consensus)): "With several wormhole routes, the moving player chooses which, if any, they use"
- [Notes] If the two systems are adjacent because of two types of wormholes, the player chooses which type of wormhole the ship moves through. <sup>2</sup>
  - Source 2 (ion-storm-flipping (Community consensus)): "With several wormhole routes, the moving player chooses which, if any, they use"

**Restored without a source** (marked * on the site)

- [Notes] If a system contains multiple wormholes of the same type, those are treated as separate wormholes. <sup>*</sup>

**Notes removed**

- [Notes] For additional information on how the Creuss interact with wormholes, see their faction notes page. _(no source (navigation link))_
